# High availability and Helm deployment

Status: built, except R-HA-053 (the Gateway the chart creates), R-HA-055 (the content host at the edge), R-HA-044's dual-stack values
of the Services (`service.ipFamilyPolicy`, `service.ipFamilies`), R-HA-046's `initContainers`, `sidecars` and `lifecycle`, R-HA-030's
`bootstrap.existingConfigMap`, R-HA-022's table `background_migration` with its pause, resume and shared runner, R-HA-013's CI matrix over
the supported PostgreSQL versions, R-HA-014's start checks of the audit objects' and the backup role's grants and R-HA-026's drill
with two clusters; the values of R-HA-031's block that the chart does not carry yet are those of `unbuiltPrefixes` in
[values_reference_test.go](../../test/chart/values_reference_test.go).

This page specifies how Quader stays available, scales out and is deployed. It covers:

- The replica model: identical, interchangeable replicas per role, with `api`, `packages` and `worker` as
  separate Deployments (the task areas of ADR-153 and ADR-155, built in phase 6a),
  `scanner` as the role of the scanning tools' Deployments without secrets, `vuln-scanner-trivy` and `malware-scanner-clamav`
  (ADR-212, ADR-221, Q-HA-372),
  pools of a role by path prefix or queue, `backup` as a CronJob (INV-2), and how replicas
  coordinate through PostgreSQL and Valkey without talking to each other (INV-3, INV-12, INV-18).
- The failure contract of every component: pod crash, node drain and node loss, PostgreSQL failover
  with reconnect and retry, Valkey failover through Sentinel and Valkey outage, object-storage
  outage, spool exhaustion and a failed migration.
- Leader-less scheduling and singleton work under advisory-lock leases.
- Node drains without outage: the capacity rule, disruption budgets, spreading and the drain
  acceptance test under npm and NuGet load.
- Rolling upgrades with expand/contract migrations (promised from the first stable release on, [Q-ARCH-340](architecture.md#q-arch-340--no-backward-compatibility-until-the-first-stable-release)),
  and the migration Job.
- PostgreSQL requirements: version floor, server settings, roles and privileges, TLS, connection
  budget, the optional transaction-mode pooler and credential rotation.
- Valkey requirements: discovery through Sentinel, credentials and TLS, supported topologies and
  the degraded mode.
- Backup, restore and disaster recovery from the deployment side: the backup CronJob, the restore
  Job, the platform layer (point-in-time recovery, bucket versioning) and why a restored database
  never points at a deleted blob. Backup format and procedure belong to
  [backup-and-restore.md](backup-and-restore.md).
- The Helm chart `deploy/helm/quader`: every resource it renders, every volume it mounts (none
  ReadWriteMany, none persistent) and its complete `values.yaml`.
- Edge-proxy requirements for large uploads, sizing guidance, the local development profile
  (kind, CloudNativePG, Valkey with Sentinel, SeaweedFS) and the failure-injection suite that
  proves all of the above.

Semantics owned elsewhere are referenced, not repeated. The probe endpoints and replica registry
are in [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md). Blob commit, garbage
collection and the object-store client are in [storage.md](storage.md). Secret sealing and
outbound TLS are in [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md). The break-glass account
is in [identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md).

Covers: the catalog pages [ha-and-deployment.md](../features/ha-and-deployment.md) (`HA`, all MVP
and P1 entries), the upgrade and backup entries of
[operations-and-monitoring.md](../features/operations-and-monitoring.md) (OPS-032 and OPS-033 on
the chart side, OPS-072, OPS-073, OPS-074, OPS-076), and the deployment side of
[storage-and-blobs.md](../features/storage-and-blobs.md) (spool volume, object-store credentials
through workload identity). The storage entries themselves belong to [storage.md](storage.md).

## Topology

The cut of phase 6a (ADR-153, ADR-155; the chart renders it). The releases before it ran one Deployment `<fullname>-web`
behind the Service `<fullname>` that served every path; no Quader release has that shape, and the chart has no path from it
([Q-HA-315](#q-ha-315--the-charts-upgrade-bridge-across-the-cut-is-removed-the-binary-keeps-the-role-web-for-development-and-tests)).

```text
             clients: npm, pnpm, Yarn, dotnet, nuget.exe, browsers, GitLab jobs
                                    │ HTTPS
                   ┌────────────────▼─────────────────┐
                   │  Ingress controller or Gateway   │  TLS ends here; one host split by path prefix (R-HA-037)
                   └───────┬─────────────────┬────────┘
     /, /ui, /auth, /api/v1 │                 │ /api, /files, /v2, /.well-known
     Service <fullname>-api │                 │ Service <fullname>-packages        (HTTPS :8080, no session affinity)
            ┌───────────────┤                 ├─────────────────────────┐
     ┌──────▼──────┐ ┌──────▼──────┐   ┌──────▼──────┐ ┌──────▼──────┐ ┌──────▼──────┐
     │ api pod     │ │ api pod     │   │ packages    │ │ packages    │ │ packages    │  Deployments <fullname>-api and
     │ :8080 :8081 │ │ :8080 :8081 │   │ :8080 :8081 │ │ :8080 :8081 │ │ :8080 :8081 │  <fullname>-packages; spool: emptyDir
     └─────────────┘ └─────────────┘   └─────────────┘ └─────────────┘ └─────────────┘
       UI, management API, sessions,     package protocols, raw files, tokens only,
       OIDC and break-glass secrets      the fills of client misses
     ┌─────────────┐         ┌─────────────┐
     │ worker pod  │   ...   │ worker pod  │  Deployment <fullname>-worker: jobs, :8081 only;
     └──────┬──────┘         └─────────────┘  optional pools by queue <fullname>-worker-<pool> (R-HA-062)
            │ HTTPS :8080, mutual TLS: one call per image (vulnerability-scanning.md R-VULN-041)
     ┌──────▼──────┐         ┌─────────────┐
     │ scanner pod │   ...   │ scanner pod │  Deployment <fullname>-vuln-scanner-trivy (R-HA-065): the analysis of images,
     └──────┬──────┘         └─────────────┘  no secret of PostgreSQL, the object store or Valkey; :8080, :8081
                                              (R-HA-070: the detection too, the database read-only in the pod,
                                              the analyser copied from its own image by an init container)
            │ HTTPS :8082, mutual TLS and a scan token: the pull of that image (R-VULN-042)
            ▼ Service <fullname>-packages-scan ──▶ the scan listener of every packages pod of the main Deployment
     ┌─────────────┐
     │ backup pod  │  CronJob <fullname>-backup ──S3──▶ backup target bucket (R-HA-060)
     └─────────────┘

  every pod ──SQL───▶ PostgreSQL primary ──streaming──▶ standbys (CloudNativePG, Patroni, RDS)
                      optional: request pool through a transaction-mode pooler, control
                      connection through a pool of its own (R-HA-058, Q-HA-20)
  api, packages, worker ─RESP─▶ Valkey primary ──replication──▶ replica; ≥ 3 Sentinels name the primary
                      (backup, restore and migration pods never connect to Valkey)
  every pod ──S3────▶ blob bucket, versioning recommended (AWS S3, MinIO, Ceph RGW, SeaweedFS)
  (the scanner pods connect to none of the three: R-HA-065)

  Helm hook before the Deployments: the migration Job. With restore.enabled: no migration Job,
  every role at zero, and the restore Job as an ordinary resource (R-HA-060, Q-HA-18)
```

Replicas of a role never open connections to each other. Every cross-replica signal goes through PostgreSQL
(job claims, leases, the replica registry, the change log that carries invalidations) or Valkey
(fetch collapse, the negative cache of remote repositories, rate-limit counters, change messages
and signals); [architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-030 assigns each mechanism (INV-12). The
pod network therefore needs no replica-to-replica rule and no peer discovery. The one seam between
roles is the image scanning's, at a trust boundary (ADR-153,
[ADR-212](../decisions.md#adr-212--the-image-analysis-runs-in-a-role-scanner-that-holds-no-secret)): a `worker` calls a
`scanner` through its Service, and the `scanner` pulls from the scan listener of `packages` through another; neither
call carries state that a later call needs, and both are admitted by ingress rules on their ports (R-HA-042, R-HA-066).
Everything a pod keeps outside these three services is scratch space for one request or one job (INV-18).

## Replica model and coordination

### R-HA-001 · Active-active replicas without a primary node
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: HA-001, HA-002, HA-010

- Every replica of a client-serving role MUST be able to serve every request of the route families of its role (`api`: the
  UI and every management request; `packages`: every package and raw-file request), and every `worker` replica every job
  kind of the queues it claims (R-ARCH-016). No replica holds state that another replica
  needs to answer a request (INV-2, INV-18): consecutive requests of one client, the requests of a
  multi-request protocol included, may reach different replicas. The only local state is the spool
  of the request or job that is running (R-HA-035) and in-process caches, which are invalidated via
  R-HA-004.
- There MUST be no primary, leader or seed replica in configuration. Work that must run once per
  cluster runs under leases that any `worker` replica can take (R-HA-005, R-HA-006).
- **Roles** (INV-2, [architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-001). A process has one role,
  `process.role: api|packages|worker|web|all`, which has no default. The chart starts each Deployment with
  `quader serve --role <role>`, the flag form that overrides `process.role` (R-HA-002), so the
  shared configuration file names no role:
  - `api` serves the route families `ui`, `api` and `ci_exchange` on the client listener and the operations listener, and
    never claims jobs or leases;
  - `packages` serves the route families `packages` and `files` on the client listener and the operations listener, with
    tokens only, and never claims jobs or leases;
  - `worker` claims jobs and leases, and serves only the operations listener;
  - `scanner` analyses container images for the worker's image scanning on its own listener and the operations listener, holds
    no credential of PostgreSQL, the object store or Valkey and no key of the key ring, and never claims jobs or leases
    ([architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-036, R-HA-065);
  - `web` is `api` and `packages` in one process without the job loops, and `all` combines every role. Both exist only
    for a binary started outside the chart: `all` for the local profile and during development, `web` as the replica of
    the integration tests (Q-HA-315). The chart renders neither.

  The `backup` role is the `quader backup` subcommand. The backup CronJob and the restore Job run it
  (R-HA-060), and it serves no listener.
- A production deployment MUST run at least two replicas of each role, on different nodes (INV-12).
  The chart enforces this unless `highAvailability.enforce` is false (R-HA-029). One replica of a
  role is supported for development only. It runs the same code path against the same dependencies
  (external PostgreSQL, Valkey and S3), so scaling is a change of a replica count and nothing else.
  The catalog's "single node with embedded database and local file storage" topology does not exist
  in Quader.
- Load is shared by adding replicas of a role (INV-12). Capacity planning assumes that the peak load
  needs more than one `packages` replica; the UI and management load fits one `api` replica. R-HA-059 states how many
  replicas a node drain needs on top.
- Adding a replica needs no configuration besides the replica count. A new `worker` replica takes
  jobs as soon as it is ready. Removing a replica needs no handover: its leases end with its
  database sessions (R-HA-006), its job leases expire (R-HA-005), and its Valkey locks expire
  ([repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-026).

Acceptance criteria:

- With two `api` replicas behind the edge, `for i in $(seq 1 300); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://quader.example.com/api/v1/system/ping; done | sort | uniq -c`
  prints only `200`, and the `X-Quader-Replica` header of authenticated calls shows both `api` pod
  names and no other; the same loop over `GET /api/npm/web/npm-all/lodash` with a token shows the three `packages` pod names.
- `kubectl scale deploy/quader-packages --replicas=4` adds a replica that serves traffic and appears in
  `GET /api/v1/system/replicas` without any other change.
- `helm upgrade … --set api.replicaCount=1 --set packages.replicaCount=1 --set worker.replicaCount=1 --set highAvailability.enforce=false`
  yields a working installation with one replica per role against the same database, Valkey and
  bucket.
- A test proxy in front of the `api` and `packages` pod IPs, routing by the path prefixes of R-HA-037, sends every request
  to a different replica of its role in strict rotation. Through it, these flows complete (INV-18): an npm web login with its polling requests,
  `dotnet nuget push` followed by a restore of the pushed version, `npm publish` followed by
  `npm view`, and a paged API listing followed to its last page.

### R-HA-002 · Role split into api, packages and worker Deployments
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: HA-015

The split is no longer optional: it is an owner constraint since 2026-10-28, and the task areas `api`, `packages` and
`worker` are the owner's cut of 2026-11-04 (INV-2,
[ADR-153](../decisions.md#adr-153--quader-is-cut-into-task-areas-roles-of-one-binary-network-seams-only-at-trust-or-load-boundaries),
[ADR-155](../decisions.md#adr-155--three-roles-api-packages-and-worker-variants-are-pools)).

**Status.** Built (phase 6a, WP6a.3): the chart renders `<fullname>-api`, `<fullname>-packages` and `<fullname>-worker`
from the list of Deployments in [_units.tpl](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/_units.tpl).

- The chart MUST always render three Deployments: `<fullname>-api`, whose container runs `quader serve --role api`,
  `<fullname>-packages`, whose container runs `quader serve --role packages`, and `<fullname>-worker`, whose container runs
  `quader serve --role worker`. While the image scanning is switched on (`config.vulnerabilities.enabled` and
  `config.vulnerabilities.images.enabled`, both `true` by default) it renders a fourth, `<fullname>-vuln-scanner-trivy`, whose container
  runs `quader serve --role scanner` (R-HA-065), and while the malware scanning is on (`config.malware.enabled`, `true` by default) a
  fifth, `<fullname>-malware-scanner-clamav`, of the same role (R-HA-068), and, while its source is the updater (the default), a sixth,
  `<fullname>-malware-updater-freshclam`, of the same role with one replica (R-HA-069). A Deployment that exists to run one third-party tool is named
  `<purpose>-scanner-<tool>` (the owner's decision [Q-HA-372](#q-ha-372--a-unit-that-runs-a-tool-carries-the-tools-name)), and every name
  an operator or an auditor reads of it carries that name too: the label `listener` of its link and its listener, the log field
  `component` of its process, the system subject of its reads, and its readiness check in camel case, `vulnScannerTrivy` and
  `malwareScannerClamav` (the owner's decision [Q-HA-373](#q-ha-373--every-name-an-operator-or-an-auditor-reads-of-a-scanner-unit-carries-its-tool)). Each has
  its own replica count, resources, autoscaler, disruption budget, termination grace period, spool size, scheduling settings and ingress
  policy (R-HA-031, R-HA-032, R-HA-042). There is no single-Deployment
  mode, and no value renders `--role all` or `--role web`.
- **Services.** `<fullname>-api` (port `http` 8080) selects only the `api` pods of the main Deployment, and
  `<fullname>-packages` (port `http` 8080) only the `packages` pods of the main Deployment; the edge routes each host's paths
  to them by prefix (R-HA-037). `<fullname>-ops` selects every serving pod on 8081. `worker` pods are reached only on the
  operations port (probes and metrics). There is no Service `<fullname>` (Q-HA-74, Q-HA-315). The image scanning adds two Services
  that no client and no edge uses, `<fullname>-vuln-scanner-trivy` and `<fullname>-packages-scan` (R-HA-066), the malware scanning one,
  `<fullname>-malware-scanner-clamav` (R-HA-068), and the updater one, `<fullname>-malware-updater-freshclam` (R-HA-069).
- **In-cluster callers** that address Quader without the edge, such as a Bastion calling the main installation by its
  Service name ([bastion.md](bastion.md) R-BAS-008) or CI runners in the cluster, address the Service of the role whose
  families they call: `<fullname>-api` for the UI, the management API and the CI exchange, `<fullname>-packages` for the
  package protocols and raw files. A request that reaches the other role's Service answers the `404` of an unknown path
  ([architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-001). A caller that needs both families in one base URL goes through the edge.
- `worker.replicaCount` (or `worker.autoscaling.minReplicas`) MUST be at least 1, otherwise no
  scheduled work runs, and `api.replicaCount` and `packages.replicaCount` MUST be at least 1, otherwise the edge has no
  backend for their families. The chart refuses to render (R-HA-029). With `highAvailability.enforce` the minimum is 2 for
  every role and every pool, so that GC and other singleton work survive a worker pod loss without waiting for a reschedule
  and no family loses its last replica in a drain.
- The roles' pods run the same image and the same configuration file; only the `--role` argument, the per-Deployment
  environment of R-HA-062 (`QUADER_POOL_NAME`, `QUADER_JOBS_QUEUES`, `QUADER_JOBS_EXCLUDE_QUEUES`) and the scan listener of the main
  `packages` Deployment (`QUADER_SERVER_SCAN_LISTEN`, R-HA-066) differ, and the scanners mount less (R-HA-065, R-HA-068). No component of
  Quader runs in a separate image. A third-party tool runs from its own image beside the Quader container of its unit: `clamd` and
  `freshclam` (R-HA-068, R-HA-069), and the image scanning's analyser, which an init container copies from its own image into the scanner
  pod, with a second Quader container `database` beside the scanner that keeps the analyser's database (R-HA-070). The Quader image carries
  no third-party tool.
- Why: background work (GC, retention runs, reindexing, the mirror's passes, the advisory sync, webhook delivery) never
  competes with request latency for CPU and memory; a surge of package traffic cannot starve the UI and the management API;
  `packages` scales on package load, `api` on UI and API load and `worker` on job load; a drain or rollout of one role does
  not touch the others; the login secrets live only in `api` pods (R-HA-030); and a further split of a role (R-HA-062) is a
  change of values, not of code.

Acceptance criteria:

- With default values, `kubectl get deploy -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=quader` lists `quader-api`, `quader-packages`,
  `quader-worker`, `quader-vuln-scanner-trivy`, `quader-malware-scanner-clamav` and `quader-malware-updater-freshclam`, and `GET /api/v1/system/replicas` shows roles
  `["api"]`, `["packages"]` and `["worker"]`, while `GET /api/v1/system/scanners` lists every pod of `quader-vuln-scanner-trivy` under the
  kind `trivy` and every pod of `quader-malware-scanner-clamav` under the kind `clamav` (a scanner has no row of the registry but one of its
  own, [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-048, Q-OPS-223); with
  `config.vulnerabilities.images.enabled: false` no `quader-vuln-scanner-trivy` is rendered.
- A manual GC run (`POST /api/v1/system/tasks/gc/run`) sent to an `api` pod is executed on a
  `worker` pod (the worker's instance ID appears in `job.locked_by` of the gc job), and the
  instance ID of no `api` or `packages` pod ever appears in `job.locked_by`.
- `helm template … --set worker.replicaCount=0` fails and names `worker.replicaCount`; `--set packages.replicaCount=0`
  fails and names `packages.replicaCount`.
- For every value set in `ci/`, the rendered containers carry the argument `--role api`, `--role packages` or
  `--role worker`, and never `web` or `all`.
- The chart test of each role (`test/chart`): a Deployment, a Service where the role serves clients, a PodDisruptionBudget,
  a HorizontalPodAutoscaler with `autoscaling.enabled`, a NetworkPolicy with the ports of R-HA-042, and the edge rules of
  R-HA-037 that point at its Service.

### R-HA-062 · Further splits of a role into several Deployments
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: HA-015

**Status.** Built (phase 6a, WP6a.3): path pools, worker pools and the endpoint pools per role
([_units.tpl](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/_units.tpl)). The environment form of the queues is a JSON list (Q-HA-82), what a
pool inherits is Q-HA-84, and the ports a path pool opens for further endpoints are Q-HA-83.

The owner allows several worker types and a split service (INV-2); a variant of a role by path prefix or by queue is a
pool of that role, rendered from values without code (ADR-155). Because every replica of a role can serve everything its
role serves, a pool is routing and scheduling only.

- **Path pools of `api` and `packages`.** Each entry of `api.pools` or `packages.pools` renders a Deployment
  `<fullname>-<role>-<name>` with `--role <role>`, its own Service `<fullname>-<role>-<name>` (port 8080, no session
  affinity), disruption budget, autoscaler, ingress policy and the keys of its role as overrides. The Ingress and the
  HTTPRoute route the entry's `paths` (path prefixes inside the same host, for example `/api/npm` and `/api/nuget` in
  `packages.pools`) to that Service; every other path of the role stays on `<fullname>-<role>`. A pool's paths MUST lie
  inside the families of its role (R-HA-037's prefix table: below `/api` but not `/api/v1`, or `/files`, `/v2`,
  `/.well-known` for `packages`; `/ui`, `/auth` or below `/api/v1` for `api`), MUST NOT equal one of the role's own prefixes
  of R-HA-037, and two pools MUST NOT list the same prefix. Use: a surge of npm traffic cannot starve NuGet clients; a heavy
  part of the management API on pods of its own.
- **Worker pools.** Each entry of `worker.pools` renders a Deployment `<fullname>-worker-<name>` with `--role worker` and
  `QUADER_JOBS_QUEUES` set to the entry's `queues` as one JSON list (`["vuln"]`, the loader's form for a list-valued variable,
  [architecture.md](architecture.md) Q-ARCH-304), so it claims only those queues (the queue names and the setting:
  [architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-016, Q-ARCH-296). The main `worker` Deployment gets `QUADER_JOBS_EXCLUDE_QUEUES`
  set, in the same form, to the union of every pool's queues and claims every other queue, so a queue never stays unclaimed, a queue a later
  release adds is claimed by the main Deployment, and no queue is claimed by two pools. Use: the advisory sync (`vuln`),
  the mirror's passes (`mirror`), indexing (`index`) or garbage collection (`maintenance`) on pods of their own. A pool's
  `jobs.workers.<queue>` slots are those of the configuration unless its `extraEnv` sets them.
- **Endpoint pools.** The pool of a further endpoint (`endpoints.<name>.pool`, [endpoints.md](endpoints.md) R-EP-008,
  Q-EP-3) is named `ep-<name>` and is a pool of the role that serves the endpoint's surface (Q-EP-70): a pool of `packages`
  for a surface within `packages` and `files`, of `api` for one within `api` and `ci_exchange`, and one of each for a surface
  that holds families of both roles. It follows every rule below, but is routed by its own port, Services and edge route
  instead of by path prefix, and its pods open only the listeners of their endpoints (R-EP-002). Endpoint pools are built
  since the MVP as pools of `web`; the cut makes them pools of the role of their surface.
- Every pool follows the rules of its role: at least two replicas with `highAvailability.enforce`, spreading, disruption
  budget, the drain rule of R-HA-059, its own ingress policy (R-HA-042), and the connection budget of R-HA-016, which counts
  pools like any other Deployment. A pool's pods carry `quader/pool: <name>`, which keeps its selectors apart from the main
  Deployment's (R-HA-028) and becomes the target label `pool` of its series (R-HA-045). The names of path and worker pools
  match `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,19}$` and may not start with `ep-`.
- **Adding a pool without a gap (Q-HA-90).** A path pool's route is rendered in the same apply that creates its Deployment, so
  the prefix would answer `503` until the pods are ready. A path pool therefore takes the key `routed` (default `true`): with
  `routed: false` the pool's Deployment, Service, budget and policy render and its prefix stays on `<fullname>-<role>`. The
  addition takes two applies: the pool with `routed: false`, then, once its pods are ready, without the key. The same
  holds for a pool whose `paths` change. An endpoint pool has no such key: enabling `endpoints.<name>.pool` on a running
  endpoint repoints that endpoint's Service in the apply that creates the pods, so the endpoint answers `503` for the start
  time of the pool's pods; a new endpoint has no earlier traffic and is not affected.
- **Refused combinations.** The chart refuses to render: worker pools that together claim every queue (the main worker's
  exclude list would leave it none, and the binary refuses to start, [architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-016); a worker
  pool with no replica (`replicaCount: 0`, or an autoscaler whose `minReplicas` is below 1), whose queues nobody would claim
  because the main worker excludes them; and an `endpoints.default.surface` that holds no family of a role (`api`, `ci_exchange`,
  `ui` for `api`; `packages`, `files` for `packages`) while no further endpoint is served by that role, so that the role's
  Deployments would serve nothing.

```yaml
api:
  pools: []                    # default (proposed); example:
  # - name: admin              # example
  #   paths: [/api/v1/projects]   # example; prefixes inside the families of api
  #   replicaCount: 2          # example; every key of api may be overridden here
packages:
  pools: []                    # default (proposed); example:
  # - name: npm                # example
  #   paths: [/api/npm]        # example; prefixes inside the families of packages
  #   replicaCount: 4          # example; every key of packages may be overridden here
worker:
  pools: []                    # default (proposed); example:
  # - name: vuln               # example
  #   queues: [vuln]           # example; queue names from architecture.md R-ARCH-016
  #   replicaCount: 2          # example; every key of worker may be overridden here
```

Acceptance criteria: with one `packages` pool for `/api/npm` and one worker pool for the queue `vuln`, R-HA-059's drain test
passes; npm requests appear only in the pool's access logs and NuGet requests only in those of `<fullname>-packages`; jobs of
the queue `vuln` run only on the pool's pods and every other kind only on `<fullname>-worker`; `helm template` fails when two
pools list the same path prefix or the same queue, when a `packages` pool lists `/api/v1/system` or an `api` pool lists
`/files`, when a worker pool lists a queue that does not exist, and when a pool's name starts with `ep-`.

### R-HA-063 · Chart TLS wiring
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: HA-018

The chart wires TLS through Quader's listeners and the platform's connections. `tls.enabled` defaults to `true`
(Q-HA-32). Every kind of pod has a TLS pair and a name of its own, and the chart issues the pairs (the owner's decision
[Q-HA-345](#q-ha-345--every-kind-of-pod-has-a-tls-pair-and-a-name-of-its-own-and-the-chart-issues-the-pairs),
[ADR-215](../decisions.md#adr-215--every-kind-of-pod-has-a-tls-pair-and-a-name-of-its-own-which-the-chart-issues)).
- **Kinds and names** ([Q-HA-346](#q-ha-346--four-kinds-hold-a-pair-each-names-its-kind-and-the-operations-service)). Six kinds
  hold a pair: `api` (the main Deployment, its path pools and its endpoint pools), `packages` (the same), `worker` (the main
  Deployment and its pools), `vuln-scanner-trivy` while the image scanning is on, `malware-scanner-clamav` while the malware scanning
  is on, and `malware-updater-freshclam` while the malware scanning takes its signatures from the updater (R-HA-065, R-HA-068, R-HA-069,
  named after their tool by [Q-HA-372](#q-ha-372--a-unit-that-runs-a-tool-carries-the-tools-name)). Each pair
  carries the DNS names `<fullname>-<kind>.<namespace>.svc` and `<fullname>-ops.<namespace>.svc`, and the usage `server auth`; the pairs of
  `worker`, `vuln-scanner-trivy`, `malware-scanner-clamav` and `malware-updater-freshclam` carry `client auth` too, because they present themselves on a link
  (R-HA-066, R-HA-068). The migration Job, the backup and restore pods and the post-restore Job hold none: they open no TLS listener and
  call no pod of Quader.
- **Issued by the chart** ([Q-HA-347](#q-ha-347--tlscertmanager-issues-a-certificate-per-kind-tlsexistingsecrets-names-a-secret-per-kind-instead)).
  With `tls.certManager.issuerRef.name` the chart renders a cert-manager `Certificate` per kind, `<fullname>-tls-<kind>`, into the Secret of the
  same name: the two names and the names of `tls.certManager.extraDnsNames` and `extraIpAddresses`, the usages above (and `key
  encipherment` for an RSA key), `duration`, `renewBefore` and the private key of `tls.certManager`, with `rotationPolicy: Always`,
  issued by `tls.certManager.issuerRef` (`kind` `ClusterIssuer` or `Issuer`, `group` `cert-manager.io`). Without an issuer, `tls.existingSecrets.<kind>`
  names an existing Secret per kind, which the chart never creates. The render fails while `tls.enabled` with neither
  `tls.certManager.issuerRef.name` nor a Secret for every kind the chart renders, with both, or with one Secret named for two kinds, and names
  the keys. Every Secret holds `tls.crt`, `tls.key` and `ca.crt` (the keys of a cert-manager TLS Secret), and all of them chain
  to one CA, the one in their `ca.crt`.
- **Mounts.** A pod mounts its kind's Secret read-only at `/var/run/secrets/quader/tls/`, as a directory volume with items and
  without `subPath`, mode `0440`: `tls.crt` and `tls.key`, and `ca.crt` only where a link verifies with it, which is while either
  scanning is on in the `worker` pods, the main `packages` pods and the scanners (R-HA-066, R-HA-068); the chart sets that file as
  `server.internal_tls.ca_file`. No pod mounts the Secret of another kind. The chart sets `server.tls.certificates` to the pod's
  pair and, when mutual TLS is configured, `server.tls.client_ca_file` with `client_auth` from `tls.clientCA.auth` (R-ARCH-035). A
  rotated Secret reaches the pods of its kind through the kubelet's swap of the whole volume, pair and CA together, and the reloader
  of R-ARCH-035 serves and presents it from the next handshake; each kind's Secret rotates on its own, and no pod restarts. The
  checksum annotation follows the settings and the paths, not the Secret's content, so a rotation does not roll the pods.
- `server.ops_tls` is explicit when `tls.clientCA` is set: `inherit: false`, the pod's pair and no client CA. Probes and scrapers
  present no client certificate, so mutual TLS on `:8080` never extends to `:8081`. Otherwise the operations listener inherits the
  pod's pair; the pair is per kind already, so the operations listener has no pair of its own.
- A further endpoint serves the pair of the kind of the pods that serve it unless its `tls.existingSecret` or `tls.extraSecrets`
  name pairs of its own, wildcard certificates included; each is mounted under `/var/run/secrets/quader/endpoints/<name>/<n>/`,
  rendered as that endpoint's `tls.certificates`, chosen by SNI and reloaded the same way ([endpoints.md](endpoints.md) R-EP-004,
  R-EP-008). Its Service port declares `appProtocol: https`, and its Ingress or HTTPRoute connects to it over TLS as below.
- Probes use `scheme: HTTPS` on the ops port (R-HA-034). The kubelet does not verify the served certificate for
  probes, so they need no CA.
- The client and ops Service ports declare `appProtocol: https`.
- With `metrics.serviceMonitor.enabled` the ServiceMonitor carries a `tlsConfig`: `ca` from `ca.crt` of the `api` kind's Secret,
  read from the ServiceMonitor's namespace, which is therefore the release namespace while `tls.enabled`, and `serverName`
  `<fullname>-ops.<namespace>.svc`, which every pair carries
  ([Q-HA-349](#q-ha-349--every-pair-also-carries-the-operations-name-and-the-scrape-verifies-that-name)).
- **The edge verifies each backend under the name of the kind that serves it**
  ([Q-HA-348](#q-ha-348--the-edge-verifies-each-backend-under-its-kinds-name-the-setting-goes-where-each-controller-reads-it)), against
  `ca.crt` of `ingress.backendTLS.caSecret`, which defaults to the Secret of the pair the backend serves (its kind's, or a further
  endpoint's own pair). A backend that serves a further endpoint's own pair is verified under its Service's name,
  `<Service>.<namespace>.svc`. `ingress.backendTLS.controller` selects where the settings go:
  - `haproxy` (the default, the primary target): `haproxy-ingress.github.io/secure-backends` and, for `clientCertSecret`,
    `secure-crt-secret` on the Ingress; `secure-sni` with the backend's name and `secure-verify-ca-secret` on each Service the
    Ingress routes to, where HAProxy Ingress reads backend keys per Service.
  - `traefik`: the Service's `serversscheme` and the `serverstransport` of its kind, `ingress.backendTLS.serversTransports.api` or
    `.packages`, a ServersTransport the operator creates for that kind's name and CA.
  - `ingress-nginx`, which reads its proxy settings per Ingress only: the rules of each kind go into an Ingress of their own, with
    `backend-protocol`, `proxy-ssl-verify`, `proxy-ssl-secret`, `proxy-ssl-name` with that kind's name and
    `proxy-ssl-server-name`. The Ingress `<fullname>` holds the rules of `api` and the `spec.tls`; `<fullname>-packages` holds those
    of `packages` with the same hosts and annotations and without `spec.tls`; a further endpoint's Ingress splits the same way into
    `<fullname>-ep-<name>` and `<fullname>-api-ep-<name>`, after its Services.
  - `manual`: the settings are the operator's, in `ingress.annotations` and `service.annotations`, with the names above.

  `ingress.backendTLS.verify` defaults to `true`, and the render fails when `serversTransports` lacks `api` or `packages` for
  `traefik`. `verify: false` encrypts the connection without verifying it, and the choice is explicit.
- A Gateway route uses a `BackendTLSPolicy` per Service, rendered only with `tls.backendTLSPolicy.enabled`, which verifies the name of
  the Service's kind and takes its CA from a ConfigMap (`caConfigMapName`) because the Gateway API takes no Secret there.
  `tls.clientCA` and `tls.backendTLSPolicy` need `tls.enabled: true`; with `tls.enabled: false` the pair values may stay and render nothing.
- The chart test renders `tls.enabled: true` and checks the Certificates, each Deployment's mount of its kind's Secret and of no
  other, the HTTPS probes, the `appProtocol` and the backend settings per kind, and that rendering without an issuer and without
  the Secrets fails.

Acceptance criteria:
- `helm template` with `tls.enabled: true` and neither `tls.certManager.issuerRef.name` nor `tls.existingSecrets` fails and names both; with one Secret
  named for two kinds it fails and names them; with `tls.enabled: false` no probe uses `scheme: HTTPS`.
- With `tls.certManager.issuerRef.name` the release renders one Certificate per kind, with the names and usages above, and the pods of each kind
  mount their kind's Secret and no other (chart test).
- Every request through the dev profile's edge is served over TLS and verified against the dev CA under its kind's name
  (R-HA-051), and a backend that serves another kind's pair is refused by the edge (a look on the kind cluster, recorded in
  Q-HA-348).
- Prometheus scrapes the ops port over TLS with the chart's ServiceMonitor, and the target is up.

### R-HA-065 · The scanner Deployment
Priority: **P1** · Covers: HA-015

The owner's decision of 2026-11-20 ([ADR-212](../decisions.md#adr-212--the-image-analysis-runs-in-a-role-scanner-that-holds-no-secret)):
the analysis of container images runs in a role `scanner` of the same binary and image, as a Deployment of its own, with no secret of the
database, the object store or Valkey. What it serves and holds is [architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-036; what it does is
[vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-041 and R-VULN-042.

- **When.** The chart renders `<fullname>-vuln-scanner-trivy` (the kind `vuln-scanner-trivy`, the image scanning's tool Trivy,
  [Q-HA-372](#q-ha-372--a-unit-that-runs-a-tool-carries-the-tools-name)) while `config.vulnerabilities.enabled` and
  `config.vulnerabilities.images.enabled` are `true` (the defaults), and nothing of it otherwise. Its container runs `quader serve --role scanner` and opens `:8080` (the scanner's
  listener) and `:8081` (the operations listener).
- **Pod.** The security context of R-HA-033: user and group 65532, `readOnlyRootFilesystem`, no privilege escalation, every capability
  dropped, seccomp `RuntimeDefault`; `automountServiceAccountToken: false`; no RBAC; and not the chart's service account, which may carry
  a cloud identity of the object store ([Q-HA-343](#q-ha-343--the-scanner-pod-names-no-service-account-of-the-chart)). The scanner's process is the first process of its
  container (no shell, no init), which Q-ARCH-530 relies on. `shareProcessNamespace` is never set.
- **Volumes, and nothing else** (R-HA-061): the spool `emptyDir` at `/var/lib/quader/spool` with `vulnScannerTrivy.spool.sizeLimit` (the
  one writable volume besides `/tmp`; the analyses work below `scan_dir` in it), `/tmp`, the configuration file, and the scanner's own
  Secret (`<fullname>-tls-vuln-scanner-trivy`, or `tls.existingSecrets.vuln-scanner-trivy`) at `/var/run/secrets/quader/tls/` with `tls.crt`, `tls.key` and `ca.crt`
  (R-HA-063): the pair its listener, its operations listener and its pull present, and the CA it verifies `packages` against. It
  holds no pair of another kind. The chart mounts no key of the key ring, no database, Valkey or object-store credential
  or CA, no login secret, no trusted CA bundle of R-HA-043 (the scanner opens no connection that it would verify), and none of the shared
  `extraVolumes`, `extraVolumeMounts`, `extraEnv`, `extraEnvFrom`, `initContainers` and `sidecars` (Q-HA-321); `vulnScannerTrivy.extraEnv` is its own.
  A chart test lists the pod's volumes and environment and fails for any other.
- **Resources** (Q-HA-316): requests 500m CPU, 1 GiB memory and 1 GiB ephemeral storage; memory limit 2 GiB; no CPU limit, `GOMAXPROCS`
  from the request (R-HA-036). The analyser's `GOMEMLIMIT` (`config.vulnerabilities.images.memory_limit`) is its soft limit; the pod's limit
  is the hard one, and an image that passes it ends that pod's analysis, which the worker records as `scanner_lost`.
- **Replicas and placement**: 2 replicas (at least 2 with `highAvailability.enforce`), a PodDisruptionBudget with `maxUnavailable: 1`, the
  two spread constraints and the tolerations of R-HA-032, an optional autoscaler on CPU (80 %). The capacity is replicas ×
  `config.vulnerabilities.images.scanner.slots`; `config.vulnerabilities.images.concurrency` should not exceed it (R-VULN-041, Q-VULN-170).
- **Probes** (R-HA-034): `/healthz` and `/readyz` on `:8081`. Readiness, the check `vulnScannerTrivy` ([operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md#q-ops-221--a-scanner-units-readiness-check-is-its-name-in-camel-case-the-same-in-the-process-that-calls-it) Q-OPS-221), holds while the listener's pair
  and the internal CA have loaded, the pair allows client authentication (the chart issues it so, R-HA-063), the analyser answers its version, the spool directory is writable, and the process is not
  draining. It does not depend on `packages`: a scan listener that cannot be reached is the call's answer (`registry_unavailable`), not the
  pod's state. Nor on Valkey: the scanner has no Valkey client and no wait for its first answer (Q-HA-330 does not apply,
  [architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-036).
- **Drain** (R-HA-011): `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 60` and the shutdown timeout derived from it. At `SIGTERM` the readiness fails at
  once and a new call is answered `503` `scanner_draining`; an analysis still running at the shutdown timeout is killed with its process
  group and answered `503` `scanner_draining`; the worker puts either off without an attempt.
- **A row of its own, not of the registry** ([operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-003, R-OPS-048,
  Q-OPS-223): the scanner has no database connection. Each replica reports itself every `system.heartbeat_interval` to the scan listener
  with its kind's certificate, and the System page and **Advisory sources** list it with its state, its reason and Trivy's version. Its
  replicas show besides as the Deployment's, as the series of the ServiceMonitor (the Service `<fullname>-ops` selects its pods on `8081` by
  their label `quader/serve`, which no Valkey policy admits by itself, Q-HA-344) and through the worker's codes and
  `QuaderVulnerabilityImageScannerUnavailable` (R-VULN-024).
- **Chart checks** (R-HA-029): the scanner's spool budget (`vulnScannerTrivy.spool.sizeLimit` minus `spool.headroom`) at least
  `slots × (max_image_size + 64 MiB)`, the failure naming the three values (Q-HA-318); `vulnScannerTrivy.replicaCount` at least 1, and at least 2 with
  `highAvailability.enforce`; with `tls.existingSecrets`, a Secret for the scanner that no other kind names (R-HA-063).
- **With the detection in the scanner and the analyser from its own image** (owner, 2026-11-21): the pod gains an init container `trivy`,
  a container `database`, and two volumes, `trivy-bin` and `trivy-db`, both read-only in the container `quader`; its analyser is
  `/opt/trivy/trivy` instead of the release image's `/usr/local/bin/trivy`. Everything else of this requirement stands; what changes is
  [R-HA-070](#r-ha-070--the-analyser-from-its-own-image-and-the-database-in-the-scanner-pod). Built on 2026-11-21: the container
  `database`, the volume `trivy-db` (and `database-tmp`, the loader's `/tmp`), then the init container `trivy`, the volume `trivy-bin` and the
  analyser's path, so the pod's volumes are the four above and those three.

Acceptance criteria:

- Chart test (`test/chart`, about 1 s): with default values the Deployment `quader-vuln-scanner-trivy` runs `--role scanner`, mounts exactly the four
  volumes above, carries no environment variable or volume that names a Secret other than its own TLS Secret, and has
  `automountServiceAccountToken: false`; `--set config.vulnerabilities.images.enabled=false` renders no scanner object; `--set
  vulnScannerTrivy.spool.sizeLimit=4Gi` fails and names `vulnScannerTrivy.spool.sizeLimit`, `spool.headroom` and `max_image_size`; a shared `extraEnvFrom`
  does not reach the scanner's container.
- End to end (set `vuln`, R-VULN-046): the running scanner pod holds no file below `/var/run/secrets/quader/` but `tls/ca.crt`,
  `tls/tls.crt` and `tls/tls.key` of the Secret `<fullname>-tls-vuln-scanner-trivy`, and nothing at `/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/`; the image has no
  shell and no `ls`, so the test reads the live pod's volumes and mounts ([Q-HA-342](#q-ha-342--the-end-to-end-case-reads-the-scanner-pods-files-from-its-live-spec)).

### R-HA-066 · The links of the image scanning inside the chart
Priority: **P1** · Covers: HA-018

- **Services.** `<fullname>-vuln-scanner-trivy`: `ClusterIP`, port `https` 8080 (`appProtocol: https`), selecting the scanner pods, `sessionAffinity:
  None`. `<fullname>-packages-scan`: `ClusterIP`, port `scan` 8082 (`appProtocol: https`), selecting the pods of the main `packages`
  Deployment (not its path pools or endpoint pools), `sessionAffinity: None`. Neither takes `service.type` or its annotations, and no Ingress
  or HTTPRoute names either, so neither port is reachable from outside the cluster whatever the client Services are (Q-HA-319).
- **The scan listener.** The main `packages` Deployment gets `QUADER_SERVER_SCAN_LISTEN=:8082` while the image scanning is on and opens the
  listener of [architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-037; its path pools and endpoint pools do not.
- **Chart-managed configuration** (R-HA-029: refused when set by hand), with the names of R-HA-063:

  | Key | Value | Read by |
  |---|---|---|
  | `vulnerabilities.images.scanner.url` | `https://<fullname>-vuln-scanner-trivy.<namespace>.svc:8080` | the worker |
  | `vulnerabilities.images.scanner.server_name` | `<fullname>-vuln-scanner-trivy.<namespace>.svc` | the worker, in the scanner's certificate |
  | `vulnerabilities.images.scanner.client_name` | `<fullname>-worker.<namespace>.svc` | the scanner's listener, in the client's certificate |
  | `vulnerabilities.images.registry.url` | `https://<fullname>-packages-scan.<namespace>.svc:8082` | the scanner |
  | `vulnerabilities.images.registry.server_name` | `<fullname>-packages.<namespace>.svc` | the scanner, in the scan listener's certificate |
  | `vulnerabilities.images.registry.client_name` | `<fullname>-vuln-scanner-trivy.<namespace>.svc` | the scan listener: the name by which it records a report of itself as one of the kind `trivy` ([operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-048) |
  | `server.scan_clients` | `[<fullname>-vuln-scanner-trivy.<namespace>.svc, <fullname>-malware-scanner-clamav.<namespace>.svc, <fullname>-malware-updater-freshclam.<namespace>.svc]`: one entry per kind of the role `scanner` the release renders (`quader.tlsKindTable`) | the scan listener, in the client's certificate |
  | `server.internal_tls.ca_file` | `/var/run/secrets/quader/tls/ca.crt` | all three, the `ca.crt` of the pod's own Secret |
- **TLS** (R-HA-063, R-ARCH-038). Each end of a link presents its own kind's pair and checks the other's name
  ([Q-VULN-185](vulnerability-scanning.md#q-vuln-185--each-end-of-a-link-proves-its-kind-the-worker-to-the-scanner-the-scanner-to-the-scan-listener)):
  the scanner's listener admits a client certificate of the CA that lists the worker's name, and nothing else; the scan listener admits one
  that lists the scanner's name; the worker verifies the scanner's name and the scanner verifies the name of `packages`. A certificate of the
  same CA with the name of another kind, or with a wildcard, is refused in the handshake on each side. Each kind's Secret rotates on its own
  and reaches its pods through the kubelet and the reloader, without a restart, for the next handshake; the worker opens a connection per
  call (R-VULN-041), so no call outlives two rotations on one connection. The TLS series of a link carry the label `listener` of the unit
  or listener it reaches, at both ends: `vuln-scanner-trivy` on the worker's call and the scanner's listener, `scan` on the scanner's pull
  and the scan listener ([Q-HA-373](#q-ha-373--every-name-an-operator-or-an-auditor-reads-of-a-scanner-unit-carries-its-tool)).
- **With `tls.enabled: false`** the chart renders both links in plain HTTP, like every other link of such an installation (H-38): no client
  certificate is asked, and the scan token and the NetworkPolicy are what remain (Q-HA-322,
  [H-1043](../security/image-scanning.md#h-1043--with-tlsenabled-false-the-scanners-links-are-not-authenticated)).
- **Ingress rules** (R-HA-042, ADR-154): the scanner's `8080` from the pods of the worker Deployment that claims `vuln`; the scan
  listener's `8082` from the scanner's pods. No egress rule.
- **The database routes** (specified, [vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-049): the scan listener admits the
  image scanner's name, `vulnerabilities.images.registry.client_name`, on `GET /scan/v1/trivy-database[/<digest>]` too, without a token. The
  loader that reads them is the container `database` of the same pod, so the rule of `8082` admits it already, and its pair is the
  scanner's: no key, rule or name more.

Acceptance criteria:

- Chart test (`test/chart`, about 1 s): the two Services with their ports, selectors and `ClusterIP` also with `service.type: LoadBalancer`;
  `QUADER_SERVER_SCAN_LISTEN` on the main `packages` Deployment only; the chart-managed keys of the table in the rendered configuration; the
  item `ca.crt` of the pod's own Secret on the `worker`, main `packages`, `vuln-scanner-trivy` and `malware-scanner-clamav` pods and on no
  `api` pod; with a worker pool `vuln`,
  the pool's pods in the scanner's ingress rule.
- Unit (`internal/httpserver`, under a second): on each link, a client certificate of the CA with another kind's name or a wildcard is
  refused by the listener, and a server certificate of the CA with another kind's name is refused by the client (R-ARCH-038).
- End to end (set `vuln`, R-VULN-046): an image of a few kilobytes pushed to a local repository is analysed: a row of `vuln_image_sbom` holds
  its digest within a minute of `POST /api/v1/system/tasks/vuln-image-scan/run`, which shows both links with the pairs the chart issued.
  A call to the scanner's listener that presents the pair of `packages` is refused in the handshake (a look on the kind cluster, recorded
  in Q-VULN-185).

### R-HA-067 · Where the scanner runs outside the chart
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

- **The local profile on kind** (R-HA-051) runs the chart, so it runs `<fullname>-vuln-scanner-trivy` with two replicas next to the pool
  `vuln`, and the chart issues the profile's four pairs (five in the profile `vuln`, which runs `<fullname>-malware-scanner-clamav` too) from the dev CA's Issuer of `deploy/dev/pki.yaml` (`tls.certManager.issuerRef` in `values-dev.yaml`), with
  `localhost` and `127.0.0.1` as extra names for the tests that reach a pod through a port-forward. Its database is `upstream/scanner-trivy` through the profile's
  network, or a local repository of the profile for a run without the internet.
- **The UI development profile** (`make ui-dev-backend`, the role `all`): one process holds the worker and `packages` and builds no
  scanner of any kind ([architecture.md](architecture.md#q-arch-563--the-role-all-builds-no-image-scanner) Q-ARCH-563, which replaced
  the in-process scanner of Q-ARCH-531 and the reported check of Q-ARCH-551). Its configuration names no `scanner.url` and opens no scan
  listener, so no link of the scanning runs there and the image scanning's job ends at once; the unset `client_name` and `scan_clients`
  would let the CA alone admit a link started beside it
  ([architecture.md](architecture.md#q-arch-553--the-role-all-keeps-one-pair-the-integration-harness-issues-one-per-role) Q-ARCH-553).
- **The integration stack** (`test/integration/testenv`): the stack starts a replica of the role `scanner` in process beside `web` and
  `worker`, each with a pair of its role (the scanner's of its kind, `vuln-scanner-trivy` or `malware-scanner-clamav`) that the harness issues from the stack's CA and the names of the links set as in the chart
  (Q-ARCH-553), and the `web` replica opens the scan listener; the scanning's tests replace the analyser at the
  seam in the scanner replica and the worker replica, as they do today, so the stack needs no analyser binary and no database download
  (R-VULN-046).
- **CI**: no new leg. The unit, chart and integration legs run what R-VULN-046 lists; the leg `e2e (vuln)` adds one case.
- **With the detection in the scanner and the analyser from its own image** (owner, 2026-11-21): the role `all` builds no image scanner,
  and its worker part calls `vulnerabilities.images.scanner.url` when one is set; without one the image scanning's job ends at once and
  touches no row ([architecture.md](architecture.md) Q-ARCH-563), so the UI development profile shows images `pending_scan` and the API
  `replicas: "none"`; the renders keep seeding the scanners' rows by SQL. Built on 2026-11-21 (`TestR_ARCH_036_TheRoleAllBuildsNoImageScanner`
  in `vulnimage`); the integration stack's loader replica too (`flow.startLoader`). The profiles' part below (the image scanning off in
  `values-dev.yaml` and `values-restore.yaml`, the analyser's image loaded in `vuln`) is built with R-HA-070 (Q-HA-386, Q-HA-387). The local profile on kind runs the
  image scanning only in the profile `vuln` (and the profiles layered on it) and in the platform matrix, and loads the analyser's image into
  the kind cluster in `vuln` as it loads ClamAV's; the matrix starts no pod and loads none (Q-HA-386) ([Q-HA-382](#q-ha-382--the-image-scanning-is-on-in-the-charts-defaults-and-off-in-every-test-profile-but-vuln-and-the-platform-matrix)).
  The integration stack starts the loader of the kind `trivy-db` in process beside the scanner replica, with a directory of the test as its
  volume, and the fake analyser runs both steps in the scanner replica.

Acceptance criteria:

- `make ui-dev-backend` with a pushed image of kilobytes shows the image's analysis stored without a scanner Deployment (a manual check of
  the profile, recorded once). This criterion goes with Q-ARCH-563.
- The integration set `vulnimage` passes with the scanner replica in process (R-VULN-041).

### R-HA-068 · The malware scanner Deployment
Priority: **P1** · Covers: HA-015

The owner's decision of 2026-11-20 ([malware-scanning.md](malware-scanning.md) Q-MAL-6): the malware scanning's scanner is a Deployment of
its own of the role `scanner`, with a container `clamd` beside it. Built: the chart's objects ([malware-scanner-clamav.yaml](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/malware-scanner-clamav.yaml),
[_malware.tpl](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/_malware.tpl)); the scanner's process and its loader of the database are built with the
malware scanning's packages 2 and 3 ([internal/malware/scanner](../../internal/malware/scanner/service.go),
[loader.go](../../internal/malware/database/loader.go)). What it does is
[malware-scanning.md](malware-scanning.md) R-MAL-005 to R-MAL-008; what it builds and holds is [architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-036
for the kind `clamav`. Its TLS pair, its name as a kind of pod and the checks of its links are R-HA-063 to R-HA-066's; this requirement
names it the kind `malware-scanner-clamav`, after its tool ([Q-HA-372](#q-ha-372--a-unit-that-runs-a-tool-carries-the-tools-name)), and
leaves their text to them.

- **When.** The chart renders `<fullname>-malware-scanner-clamav` while `config.malware.enabled` is `true` (the default), and nothing of
  it otherwise. Its container `quader` runs `quader serve --role scanner` with `QUADER_PROCESS_SCANNER_KIND=clamav` and opens `:8080` and
  `:8081`.
- **The container `clamd`** ([Q-HA-360](#q-ha-360--clamd-runs-in-a-container-of-the-official-image-beside-the-scanner)): the image
  `clamav.image`, held to `tools/versions.env`'s `CLAMAV_IMAGE` by a chart test (the project's `_base` image, without a database, by its
  digest, [malware-scanning.md](malware-scanning.md) Q-MAL-80; one value for `clamd` and `freshclam`,
  [Q-HA-363](#q-ha-363--one-image-value-for-clamd-and-freshclam-and-fixed-paths-the-containers-share)), started with a command that waits
  for the marker `/var/lib/clamav/.quader-loaded` the scanner writes after its first database load and then runs
  `clamd --foreground --config-file=/etc/clamd/clamd.conf`. The chart renders `clamd.conf` in a ConfigMap from `config.malware.scanner`:
  `LocalSocket /run/clamd/clamd.sock`, no `TCPSocket`, `DatabaseDirectory /var/lib/clamav`, `TemporaryDirectory /var/tmp/clamd`,
  `MaxThreads` = `slots`, `MaxFileSize` and `StreamMaxLength` = `max_file_size`, `MaxScanSize` = `max_scan_size`, `MaxScanTime` =
  `scan_timeout`, `AlertExceedsMax`, `AlertEncrypted`, `AlertEncryptedArchive` and `AlertEncryptedDoc` `yes`, `DetectPUA no`,
  `ConcurrentDatabaseReload no`, `SelfCheck 0`, logging to standard error (every option checked with `clamconf` of 1.5.5). Its probes:
  liveness and readiness by `clamdscan --ping` over the socket once the marker exists; before it they pass, the container waiting.
- **Pod.** The security context of R-HA-033 for both containers (user and group 65532, `readOnlyRootFilesystem`, no privilege escalation,
  every capability dropped, seccomp `RuntimeDefault`); `automountServiceAccountToken: false`; no RBAC; `shareProcessNamespace` never set.
- **Volumes, and nothing else** (R-HA-061): the quader container's spool `emptyDir` and `/tmp`, its configuration file, its TLS pair and
  the internal CA (R-HA-063 to R-HA-066); shared by both containers: `clamd-run` (`emptyDir`, `medium: Memory`, 1 MiB, the socket, at
  `/run/clamd` in both), `clamd-db` (`emptyDir`, `malwareScannerClamav.database.sizeLimit`, default 1 GiB, written by the scanner, read by
  `clamd`, at `/var/lib/clamav` in both, read-only in `clamd`); `clamd-tmp` (`emptyDir`, `malwareScannerClamav.clamdTmp.sizeLimit`, default 8 GiB,
  `clamd`'s temporary files, in `clamd` only); and `clamd.conf` (the ConfigMap `<fullname>-clamd`) for `clamd`. `clamd` mounts
  no TLS pair, no CA and no configuration file of Quader. None of the shared `extraVolumes`, `extraEnv`, `sidecars` and the like reach the
  pod; `malwareScannerClamav.extraEnv` is its own.
- **Resources** ([Q-HA-361](#q-ha-361--the-malware-scanners-default-size)): the quader container requests 250m CPU and 256 MiB with a memory
  limit of 512 MiB; `clamd` requests 500m CPU and 1280 MiB with a memory limit of 2 GiB (measured: 1.0 GiB resident with ClamAV's whole
  database, no second copy during a reload, since `ConcurrentDatabaseReload` is off). No CPU limit. The sizing profiles of R-HA-050 size
  the pods and their count.
- **Replicas and placement**: 2 replicas (at least 2 with `highAvailability.enforce`), a PodDisruptionBudget with `maxUnavailable: 1`, the
  spread constraints and tolerations of R-HA-032, an optional autoscaler on CPU. The capacity is replicas × `config.malware.scanner.slots`
  (2); `config.malware.concurrency` (4) should not exceed it.
- **Probes and drain.** Readiness, the check `malwareScannerClamav` ([operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md#q-ops-221--a-scanner-units-readiness-check-is-its-name-in-camel-case-the-same-in-the-process-that-calls-it) Q-OPS-221), holds while the TLS material is loaded, the first database is
  loaded and `clamd` answers `PING`, and the process is not draining; the label `listener` of its listener and of the worker's link to it is
  `malware-scanner-clamav` ([Q-HA-373](#q-ha-373--every-name-an-operator-or-an-auditor-reads-of-a-scanner-unit-carries-its-tool)); liveness is the scanner's `/healthz`. `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 60`; at `SIGTERM` new calls are answered
  `503 scanner_draining`.
- **Service and policies.** `<fullname>-malware-scanner-clamav`: `ClusterIP`, port `https` 8080, no `service.type`, no Ingress. NetworkPolicy
  (R-HA-042): `:8080` from the pods of the worker Deployments that claim the queue `malware`; `:8081` from the ops sources; the scan listener
  `:8082` of `packages` also from the malware scanner pods. The chart sets `config.malware.scanner.url` and `config.malware.scan_listener.url`
  as R-HA-066 sets the image scanning's, refused when set by hand (R-HA-029), and renders `QUADER_SERVER_SCAN_LISTEN=:8082` on the main
  `packages` Deployment while either scanning is on. The names of the two links, chart-managed as well: `malware.scanner.server_name`
  `<fullname>-malware-scanner-clamav.<namespace>.svc` and `malware.scanner.client_name` `<fullname>-worker.<namespace>.svc` (the call),
  `malware.scan_listener.server_name` `<fullname>-packages.<namespace>.svc` and `malware.scan_listener.client_name`
  `<fullname>-malware-scanner-clamav.<namespace>.svc` (the read, [malware-scanning.md](malware-scanning.md) Q-MAL-61, and the name by which
  the scan listener records the malware scanner's report of itself as one of the kind `clamav`,
  [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-048), and the malware scanner's
  name as one more entry of `server.scan_clients` (the configuration refuses a `scan_listener.client_name` outside that list). The pool
  list of the worker accepts the queue `malware` (R-HA-062).
- **Alerts.** The chart's rules carry the four alerts of [malware-scanning.md](malware-scanning.md) R-MAL-026 while the malware scanning
  is on: `QuaderMalwareFound`, `QuaderMalwareDatabaseStale` (its threshold `config.malware.database.stale_after`, default 48 h),
  `QuaderMalwareScannerUnavailable` and `QuaderMalwareBacklog`, with their `promtool` tests in
  [rules_test.yaml](../../deploy/helm/quader/tests/rules_test.yaml).
- **The signatures' alerts and anchors.** The rules carry the three alerts of [signatures.md](signatures.md) R-SIG-039 and the one of its
  gate per repository (R-SIG-075) while `config.signatures.enabled` (the default): `QuaderSignatureInvalid`, `QuaderSignatureBacklog`,
  `QuaderSignatureTrustRootStale`, `QuaderSignatureGatePending`. The values'
  `signatures.anchors` (R-SIG-018) render into `config.signatures.anchors`; material from a `<member>From.configMapKeyRef` is mounted
  read-only into the migration Job alone ([Q-SIG-122](signatures.md#q-sig-122--anchors-of-the-configuration-are-a-map-and-their-material-a-mounted-file)).
- **Chart checks** (R-HA-029): `clamd-tmp`'s size at least `slots × (max_file_size + max_scan_size)`, the failure naming the three values;
  `clamd`'s memory limit at least 1.5 GiB; `malwareScannerClamav.replicaCount` at least 1.

Acceptance criteria:

- Chart test (`test/chart`, about 1 s): with default values the Deployment `quader-malware-scanner-clamav` has the containers `quader`
  (`--role scanner`, the kind `clamav`) and `clamd` (the pinned image), the volumes above and no other, no Secret but the TLS pair and the CA in
  `quader`, none in `clamd`; `clamd.conf` holds `LocalSocket`, no `TCPSocket`, `AlertExceedsMax yes` and `ConcurrentDatabaseReload no`; the
  policy admits `:8080` from the worker pool that claims `malware` only; with `config.malware.enabled: false` nothing of it renders.

### R-HA-069 · The updater Deployment `malware-updater-freshclam`
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

The owner's decision of 2026-11-21: "Ich sehe gerade du hast freshcalm an die worker gehängt, das ist natürlich falsch. Gliedere Freshclam aus,
es wird als seperates deployment ins helm integriert. Default reicht uns 1 replica." It replaces the container `freshclam` of every worker
that claimed `malware` ([Q-HA-362](#q-ha-362--freshclam-runs-beside-the-worker-without-a-credential), superseded). What the updater does is
[malware-scanning.md](malware-scanning.md) R-MAL-010 and R-MAL-032; its name follows the owner's rule of naming a unit after its tool
([Q-HA-375](#q-ha-375--the-updater-is-malware-updater-freshclam)). The chart's part is built
([malware-updater-freshclam.yaml](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/malware-updater-freshclam.yaml), [_malware.tpl](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/_malware.tpl)
`quader.malwareUpdaterOn`, `quader.freshclamConf`, `quader.validateMalwareUpdater`); the process of its `quader` container is R-MAL-032's.

- **When.** The chart renders `<fullname>-malware-updater-freshclam` (the kind `malware-updater-freshclam`) while `config.malware.enabled`
  is `true` and `config.malware.database.source` is `updater` (both the defaults), and nothing of it otherwise. No worker carries anything of
  `freshclam` any more: no container, no volume `freshclam-db`, no ConfigMap `<fullname>-freshclam` mounted into it.
- **Replicas** ([Q-HA-376](#q-ha-376--one-updater-replaced-not-rolled-and-outside-the-rule-of-two)): `malwareUpdaterFreshclam.replicaCount`,
  default 1, at least 1, and exempt from `highAvailability.enforce`: one fetcher per network is ClamAV's guidance, and nothing waits for the
  updater. `strategy: Recreate`, so two `freshclam` never fetch at once; no autoscaler, no disruption budget, no spread constraints. A drain
  that evicts it delays an update by the pod's start; the scanning goes on with the set in use (R-MAL-010). It is not in the expression of
  `QuaderReplicasNotReady`, whose bound is two; an updater that stays away shows on the System page (its row of R-OPS-048 is `lost`) and,
  after `stale_after`, in `QuaderMalwareDatabaseStale`.
- **The container `freshclam`**: the image `clamav.image` (the pin `CLAMAV_IMAGE`, one value with `clamd`,
  [Q-HA-363](#q-ha-363--one-image-value-for-clamd-and-freshclam-and-fixed-paths-the-containers-share)), started with
  `freshclam --version > /var/lib/clamav/.quader-tool-version; until [ -f /var/lib/clamav/.quader-seeded ]; do sleep 2; done; exec freshclam
  --foreground --daemon --config-file=/etc/freshclam/freshclam.conf`. The chart renders `freshclam.conf` in the ConfigMap
  `<fullname>-malware-updater-freshclam` ([Q-HA-377](#q-ha-377--freshclamconf-whole-signed-files-no-notifyclamd-and-the-mirror-as-a-value)):
  `DatabaseDirectory /var/lib/clamav`, `DatabaseMirror database.clamav.net` or, with `malwareUpdaterFreshclam.privateMirror` set,
  `PrivateMirror <that URL>` and no `DatabaseMirror`, `Checks 12`, `ScriptedUpdates no`, `TestDatabases no`, `Foreground yes`, `LogTime yes`,
  logging to standard error, and `HTTPProxyServer` and `HTTPProxyPort` from `malwareUpdaterFreshclam.proxy` when set. No `NotifyClamd`: the
  option takes the path of a `clamd.conf`, and the `NotifyClamd no` rendered before was read as a file name and logged an error at every
  update (the finding of 2026-11-21); no `clamd` runs in this pod. No probe: `freshclam` ends its container when it fails, and the kubelet
  starts it again.
- **The container `quader`**: `quader serve --role scanner` with `QUADER_PROCESS_SCANNER_KIND=freshclam`, `:8080` (the listing and the files,
  R-MAL-032) and `:8081`; readiness the check `malwareUpdaterFreshclam`, liveness `/healthz`, both on `:8081` over HTTPS (R-HA-034).
- **Pod.** The security context of R-HA-033 for both containers (user and group 65532, `readOnlyRootFilesystem`, no privilege escalation,
  every capability dropped, seccomp `RuntimeDefault`); `automountServiceAccountToken: false`; no RBAC; not the chart's service account;
  `shareProcessNamespace` never set; `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30`.
- **Volumes, and nothing else** (R-HA-061): `freshclam-db` (`emptyDir`, `malwareUpdaterFreshclam.database.sizeLimit`, default 1 GiB), at
  `/var/lib/clamav` in both containers, written by both (the seed and the markers by `quader`, the containers by `freshclam`); `/tmp` of each
  container (`tmp` in `quader`, `freshclam-tmp` in `freshclam`, each `tmp.sizeLimit`); `freshclam.conf` (read-only) in `freshclam`; no spool,
  so no `QUADER_STORAGE_SPOOL_MAX_BYTES`; the configuration file, the updater's own TLS Secret
  (`<fullname>-tls-malware-updater-freshclam`, or `tls.existingSecrets.malware-updater-freshclam`) with `tls.crt`, `tls.key` and `ca.crt` in
  `quader` (R-HA-063). `freshclam` mounts no Secret, no TLS pair and no configuration of Quader. No key of the key ring, no database, Valkey or
  object-store credential and none of the shared `extraVolumes`, `extraEnv`, `extraEnvFrom`, `initContainers` and `sidecars` reach the pod;
  `malwareUpdaterFreshclam.extraEnv` is the `quader` container's own.
- **Resources** (not measured; [malware-scanning.md](malware-scanning.md) R-MAL-027): `quader` requests 50m CPU, 64 MiB and 64 MiB of
  ephemeral storage, memory limit 256 MiB; `freshclam` requests 50m CPU and 128 MiB, memory limit 512 MiB (`TestDatabases no` keeps it from
  loading what it fetched). No CPU limit.
- **Service and policies.** `<fullname>-malware-updater-freshclam`: `ClusterIP`, port `https` 8080 (`appProtocol: https`), no
  `service.type`, no Ingress or HTTPRoute. NetworkPolicy (R-HA-042, ingress only, ADR-154): `:8080` from the pods of the worker Deployments
  that claim the queue `malware`; `:8081` from the ops sources; and the scan listener `:8082` of `packages` admits the updater's pods too
  (its seed and its report). Its pods carry `quader/serve: "true"`, so `<fullname>-ops` selects them and the scrape reaches the metric of
  R-MAL-032 on `:8081`.
- **Chart-managed configuration** (R-HA-029: refused when set by hand): `malware.updater.url`
  `https://<fullname>-malware-updater-freshclam.<namespace>.svc:8080`, `malware.updater.server_name`
  `<fullname>-malware-updater-freshclam.<namespace>.svc` and `malware.updater.client_name` `<fullname>-worker.<namespace>.svc` (the worker's
  call), `malware.scan_listener.updater_client_name` `<fullname>-malware-updater-freshclam.<namespace>.svc` (the scan listener's admission of
  the seed and the report), and the updater's name as one more entry of `server.scan_clients`. The updater reads `malware.scan_listener.url`
  and `server_name` as the malware scanner does.
- **The kind table** (`quader.tlsKindTable`, R-HA-063) gains `malware-updater-freshclam` with `client` and `scanClient` true, on while the
  updater renders: a Certificate, a Secret, the name `<fullname>-malware-updater-freshclam.<namespace>.svc` and the name-length check of
  R-HA-029. That name is the longest the chart builds from `<fullname>` alone (26 characters more), so the chart now refuses a `<fullname>` of
  more than 37 characters ([Q-HA-374](#q-ha-374--the-chart-refuses-a-fullname-too-long-for-the-names-it-builds-and-never-cuts-it)).
- **The way out of the cluster** is `freshclam`'s alone: DNS (port 53 to the cluster's resolver) and HTTPS (443) to `database.clamav.net`,
  which Cloudflare serves from addresses of its own that change, so an egress policy by address needs Cloudflare's published ranges and one by
  name a policy engine that can match a name; or the host and port of `privateMirror`; or the proxy of `proxy`. The chart renders no egress
  rule ([H-516](../security/egress.md#h-516--the-chart-restricts-no-egress-of-its-pods)); an operator's egress policy admits the updater's
  pods by a label of `malwareUpdaterFreshclam.podLabels` ([security/malware-scanning.md](../security/malware-scanning.md) H-1106). The worker
  no longer needs a way to ClamAV's network.
- **Values** (R-HA-031): `malwareUpdaterFreshclam.replicaCount`, `privateMirror`, `proxy`, `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`, `resources`,
  `freshclam.resources`, `database.sizeLimit`, `affinity`, `nodeSelector`, `tolerations`, `priorityClassName`, `podAnnotations`,
  `podLabels`, `extraEnv`. `privateMirror` must be an `http` or `https` URL whose host is not `clamav.net` and does not end in `.clamav.net`
  (`freshclam` refuses such a `PrivateMirror`); `proxy` must be `http://<host>[:<port>]` (port 80 when none is given); neither may hold
  whitespace, credentials, a query or a fragment ([Q-HA-384](#q-ha-384--the-mirror-and-the-proxy-are-checked-so-that-no-value-adds-a-line-to-freshclamconf)).
  The chart refuses another value and names the key. The values `freshclam.*` and the configuration keys `malware.database.freshclam`,
  `freshclam_dir`, `proxy` and `keep` are gone; `values.schema.json` refuses the first.

Acceptance criteria:

- Chart test (`test/chart`, about 1 s): with default values the Deployment `quader-malware-updater-freshclam` has one replica, `Recreate`, the
  containers `freshclam` (the pinned image) and `quader` (`--role scanner`, the kind `freshclam`), the volumes above and no other, no Secret but
  the TLS pair in `quader` and none in `freshclam`; its `freshclam.conf` holds `ScriptedUpdates no` and `DatabaseMirror database.clamav.net`
  and no `NotifyClamd`; with `privateMirror` it holds `PrivateMirror` and no `DatabaseMirror`, with `proxy` the two proxy lines; the policy
  admits `:8080` from the worker pool that claims `malware` only, and `packages`' `:8082` rule lists the updater; no worker Deployment has a
  container, a volume or a mount of `freshclam`; `highAvailability.enforce: true` with one replica renders, `replicaCount: 0` fails and names
  the key; `privateMirror: https://database.clamav.net` fails, and so do an `ftp` mirror, a mirror with whitespace and an `https` proxy;
  `config.malware.database.source: repository` and `config.malware.enabled: false` render nothing of the updater; a `<fullname>` of 38
  characters fails and names the Service. Built: `TestR_HA_069_TheUpdaterDeployment` ([malware_test.go](../../test/chart/malware_test.go)),
  the bound in `TestChart` ([chart_test.go](../../test/chart/chart_test.go)).

### R-HA-070 · The analyser from its own image, and the database in the scanner pod
Priority: **P1** · Covers: HA-015

The owner's decisions of 2026-11-21 ([ADR-229](../decisions.md#adr-229--the-scanner-unit-detects-as-well-and-the-analyser-comes-from-its-own-image)):
"Option B, nach der umbenennung. Trivy dann aus den anderen Images entfernen.", and, for where the scanner's analyser comes from, "Option
b": the analyser's own image as an init container that copies the binary into a volume of the scanner pod, not a second image built with
every release, in the pattern of the ClamAV image. It changes the pod of R-HA-065 and the release image of R-HA-033. **Built on
2026-11-21:** the container `database`, the volume `trivy-db`, its check and the values `vulnScannerTrivy.database.sizeLimit` and
`.resources` ([vuln-scanner-trivy.yaml](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/vuln-scanner-trivy.yaml), `quader.validateVulnScannerTrivy` in
[_vuln.tpl](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/_vuln.tpl)); the loader's budget reaches it as
`QUADER_VULNERABILITIES_IMAGES_DATABASE_DIR_BUDGET` ([Q-VULN-209](vulnerability-scanning.md#q-vuln-209--the-loaders-room-is-a-key-of-the-configuration-that-the-chart-sets-to-the-volumes-size)).
**Built on 2026-11-21, the next step:** the init container `trivy`, the volume `trivy-bin`, the values `trivy.image`, `trivy.pullPolicy`
and `trivy.resources`, the 1,280 MiB request of `quader`, the default `/opt/trivy/trivy` of `vulnerabilities.images.binary`
([vulnerabilities.go](../../internal/config/vulnerabilities.go)), the pin `TRIVY_IMAGE` and its Renovate group, the Containerfile without the
analyser (the image 246,494,610 bytes before and 83,309,810 after on arm64, the difference the binary's 163,184,800), `make trivy` and
`make trivy-dir` out of the image ([Makefile](../../Makefile), Q-HA-388), the job `container-scan` on that binary, `.trivyignore.yaml` without
its entry, and the test profiles of Q-HA-382 (`values-dev.yaml`, `values-vuln.yaml`, `deploy/dev/up.sh`, `values-restore.yaml` by
Q-HA-387, the platform matrix by Q-HA-386).

- **When.** Everything below renders with `<fullname>-vuln-scanner-trivy`, while the image scanning is on, and nothing of it otherwise.
- **The init container `trivy`** ([Q-HA-378](#q-ha-378--the-analysers-binary-is-copied-by-an-init-container-of-its-own-image-into-a-volume-the-scanner-mounts-read-only)):
  the image `trivy.image` (default `docker.io/aquasec/trivy:0.76.2@sha256:8f6bb947dbc528902e11f2f5be52f7b519f6a39d5d148f41166f2040499768fb`,
  the pin `TRIVY_IMAGE`), `imagePullPolicy` `trivy.pullPolicy` (`IfNotPresent`), the command `["cp", "/usr/local/bin/trivy",
  "/opt/trivy/trivy"]` in place of the image's entry point `trivy`; the security context of R-HA-033 (the pod's user 65532, which the
  image does not set itself, a read-only root file system, no privilege escalation, every capability dropped, seccomp `RuntimeDefault`);
  one volume, `trivy-bin`, read-write at `/opt/trivy`, and no Secret, configuration or token. Resources `trivy.resources`: requests 10m CPU
  and 32 MiB, memory limit 128 MiB (not measured). Measured with Docker on 2026-11-21, not in a pod: the copy runs as user 65532 under these
  restrictions in 0.35 s with the container's start, and the copy is owned by 65532 with mode 0755. Measured in a pod of the kind cluster the
  same day (arm64, under the load of other builders): the init container ran as user and group 65532 with a read-only root file system, no
  capability, no new privileges and the runtime's seccomp profile, its process took 0.33 and 0.95 s, and the copy is 163,184,800 bytes owned
  by 65532 with mode 0755 ([developer/vulnerabilities.md](../developer/vulnerabilities.md#the-analyser-from-its-own-image-r-ha-070)).
- **The volume `trivy-bin`**: an `emptyDir` on the node's disk, `sizeLimit` 256 MiB (the binary is 163,184,800 bytes), read-only in the
  container `quader` at `/opt/trivy`, where `vulnerabilities.images.binary` points by default (`/opt/trivy/trivy`). The copy belongs to the
  pod's user, so only the read-only mount keeps an analyser from replacing the binary that the pod's later analyses and detections run.
- **The container `database`** (the loader of [vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-049; [architecture.md](architecture.md)
  [Q-ARCH-564](architecture.md#q-arch-564--the-loader-of-the-analysers-database-is-a-kind-of-the-role-scanner-trivy-db)): the Quader image of
  the release, `quader serve --role scanner` with `QUADER_PROCESS_SCANNER_KIND=trivy-db` and `QUADER_SERVER_OPS_LISTEN=:8083` (the scanner
  holds `:8081` of the pod's network); its budget from `vulnScannerTrivy.database.sizeLimit`; the security context of R-HA-033; volumes: the
  configuration file, the scanner's own TLS Secret (the same Secret, R-HA-063: it reads the scan listener as the scanner does), `trivy-db`
  read-write at `/var/lib/quader/trivy-db`, and a `/tmp` of its own; no listener but the operations listener; liveness `/healthz` on `:8083`
  (R-HA-034) and no readiness probe, because the scanner's readiness and report carry what matters of it. Resources
  `vulnScannerTrivy.database.resources`: requests 50m CPU, 64 MiB and 2 GiB of ephemeral storage (one database), memory limit 256 MiB (not
  measured). No writable volume is shared between `quader` and `database` but `trivy-db`, which is read-only in `quader`. The scanner's
  NetworkPolicy gains no rule for `:8083`: only the kubelet's probe reaches it, and traffic from the pod's own node is not restricted by a
  NetworkPolicy.
- **The volume `trivy-db`** ([Q-HA-380](#q-ha-380--the-database-volume-follows-spooltype-5-gi-by-default-and-the-chart-refuses-less-than-4-gi)):
  follows `spool.type` as the spool does (an `emptyDir` with `sizeLimit` `vulnScannerTrivy.database.sizeLimit`, default 5 Gi, or a generic
  ephemeral volume of that size), read-write in `database`, read-only in `quader`. The chart refuses a `sizeLimit` below 4 GiB, two databases
  at the allowance of 2 GiB each (H-872's constant, which moves here from the worker's spool), and names the key.
- **The container `quader`** gains the two read-only mounts and 256 MiB on its ephemeral-storage request (1 GiB to 1,280 MiB) for the
  copy; `shareProcessNamespace` stays unset, so no container of the pod sees another's processes.
- **The pin** ([Q-HA-381](#q-ha-381--one-pin-by-digest-the-charts-value-held-equal-by-a-chart-test-and-one-renovate-group-that-reviews-a-new-version)):
  `TRIVY_IMAGE` in `tools/versions.env`, by its index digest, replaces `TRIVY_VERSION` and the four `TRIVY_SHA256_*` digests of the release
  archive; `trivy.image` holds the same value and a chart test holds them equal, as `clamav.image` and `CLAMAV_IMAGE`; Renovate updates both
  in one group (`trivy`), merges a new digest of the same version by itself and opens a new version as a pull request to review. The
