  Containerfile loses its stage `trivy` and its three build arguments, and `make image` and `build.yml` pass none; the release image holds
  the binary of Quader and nothing else on its base. `make trivy` takes the binary out of `TRIVY_IMAGE` for the host's architecture on
  Linux (`docker create` and `docker cp`) and refuses elsewhere with a message that names the image; the job `container-scan` uses it, so
  the scan of the release image runs the scanner's own analyser, one version in the repository. `.trivyignore.yaml` loses its entry at
  `usr/local/bin/trivy`, a path the release image no longer has.
- **An installation that mirrors images** ([Q-HA-383](#q-ha-383--a-private-mirror-changes-one-value-per-image-and-nodes-without-a-registry-load-the-images-beforehand)):
  mirrors, by their index digests, the Quader image, `TRIVY_IMAGE` while the image scanning is on and `CLAMAV_IMAGE` while the malware
  scanning is on (a copy of the whole index, for example `skopeo copy --all` or `crane copy`, keeps the digest), and sets
  `image.registry` and `image.repository`, `trivy.image` and `clamav.image` to the mirror's names with the same digests;
  `global.imagePullSecrets` reaches the init container like every container of the pod. The analyser's database does not come from an
  image of a node: it stays the repository's (R-VULN-044), whose address an administrator points at the mirror, or a local repository.
- **An installation whose nodes reach no registry** loads the three images into each node's container runtime beforehand and keeps
  `pullPolicy: IfNotPresent`; or it switches the image scanning off (`config.vulnerabilities.images.enabled: false`) and pulls nothing of the
  analyser. Nodes that reach Quader's own registry can pull the analyser's image through a remote OCI repository of Quader that fronts Docker
  Hub (`trivy.image` set to that address, a level the node can read or a pull secret): the scanner is not needed for Quader to start, so this
  needs no order of its own, but a scanner pod cannot start while Quader's registry is down.
- **What a pod start costs**: the pull of `TRIVY_IMAGE` once per node and pin (58,549,893 bytes compressed for arm64, 63,436,811 for amd64;
  3.3 s on the measuring machine's network with Docker; 13.5 and 15.6 s by a kind node of that machine under the load of other builders,
  measured 2026-11-21), the copy (0.33 and 0.95 s in a pod), then the scanner's start as before (0.6 and 1.7 s from the container's start to
  its listener, which follows the analyser's answer of its version; the pod ready 19 and 21 s after it was scheduled); the database's load
  follows beside it (R-VULN-049). The pull and the copy on the owner's installation are recorded after the first release that carries it. The price, named to the owner: a node pulls a third party's image when
  a scanner pod starts ([H-1182](../security/image-scanning.md#h-1182--a-node-pulls-the-analysers-image-from-a-third-partys-registry-when-a-scanner-pod-starts)).
- **Values** (R-HA-031, whose copy of the values file gains them with the change that builds them): `trivy.image`, `trivy.pullPolicy`,
  `trivy.resources`, `vulnScannerTrivy.database.sizeLimit`, `vulnScannerTrivy.database.resources`.

Acceptance criteria:

- Chart test (`test/chart`, about 2 s): with default values the scanner pod has the init container `trivy` with `trivy.image`, the copy's
  command, the security context and the one volume `trivy-bin`; the container `quader` mounts `trivy-bin` and `trivy-db` read-only; the
  container `database` runs the kind `trivy-db` with `:8083`, mounts `trivy-db` read-write, the scanner's Secret and a `/tmp` of its own, and
  has a liveness probe and no readiness probe; `trivy.image` equals `TRIVY_IMAGE` of `tools/versions.env`; `vulnScannerTrivy.database.sizeLimit:
  3Gi` fails and names the key; with `config.vulnerabilities.images.enabled: false` nothing of it renders; no other Deployment has an init
  container, `trivy-bin` or `trivy-db`; `global.imagePullSecrets` is on the pod. Built:
  `TestR_HA_070_TheLoaderWritesTheDatabaseThatTheScannerReadsReadOnly` in [vuln_scanner_trivy_test.go](../../test/chart/vuln_scanner_trivy_test.go)
  (with a mirrored image, another pull policy and an image without a tag refused), and the volumes and the one init container in
  `TestR_HA_065_TheScannerHoldsNoSecretOfTheInstallation`.
- Check (`make versions-check`, seconds): `TRIVY_IMAGE` carries a digest; no `TRIVY_SHA256_*` line and no `trivy` stage in the
  Containerfile remain; `make trivy` puts the binary of `TRIVY_IMAGE`'s tag on the path. Built in the [Makefile](../../Makefile), with a
  `trivy` on `PATH` compared as well (Q-HA-388).
- End to end (set `vuln`, R-VULN-046): the analysis runs the copied binary, and the live pod's spec lists the three containers and their
  mounts as above (Q-HA-342). Built in `TestVuln_R_VULN_041_AnImagePushedToALocalRepositoryIsAnalysedAndDetectedByAScannerPod`
  ([vuln_scanner_test.go](../../test/e2e/vuln_scanner_test.go)): the init container `trivy` terminated with exit code 0, its command and
  its one mount, `trivy-bin` read-only in `quader` alone, and every image scanner ready with the version of `TRIVY_IMAGE`'s tag, which only
  the copied binary can answer, the release image holding none.
- Recorded once after the first release that carries it, on the owner's installation: the pull and the copy from the pod's events.

### R-HA-071 · The signing identity's Secret, in the worker pods only
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

Built (templates/_signing.tpl, templates/signing-certificate.yaml, the mount in templates/_secrets.tpl, the four alerts in
templates/_rules.tpl). The chart's side of Quader's signing identity ([signatures.md](signatures.md) R-SIG-045, R-SIG-046; the owner's
reading r8 of [Q-SIG-16](signatures.md#q-sig-16--the-eight-readings-of-the-request): "through Helm, a Secret that cert-manager may issue";
[Q-HA-385](#q-ha-385--the-signing-identitys-secret-reaches-the-worker-pods-only-and-the-chart-renders-its-certificate-on-request)).

- **Two sources, at most one.** `signing.identity.existingSecret` names an existing Secret with `tls.crt` (the leaf and its intermediates),
  `tls.key` (an ECDSA P-256 key) and `ca.crt` (the root), the keys of a cert-manager TLS Secret; the chart never creates it. Or, with
  `signing.identity.certManager.issuerRef.name`, the chart renders a cert-manager `Certificate` `<fullname>-signing` into the Secret of the same
  name: `commonName` and `subject` (organizations, countries, provinces, localities, organizational units) from the values, `uris` the base
  URL (`config.server.base_url`, which the chart requires) and `signing.identity.certManager.uris`, `usages: [digital signature, code signing]`,
  `privateKey: {algorithm: ECDSA, size: 256, rotationPolicy: Always}`, `duration` and `renewBefore` from the values, `issuerRef` (an `Issuer`
  of the release namespace or a `ClusterIssuer`, group `cert-manager.io`). The values of cert-manager's API used here were read in its API
  reference on 2026-11-21. The render fails with both sources set, naming the two keys. With neither, the chart sets nothing and an
  identity comes from the admin area (R-SIG-047).
- **Mounts.** The pods of the kind `worker` (its main Deployment and its pools) mount the Secret read-only at `/var/run/secrets/quader/signing/`,
  as a directory volume with items and without `subPath`, mode `0440`, and the chart sets `signing.identity.cert_file`, `key_file` and
  `ca_file` to its three files. The configuration file is shared, as it is for the login secrets that only `api` mounts; only the roles
  `worker` and `all` read the three keys ([signatures.md](signatures.md) R-SIG-049). No pod of `api`, `packages`, a scanner, the updater or a Job mounts it.
  The three keys join the chart's managed paths: set under `config`, they fail the render, as `secrets.encryption_key_files` does.
- **Rotation without a restart.** cert-manager renews the certificate with a new key `renewBefore` its end; the kubelet swaps the volume, the
  worker's reloader reads it (R-SIG-046), and the identity is announced and then switched (R-SIG-048). The pod's checksum follows the
  Secret's name and the paths, not its content, so a renewal rolls nothing.
- **The values** (R-HA-031's copy of the values file holds them with their defaults): `signing.identity.existingSecret`,
  `signing.identity.certManager.issuerRef` (`kind`, `name`, `group`), `commonName`, `subject` (cert-manager's fields: organizations,
  countries, provinces, localities, organizationalUnits, streetAddresses, postalCodes, serialNumber), `uris`, `duration`, `renewBefore`;
  `values.schema.json` declares each. The tuning keys are `config.signing` (signatures.md R-SIG-058).

Acceptance criteria:

- Chart test (`test/chart`, about 1 s): with `existingSecret` the worker Deployment and its pools mount the Secret at the path above and the
  rendered configuration names the three files, and no other Deployment or Job mounts it; with `certManager.issuerRef.name` the
  `Certificate` renders with ECDSA 256, `rotationPolicy: Always`, the usages `digital signature` and `code signing` and the base URL as a URI;
  with both the render fails and names both keys; with neither nothing of it renders.

### R-HA-073 · The accounts of the upstream registries from existing Secrets
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

Built (templates/_upstream_accounts.tpl, the mount and the volume in templates/_deployment.tpl, the managed key in templates/_helpers.tpl,
the check in templates/_validate.tpl). The chart's side of [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-077, the
owner's wish of 2026-11-25 (Q-REPO-483): the accounts of the registries of the built-in project `upstream` come from Secrets that exist,
which the chart names and never creates.

- **The value.** `secrets.upstreamAccounts` is a map by the key of a repository of the project `upstream` (the key Admin area ›
  Upstream registries shows: `docker-hub`, `quay`, `ghcr`, `gitlab`, `npmjs`, …, `scanner-trivy`), each entry `existingSecret`
  (required), `authMode` (`basic`, the default, or `bearer`), `usernameKey` (`username`; `basic` only) and `passwordKey` (`password`)
  ([Q-HA-494](#q-ha-494--secretsupstreamaccounts-is-a-map-by-the-registrys-key-and-authmode-defaults-to-basic)). The default `{}` declares none.
- **The mount** ([Q-HA-493](#q-ha-493--the-accounts-of-the-upstream-registries-are-one-projected-volume-with-optional-sources-in-the-pods-of-api-packages-and-worker)). One projected volume `upstream-accounts`, `defaultMode: 0440`, read-only, without `subPath`, at
  `/var/run/secrets/quader/upstream-accounts/`, with one source per entry: the Secret, `optional: true`, its items `<key>/username`
  (`basic` only) and `<key>/password`. Every Deployment of `api`, `packages` and `worker` mounts it (the main Deployments, their pools
  and their endpoint pools), since each fetches from upstreams (a client's fill, the upstream test and the catalogue, the download queue,
  the mirror passes and the image scanning's database); no scanner, the updater, the migration Job, a backup, restore or post-restore
  Job, nor the Bastion's chart mounts it. A Secret or a key that does not exist starts every pod: the source is optional, and that
  registry's fetches fail until it exists (R-REPO-077).
- **The configuration.** The chart renders `config.repositories.upstream_accounts.<key>` with `auth_mode`, `password_file`,
  `username_file` (`basic` only) below the mount path, and `secret_name` (the entry's `existingSecret`), into the configuration file and
  the migration Job's copy; never a value. `config.repositories.upstream_accounts` set under `config` fails the render.
- **Rotation without a restart.** A changed Secret reaches the files within the kubelet's sync (R-HA-030's 2 minutes) and every replica
  reads them again after 10 s. The pod's checksum follows the rendered configuration, so adding or removing an entry rolls the pods
  once (the scanners' and the updater's too, whose checksum covers the same file, though they mount nothing of it), and a rotation rolls
  nothing.
- **Refusals of the render**: `config.repositories.upstream_accounts` set directly; `usernameKey` beside `authMode: bearer`; a key that
  does not match `^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$` and an entry without `existingSecret` (the schema). Whether the key names a repository is
  checked by `quader migrate`, which fails the upgrade naming it (R-REPO-077).
- **No env, no port, no rule.** No variable carries a Secret's value, and no Service, NetworkPolicy or PDB changes: the pods reach the
  upstreams they reached before.

Acceptance criteria:

- Chart test (`test/chart`, about 1 s): with two entries over `ci/roles-pools.yaml`, the nine Deployments of `api`, `packages` and
  `worker` mount the projected volume with the two optional sources, their items and `0440`, read-only without `subPath`, and no other
  Deployment, Job or CronJob mounts it; the configuration file and the migration Job's copy name the paths and the Secrets; without an
  entry nothing of it renders; the three refusals fail the render.

### R-HA-072 · The object-store connections in the chart
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

The chart's side of several object-store connections ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-050; the owner's decision 9 of 2026-11-22:
connections are kept in the chart as a list, their credentials come from Secrets as today, the admin area only shows them).

**Status.** Built in the chart ([_storage.tpl](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/_storage.tpl), the values, the schema, the alerts;
`test/chart/storage_test.go`); `config.storage.s3`, `secrets.s3`, `secrets.s3CA`, `secrets.backupSource` and `secrets.journalReader` are
gone and refused with the keys that took their place
([Q-HA-395](#q-ha-395--the-values-of-the-one-store-are-refused-by-the-templates-with-the-keys-that-took-their-place)). The backup's
read login and the journal reader of every connection are rendered in their target form since the rest of package E: an element of
`backup.source.connections` per entry with `backupSource`, an element of the journal credentials file per connection
([backup-and-restore.md](backup-and-restore.md) R-BAK-030; Q-HA-396 is superseded). `encrypted` is passed through and `keyed_names` without it
refused since package 6 of the encryption of stored content (2026-11-23, `TestR_HA_072_AnEncryptedConnection`); the value set
`ci/connections.yaml` renders its second connection encrypted.

- **The list** is `config.storage.connections`, passed through like every key of `config` with each element's `id` filled in and the
  `*_file` keys below; the values file holds one element with the defaults of the plain path. A list given in the values replaces it
  whole, so an element carries only what it sets, and an element without `id` is `default`, as in the binary
  ([Q-HA-394](#q-ha-394--an-element-without-id-is-default-in-the-chart-as-in-the-binary)): an installation with one connection sets
  `[{bucket: …}]` (or a provisioner's key below) and nothing else. The schema checks an element against the keys of
  [storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-050 ([Q-HA-397](#q-ha-397--the-schema-checks-an-element-against-the-keys-of-r-stor-050)):

  ```yaml
  config:
    storage:
      connections:
        - id: default                 # the default; storage.md R-STOR-050
          bucket: ""                  # required unless secrets.storageConnections[].bucketKey; example: quader-blobs
          prefix: quader
          region: ""                  # example: eu01
          endpoint: ""                # example: object.storage.eu01.onstackit.cloud (a host means https://)
          force_path_style: false
          credentials_source: default # default | webIdentity | static
          encrypted: false            # the default of storage.md R-STOR-075; true: the provider keeps ciphertext only; no Secret of the chart for it
  secrets:
    storageConnections: []            # one entry per connection that needs a Secret; example:
    #  - connectionId: default        # matches config.storage.connections[].id
    #    existingSecret: quader-s3    # the static credential, or the Secret of an S3 provisioner when a *Key below is set
    #    accessKeyIdKey: access-key-id
    #    secretAccessKeyKey: secret-access-key
    #    sessionTokenKey: ""          # empty = no session token
    #    bucketKey: ""                # example (provisioner Secret): S3_BUCKET; set = the chart sets bucket_file
    #    regionKey: ""                # example: S3_REGION; set = region_file
    #    endpointKey: ""              # example: S3_ENDPOINT; set = endpoint_file
    #    ca:                          # renders the connection's ca_file; empty = the outbound trust store
    #      existingSecret: ""
    #      key: ca.crt
    #    backupSource:                # the backup pods only: a login that may only read this connection (backup-and-restore.md R-BAK-030)
    #      existingSecret: ""
    #      accessKeyIdKey: access-key-id
    #      secretAccessKeyKey: secret-access-key
    #    journalReader:               # the post-restore and restore Jobs only: a login that lists this connection's object versions
    #      existingSecret: ""
    #      accessKeyIdKey: access-key-id
    #      secretAccessKeyKey: secret-access-key
  ```

  `secrets.s3`, `secrets.s3CA`, `secrets.backupSource` and `secrets.journalReader` go; their keys are fields of an entry
  ([Q-HA-390](#q-ha-390--each-connections-secrets-are-an-entry-of-one-list-keyed-by-the-connection)).
- **Mounts**, each with `items`, `defaultMode: 0440` and no `subPath`, so a rotation reaches the files (R-HA-030):

  | Entry field | Pods | Mount path | Key the chart sets in the element of that `id` |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `existingSecret` with `credentials_source: static` | `api`, `packages`, `worker` and the restore and post-restore Jobs | `/var/run/secrets/quader/s3-<id>/` | `access_key_id_file`, `secret_access_key_file`, `session_token_file` |
  | `bucketKey`, `regionKey`, `endpointKey` | the same pods and the backup pods | `/var/run/secrets/quader/s3-<id>-location/` | `bucket_file`, `region_file`, `endpoint_file` |
  | `ca` | the same pods and the backup pods | `/var/run/secrets/quader/s3-<id>-ca/` | `ca_file` |
  | `backupSource` | the backup pods only | `/var/run/secrets/quader/s3-<id>-backup/` | the element of that connection in `backup.source.connections` (`connection`, `credentials_source: static`, the two key files; R-BAK-030), while `backup.enabled` |
  | `journalReader` | the post-restore and restore Jobs only, with their `journalCredentials.source: static` | `/var/run/secrets/quader/s3-<id>-journal/` | the element of that connection in the credentials file of `--credentials-file` and `--journal-credentials-file` (R-BAK-030, Q-BAK-73); with `journalCredentials.source: default` the file holds an element `credentials_source: default` per connection |

  Each field is a volume of its own, `secret-s3-<id>`, `secret-s3-<id>-location`, `secret-s3-<id>-ca`, `secret-s3-<id>-backup`,
  `secret-s3-<id>-journal`, because the pods that read them differ; a provisioner's location is projected into the backup pods without
  its credentials. An empty plain `bucket`, `region` or `endpoint` is left out where its file takes its place. The migration Job and the
  scanner pods mount nothing of a connection.

  The keys the chart sets join its managed paths: set under `config` in that element, they fail the render; the static key files
  (`access_key_id_file`, `secret_access_key_file`, `session_token_file`) fail in every element, because only an entry provides them
  ([Q-HA-398](#q-ha-398--what-of-an-element-the-chart-manages-and-an-entry-that-nothing-reads)).
- **Refusals** (R-HA-029; each names the values and the connection by index and id), checked after the values of before
  (Q-HA-395):
  - `config.storage.connections` empty or not a list, more than eight elements, an `id` outside `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,30}[a-z0-9]$`, or
    two elements with one `id` (two elements without `id` are two of `default`, Q-HA-394);
  - an element without `bucket` and without an entry whose `bucketKey` is set, and a plain `bucket`, `region` or `endpoint` beside the
    file that replaces it;
  - `credentials_source: static` without an entry with `existingSecret` for that `id`;
  - an entry whose `connectionId` names no element, two entries of one connection, a `bucketKey`, `regionKey`, `endpointKey` or
    `sessionTokenKey` without `existingSecret`, and an `existingSecret` that nothing reads (neither `credentials_source: static` nor a
    `*Key`, Q-HA-398);
  - `keyed_names` on an element without `encrypted: true` ("config.storage.connections[0] (default) has keyed_names without encrypted:
    true: keyed_names is a detail of an encrypted connection; on a connection that is not encrypted the content is readable anyway
    (storage.md R-STOR-075)"); `encrypted: true` passes through like every key (until the encryption of stored content was built the chart
    refused it). The part sizes that an encrypted element needs are the binary's to check at start (storage.md R-STOR-075 rule 2): the
    chart's byte parser does not read every unit the binary does. The chart renders no key and no Secret for the stored content: Quader draws
    the storage keys and keeps them sealed in the database ([Q-HA-415](#q-ha-415--the-chart-carries-no-key-of-the-stored-content));
  - `drain: true` on every element, or `config.storage.replication.min_copies` outside 1 to the number of elements without it;
  - two elements on one endpoint and bucket whose prefixes are equal or contain each other (an empty endpoint compares as the AWS
    endpoint of its region; an element whose bucket or endpoint comes from a file is the binary's to compare, whose marker of R-STOR-051
    catches it), and the backup target at any element's location (the rule of R-HA-029 for the target, per connection);
  - with `backup.enabled`, an element with `credentials_source: static` whose entry has no `backupSource` (R-BAK-030, Q-BAK-64); with a
    `journalCredentials.source: static` of `restore` or `postRestore`, an element without `drain: true` whose entry has no `journalReader`
    (the refusal names each, [Q-HA-399](#q-ha-399--a-static-journal-reader-is-required-for-every-connection-without-drain)).
- **The PrometheusRule** carries the alerts of [storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-060 and `QuaderStorageUnknownKey` of R-STOR-088 (R-HA-045).
- The development and test profiles (`deploy/dev`, the stack of `test/integration`) render one connection; the integration case with
  two connections sets the list itself ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-063). The chart's value set `ci/connections.yaml` renders two,
  one from a provisioner's Secret, in place of the one of the provisioner before, so the render tests of every value set see two
  connections at no added cost.

Acceptance criteria (chart render tests, about 1 s):

- One element with `bucket` renders a configuration whose `storage.connections` has that element and every pod mounts no S3 Secret;
  with `credentials_source: static` and an entry, the `api`, `packages` and `worker` Deployments mount `/var/run/secrets/quader/s3-default/`
  and the element names the two files; the backup CronJob does not mount it and mounts the entry's `backupSource` instead
  (`TestR_HA_072_OneConnection`).
- A provisioner entry with `bucketKey: S3_BUCKET` and no `bucket` renders `bucket_file` and passes; without the entry the render fails
  naming the element (`TestR_HA_072_SeveralConnectionsAndAProvisioner`, `TestR_HA_072_Refusals`).
- Each refusal above fails the render with the values named (`TestR_HA_072_Refusals`); each value of before fails naming its new keys
  (`TestR_HA_072_MovedValues`, `TestR_HA_072_AnInstallationMoves`).
- `encrypted: true`, alone and with `keyed_names: false`, renders the element as given, and no pod mounts more than with a plain connection
  (`TestR_HA_072_AnEncryptedConnection`).
- The rendered file passes the binary's own validator for every pod of every value set, with the files of the pod's object-store
  mounts in place (`TestRenderedConfigurationPassesTheBinary`).

### R-HA-003 · Replica registry as the coordination view
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: HA-006, HA-009

The replica registry of R-OPS-003 (table `replica`, heartbeat every `system.heartbeat_interval`,
stale after `system.heartbeat_stale_after`) is the single source of truth for "which replicas are
alive, with which version and roles, on which node". This page uses it for four HA mechanisms. The
table, the heartbeat, the pruning of stale rows and the read-only API `GET /api/v1/system/replicas`
are therefore MVP (Q-HA-12). The node comes from `QUADER_NODE_NAME`, which the chart sets from the
downward API (R-HA-030); the registry also records how many Sentinels each replica reaches
(`valkey_sentinels_reachable`, R-HA-057). The UI status screen is MVP as well
([api-and-ui.md](api-and-ui.md) R-UI-038, Q-API-8, Q-UI-7): it groups the replicas by role, states
per role whether two ready replicas run on different nodes, summarises the replicas' Valkey views
and shows the backup summary of R-API-050. It is the only UI view of the replicas, the scheduled
tasks and the key ring. R-HA-001 and R-HA-020 verify rollouts through the replica API.

| Use | Rule |
|---|---|
| Contract-migration guard | A contract step runs only when no live replica runs a version that still uses the dropped object (R-HA-018). |
| Cluster minimum version | `min(version)` over live replicas gates features and background migrations whose data the previous release cannot interpret (R-HA-020, R-HA-022). |
| Connection budget check | The migration Job compares `max_connections` with the budget derived from the expected replica counts per role (R-HA-016). |
| Post-restore cleanup | `quader admin post-restore` empties the table, because every row in a restored database describes a pod that no longer exists (R-HA-025). |

- "Live" means `heartbeat_at > now() - system.heartbeat_stale_after`, evaluated with PostgreSQL's
  clock. Replica clocks are never compared with each other (R-HA-005).
- A replica in state `draining` still counts as live for the contract guard while its heartbeat is fresh: it may still run old
  code for up to its grace period. Once its heartbeat is stale it has signed off: it is not listed and counts nowhere
  ([operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-003, Q-OPS-210).
- The migration Job, the backup CronJob's pods and the restore Job do not insert a `replica` row.
  They are not serving replicas and must not appear in the minimum-version computation.

Acceptance criteria:

- During a rolling upgrade from 0.3.0 to 0.4.0, `GET /api/v1/system/replicas` shows both versions;
  after `kubectl rollout status` of `deploy/quader-api`, `deploy/quader-packages` and `deploy/quader-worker` returns, only 0.4.0 is
  listed within `system.heartbeat_stale_after`.
- `kubectl delete pod --grace-period=0 --force <pod>` makes the row stale within 30 s; the
  contract guard of a migration started afterwards ignores it.

### R-HA-004 · Cross-replica invalidation through the change log and Valkey
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: HA-006

Since 2026-10-28 Quader issues no `LISTEN` and no `NOTIFY`,
and no replica holds a coordination session for invalidations ([architecture.md](architecture.md)
R-ARCH-018, Q-ARCH-15). A change reaches the other replicas through a change log in PostgreSQL,
which carries correctness, and through a Valkey Pub/Sub message, which carries speed. The writing
transaction raises the area's row in `cluster_epoch` and inserts the change into `cluster_change`;
every `web` and `worker` replica polls both tables every `cluster.epoch_poll_interval` on its
control connection. This requirement fixes the HA rules that mechanism MUST satisfy.

- **Delivery of a message is never a correctness condition.** Every cache that a change keeps
  fresh is self-validating or carries a maximum entry age; its owner sets the age, and this page
  requires one to exist (R-ARCH-018, ADR-031). The change-log poll applies every committed change
  within `cluster.epoch_poll_interval`, whatever Valkey does, and only the poll advances a
  replica's applied epoch of an area. A Valkey message only evicts early and never advances the
  applied epoch, so a lost, late, duplicated or forged message can neither suppress nor reorder a
  change.
- **Only committed changes are announced.** The change-log row commits with the change, and the
  Valkey message is published only after commit.
- **Valkey loss degrades, PostgreSQL loss gates.** While Valkey is unavailable, changes take effect
  at the next poll, typically within a second, and the replica stays ready (INV-12, Q-HA-13). A
  missing Valkey delivery only reports `valkey` as degraded (R-HA-008); it never fails a check that
  gates readiness. The `invalidation` readiness check of R-ARCH-018 passes while the last
  successful poll is younger than `cluster.epoch_max_staleness`. A replica that cannot poll the
  change log fails it after that, because it can then no longer bound how stale its revocations
  are; R-HA-008 debounces the check so that it never undercuts the `database` check.
- **No connection outside the main pool.** The poll runs on the replica's control connection, a
  reserved connection of the main class ([architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-019), so it
  works through a transaction-mode pooler (R-HA-058) and needs no session connection. A `web`
  replica therefore holds no PostgreSQL connection outside its main pool (R-HA-016). Behind a
  pooler, the control connection uses a server pool that request traffic cannot exhaust
  (Q-HA-20), so a saturated request pool cannot stall the poll.
- **Rolling upgrades.** Payloads are versioned. A replica that reads a payload version it does not
  know flushes the caches of that area instead of ignoring the row (R-HA-020: during a rolling
  upgrade, the newer release may write rows the older one cannot parse).
- **Failover and restore.** After a PostgreSQL failover that lost committed transactions
  (asynchronous replication, R-HA-013) or after a point-in-time restore, an area's epoch in
  PostgreSQL can be lower than the epoch a replica last applied, or later writes can already have
  raised it again to the same or a higher number, which then stands for different changes. The
  replica detects both: with its applied epoch it keeps the `changed_at` it read, which equals the
  `created_at` of the change row at that epoch, because both come from the writing transaction's
  `now()` ([architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-018, [authorization.md](authorization.md)
  R-AUTHZ-028, "A reused epoch"). An area whose epoch went backwards, whose epoch equals the
  applied one with a different `changed_at`, or whose change row at the applied epoch carries a
  different `created_at` MUST be flushed, and the replica takes the database's current epoch as its
  new starting point, so that later changes are not skipped as already applied. Two transactions
  separated by a failover never share that timestamp. A replica started after the restore starts
  from the current epochs anyway.
- Payloads stay below 1 KiB (R-ARCH-018). A change that touches many objects sends one "flush"
  entry per cache, not one entry per object.

Acceptance criteria:

- With Valkey's Pub/Sub connection of one replica killed (`CLIENT KILL TYPE pubsub`), a permission
  change made through another replica takes effect on it within `cluster.epoch_poll_interval` plus
  1 s, and `/readyz` keeps answering `200`.
- With Valkey stopped, a token revoked through one replica is rejected on every replica within
  `cluster.epoch_poll_interval` plus 1 s.
- A NetworkPolicy that denies one replica's egress to PostgreSQL makes it fail `invalidation` (and
  `database`) and leave the Service; after removal it applies every change it missed before it is
  ready again.
- A test lowers an area's epoch below the epochs the replicas have applied, as a failover with lost
  transactions would. Every replica flushes that area's caches, and the next change of the area
  takes effect on every replica.
- A test reuses an epoch: with Valkey stopped and one replica's poll paused by a test hook, it
  deletes the newest `cluster_change` row of an area, resets the area's `cluster_epoch` row to the
  previous epoch and `changed_at`, and commits a different change through another replica, which
  takes the same epoch number again. When the hook is lifted, the paused replica flushes the area
  (`quader_cache_flushes_total` rises) within `cluster.epoch_poll_interval` plus 1 s and serves the
  new change; a further change that raises the epoch above the reused one before the hook is
  lifted is detected the same way through the change row's `created_at`.

### R-HA-005 · Leader-less scheduling and job leases
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: HA-002, HA-007

Background work runs through the PostgreSQL job queue ([architecture.md](architecture.md) owns
the table and the worker loop). Schedules (cron expressions) belong to the subsystems that own the
work. This requirement fixes the HA guarantees both must give.

**Scheduling without a fixed leader.**

- One scheduler loop runs on each `worker` replica. Each tick (`jobs.schedule_tick`)
  tries to take the `scheduler` lease (an advisory-lock lease, R-HA-006). Only the holder enqueues
  due work. When the holder dies, its session ends, PostgreSQL releases the lock, and the next tick
  of another replica takes over. No replica is configured as scheduler.
- Enqueuing MUST also be safe without the lease. A due schedule is claimed with a conditional
  update in the same transaction that inserts the job:

  ```sql
  UPDATE schedule
     SET next_run_at = $next, last_enqueued_at = now()
   WHERE name = $1 AND enabled AND next_run_at <= now()
  RETURNING name;
  -- zero rows: another replica enqueued it first; do nothing
  ```

  Under READ COMMITTED, a second concurrent `UPDATE` waits for the first and re-evaluates the
  `WHERE` clause against the committed row, so the same occurrence is never enqueued twice, even if
  two replicas briefly both believe they hold the lease
  ([UPDATE under READ COMMITTED](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/transaction-iso.html#XACT-READ-COMMITTED)).
- The next due slot is computed from the task's cron expression and its last inserted slot
  (`job_task_slot`, Q-ARCH-29), not from the replica clock. Runs
  missed during an outage are coalesced into one run, never replayed one by one.

**Job leases.**

- A worker claims queued jobs with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` in a short transaction that sets
  `state = 'running'`, `locked_by` (the replica's `instance_uid`) and
  `locked_until = now() + jobs.lease_duration`, then commits. No transaction stays open while the
  job runs.
- The worker extends the lease every `jobs.heartbeat_interval`. A row that another replica has taken
  cancels the job's context at once. A failed extension (database unreachable) cancels it only once
  the lease could already have expired, measured on the worker's monotonic clock from its last
  confirmed extension (Q-HA-31). Until then the handler keeps running, so a database blip shorter
  than the lease does not cancel the work. A cancelled handler stops changing shared state for the job.
- A reaper (part of the scheduler tick) returns jobs whose `locked_until < now()` to `queued`. It does
  not increment `attempt`: the claim that starts the next attempt does. A job whose attempts are used
  up ends `failed` with `attempts_exhausted`.
- All lease and heartbeat timestamps use PostgreSQL's `now()`. Replica clocks never decide whether a
  lease has expired.
- During a rolling upgrade a worker claims only job kinds it implements (`WHERE kind = ANY($known)`,
  [architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-016). A kind whose arguments change incompatibly gets a
  new kind name, so older workers leave it to newer ones.

HA-relevant columns of the job table (sketch; [architecture.md](architecture.md) owns the full
definition):

```sql
CREATE TABLE job (                           -- excerpt; full definition in architecture.md R-ARCH-016
  id               uuid        PRIMARY KEY,
  kind             text        NOT NULL,
  state            job_state   NOT NULL DEFAULT 'queued',
  run_at           timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  attempt          integer     NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  max_attempts     integer     NOT NULL DEFAULT 10,
  locked_by        uuid,                       -- replica.instance_uid
  locked_until     timestamptz,                -- lease, extended by heartbeat
  checkpoint       jsonb                       -- persisted cursor of a restartable job
);
CREATE INDEX job_fetch ON job (queue, priority, run_at) WHERE state = 'queued';
CREATE INDEX job_lease ON job (locked_until) WHERE state IN ('running', 'cancelling');

-- No schedule table. Each task's slots are job rows; the unique index job_task_slot on
-- (task, scheduled_for) keeps one job per slot (architecture.md R-ARCH-016, Q-ARCH-29).
```

Configuration:

```yaml
jobs:                       # section owned by architecture.md (R-ARCH-016)
  schedule_tick: 10s        # default (proposed)
  lease_duration: 60s       # default (proposed); must be ≥ 3 × heartbeat_interval
  heartbeat_interval: 15s   # default (proposed)
```

Acceptance criteria:

- With three worker replicas and a schedule `* * * * *` for a test job that records its start, 60
  minutes produce exactly 60 runs, also while one replica is restarted every 5 minutes.
- `kubectl delete pod --grace-period=0 --force` of the replica that runs a long test job makes
  another replica run it again after at most `lease_duration` plus one tick; `attempt` is 2.
- Setting a replica's system clock 10 minutes ahead (test build with a fake clock) changes neither
  the number of runs nor any lease decision.

### R-HA-006 · Singleton work under advisory-lock leases with fencing
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: HA-007

Work that must not run twice at the same time (the scheduler tick, secret re-encryption,
background migrations) runs under an *advisory-lock lease* (INV-12). Two kinds of work are not on
this list:

- **Storage maintenance runs.** Garbage collection, the orphan sweep, retention runs, the scrub and
  remote-cache cleanup are kept apart by exclusive job keys in the job table
  ([architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-016), not by a lease; cap enforcement claims its
  outbox rows with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-044). Their safety
  rests on row locks and, for S3 deletes, on the hand-over rule of [storage.md](storage.md)
  R-STOR-024: two overlapping runs cannot delete a referenced blob, so exclusion is an efficiency
  property there ([storage.md](storage.md) Q-STOR-13). They write through the main pool and need no
  session connection.
- **Reindexing.** A manual reindex and an automatic index rebuild are jobs with the dedup key
  `index:<repository id>` (R-ARCH-016), which keeps two runs for one repository apart without a
  lease, because leases carry registered numbers only (R-ARCH-017).

A lease works as follows:

1. The worker takes a connection from the dedicated lease pool (`database.lease_pool_size`) and
   calls `pg_try_advisory_lock(<class>, <key>)`, a session-level lock
   ([advisory locks](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/explicit-locking.html#ADVISORY-LOCKS)).
   Failure to acquire means another replica holds the lease, so the worker skips the work.
2. **Fencing.** Every state change the singleton makes in PostgreSQL MUST be executed on that same
   session. The lease and the writes share one session. If the session has died, the lock is gone,
   *and* the write fails, so a replica that lost its lease cannot commit anything. Actions outside
   PostgreSQL happen only after the database change that authorizes them has committed on that
   session. (The S3 deletes of storage maintenance follow R-STOR-024's hand-over rule instead,
   because no database fence can stop a request that was already sent.)
3. The worker checks the session every `database.lease_check_interval` (`SELECT 1`). On failure it
   cancels the work, records the loss (`quader_lease_lost_total{task}`), and does not try to
   re-acquire in the same run. The next scheduled run starts fresh. All singleton jobs MUST be
   restartable from their persisted cursor.
4. A partitioned replica detects the loss of its session through TCP keepalive and user timeout
   (`database.keepalive.*`, R-HA-015) before the server releases the lock through its own keepalive
   (R-HA-013). Quader sends the server-side keepalive settings as startup parameters on every
   session that holds advisory locks (R-HA-015), so the server-side bound holds even where the
   server's own settings are left at the operating-system default. Client-side detection
   (default ≤ 30 s) is shorter than server-side release (default ≤ 120 s), and fencing (2) covers
   the remaining window. A *silent* holder, whose process stopped while its kernel keeps the
   connection (a paused container, a stopped process), answers every keepalive probe, so the
   keepalive never ends its session. The lease sessions therefore also carry
   `idle_session_timeout` at the same bound (`idle + interval × count` of
   `database.server_keepalive`, R-HA-015): the server ends a session that sent no statement for that
   long, and the lock with it. A live holder sends `SELECT 1` every `database.lease_check_interval`
   (3), and the configuration refuses a bound below three of those (Q-HA-127).
5. Session-level locks need a session that stays on one server connection, which
   transaction-mode and statement-mode poolers break. Only three things therefore connect to the
   *session host* (`database.session_host`, R-HA-058): the lease pool of `worker` replicas,
   `quader migrate` (the migration lock) and `quader backup` (the backup's snapshot and export
   connections, and the restore's writes). The session host is PostgreSQL directly, or a
   session-mode pooler such as PgBouncer with `pool_mode = session`. `web` replicas hold no
   coordination session and no session connection at all: their only class is the main pool,
   which MAY go through a transaction-mode pooler (Q-HA-6). A session connection that lands on a
   transaction-mode pooler is refused before its first use ([architecture.md](architecture.md)
   R-ARCH-017). That is a guard, not a proof; the supported setups are the ones named here.

**Lock key registry.** Every advisory lock uses the two-argument form with a registered category as
`classid`, as fixed by the registry of [architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-017, so `pg_locks`
names every lock (ADR-077). This page uses two of its categories and keeps the retired one listed:

| `classid` | Category | Key (`objid`) | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `lease` | registered lease number of the task (`internal/cluster/locks.go`; `scheduler` = 1) | singleton leases of this requirement and R-HA-005 |
| 2 | `fetch` (retired, reserved) | — | Nothing since 2026-10-28: the fetch lock lives in Valkey ([architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-033, [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-026). The number stays reserved and is never reused |
| 3 | `migration` | 0 | schema migration, exclusive (R-HA-019); the database phase of a backup, shared (R-HA-060) |

Configuration:

```yaml
database:
  lease_pool_size: 4        # default (proposed): concurrent singleton leases per replica
  lease_check_interval: 5s  # default (proposed)
```

Acceptance criteria:

- With the `scheduler` lease held by worker A,
  `SELECT classid, objid, pid FROM pg_locks WHERE locktype = 'advisory' AND classid = 1 AND objid = 1`
  shows one row; terminating that backend (`pg_terminate_backend`) stops A's scheduler tick within
  `lease_check_interval` + 1 s, A logs the lease loss (`quader_lease_lost_total{task="scheduler"}`
  rises), no further `schedule` update or job insert from A's scheduler appears, and another worker
  holds the lease within `cluster.lease_retry_interval` + 1 s.
- A fault-injection test blocks A's traffic to PostgreSQL (NetworkPolicy) while A holds the
  `scheduler` lease and a schedule `* * * * *` is due. A commits no `schedule` update and no job
  insert after its session is gone, B takes the lease after the server releases the session, and
  every minute's occurrence is enqueued exactly once.
- A holder falls silent with its connection open (its traffic relayed through a TCP relay that stops
  moving bytes and closing sockets): the server ends its session within `idle + interval × count` of
  `database.server_keepalive`, another worker holds the lease within that bound plus
  `cluster.lease_retry_interval`, and at no instant do two sessions hold it
  (`TestLeases_R_HA_006_FrozenHolder`).
- With three workers and no other singleton work running, a GC run and a retention run in progress
  hold no advisory lock of category 1 (`pg_locks` shows only the `scheduler` lease), and their job
  rows carry an exclusive dedup key (Q-STOR-13).

## Failure modes

### R-HA-007 · Failure-mode contract
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: HA-003, HA-004

Quader MUST behave as in this table. Each row is exercised by the failure-injection suite
(R-HA-052). "Client effect" assumes at least two replicas.

| Failure | Detection | Quader behavior | Client effect | Recovery |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Container crash (panic, OOM kill) | kubelet; session end releases locks | In-flight requests of that pod end; nothing half-committed (a `201` means durable, R-STOR-004); its job leases expire; its advisory locks are released immediately; its Valkey locks expire after their TTL | Requests on that pod fail with connection reset or `502` from the proxy; npm (`fetch-retries`) and NuGet clients retry | kubelet restarts the container; the spool directory is emptied at start (R-HA-012) |
| Pod eviction, node drain, rolling restart, autoscaler scale-down | `SIGTERM` | Drain (R-HA-011): readiness fails at once, in-flight requests finish within the grace period, jobs are released | None for requests shorter than the grace period; longer transfers are cut (tolerance in R-HA-059) | PDB keeps all but one replica per role serving (R-HA-032); the capacity rule of R-HA-059 keeps the rest from overload |
| Node loss (no `SIGTERM`) | Node controller marks the node not ready | Endpoints of the lost pods are removed when their Ready condition flips; job leases expire; advisory locks are released by the server's TCP keepalive, which Quader sets on its lock-holding sessions (R-HA-013, R-HA-015); Valkey locks expire | Requests routed to the lost pods fail until the endpoints are removed (tens of seconds) | Pods are recreated after `nodeFailureTolerationSeconds` of their role (R-HA-032) |
| Processes stopped with their connections open (a paused node or container, `SIGSTOP`) | Their kernel keeps answering TCP keepalives, so the keepalive sees nothing; the node controller marks a paused node not ready | Job leases expire; the server ends a lock-holding session after `idle + interval × count` of `database.server_keepalive` without a statement (`idle_session_timeout` of the lease sessions, R-HA-006, Q-HA-127), which releases its advisory locks; when the processes run again their lease sessions are gone, so they commit nothing under a lease | As for node loss while the node is marked not ready | Automatic; the pods come back with the node, or are replaced after `nodeFailureTolerationSeconds` |
| One replica cut off from PostgreSQL | `database` check (R-OPS-001) | That replica answers `503` and turns not ready once the cut has lasted the check threshold and `health.database_outage_grace` (Q-OPS-31); its singleton work stops (R-HA-006) | Traffic moves to the other replicas | Automatic when the network heals |
| PostgreSQL switchover or failover | Connection errors, SQLSTATE `57P01`, `25006`, class `08` | Retry with backoff within `database.retry.max_elapsed`, pool reset, the change-log poll resumes (an area whose epoch went backwards or was reused is flushed, R-HA-004), singleton work aborts and resumes on the next run (R-HA-009) | Requests stall for up to the retry budget, the wait for a pooled connection and the dial of a new one included; those that exceed it get `503` with `Retry-After` ([Q-HA-259](#q-ha-259--the-retry-budget-bounds-the-wait-for-a-pooled-connection)). Behind a transaction-mode pooler only with its `server_login_retry` of 1 s and its `server_connect_timeout` of 5 s (R-HA-058, Q-HA-302, Q-HA-371); with PgBouncer's default of 15 s for either a switchover can be the next row | Automatic |
| PostgreSQL unavailable beyond the retry budget | `database` check on every replica | Every replica answers `503` and turns not ready; liveness stays `200`, so nothing restarts; authorization decides nothing on a grant index unconfirmed for longer than `authz.cache.max_staleness` (10 s); such requests wait within the retry budget like database calls, then get `503` `authz_stale` ([authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-028, Q-AUTHZ-13) | `503` for everything (the Service has no ready endpoints) | Readiness returns when PostgreSQL does; no manual step |
| PostgreSQL connection limit reached (`53300`) | Connect error | Backoff and retry inside the budget; metric `quader_db_retries_total{kind="too_many_connections"}` | Latency, then `503` | Size the budget (R-HA-016) |
| PostgreSQL saturated: every request connection, or every server connection of the request pooler, busy | `quader_db_pool_acquire_duration_seconds`, alert `QuaderDatabasePoolSaturated` | Requests wait for a connection within their deadline; those that exceed it get `503` with `Retry-After`. The control connection keeps the change-log poll, the `database` check and the job heartbeats off the request pool: directly on its own backend, behind a pooler on a pool of its own (R-HA-008, Q-HA-20). Replicas stay ready and keep their jobs | Higher latency, some `503`; no replica leaves the Service because of the load | Scale the database, or lower the load |
| Instance of a transaction-mode pooler stopped or lost (request or control pooler, R-HA-058) | Connection errors of class `08` on the main pool | Retry with backoff (R-HA-009); the new connection reaches another instance of the same pooler through its Service; session-host connections are unaffected | A graceful stop that outlasts Quader's connection lifetime: none. A lost instance: only requests whose `COMMIT` was in flight get `503` with `Retry-After` | Automatic |
| Object storage unreachable from all replicas, for any duration (every connection; one of several unreachable is [storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-036's second table) | Circuit breaker (R-STOR-033), `objectStore` check, alert `QuaderObjectStoreUnreachable` | Behavior per [storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-036: new uploads `503`, downloads of stored content `503`, metadata, listings, deletes, deduplicated uploads and the API keep working. Running replicas stay ready (R-HA-008, Q-HA-1). A replica that starts during the outage stays not ready until its startup check (R-STOR-035) succeeds; it retries without exiting, so it becomes ready as soon as the store returns | Degraded: reads of metadata, the UI, logins and CI token exchange succeed; blob transfers fail with retryable `503` | Automatic; no blob is marked missing because of errors |
| Object storage unreachable from one replica only | Its circuit opens; peers' do not; alert `QuaderObjectStoreUnreachableSingleReplica` | That replica's blob requests fail fast with `503` and `Retry-After`; it stays ready | Blob requests that hit it fail; clients' retries are balanced by the edge proxy and usually reach another replica | Automatic when its network path heals; otherwise the responder deletes the pod |
| S3 throttling (`503 SlowDown`) | SDK retryer | Retries with backoff (R-STOR-033) | Higher latency | The content-addressed key layout spreads load across prefixes (R-HA-050) |
| S3 credentials fail (expired web identity, revoked key) | `InvalidAccessKeyId`, `SignatureDoesNotMatch`, `ExpiredToken` and the other answers that name the credential, or a refresh error; a plain `AccessDenied` for one operation is an answer about the request and does not count ([Q-HA-254](#q-ha-254--a-store-answer-that-rejects-the-credential-counts-against-the-object-store-circuit)) | Counted as object-store failure: the circuit opens after `failure_threshold` of them; one `WARN` line when it opens, with the credential source and the store's code, never the secret | As the outage rows | Fix the credential; static key files are re-read (R-STOR-031) |
| Valkey primary lost or switched over (Sentinel failover) | Command errors, timeouts, `READONLY`, closed connections; Sentinel's `switch-master` event as an early hint | Each Valkey use falls back for that call (R-HA-057); the client re-resolves the primary through Sentinel and checks its `ROLE` (R-HA-056); after `valkey.circuit_breaker.failure_threshold` failures the circuit skips Valkey for `open_duration`; replicas stay ready (Q-HA-13); a replica that starts during the failover holds its first readiness until the new primary answers, at most `valkey.startup_answer_timeout` (Q-HA-293) | None; latency rises; a concurrent cache miss may be fetched upstream once per replica instead of once | Automatic, within Sentinel's `down-after-milliseconds` plus the failover and one reconnect backoff; when the election of the remaining Sentinels is split (two Sentinels left after a drain or a node loss), Sentinel starts the next automatic failover only after twice `failover-timeout` (2 minutes at the default), and Quader runs degraded until then or until the primary returns (R-HA-057) |
| Sentinel quorum lost (fewer than a majority of Sentinels reachable) | Sentinel queries fail or time out; `quader_valkey_sentinels_reachable`, the number of configured Sentinels that answered the last probe of all of them (R-HA-056 step 4, R-HA-057) | Existing connections to the primary keep working; a reconnect needs one reachable Sentinel; no failover can happen meanwhile | None while the primary is healthy; if the primary fails too, as the next row | Restore the Sentinels; alert `QuaderValkeySentinelsDegraded` |
| Valkey unavailable for every replica, for any duration | Circuit open on every replica, `valkey` check, alert `QuaderValkeyUnavailable` | Degraded mode (R-HA-057): fetch collapse and negative caching per replica, rate limits approximated per replica, changes applied at the next change-log poll (R-HA-004); replicas stay ready; a replica started during the outage becomes ready degraded once `valkey.startup_answer_timeout` (30 s) has passed without an answer (Q-HA-13, Q-HA-293) | None; upstream load rises, changes take up to `cluster.epoch_poll_interval` | Automatic; nothing to repair in Valkey |
| Valkey unreachable from one replica only | Its circuit opens; peers' do not; alert `QuaderValkeyUnavailableSingleReplica` | That replica runs in degraded mode; it stays ready | None | Automatic when its path heals; otherwise the responder deletes the pod |
| Valkey content lost (flush, restart without persistence, a failover that drops writes not yet replicated) | Not detected, and not needed | A lost fetch lock causes a duplicate upstream fetch, which content addressing makes harmless (INV-11); negative-cache entries are fetched again; rate-limit counters restart; an entry that an older primary brings back is ignored when a newer invalidation covers it (R-ARCH-030) | None | Automatic |
| Valkey rejects Quader's credentials or certificate (rotation mistake) | `WRONGPASS`, `NOAUTH`, `NOPERM`, TLS verification error | Running replicas: as "Valkey unavailable". New replicas: not ready until fixed, because a configuration error gates the first readiness (Q-HA-13); a new replica waits up to `valkey.startup_answer_timeout` for that answer, so a rollout stalls instead of degrading every replica also when its first attempts get no answer (Q-HA-293) | None from running replicas | Fix the Secret or the Valkey user |
| Backup pod evicted, crashed or cut off during a run | Pod failure; Job controller | A drain eviction is not counted against `backoffLimit` (R-HA-060); the Job starts a new pod; an incomplete run is never listed as a backup ([backup-and-restore.md](backup-and-restore.md)) | None; serving replicas are not involved | Automatic; `QuaderBackupFailed` when a run ends `failed` or `abandoned` (an `interrupted` run does not count), `QuaderBackupStale` when no run succeeds within 1.5 × `backup.expected_interval` (R-HA-045) |
| Restore pod evicted, crashed or cut off during a restore | Pod failure; Job controller | A drain eviction is not counted against `restore.backoffLimit`; the Job's next pod resumes from the restore anchor ([backup-and-restore.md](backup-and-restore.md) R-BAK-021); `quader migrate` refuses the anchored database meanwhile (R-HA-019) | None beyond the restore's own downtime; both roles are at zero | Automatic; a Job that failed for good is deleted and created again (R-HA-060) |
| Spool volume full | Spool budget (R-STOR-004) | New uploads `503` with `Retry-After`; uploads larger than the whole budget `413` | Retry succeeds when space frees | R-HA-035 sizing |
| Migration Job fails | Helm sees the hook Job fail | Old pods keep running on the unchanged or expanded schema; new pods are never created (pre-upgrade runs before the new manifests are applied) | None | Fix the cause, re-run `helm upgrade` (R-HA-019) |
| Encryption key set differs on a new replica | Startup check (R-HA-027) | The new replica refuses to start | None (old replicas keep serving; the rollout stalls) | Fix the Secret |
| OIDC provider unreachable | Login fails | Browser logins fail; sessions, PATs, service-account and CI tokens keep working, because Quader validates its own tokens (INV-8) | Only new browser logins fail | Automatic |
| GitLab JWKS unreachable | Exchange fails or uses cached keys | Per [gitlab-ci-oidc.md](gitlab-ci-oidc.md) | CI token exchange may fail | Automatic |
| Upstream registry unreachable | Upstream circuit | Stale metadata is served (INV-11, [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md)) | Cached content keeps working | Automatic |
| Edge proxy pod loss | Platform | Not Quader's; the controller must run highly available | Depends on the controller | Platform |

Acceptance criteria: every row is a scenario of R-HA-052 with the stated client effect as its pass
condition.

### R-HA-008 · Readiness and liveness under dependency failure
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: HA-023

R-OPS-001 defines the probe endpoints and the check list. This requirement fixes the HA rules that
the check thresholds and the chart's probe settings (R-HA-034) must satisfy together.

- Liveness MUST NOT depend on PostgreSQL, object storage, the OIDC provider or any upstream. A
  dependency outage must never restart replicas, because restarts do not repair a shared
  dependency and they discard warm caches and in-flight work. The chart's liveness probe uses
  `/healthz` only.
- Readiness MUST become false within about 15 s (`health.check_interval` × `health.failure_threshold`
  + one probe period) when the replica cannot reach PostgreSQL, and MUST become true again without
  a restart.
- Readiness and the retry budget interact. During a PostgreSQL switchover shorter than the
  readiness window, replicas stay ready and requests ride out the switchover in their retry loop
  (R-HA-009). A longer outage removes all replicas from the Service, so the edge proxy answers
  `503` at once instead of letting requests queue.
- Object storage gates readiness only until a replica is ready for the first time (Q-HA-1). A
  replica becomes ready only after its object-store startup check (R-STOR-035,
  `storage.object_store.startup_check: true`, per connection, storage.md R-STOR-060) has passed, so a release with a wrong bucket, endpoint,
  credential or CA never replaces working pods: the rollout stalls with `maxUnavailable: 0`.
  After that, the `objectStore` check keeps running and is reported (verbose `/readyz`, the
  replica registry, metrics), but its failure MUST NOT make the replica unready. Blob requests
  degrade one by one through the circuit breaker (R-STOR-033, R-STOR-036), and the two alerts of
  R-HA-045 tell a shared outage from a single replica's problem.
- `health.require_object_store` defaults to `false` and implements this rule. `true` makes the
  `objectStore` check gate readiness continuously, debounced by R-OPS-001's
  `health.failure_threshold` and `health.success_threshold`. It is meant for an installation behind
  an outer load balancer that can fail over to a second installation. The chart passes
  `config.health.require_object_store` through unchanged.
- **Valkey never gates readiness after the first one** (INV-12, Q-HA-13). The `valkey` check runs
  every `valkey.health_check_interval` and is reported in verbose `/readyz`
  (`"degraded":["valkey"]`), in the replica registry and as `quader_valkey_available`. Before a
  replica is ready for the first time, two things hold it back:
  - **Valkey's first answer, for a bounded time** (the owner's decision
    [Q-HA-293](#q-ha-293--a-replica-waits-for-valkeys-first-answer-before-its-first-readiness-for-a-bounded-time)).
    The last start step waits until Valkey has answered a connection attempt once, accepted or
    refused, or until `valkey.startup_answer_timeout` (default 30 s, [Q-HA-332](#q-ha-332--the-bound-is-the-setting-valkeystartup_answer_timeout-30-s-by-default))
    has passed since the client started; meanwhile `/readyz` fails with the `startup` check's reason
    `waiting_for_valkey` ([Q-HA-330](#q-ha-330--step-10-waits-for-valkeys-first-answer-and-the-startup-check-names-the-wait)).
    What an answer is and what is silence is [Q-HA-331](#q-ha-331--an-answer-is-the-login-or-its-refusal-and-the-first-connection-also-writes-the-probe-key-and-runs-the-take-script).
    A start during an ordinary failover gets its answer inside the bound; a Valkey that stays
    silent longer lets the replica become ready in degraded mode at the bound, and the log names
    the bound and the reason, so the autoscaler and a drain can still add capacity.
  - **A configuration error found by that answer:** Valkey or a Sentinel rejects the credentials
    (`WRONGPASS`, `NOAUTH`, an ACL denial `NOPERM`, also for the probe write and the take script of
    the first connection), TLS verification fails, or every reachable Sentinel answers that it does
    not know `valkey.sentinel.primary_name`. The replica stays unready, does not exit, keeps
    retrying, and becomes ready once a later attempt is accepted.

  A rollout with a mistyped Valkey setting or a wrong ACL therefore stalls with `maxUnavailable: 0`
  instead of degrading every replica, unless Valkey stayed silent to the new pod for the whole bound.
- **Load never fails a check.** The `database` check ([operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md)
  R-OPS-001) and the change-log poll behind the `invalidation` check run on the replica's control
  connection ([architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-019), never on the request pool. A request
  pool that is exhausted under load therefore makes requests wait or fail with `503`, but never
  takes replicas out of the Service one after another, which would push their load onto the rest
  and turn overload into an outage. Behind a transaction-mode pooler, the control connection uses
  a server pool of its own for the same reason (R-HA-058, Q-HA-20).
- **A switchover does not empty the Service.** The `database` and `schema` checks tolerate a
  PostgreSQL outage shorter than `health.database_outage_grace` (default 20 s, always below
  `database.retry.max_elapsed`) once a replica has been ready, and show `degraded` meanwhile
  ([operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-001, Q-OPS-31). A
  CloudNativePG switchover of up to 15 s therefore never flips readiness, while an outage of 30 s
  does, about 20 to 25 s in.
- **No check undercuts the PostgreSQL window.** The `invalidation` check of
  [architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-018 also depends on PostgreSQL, through the change-log
  poll. It MUST NOT turn a replica unready sooner than the `database` check does. Its evaluations
  start failing only once the poll has been stale for `cluster.epoch_max_staleness` (default 5 s),
  and it is debounced with the same thresholds as `database` (`health.failure_threshold`,
  `health.success_threshold`, [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md)
  R-OPS-001). For one outage, `invalidation` therefore turns a replica unready no earlier than
  `database`, which keeps architecture.md's 5 s default. Otherwise a switchover of a few seconds
  would empty the Service through `invalidation`, although requests ride it out in their retry loop
  (R-HA-009). Raising `cluster.epoch_max_staleness` to the readiness window (about 15 s) would be
  the alternative, at the cost of a slower readiness signal for a replica cut off from the change
  log. Code paths that must fail closed sooner, such as authorization
  ([authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-028), read the change-log freshness directly
  instead of relying on readiness.
- A replica whose schema is behind its `requiredSchema` (R-HA-018) stays not ready and logs the
  required schema version once per minute. It does not exit, so the rollout stalls visibly with
  `maxUnavailable: 0` (R-HA-020) instead of crash-looping, and the replica becomes ready as soon as
  the migration has run. A binary older than `compat_floor` can never serve against that schema and
  exits instead ([architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-026).
- Because a PostgreSQL outage (and, with `health.require_object_store: true`, an object-storage
  outage) makes every replica unready at once, the PodDisruptionBudget uses
  `unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy: AlwaysAllow` (R-HA-032). Otherwise a node drain during the outage
  would be blocked, since the default policy treats unready pods as already disrupted
  ([PDB unhealthy pod eviction policy](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/run-application/configure-pdb/#unhealthy-pod-eviction-policy),
  stable since Kubernetes 1.31).

Acceptance criteria:

- With a NetworkPolicy that denies egress to PostgreSQL applied to all pods for 3 minutes, no
  container restarts (`kubectl get pods` restart count unchanged), every `/readyz` answers `503`,
  and all pods return to ready within 15 s after removal.
- With that policy applied, `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`
  evicts the Quader pod on that node instead of waiting.
- A replica whose Valkey does not answer at its start answers `/readyz` with `503` and the
  `startup` reason `waiting_for_valkey` until Valkey answers or `valkey.startup_answer_timeout` has
  passed. An answer ends the wait at once: ready, or unready with the `valkey` check's configuration
  error when it was a refusal; the bound ends it with `200` and `"degraded":["valkey"]` and a WARN
  line that names the bound and the reason. A replica that has been ready never waits for Valkey
  again: a later loss leaves it ready and degraded.
- A test endpoint of the test build holds every request connection of every `web` replica in
  `SELECT pg_sleep(4)` transactions for 60 s, once with direct connections and once with the
  pooler profile (R-HA-058), where it also occupies every server connection of the request pooler.
  `/readyz` answers `200` on every replica throughout, and no `worker` job returns to `queued`
  because a heartbeat was late.

### R-HA-009 · PostgreSQL failover: reconnect and retry
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: HA-064

The pgx driver ([pgconn](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgconn),
[pgxpool](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgxpool)) does not retry statements itself.
Quader MUST implement the following.

**Finding the primary.**

- `database.host` MAY list several hosts separated by commas (libpq style; pgx tries them in
  order). With `database.target_session_attrs: read-write` (default) a connection is accepted only by
  a server that accepts writes, so a demoted former primary is skipped.
- With CloudNativePG the single host is the cluster's read-write Service
  ([service management](https://cloudnative-pg.io/docs/1.30/service_management)), which always
  points at the current primary. With Amazon RDS it is the instance or cluster endpoint whose DNS
  record moves on failover. Go's resolver does not cache DNS answers, so each new connection
  resolves the name again.
- With a transaction-mode pooler (R-HA-058), `database.host` names the pooler, and the pooler
  follows the primary. A failover then reaches Quader as errors on pooled connections (class `08`,
  `25006` from a server connection that the pooler opened before the switch), which the table below
  retries. The session host follows the rules above.

**Detecting dead connections.**

- The dialer MUST enable TCP keepalive (`database.keepalive.idle`, `interval`, `count`) and, on
  Linux, `TCP_USER_TIMEOUT` (`database.keepalive.user_timeout`), so a connection to a vanished
  server (node loss, no RST) fails within about 30 s instead of the operating system default of
  hours.
- Every statement runs with a context deadline (request deadline or `database.session.statement_timeout`).

**Retry classification.** A whole transaction is the unit of retry. Transaction bodies MUST be
written as functions that can run again from the start: no side effects outside PostgreSQL inside
the function. S3 writes happen before the transaction and are idempotent by content address
(R-STOR-005).

| Error | Retry? | Extra action |
|---|---|---|
| Error before anything was sent (`pgconn.SafeToRetry`) | yes | — |
| Connection failure while acquiring or dialing, SQLSTATE class `08` | yes | — |
| `57P01` admin_shutdown, `57P02` crash_shutdown, `57P03` cannot_connect_now | yes | Discard the connection |
| `25006` read_only_sql_transaction | yes | Discard all pooled connections: the pool reached a demoted primary |
| `40001` serialization_failure, `40P01` deadlock_detected | yes | — |
| `53300` too_many_connections | yes, with the backoff | Metric |
| Connection lost after `COMMIT` was sent | no (outcome unknown) | Answer `503` with `Retry-After`; see below |
| Anything else | no | — |

- Backoff: exponential from `database.retry.initial_backoff` to `database.retry.max_backoff` with
  full jitter, bounded by `database.retry.max_elapsed` and by the request's own deadline.
- **Unknown commit outcome.** When the connection drops after `COMMIT` was sent, the transaction
  may or may not have committed. Quader MUST NOT retry it blindly. Writes that a client may
  repeat MUST be idempotent at the protocol level: re-uploading identical content to the same path
  is a no-op success (R-STOR-005, overwrite rule). So the client's own retry after the `503` is
  safe. Format pages decide how a repeated publish of an existing version answers when the content
  is identical.
- Background jobs retry through their own attempt counter (R-HA-005) in addition to the per
  transaction retry.

**After a failover.**

- The change-log poll resumes on the control connection, a reserved connection of the main class.
  An area whose epoch went backwards because the failover lost committed transactions, or whose
  epoch number was reused by later writes, is flushed (R-HA-004).
- Singleton leases are lost with their sessions. The work aborts and resumes from its cursor on the
  next scheduled run (R-HA-006).
- The pool refills on demand. `database.pool.min_conns` connections are re-established in the
  background.

Configuration:

```yaml
database:
  target_session_attrs: read-write # default (proposed): read-write | primary | any
  retry:
    initial_backoff: 100ms         # default (proposed)
    max_backoff: 2s                # default (proposed)
    max_elapsed: 30s               # default (proposed); request deadlines may cut it shorter
  keepalive:
    idle: 15s                      # default (proposed)
    interval: 5s                   # default (proposed)
    count: 3                       # default (proposed)
    user_timeout: 30s              # default (proposed); Linux TCP_USER_TIMEOUT
```

Metrics (R-OPS-007 conventions): `quader_db_retries_total{kind}` with `kind` in `connection`,
`shutdown`, `read_only`, `serialization`, `too_many_connections`;
`quader_db_pool_resets_total`; `quader_db_commit_unknown_total`.

Acceptance criteria:

- Two replicas, CloudNativePG with two instances. While a loop runs `npm ci` (npm's default
  `fetch-retries`) and `dotnet restore --no-cache` against Quader, `kubectl cnpg promote quader-db 2`
  ([kubectl plugin](https://cloudnative-pg.io/docs/1.30/kubectl-plugin)) completes. No client
  iteration fails, and `quader_db_retries_total` increases.
- `kubectl delete pod quader-db-1 --grace-period=0 --force` (unplanned failover of the primary):
  at most the requests in flight during the first `retry.maxElapsed` fail, all with `503` and
  `Retry-After`; the next loop iteration succeeds.
- A unit test with an injected connection drop after `COMMIT` returns `503` and does not run the
  transaction function a second time.

### R-HA-010 · Object-storage outage
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: HA-004

[storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-036 is the normative table for every operation during an
object-storage outage, and R-STOR-033 specifies the per-replica circuit breaker. On top of that,
this page requires the following:

- An upload that sends `Expect: 100-continue` and is rejected because the circuit is open MUST be
  rejected *before* the body is read, after authentication and authorization (`503` with `Retry-After`), so clients that send it
  (`dotnet nuget push`, `curl -T`) do not transfer the body at all. A write without `Expect` is read
  and a deduplicated upload succeeds ([Q-STOR-149](storage.md#q-stor-149--an-upload-that-waits-for-100-continue-is-refused-before-its-body-while-the-circuit-is-open)).
- `Retry-After` on these `503` responses is `storage.object_store.circuit_breaker.open_duration` rounded up to
  whole seconds, at least 5.
- The circuit state is a per-replica gauge (`quader_storage_s3_circuit_open`). The chart's alert
  rules distinguish a shared outage (all replicas open) from a single replica's network problem
  (one replica open), because the two need different responders (R-HA-045).
- While the circuit is open, garbage collection and the orphan sweep pause their S3 phase. This is
  already required by R-STOR-036, and it means an outage never turns into lost blobs.

Acceptance criteria (in addition to R-STOR-036's):

- With the local profile's S3 store scaled to 0 for 5 minutes during an `npm ci` loop against a
  virtual repository whose tarballs are cached: `npm view <pkg> versions` keeps succeeding for the
  whole period, every replica's `/readyz` keeps answering `200`, while
  `curl -T big.bin https://quader.example.com/files/web/generic-local/x.bin -H 'Expect: 100-continue'`
  receives `503` without sending the body. Within `storage.object_store.circuit_breaker.open_duration`
  plus 10 s of the store returning, both work.
- A pod deleted during that outage is replaced, and the replacement stays not ready until the store
  returns. Its container restart count stays unchanged throughout, because the startup check
  retries transient errors without exiting (R-STOR-035), and it becomes ready within 60 s after the
  store returns.
- The alert `QuaderObjectStoreUnreachable` fires during the outage, and
  `QuaderObjectStoreUnreachableSingleReplica` does not.

### R-HA-011 · Graceful termination and connection draining
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: HA-047

On `SIGTERM` a replica follows R-OPS-001: it fails readiness at once, keeps serving for
`health.shutdown_drain_delay` so every proxy notices the endpoint removal, then stops accepting
connections and waits for in-flight requests. This page fixes the time budget and what happens to
background work.

- The chart sets `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` per role (default 120 s for `web`, 300 s for
  `worker`, 60 s for each scanner, `vuln-scanner-trivy` and `malware-scanner-clamav`). The server shutdown timeout ([architecture.md](architecture.md)) MUST be derived
  from it: `server.shutdown_timeout = terminationGracePeriodSeconds − health.shutdown_drain_delay − 5 s`.
  The chart passes the grace period to the process as `QUADER_RUNTIME_TERMINATION_GRACE_PERIOD`, so
  the two cannot drift apart. The process exits before the kubelet's `SIGKILL`.
- No `preStop` hook is needed or rendered. The delay is implemented in the process, because the
  image contains no shell or `sleep` binary.
- Responses completed during the drain carry `Connection: close`, so clients reconnect through the
  Service to a remaining replica.
- Workers stop claiming jobs at `SIGTERM`. Running jobs get the shutdown timeout to finish or to
  persist their cursor; a job's call to a scanner is cancelled with its handler (R-VULN-041). A scanner admits no new analysis at
  `SIGTERM` (`503` `scanner_draining`) and kills an analysis still running at its shutdown timeout, answering it `503`
  `scanner_draining`, which the worker puts off without an attempt (R-HA-065). A handler still running 11 s before the deadline is cancelled and its job
  lease released explicitly (`state = 'queued'`, `attempt` unchanged): the release write has the
  whole settle deadline of the worker, 15 s with its retries, before the process stops waiting for
  it ([architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-024 step 4, Q-ARCH-329), so a release during a
  PostgreSQL switchover is not left to the lease's expiry and the reaper. The advisory-lock
  sessions are closed at the end. A handler that is only waiting when the shutdown begins (for time
  to pass, not for work of its own) gives its job up at `SIGTERM` and the job is released at once
  ([architecture.md](architecture.md) Q-ARCH-501); the settle wait of a garbage collection run is
  one ([storage.md](storage.md) Q-STOR-217).
- The two writes a stopping replica makes to its registry row, the mark `draining` and the final
  deletion, are retried within their step instead of tried once: a switchover of the primary ends
  every connection for some seconds. The deletion retries for at most 15 s and never past the close
  deadline, so it cannot take the exit deadline either
  ([Q-HA-307](#q-ha-307--the-registry-rows-shutdown-writes-are-retried-within-their-step)).
- A fetch that the replica leads for other waiters (R-REPO-026) finishes within the shutdown timeout
  or is abandoned; either way the replica releases its Valkey fetch lock explicitly (delete only if
  the lock still carries this replica's token), so waiters on other replicas take over at once
  instead of after the lock's TTL. From `SIGTERM` on, the replica holds no new cross-replica
  flight; a request on it joins a flight held elsewhere or fetches under its in-process
  single-flight only ([repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-026, Q-REPO-7).
- Leases are released explicitly, and the lease connections, the Valkey connections and the pools
  are closed last (R-ARCH-024). One exception: the `scheduler` lease is released at `SIGTERM`
  ([operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-001 shutdown step 1,
  R-OPS-019), not after the running jobs, so a worker drain hands over scheduling within
