4. **Run `quader admin post-restore --restored-to <t>`** as a one-off pod with the release's
   configuration (`kubectl run … -- quader admin post-restore …`, or
   `helm upgrade … --set postRestore.enabled=true`, which renders a hook Job; the chart refuses that upgrade while any
   role has replicas, as it does for `restore.enabled`). Its first transaction commits the marker
   `system_state.post_restore_in_progress`, which fails the schema check of every replica (running or started later) as
   `restore_in_progress` does, and its last transaction deletes the marker, after the replay and `system.restored`
   (Q-HA-157). It:
   - deletes all rows of `replica` (they describe pods that no longer exist);
   - returns every `running` job to `queued` without incrementing `attempt`;
   - sets the deletion pause (below), so GC and the orphan sweep delete nothing until an operator
     resumes them;
   - ends every UI session (`quader admin sessions end --all`, R-AUTH-015);
   - runs two fix-ups of [backup-and-restore.md](backup-and-restore.md) R-BAK-022 in one
     transaction: a new random `system_state.keyspace_id`, so that no replica reads a lock,
     negative-cache entry or counter written after *t* (R-HA-057, rule 7), and the offset of 2^32
     on every column registered with `meta.RegisterRevisionColumn` (`packages.rev_seq`,
     `repositories.config_version`, `cluster_epoch.epoch` and the others R-BAK-022 lists). A PITR
     brings back the old keyspace ID and the old revision counters exactly as a backup restore
     does. A Valkey flush instead would leave the revision counters uncovered: a client holding an
     `ETag` from after *t* would get `304` for different content, and an `If-Match` would match it;
   - sets the `system_state` key `restored_at` to the current time; single-use CI issuers refuse
     subject tokens issued up to `clock_skew` after it ([gitlab-ci-oidc.md](gitlab-ci-oidc.md)
     R-CI-018);
   - runs `quader admin storage verify` over every live blob (no `--since`, Q-HA-213) and prints the
     number of referenced blobs whose objects are missing;
   - re-applies the revocation journal entries newer than *t* (R-HA-054) and prints one line per
     entry, including every object it suspended;
   - writes the audit event `system.restored` with *t*, records *t* in `system_state.post_restore_done` and deletes the
     marker; a run for a *t* that is recorded changes nothing (no session ends, no revision offset, no new keyspace), a
     run after a failed one with the same *t* resumes at the replay, and a run for another *t* while one is unfinished
     is refused (Q-HA-157);
   - prints a reminder that access granted after *t* is gone and that revocations newer than the
     last shipped journal entry are undone (H-37).
5. **Repair missing blobs** if step 4 reported any and the bucket is versioned:
   `quader admin storage restore-versions --before <t>` removes the delete markers younger than *t* from the keys of the
   referenced blobs whose object is missing, on each connection or the one `--connection` names (it runs the check of
   `quader admin storage verify` over every present copy first, [storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-058),
   so that the version before the marker is current again. It prints one line per such blob and a totals line, and exits 5 while
   a blob is still without an object (no delete marker younger than *t*, or no object version below its markers). `--dry-run`
   lists what it would do and removes nothing. This needs a separate credential with `s3:ListBucketVersions` and
   `s3:DeleteObjectVersion`, passed only to this command (`--credentials-file`, the file of `post-restore`). The runtime
   credential deliberately lacks these permissions (R-HA-023). A run that removed markers writes the audit event
   `system.storage.versions_restored`.
6. **Start.** `helm upgrade` with the normal values, which also resumes the backup CronJob. The
   migration Job brings an older restored schema forward.
7. **Resume deletions** after verification: `quader admin maintenance resume-deletions`. It clears the pause, prints when and why
   it had been set, and writes the audit event `system.deletions_resumed`; a repeat says that nothing changed and exits 0.

Deletion pause (sketch; `system_state` is defined in R-OPS-024):

```sql
ALTER TABLE system_state
  ADD COLUMN deletions_paused_at     timestamptz,
  ADD COLUMN deletions_paused_reason text;
```

- GC, the orphan sweep, retention runs, cap enforcement ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-044) and
  remote-cache cleanup (R-STOR-045) MUST check the pause before every batch of deletions, and skip
  the batch while it is set. A paused collection or sweep run ends with `result.paused: true`; a
  paused retention run ends `stopped` with `error.code = deletions_paused`; cap enforcement claims
  nothing while the pause is set (R-STOR-024, R-STOR-026, R-STOR-040, R-STOR-044, R-STOR-045).
- `quader admin maintenance pause-deletions --reason …` sets the pause by hand, for example
  before a planned restore drill. A pause that is already set keeps its time and reason; a change writes the audit event
  `system.deletions_paused`.

Acceptance criteria (point-in-time restore drill, part of R-HA-052, run weekly in CI):

- Steps 1–7 against the local profile restore a database to *t* = 10 minutes ago.
  - `npm view` shows exactly the versions published before *t*.
  - A package published after *t* is absent, and its object is not deleted while the pause is set.
  - After `resume-deletions` and an orphan sweep with the test `min_age`, that object is removed.
  - A token revoked after *t* is rejected after step 4 (R-HA-054). With
    `backup.revocation_journal.enabled: false` it works again, which documents H-37.
  - After step 4, `system_state.keyspace_id` differs from its value before the restore, and the
    replicas write only keys of the new keyspace.
  - An npm client that fetched a package document after *t* from the old database keeps its
    `ETag`; after the restore and one publish to the same package, the same conditional request
    answers `200`, not `304` (revision offset of R-BAK-022).

### R-HA-026 · Cross-site disaster recovery
Priority: **P1** · Covers: OPS-033

- **Topology.** The primary site runs Quader. The recovery site keeps:
  - a CloudNativePG replica cluster fed from the primary's WAL archive or by streaming
    ([replica clusters](https://cloudnative-pg.io/docs/1.30/replica_cluster)), or a managed
    cross-region read replica;
  - a bucket filled by one-way replication of the blob bucket
    ([S3 replication](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication.html)), or, simpler and independent of the
    store's features, a connection of the installation at the recovery site, which Quader's reconciliation fills
    ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-050, R-STOR-056; [Q-HA-392](#q-ha-392--a-connection-at-the-recovery-site-is-the-second-way-to-a-second-site));
    a bucket that the store replicates is never itself a connection (R-STOR-035 A4);
  - an installed Helm release with both roles at replica count 0, the backup CronJob suspended,
    the same encryption key Secret, and values that differ only in database host, bucket, region
    and Valkey addresses;
  - a Valkey with Sentinel of its own (R-HA-056). Nothing is replicated into it: its content is
    ephemeral (INV-3), and the recovery site starts with an empty keyspace.

  Active-active operation across sites is not supported. R-STOR-035 assumption A4 allows one
  installation per location, and federation is Later. With a connection at the recovery site the release
  there lists the same connections with the recovery site's first, and its RPO for blobs is the
  reconciliation's queue age instead of the bucket replication's lag.
- **Replicate deletes or not.** Delete-marker replication SHOULD be off. The recovery bucket then
  only grows, and a GC delete on the primary can never remove an object that the (lagging) replica
  database still references. After a failover, the orphan sweep at the recovery site removes the
  surplus.
- **Failover.**
  1. Promote the replica cluster.
  2. Move the DNS name of `server.base_url` to the recovery site's edge. Keeping the same base URL
     keeps clients' configuration, tokens and every URL embedded in cached metadata valid.
  3. Run `quader admin post-restore --restored-to <last replayed transaction time>` while both roles
     are still at zero. It pauses deletions, reports blobs whose objects have not arrived yet and
     gives the installation a new keyspace ID (R-HA-025 step 4).
  4. Scale both roles up, and resume the backup CronJob with a target at the recovery site.

  The order matters: a replica reads the keyspace ID once, at start-up, after any restore has
  finished ([architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-030, R-ARCH-024), so replicas started before
  `post-restore` would keep the old keyspace until they restart. Operators who scaled up first
  restart both roles after `post-restore` (`kubectl rollout restart`). The CI restore cut-off
  `restored_at` does not depend on the order, because the token exchange reads it in its own
  transaction ([gitlab-ci-oidc.md](gitlab-ci-oidc.md) R-CI-018).
- The Quader backups of R-HA-060 are a second way back when both the database replica and the
  bucket replica are unusable: their target SHOULD be in a third location, or at least not at the
  primary site.
- **Replication lag.** The database replica can be ahead of bucket replication. A blob committed on
  the primary shortly before the disaster may be referenced but not yet copied. Its reads answer
  `503` (R-HA-024) until the object arrives, if it ever does. Remote-repository content heals by
  re-fetching. Local content written in the lag window is lost if the primary site's bucket is lost
  too. AWS S3 Replication Time Control bounds that window.
- **Recovery point and time:**
  - RPO = max(database replication lag, bucket replication lag);
  - RTO = promotion + DNS TTL + pod start + post-restore, typically minutes.

  Both are measured in the drill, not promised.

Acceptance criteria:

- Drill in CI with two kind clusters (two "sites"): fail over while an `npm publish` loop runs.
  - Every package acknowledged at least `max lag` before the cut-off installs at the recovery site.
  - Packages in the lag window either install or answer `503`, never `404`.
  - Measured RPO and RTO are reported.

### R-HA-027 · Encryption keys for sealed secrets in a replicated deployment
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: HA-016, HA-031

Secrets stored in PostgreSQL (upstream credentials, webhook secrets, …) are sealed with AES-256-GCM
under the key ring of [architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-021: `secrets.encryption_key_files`
lists the key files, the file name without `.key` is the key ID, `secrets.active_key_id` names the
sealing key, and the `secret_key_canary` table stops a replica whose ring cannot open a key ID that
sealed rows still reference. This requirement covers what HA and the chart add:

- **Same keys on every replica.** All Deployments, the migration Job and the restore Job mount the
  same Secret (`secrets.encryption.existingSecret`). The backup CronJob does not mount it
  (R-HA-060). `secrets.encryption.keys` is the ordered list of key files
  of that Secret. The chart renders `secrets.encryption_key_files` from the whole list and
  `secrets.active_key_id` from the first entry.
- **Never generated by the chart.** The chart MUST NOT create the key. It fails rendering when no
  Secret is named (R-HA-029). A key generated at install time is lost or regenerated on the next
  render wherever Helm's `lookup` is unavailable (`helm template`, Argo CD). A regenerated key
  silently makes every sealed value undecryptable. R-ARCH-021 likewise has no default and no
  generated key. The operator creates the Secret before the first install (Q-HA-8), by hand as
  below or through the cluster's secret tooling (an external-secrets operator, a vault injector,
  sealed secrets). When `secrets.encryption.existingSecret` or `secrets.encryption.keys` is empty,
  the rendering error (R-HA-029) prints this command:

  ```shell
  kubectl -n quader create secret generic quader-encryption-keys \
    --from-file=2026-10.key=<(head -c 32 /dev/urandom | base64)
  ```

  The file name without `.key` is the key ID, here `2026-10`, the form R-ARCH-021 uses.
- **Missing keys.** The canary check of R-ARCH-021 stops a replica whose ring lacks a key ID that
  sealed rows reference; it logs the expected and found key IDs, never key material. Old and new
  replicas with different active keys during step 2 of a rotation are expected and harmless,
  because by then every ring holds both keys.
- **Rotation without a decryption gap.** A plain "new key first, roll out" would let new pods seal
  with a key that old pods do not have yet. Rotation therefore takes two rollouts before the
  re-encryption of R-ARCH-021. Each step can be checked without a shell in a pod through
  `GET /api/v1/system/encryption` ([api-and-ui.md](api-and-ui.md) R-API-049, permission
  `system.read`):
  1. Add the new key to the Secret and *append* it to `secrets.encryption.keys` (decrypt-only
     everywhere). `helm upgrade`.
  2. Before this step, check that `GET /api/v1/system/encryption` lists the new key ID in every
     replica's `keyIds` and reports `ringsCompatible: true`. Then move the key to the first
     position, which makes it `secrets.active_key_id`. `helm upgrade`. Every replica already holds
     it, so values sealed by new pods are readable by old pods.
  3. Start the re-encryption with `POST /api/v1/system/tasks/secrets-reencrypt/run` (R-API-049;
     the `secrets-reencrypt` task of R-ARCH-021 and R-ARCH-016). It answers `409`
     `key_ring_incompatible` while a live replica's ring lacks a key ID that is active somewhere or
     still referenced, and `409` with the running job while one runs.
  4. When `quader admin secrets status` or `GET /api/v1/system/encryption` (R-API-049) reports no
     values under the old key ID, remove it from the list, `helm upgrade`, then remove it from the
     Secret.

  The chart adds a checksum of `secrets.encryption.keys` (names only) to the pod template, so a
  change to the list rolls the pods.

Acceptance criteria:

- `helm template` without `secrets.encryption.existingSecret` fails and names the value.
- Rotation steps 1–4 during an `npm ci` loop against a remote repository with Basic credentials to
  a private upstream: no iteration fails with `502 upstream_secret_unavailable`.
- A pod started with a different Secret content exits with the key-ring mismatch message of
  R-ARCH-021, while the others keep serving.

### R-HA-054 · Revocation journal in object storage
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: quader-only

A database restore to time *t* undoes every access removal made after *t* (H-37), and every
withdrawal or reservation of a package version made after *t*. Quader therefore records every
change to an access-bearing object, and every change that withdraws or reserves a version number
where a format page asks for it, a second time, outside PostgreSQL, and `quader admin post-restore`
re-applies the removals and reservations among the entries newer than *t* (R-HA-025, step 4;
Q-HA-9). A restore of a Quader backup replays the journal the same way, with *t* the backup's
snapshot time ([backup-and-restore.md](backup-and-restore.md), R-HA-060). Replay never grants
access and never deletes content; it may destroy a storage key that was destroyed after *t*
([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-097, [Q-HA-416](#q-ha-416--a-destruction-of-storage-keys-is-journaled-and-replayed-after-a-restore)).

**What is journaled.** Transactional audit events (R-OPS-015) whose entry in the event registry
(R-OPS-014) declares `journal: revocation`. When the audit writer inserts such an event, it inserts
a `revocation_outbox` row in the same transaction. A committed change therefore always has its
journal row, and a rolled-back change never has one. The owning pages flag their events and define
what an entry carries. An event type added later is covered by setting its flag, without a change
to this mechanism. At least these events are flagged:

| Audit event | Owner | Replay |
|---|---|---|
| `token.revoked`, `ci.token.revoked` | [identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md) R-AUTH-029, [gitlab-ci-oidc.md](gitlab-ci-oidc.md) R-CI-017 | Revoke the token, with the cascade of R-AUTH-029. A disable or deletion that revokes a principal's tokens (a user's or service account's with `revokeTokens` or on deletion, a Bastion registration's on deletion) records one `token.revoked` per token as well ([Q-AUTH-198](identity-and-authentication.md#q-auth-198--a-disable-or-deletion-journals-every-token-it-revokes-and-clearing-auto-join-is-journaled)) |
| `token.rotated` | identity R-AUTH-030 | Set the predecessor's `expires_at` to the earlier of its current and its journaled value; revoke it when the overlap was 0 |
| `user.disabled`, `user.deleted` | identity R-AUTH-016, R-AUTH-021, R-AUTH-039 | Disable the user |
| `user.updated` (the pending identity links it removed) | identity R-AUTH-016, R-AUTH-041 | Remove the pending link of each journaled provider from the user; never a linked identity ([Q-AUTH-205](identity-and-authentication.md#q-auth-205--userupdated-carries-the-pending-identity-links-it-removed-and-the-replay-removes-them)) |
| `serviceaccount.disabled`, `serviceaccount.deleted` | identity R-AUTH-020 | Disable the service account |
| `serviceaccount.updated` | identity R-AUTH-020, R-AUTHZ-039 | Narrow the actions of a repository's service account to the journaled after-set; disable it when that is a narrowing on top of a broadening the restored database lacks |
| `bastion.disabled`, `bastion.deleted` | [bastion.md](bastion.md) R-BAS-004 | Disable the Bastion registration ([Q-BAS-145](bastion.md#q-bas-145--a-disabled-or-deleted-registration-is-journaled-and-replayed-as-disabled)) |
| `bastion.handover.disabled` | [bastion.md](bastion.md) R-BAS-071 | Switch the registration's handover per blob off (`bastion.handover`), which keeps the links of the object store from that Bastion; `already in effect` when it is off, `subject unknown` for an ID that names no registration; the entry is `{principalId, name}` ([handover.go](../../internal/bastionmain/handover.go)) |
| `group.deleted` | identity R-AUTH-018 | Delete the group |
| `group.members.changed`, `user.groups.synced` | identity R-AUTH-018, R-AUTH-008, R-AUTH-039 | Remove each removed membership with its source; added members are ignored |
| `authz.role.unbound` | [authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-022 | Remove the role binding |
| `authz.policy.deleted` | authorization R-AUTHZ-021 | Delete the policy |
| `authz.ownership.removed`, `authz.ownership.released` | authorization R-AUTHZ-019 | Remove the owner |
| `authz.project.deleted`, `authz.project.member_removed` | authorization R-AUTHZ-026, R-AUTHZ-031 | Delete the project (when empty), remove the membership |
| `authz.project.visibility_changed` | authorization R-AUTHZ-033, R-AUTHZ-036 | Update rule below with the level comparator of R-AUTHZ-036: set the project's level to the journaled one when it is not higher than the current one, and lower its repositories as R-AUTHZ-033 rule 3 says; a higher level is `skipped` |
| `user.external_changed` | identity R-AUTH-044, R-AUTH-041 | Set the `external` flag when the journaled value is `true`; clearing it is not replayed (setting the flag narrows) |
| `repository.moved` | authorization R-AUTHZ-031, [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-060 | Disable the repository when the restored database holds it in the source project, and report it `suspended` |
| `repository.disabled`, `repository.deleted` | authorization R-AUTHZ-031, [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-004, R-REPO-013 | Disable the repository ([Q-AUTHZ-238](authorization.md#q-authz-238--disabling-a-repository-is-journaled-as-repositorydisabled-with-a-handler-of-its-own), [Q-AUTHZ-239](authorization.md#q-authz-239--a-deleted-repository-is-journaled-and-replayed-as-disabled)) |
| `repository.narrowed` | [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-061, [vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-002 | Re-apply each narrowing part to the restored repository: keep the include patterns both lists hold, add the exclude patterns, switch `autoClaim` on, take the members out, add or reduce the pin rules, take the more blocking `vulnerabilities` values. Where a part could widen (an empty include list, a removed member whose `members` claim would leave effect beside another member, a pin rule that a claim or another rule overlaps), disable the repository instead (`suspended`) |
| `repository.claims_changed` | [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-023, R-REPO-061 | Create each added claim, or widen it to `global`; an auto claim not where another repository's claim covers the name; a manual claim that overlaps a claim of another repository in effect together with it is created and its repository disabled (`suspended`). An entry with no added claim is `already in effect` |
| `group.updated` (the auto-join flag and a rename) | identity R-AUTH-019, R-AUTH-041 | Update rule below: clear the flag, never set it (Q-AUTH-198). A rename keeps the restored name and detaches the group from group synchronization ([Q-AUTH-206](identity-and-authentication.md#q-auth-206--a-group-renamed-after-the-restore-point-is-detached-from-group-synchronization-not-renamed)) |
| `ci.issuer.*` and `ci.mapping.*` disables and deletions | gitlab-ci R-CI-002, R-CI-019, R-CI-020 | Disable the issuer or mapping. Disabling a mapping that was enabled also suspends every later enabled mapping of its tier, so no job falls through to a mapping that grants more ([Q-CI-11](gitlab-ci-oidc.md#q-ci-11--replaying-a-mapping-disable-under-first-match)) |
| `authz.policy.updated`, `authz.project.member_changed`; `ci.issuer.*` and `ci.mapping.*` updates; `settings.auth.changed` (the token lifetime maxima, R-AUTH-040) and `authz.settings.changed` (the repository settings, the visibility levels among them, R-AUTHZ-031) | the pages above | Update rule below; the lifetime maxima value by value to the smaller ([Q-AUTH-207](identity-and-authentication.md#q-auth-207--the-token-lifetime-maxima-are-journaled-and-the-replay-lowers-each-to-the-smaller-value)) |
| `endpoint.exposure.deleted`; `endpoint.exposure.updated` | [endpoints.md](endpoints.md) R-EP-020 | Delete the rule; the update rule below with the exposure comparator of R-EP-020, whose suspension disables the rule |

Nothing is deleted; `quader admin npm reinstate` reverses it |
| `oci.manifest.deleted` | [formats/oci.md](formats/oci.md) R-OCI-033 | Withhold the manifest: write its mark in `oci_tombstones` and increment `packages.rev_seq` when the restored repository holds the manifest under the name (`applied`), leaving its items and bytes stored and unserved; `already in effect` when the mark exists; otherwise `subject unknown`. Nothing is deleted; `quader admin oci reinstate` reverses it |
| `vulnerability.finding.status_changed`, `vulnerability.finding.reopened` when the change sets a download block (`block: set`) | [vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-012, R-VULN-013, R-VULN-026, Q-VULN-48 | Written by a triage, a reopen and every evaluation change that sets a block ([Q-VULN-130](vulnerability-scanning.md#q-vuln-130--every-change-of-the-evaluation-that-sets-a-download-block-records-vulnerabilityfindingstatus_changed-with-block-set-its-cause-and-the-journal-entry)). Block the finding of the journaled ID when it has the entry's repository, package version and advisory, else the finding of the entry's repository, package version and advisory, else a finding the replay creates; `subject unknown` when the restored database holds no such repository of the entry's ecosystem. A stored version's finding is set `blocked` whatever its status; the finding of a version the repository does not store becomes `resolved` with `version_removed` while `blocked`, which the remote miss and a commit count until the ecosystem has synced since the restore; `already in effect` when the finding has that shape ([Q-VULN-114](vulnerability-scanning.md#q-vuln-114--a-replayed-block-sets-blocked-on-the-restored-finding-whatever-its-status-so-a-block-lifted-after-the-restore-point-comes-back), [Q-VULN-115](vulnerability-scanning.md#q-vuln-115--a-replayed-block-names-its-finding-by-id-and-by-its-immutable-package-version-and-writes-the-findings-own-history), [Q-VULN-131](vulnerability-scanning.md#q-vuln-131--a-replayed-block-names-its-repository-and-package-version-creates-the-finding-the-restored-database-lacks-and-leaves-the-shape-both-download-gates-read), [Q-VULN-132](vulnerability-scanning.md#q-vuln-132--a-blocked-finding-whose-version-is-gone-counts-until-its-ecosystem-has-synced-since-the-restore-at-the-remote-miss-and-at-a-commit)). The entry is optional: a change that lifts a block or sets none is not journaled |
| `system.storage.keys_destroyed` | [storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-097, R-STOR-099 | Destroy the keys again, per identifier of the entry `{connection, keyIds, destroyedAt}`, unless the restoring configuration names the connection (`skipped` with its note); the rule below the table ([Q-HA-416](#q-ha-416--a-destruction-of-storage-keys-is-journaled-and-replayed-after-a-restore), [Q-HA-417](#q-ha-417--the-replay-destroys-the-keys-only-of-a-connection-the-restoring-configuration-does-not-name)) |
| `remote.examination.discarded` | [remote-curation.md](remote-curation.md) R-CUR-016 | Evict what the restored repository stores of the entry's subject (`name`, and `version` or every version) and its rules still do not deliver, and remove the versions' examination rows; a version the rules deliver is left. The replay removes nothing itself: it makes the subject's examination rows due (a stored version without a row gets one) and queues a run of the task `remote-examination-cleanup` (`jobs.EnqueueTx`), whose run evicts each due version the rules still do not deliver ([remote-curation.md](remote-curation.md) Q-CUR-144); a replay that finds the rows due already answers already in effect ([journal_replay.go](../../internal/remotecuration/retention/journal_replay.go)) |
| `package.published`, `package.deleted` (from P1 also the copy and move events of R-STOR-019) of local NuGet repositories | [formats/nuget.md](formats/nuget.md) R-NUGET-033 | Addition of an absent version: write a `reserved` tombstone for the journaled SHA-512; an addition that meets a `reserved` tombstone for other bytes turns it into `removed` and warns ([Q-NUGET-112](formats/nuget.md#q-nuget-112--two-replayed-additions-of-one-version-that-name-different-bytes-leave-its-number-refusing-every-package)). Removal: an absent version's tombstone becomes or is written as `removed`; a present version with the journaled SHA-512 is reported `revived`; never delete |

**The destruction of storage keys** (built with package 7 of the encryption; `ReplayDestroyed` in
[internal/blob/keys/replay.go](../../internal/blob/keys/replay.go), registered from
[wire_storage_keys.go](../../internal/app/wire_storage_keys.go)). `system.storage.keys_destroyed` ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-097,
R-STOR-099) is in the table above. Its replay, per identifier of the entry `{connection, keyIds, destroyedAt}`:
an entry whose connection the restoring installation's configuration names is `skipped` and changes nothing: a configured connection is not
retired, so the entry is forged or stale; its reason ("connection archive is in this installation's configuration; its keys are not
destroyed") is the entry's note, which the replay prints as a warning line and lists among its warnings, and the restore goes on
([Q-HA-417](#q-ha-417--the-replay-destroys-the-keys-only-of-a-connection-the-restoring-configuration-does-not-name)). The restore and
`quader admin post-restore` hand the replay the ids of their configuration's `storage.connections`; a replay that was handed none skips
every such entry with the note "the restore did not name the connections of its configuration" and destroys nothing
([Q-HA-425](#q-ha-425--the-replay-of-a-destruction-that-knows-no-configured-connection-destroys-nothing)). Otherwise: a sealed row is
destroyed at the entry's time, or now when that lies in the future (`applied`); a destroyed row is `already in effect`; no row: a destroyed
row is inserted from the identifier with `created_at` = `destroyedAt` (`applied`), so that no later import or reuse of the connection id
brings the key back, unless the database holds that kind and generation of the connection under another identifier, which is left; when no
identifier changes and none was destroyed already, the outcome is `subject unknown`. An entry whose connection is no connection id or that
names a key of another connection is malformed and `skipped`. The area `storage_keys` is announced with the payload's version 2, no audit
event is written ([Q-HA-416](#q-ha-416--a-destruction-of-storage-keys-is-journaled-and-replayed-after-a-restore)). Acceptance criterion
(unit, the handler): four cases: `applied` on a sealed row, `already in effect` on a destroyed row, `applied` with an inserted destroyed row,
and an entry for a connection of the configuration `skipped` with its note, its keys still sealed
(`TestR_HA_054_TheReplayOfADestruction` in `internal/blob/keys`; the registration and the mapping of the outcomes in `internal/app`).

**Dispatch.** An entry of a format event is dispatched to that format's replay handler, which the
format page specifies (the two rows above). An entry of a format without a replay handler is
reported `skipped`. Access entries are replayed by the rules below.

The break-glass account's `enabled` state lives in the configuration file, not in PostgreSQL, so a
restore does not revive it and it is not journaled.

**Replay rules.**

- Removals (revoke, disable, delete, remove) are applied as recorded. Each is idempotent: a subject
  already in the recorded state is reported `already in effect`, one missing from the restored
  database `subject unknown`. A deleted user, service account, Bastion registration, CI issuer,
  mapping or repository is disabled rather than deleted, so a mistaken or forged entry stays
  reversible and replay never deletes content; disabling already makes its tokens fail, and a
  disabled repository takes no part in resolution, download or deploy (R-AUTH-016, R-AUTH-020,
  R-BAS-004, R-CI-017, R-REPO-004). The tokens such a principal lost carry entries of their own,
  so enabling the restored principal again brings none of them back.
- **Update rule.** An update entry carries the object's state before and after the change, without
  secrets. Replay compares the object's *current* state with the journaled after-state through the
  owning page's comparator `narrows(current, after)`. The comparator answers true only when the
  after-state grants nothing that the current state does not, and false whenever it cannot tell.
  1. True: the access-bearing fields are set to the after-state (`applied`). Replay never changes
     identifying fields (names, keys).
  2. False, and the journaled before-state is contained in the after-state (the change only added
     access): the entry is skipped (`skipped`). Access granted after *t* is not restored.
  3. False otherwise: the object is suspended (`suspended`). A policy loses all its entries, an
     issuer or mapping is disabled, an access setting takes its most restrictive value. The output
     prints the journaled after-state, so an administrator can review and re-apply it.

  Case 3 is a narrowing on top of a broadening that the restored database lacks. Applying it to the
  older state could keep access the narrowing removed, so replay fails closed instead. Comparators
  MUST be conservative: an emptied include list, for example, is unrestricted under R-AUTHZ-005, so
  removing the last include pattern never counts as narrowing.
- **Forged entries cannot escalate.** Whoever holds the runtime S3 credential can write journal
  objects. A removal only removes; a forged `system.storage.keys_destroyed` does not escalate either, and the replay applies it only to
  a connection the restoring configuration does not name (Q-HA-417), so at worst it destroys the keys of a connection that is already
  retired before the operator did, which cuts off a recovery of its leftovers through the offline tool
  ([H-1375](../security/stored-content-keys.md#h-1375--a-forged-journal-entry-can-destroy-a-retired-connections-keys-at-a-restore-before-the-operator-does)). Where removing one object can widen what another grants, the
  owning page adds a fail-closed step: a disabled CI mapping would let its jobs fall through to the
  next mapping of its tier, so replay suspends those mappings too (R-CI-020, Q-CI-11); a virtual
  member whose claims would leave effect, and a pin rule or a claim that would route a name to
  another member, disable the repository instead ([repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md)
  R-REPO-061); a group rename only detaches the group from synchronization (Q-AUTH-206). The order
  of the entries is the writers' choice (`at` is part of the object), so where the order of two
  entries would decide what a restriction admits, the end state does not depend on it: two NuGet
  additions of one version that name different bytes leave its number refusing every package, so an
  entry with an earlier time cannot take the number for its bytes ([formats/nuget.md](formats/nuget.md)
  R-NUGET-033, Q-NUGET-112); that holds where the replay sees the genuine object (every version of
  a key read, or a bucket that refuses both overwrites and deletions of journal objects, for example by object lock), and with the default `source: runtime` the same
  credential overwrites or deletes it instead (H-553). An update is
  applied only when it grants nothing beyond the
  object's current state, and the forgeable before-state only chooses between skipping and
  suspending. An entry of an unknown event type is reported and skipped. An entry that holds a value the database refuses (SQLSTATE class 22, 23 or 54: a NUL byte, a text beyond a limit, a constraint) is rolled back and reported `skipped` with its subject, and the replay goes on; a lost connection or a serialization failure still ends it. The subject of a printed line comes from the entry and is printed quoted.
- Within the replay margin (below), an update that is already reflected in the restored database
  can undo a broadening made shortly before *t*. Replay then fails closed, too.
- **Follow-up work.** A handler whose narrowing needs work that runs later (the re-evaluation of a
  repository whose scanning it strengthened, R-REPO-061) writes the job row in its own transaction,
  so the job exists exactly when the entry's change commits; the workers that start after the
  restore run it ([Q-HA-180](#q-ha-180--a-replay-handler-starts-follow-up-work-by-writing-a-job-row-in-its-own-transaction)).

**Outbox and shipping.**

- A worker job ships the rows in `id` order to
  `<prefix>/_journal/revocations/<yyyy>/<mm>/<dd>/<id>.json` of every connection that is not draining ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-059), one object per entry, through each
  connection's guarded client, and deletes each row once every such connection holds its object (`revocation_outbox_shipped` records the
  ones that do, [Q-STOR-241](storage.md#q-stor-241--the-journal-goes-to-every-connection-and-an-outbox-row-waits-for-each)). A row whose object was written but whose deletion
  did not commit is shipped again under the same key with identical content, which is harmless.
  Quader never deletes a journal object. `_journal/` is a key family of
  [storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-001, so the orphan sweep leaves it alone.
- Shipping is triggered by a signal ([architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-018) and runs at
  least every `backup.revocation_journal.ship_interval`.
- A change never waits for object storage. During an object-store outage the outbox grows and ships
  afterwards; an outage of one connection keeps only that connection's copy pending. The gauge
  `quader_revocation_journal_pending{connection}` shows the backlog per connection.

**Replay run.**

- `quader admin post-restore --restored-to <t>` lists the entries with
  `at > t − backup.revocation_journal.replay_margin` and sorts them by `at` and `id`. It applies
  them in that order, each to the state its predecessors left.
- The replay starts at the earlier of *t* and the newest `audit_event.occurred_at` of the restored database, minus the
  margin, so a `--restored-to` that lies later than the database does not skip revocations (Q-HA-158).
- The replay reads the journal on every reachable connection of the source and merges by key; identical bytes under one key on two
  connections are one copy ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-059).
- Every readable copy of an entry is replayed: an ID that appears under two keys and a key whose versions differ are
  somebody else's writes, each copy is replayed (the handlers only remove or narrow) and the output flags them
  (Q-HA-158). With version listing the replay reads every version of a key.
- It prints one line per entry (`applied`, `already in effect`, `subject unknown`, `skipped`,
  `suspended`, `revived`) and writes the audit event `system.restore.journal_replayed` with the
  count of each outcome. `revived` marks a version that a format handler found present although the
  journal recorded its removal, and that it leaves in place because replay never deletes
  ([formats/nuget.md](formats/nuget.md) R-NUGET-033).
- The margin covers transactions that started before *t* and committed after it (`at` is the
  transaction's `now()`).
- With bucket versioning and the restore credential of R-HA-025 step 5 (`--credentials-file`),
  replay lists object versions as well, so a delete marker set with the runtime credential cannot
  hide an entry. Without versioning, a holder of the runtime credential can delete journal objects
  and so revive what they recorded.
- If replay leaves no `admin` role binding, the output says so. The break-glass account
  (R-AUTH-014) is the way back in.

**Residual gap.** Entries not yet shipped when the old database stopped (normally less than one
shipping interval). Access granted after *t*, including reactivations, is absent from the restored
database and never replayed; an administrator grants it again. Objects suspended under case 3 of
the update rule grant nothing until an administrator reviews them.

**Retention.** Journal objects are kept until the operator expires them, for example with a bucket
lifecycle rule on the `_journal/` prefix that is longer than `backup.recovery_window`. An entry is a
few hundred bytes, an update entry a few kilobytes.

```sql
CREATE TABLE revocation_outbox (
  id     uuid        PRIMARY KEY,        -- the audit event's ID (UUIDv7)
  at     timestamptz NOT NULL,           -- the audit event's occurred_at, the transaction's now()
  event  text        NOT NULL,           -- registry name, e.g. 'token.revoked'
  entry  jsonb       NOT NULL            -- the journal object body; no secrets, no token hashes
);
```

Journal objects (examples, one object per line). The envelope is `v`, `id`, `at` and `event`; `entry` is the object the
producer passed with the audit event, verbatim (Q-HA-140). The names inside `entry` are the owning page's:

```json
{"v": 1, "id": "0192f0c4-7a1e-7c3b-9d2e-5b8f1a2c3d4e", "at": "2026-10-28T12:00:03.114Z", "event": "token.revoked", "entry": {"tokenId": "0192f0a1-…", "reason": "admin"}}
{"v": 1, "id": "0192f0d2-…", "at": "2026-10-28T12:04:41.902Z", "event": "authz.policy.updated", "entry": {"policyId": "0191aa07-…", "name": "team-web-publish", "before": {"entries": [{"principal": "group:team-web", "actions": ["deploy", "read"]}]}, "after": {"entries": [{"principal": "group:team-web", "actions": ["read"]}]}}}
```

Configuration:

```yaml
backup:
  revocation_journal:
    enabled: true          # default (proposed)
    ship_interval: 5s      # default (proposed)
    replay_margin: 5m      # default (proposed); longer than any transaction (R-HA-015 timeouts)
```

Acceptance criteria:

- Revoke a personal access token, wait `ship_interval`, restore the database to a point before the
  revocation and run `post-restore`: the token is rejected with `401`, and the output lists
  `token.revoked … applied`.
- Remove `deploy` from a policy entry and unbind `admin` from a group, then restore to a point
  before both changes and run `post-restore`: the entry holds only `read`, and the group's members
  are not administrators. A policy that was first broadened and then narrowed after *t* ends
  `suspended` and grants nothing.
- With the S3 store stopped, revoking a token takes effect at once; its journal object appears
  within `ship_interval` after the store returns.
- Three hand-written journal objects (one with an unknown event type, one whose after-state adds an
  action to a policy, one whose before-state is forged so that the addition looks like a
  narrowing) are reported `skipped` or `suspended`, and no principal gains access.

## Helm chart

### R-HA-028 · Chart scope, rendered resources and naming
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: HA-029, HA-032, HA-038, HA-021

- The chart `quader` lives in `deploy/helm/quader`, `apiVersion: v2`, and follows the
  [Helm chart best practices](https://helm.sh/docs/chart_best_practices/): camelCase values,
  standard `app.kubernetes.io/*` labels, no CRDs shipped, no subcharts. It is released with
  `version` = `appVersion` = Quader's version.
- There is no bundled database, no bundled Valkey and no bundled object store, because production
  needs all three to be highly available (INV-12). The local development profile (R-HA-051)
  installs them separately.
- **The chart never creates or generates a Secret.** Every credential is a reference to an
  existing Secret (R-HA-030). This removes a whole class of upgrade failures: no generated value
  can change on re-render.

Rendered resources (`<fullname>` is the release name, or `<release>-quader` when the release name
does not contain `quader`, overridable by `fullnameOverride`; it is never cut, and the render fails when it is too long for a name built
from it, R-HA-029 and [Q-HA-374](#q-ha-374--the-chart-refuses-a-fullname-too-long-for-the-names-it-builds-and-never-cuts-it)):

| Kind | Name | Rendered when |
|---|---|---|
| Deployment | `<fullname>-api`, `<fullname>-packages`, `<fullname>-worker` | always (R-HA-002) |
| Deployment, Service | `<fullname>-api-<pool>`, `<fullname>-packages-<pool>`, `<fullname>-worker-<pool>` (Deployment only) | per entry of `api.pools`, `packages.pools` and `worker.pools` (R-HA-062) |
| Service (ClusterIP) | `<fullname>-api` and `<fullname>-packages`, port `http` 8080 → the main Deployment's pods of that role, `sessionAffinity: None` | always |
| Service (ClusterIP) | `<fullname>-ops`, port `ops` 8081, every serving pod (`api`, `packages`, `worker`, `web`) | always (probes from the kubelet do not need it; ServiceMonitor does) |
| ConfigMap | `<fullname>-config` (`quader.yaml`) | always |
| ServiceAccount | `<fullname>` | `serviceAccount.create` |
| ConfigMap, ServiceAccount (hooks, weight −10) | `<fullname>-migrate` | `migrations.mode: hook` and not `restore.enabled` |
| Job (hook, weight 0) | `<fullname>-migrate` | `migrations.mode: hook` and not `restore.enabled` |
| Job | `<fullname>-restore` | `restore.enabled` (R-HA-060) |
| ServiceAccount | `<fullname>-restore` | `restore.enabled` and `restore.serviceAccount.create` |
| Job (hook) | `<fullname>-post-restore` | `postRestore.enabled` |
| CronJob | `<fullname>-backup` | `backup.enabled` (R-HA-060) |
| ServiceAccount | `<fullname>-backup` | `backup.enabled` and `backup.serviceAccount.create` |
| PodDisruptionBudget | per Deployment, none for Jobs | `podDisruptionBudget.enabled` of the role or pool |
| HorizontalPodAutoscaler (`autoscaling/v2`) | per Deployment | `autoscaling.enabled` of the role or pool |
| Ingress | `<fullname>`: per host the path rules of R-HA-037 to the role Services | `ingress.enabled` |
| HTTPRoute | `<fullname>`: the same path rules | `gateway.enabled` |
| Gateway | `<fullname>-gateway` | `gateway.enabled` and `gateway.create.enabled` (P1, R-HA-053) |
| NetworkPolicy | one per Deployment, named as the Deployment (`<fullname>-api`, `<fullname>-packages`, `<fullname>-worker`, each pool, each endpoint pool), and `<fullname>-migrate`, `<fullname>-restore`, `<fullname>-backup`; ingress rules only, each with its port (R-HA-042) | `networkPolicy.enabled` |
| Service, Ingress, HTTPRoute | `<fullname>-ep-<name>` per further endpoint, and `<fullname>-api-ep-<name>` when its surface holds families of both roles: its Services and port, its own Ingress or HTTPRoute with its class, hosts (a wildcard host included), TLS entries and the path rules of its surface ([endpoints.md](endpoints.md) R-EP-008, Q-EP-71) | per entry of `endpoints`; the Ingress with its `ingress.enabled`, the HTTPRoute with its `gateway.enabled` |
| Deployment, PodDisruptionBudget, HorizontalPodAutoscaler | `<fullname>-packages-ep-<name>` and `<fullname>-api-ep-<name>`, the optional pool of an endpoint, one per role its surface holds ([endpoints.md](endpoints.md) R-EP-008, Q-EP-70) | `endpoints.<name>.pool.enabled` |
| ServiceMonitor, PrometheusRule | `<fullname>` | `metrics.serviceMonitor.enabled`, `metrics.prometheusRule.enabled` |
| anything | from `extraObjects` | listed |

- The chart renders no StatefulSet, no PersistentVolumeClaim and no Valkey, PostgreSQL or object
  store (R-HA-061).
- Labels on every object: `app.kubernetes.io/name: quader`, `app.kubernetes.io/instance`,
  `app.kubernetes.io/version`, `app.kubernetes.io/managed-by`, `helm.sh/chart`, and
  `app.kubernetes.io/component` (`api`, `packages`, `worker`, `migrate`, `restore`, `backup`). The
  pods of `api`, `packages` and `worker` also carry `quader/pool` (name proposed): `<name>` for the pods of a pool of
  R-HA-062 (`ep-<name>` for an endpoint pool), and the empty value for the main Deployments. The ServiceMonitor sets the target label `pool`
  from it, and Prometheus drops an empty label, so the main Deployments' series carry no `pool`
  (R-HA-045). Selectors use name, instance, component and, for the serving roles, `quader/pool`,
  from the MVP on, because selector labels are immutable: adding a pool later then never overlaps
  the main Deployment's or the role Service's selector and never changes an immutable one.
- **Ports (HA-021).** Containers listen on 8080 (`http`, the default endpoint's client listener),
  8081 (`ops`) and the port of each further endpoint they serve ([endpoints.md](endpoints.md)
  R-EP-002, R-EP-008), and nothing else (INV-6). Every port is unprivileged, so no capability is
  needed. Replicas need no port open towards each other.
- The pod template carries `checksum/config` (hash of the rendered ConfigMap), so every
  configuration change rolls the pods. Secret contents are not hashed, because the chart does not
  read them. Rotated Secret files are re-read by their consumers where the owning page says so
  (database password, OIDC client secret, CA bundles, break-glass password). Other changes need
  `kubectl rollout restart`.

Acceptance criteria:

- `helm lint deploy/helm/quader` and `helm template` with `ci/*.yaml` value sets pass in CI. A
  kubeconform run validates the output against the Kubernetes and Gateway API schemas of the
  supported versions.
- `helm template … | grep -c '^kind: Secret$'` prints `0` for every CI value set.

### R-HA-029 · Fail-fast chart validation
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: HA-030

The chart MUST refuse to render, naming the offending value, before anything is applied:

| Condition | Message names |
|---|---|
| `config.server.base_url` empty | `config.server.base_url` |
| `config.database.host` or `secrets.database.existingSecret` empty | the value |
| `config.storage.s3`, `secrets.s3`, `secrets.s3CA`, `secrets.backupSource` or `secrets.journalReader` set (the values of the one store, checked first, Q-HA-395) | the value and the keys that took its place |
| `config.storage.connections` empty, two elements with one `id` (an element without one is `default`, Q-HA-394), an element without `bucket` (and without a `bucketKey`), and the other refusals of R-HA-072 | the value and the connection |
| An element with `credentials_source: static` without an entry of `secrets.storageConnections` with `existingSecret` (R-HA-072) | both |
| `secrets.encryption.existingSecret` or `secrets.encryption.keys` empty | the value, and the key-creation command of R-HA-027 |
| `highAvailability.enforce` and fewer than 2 replicas (`replicaCount`, or `autoscaling.minReplicas`) for `api`, `packages`, `worker` or a pool, a disabled PDB, or a missing host spread constraint, one that is not `DoNotSchedule`, or one without `nodeTaintsPolicy: Honor` (R-HA-059 rule 3) | the Deployment and the value |
| `worker.replicaCount`, `api.replicaCount` or `packages.replicaCount` (or its `autoscaling.minReplicas`) < 1 | the value |
| `config.storage.upload.max_size` > the spool budget derived from the `packages` spool size; the upload limit of the UI's content route (`config.ui.deploy.max_upload_bytes`, or `config.storage.upload.max_size` when it is 0) > the spool budget of `api` (R-HA-035, Q-UI-106) | both |
| `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` of a role < `config.health.shutdown_drain_delay` + 15 s | both |
| `api`, `packages`, a path pool or an endpoint pool without `resources.limits.memory`, or with one that admits fewer than 64 requests: ⌊0.8 × `config.runtime.memory_limit_ratio` × the limit ÷ the request bytes of R-ARCH-005⌋, from `config.storage.download.buffer_size`, `hold_back` and `config.storage.object_store.http.receive_window` (R-HA-036, Q-HA-70), or whose kernel share holds fewer than 64 send buffers: ⌊0.8 × (1 − the ratio) × the limit ÷ twice `config.server.send_buffer` (4 MiB with `0`)⌋ (Q-ARCH-500) | the limit, the Deployment or the slot count and the values it comes from |
| `config.valkey.mode: sentinel` with `config.valkey.sentinel.addresses` or `config.valkey.sentinel.primary_name` empty | the value |
| `highAvailability.enforce` and `config.valkey.mode` other than `sentinel`, or fewer than 3 Sentinel addresses | `config.valkey.mode` or `config.valkey.sentinel.addresses` |
| `secrets.valkey.existingSecret` empty | the value |
| `config.valkey.tls.mode: disable` without `config.valkey.allow_insecure: true` | both |
| `config.database.pooler.mode: transaction` with `config.database.session_host` empty or equal to `config.database.host` | `config.database.session_host` |
| `config.database.pooler.mode: transaction` with a control endpoint (`control_host`, `control_port`, `control_name`, each defaulting to its main counterpart) equal to the request endpoint (Q-HA-20) | `config.database.control_host` |
| `backup.enabled` and `config.backup.target.bucket` empty (the backup is off by default and needs no bucket then, Q-HA-17) | both |
| `restore.enabled` and `config.backup.target.bucket` empty | both |
| `backup.schedule` in a form that Quader's cron parser rejects: six fields, `?`, day-of-week `7`, `@every`, `TZ=` or `CRON_TZ=` ([operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) Q-OPS-7, [storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-025) | `backup.schedule` |
| The backup target on the endpoint and bucket of any connection ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-050) without `config.backup.target.allow_same_bucket: true`, or with one prefix containing the other (R-HA-060; `quader backup create` exits `2` on the same rule, R-BAK-002). Checked for any configured target, the backup on or off, because every replica's configuration check refuses it as well | both locations |
| `config.backup.target.credentials.source: static` without `secrets.backupTarget.existingSecret`, while `backup.enabled` or `restore.enabled` renders a Job that mounts it | both |
| `restore.enabled` without `restore.backupId` | `restore.backupId` |
| `restore.enabled` with a replica count above 0 or autoscaling enabled for any role or pool | `restore.enabled` and the value |
| Two pools of a role with the same name, two pools with the same path prefix or queue, a pool path outside the families of its role or equal to one of the role's own prefixes of R-HA-037, a worker pool queue that does not exist, or a pool whose name starts with `ep-` (R-HA-062) | the pools |
| Worker pools that claim every queue; a worker pool without a replica; an `endpoints.default.surface` without a family of a role that no further endpoint is served by (R-HA-062) | the pool or the surface |
| A provider of `config.auth.oidc.providers` with a `client_auth_method` other than `none` and no entry in `secrets.oidc` (R-HA-030, Q-HA-93) | the provider |
| A `<fullname>` too long for a name built from it alone: the Service and the certificate name `<fullname>-<kind>` of every kind of `quader.tlsKindTable`, rendered or not, `<fullname>-ops` and `<fullname>-packages-scan` (DNS labels of at most 63 characters), the Jobs `<fullname>-migrate`, `-restore` and `-post-restore-<8 hex>` (at most 63) and the CronJob `<fullname>-backup` (at most 52); the tightest decides, today `<fullname>-malware-scanner-clamav`, so `<fullname>` has at most 40 characters ([Q-HA-374](#q-ha-374--the-chart-refuses-a-fullname-too-long-for-the-names-it-builds-and-never-cuts-it)) | the name that is too long, its length, and the longest release name and `fullnameOverride` that fit |
| An endpoint whose `port` equals 8080, 8081 or another endpoint's port; an invalid endpoint name or one for which `<fullname>-api-ep-<name>` (a surface with families of both roles) or `<fullname>-packages-ep-<name>` (a pool) exceeds 63 characters; a missing `baseUrl`; a host in two endpoints; `extraSecrets` or `clientCaSecret` with `tls.enabled: false`; an endpoint pool below two replicas with `highAvailability.enforce` ([endpoints.md](endpoints.md) R-EP-008) | the endpoint and the value |
| `gateway.enabled` without `gateway.parentRefs` and without `gateway.create.enabled` | `gateway.parentRefs` |
| `gateway.enabled` and `.Capabilities.APIVersions` lacks `gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1/HTTPRoute` | the missing API |
| `metrics.serviceMonitor.enabled` (or `prometheusRule`) and the `monitoring.coreos.com/v1` API missing | the missing API |
| A chart-managed configuration key set inside `config` (secret file paths, among them those of `valkey` and `backup.target`; `storage.spool.dir`; `server.content_base_url`; `server.endpoints`; `backup.manual_run`) | the key |
| `contentOrigin.host` equal to the host of `config.server.base_url` or of a `config.server.additional_base_urls` entry (P1, R-HA-055) | `contentOrigin.host` |
| `podDisruptionBudget` with both `minAvailable` and `maxUnavailable` set | both |

- `values.schema.json` validates every chart-owned value (types, enums, `additionalProperties:
  false`); Helm checks it on install, upgrade, lint and template
  ([schema files](https://helm.sh/docs/topics/charts/#schema-files)). It uses JSON Schema
  draft-07 keywords only. Its enums admit only `ReadWriteOnce` and `ReadWriteOncePod` as access
  modes of a generic ephemeral volume (R-HA-061).
- The `config` subtree is validated against the schema the binary emits (`quader config schema`).
  CI regenerates it from the Go configuration types and fails on drift. A typo in a configuration
  key therefore fails `helm install`, not silently at runtime (catalog trap HA-036). The binary
  rejects unknown keys at startup as a second line.
- Offline rendering (`helm template`) has no cluster capabilities. CI passes
  `--api-versions gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1/HTTPRoute --api-versions monitoring.coreos.com/v1`
  where needed.

Acceptance criteria: a CI test renders one value set per row of the table and asserts the failure
and the named value. Another renders `values-dev.yaml` and the three profiles successfully.

### R-HA-030 · Configuration rendering and secret wiring
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: HA-033, HA-035, HA-036, HA-037, HA-053

**Configuration file.**

- The chart renders `config` into `/etc/quader/quader.yaml` (INV-15), merged with chart-managed
  keys. One file serves every Deployment and Job; what differs per Deployment, the role, is the
  container argument `--role` (R-HA-002), not a key in the file. The chart-managed keys:
  - secret file paths;
  - `storage.spool.dir`;
  - `server.content_base_url`, rendered as `https://<contentOrigin.host>` when `contentOrigin.host`
    is set (P1, R-HA-055);
  - `backup.manual_run.namespace` (the release namespace) and `backup.manual_run.cronjob`
    (`<fullname>-backup`), which the API's backup summary and the UI read to show the manual-run
    command ([api-and-ui.md](api-and-ui.md) R-API-050, Q-API-10; R-HA-060);
  - `server.endpoints`, rendered from the `endpoints` values, with the certificate file paths of
    their mounted Secrets ([endpoints.md](endpoints.md) R-EP-008). The rate-limit classes
    `server.endpoint_rate_limits` stay ordinary `config` keys.
- Precedence follows INV-15: environment variable `QUADER_<SECTION>_<KEY>` (nested keys joined
  with `_`, e.g. `QUADER_DATABASE_POOL_MAX_CONNS`) > file > built-in default. `extraEnv` can
  therefore override any file value. The chart itself sets only:
  - `QUADER_RUNTIME_MEMORY_LIMIT_BYTES` and `QUADER_RUNTIME_TERMINATION_GRACE_PERIOD` per
    Deployment, and `QUADER_DATABASE_PREFLIGHT_EXPECTED_SERVING_REPLICAS` (`..._WEB_REPLICAS` before phase 6a) and
    `QUADER_DATABASE_PREFLIGHT_EXPECTED_WORKER_REPLICAS` for the migration Job, the variables of the
    schema keys `runtime.memory_limit_bytes`, `runtime.termination_grace_period`,
    `database.preflight.expected_serving_replicas` and `database.preflight.expected_worker_replicas`
    (R-OPS-028 mapping; the chart is their only source; R-HA-016);
  - `QUADER_POOL_NAME` on the Deployment of each pool (R-HA-062, R-OPS-003), and on worker Deployments
    `QUADER_JOBS_QUEUES` (a pool) or `QUADER_JOBS_EXCLUDE_QUEUES` (the main `worker` beside pools), the variables of
    `jobs.queues` and `jobs.exclude_queues` ([architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-016);
  - `QUADER_STORAGE_SPOOL_MAX_BYTES` per Deployment, derived from the role's spool size when
    `config.storage.spool.max_bytes` is unset (R-HA-035);
  - `QUADER_SERVER_SCAN_LISTEN=:8082` on the main `packages` Deployment while the image scanning or the malware scanning is on,
    the scan listener of R-HA-066 and R-HA-068;
  - `QUADER_PROCESS_SCANNER_KIND=clamav` on the malware scanner (R-HA-068), the variable of `process.scanner_kind`; the image
    scanning's scanner runs its default, `trivy`;
  - `GOMAXPROCS` (R-HA-036);
  - in every Quader pod (`api`, `packages`, `worker`, both scanners, `web`, backup, restore, migration and post-restore), from the
    downward API: `QUADER_POD_NAME` (`fieldRef: metadata.name`), `QUADER_POD_NAMESPACE`
    (`metadata.namespace`) and `QUADER_NODE_NAME` (`spec.nodeName`). R-OPS-028 reserves these
    names. They feed the replica registry, including its `node` column that the status screen
    groups by ([api-and-ui.md](api-and-ui.md) R-UI-038, Q-UI-7), the `replica` field of every log
    record and the trace resource (R-OPS-003, R-OPS-009, R-OPS-018). `spec.nodeName` is offered
    by the downward API as an environment variable only, not as a volume file.
- There is no "complete configuration file from a Secret" mode. It would let an operator replace
  chart-managed paths and lose the validation of R-HA-029. Everything that is not a secret goes
  through `config`.
- `enableServiceLinks: false` on every pod. Kubernetes otherwise injects variables named after
  Services in the namespace. A Service named `quader-database` would inject
  `QUADER_DATABASE_PORT=tcp://…`, which collides with Quader's own variable prefix and fails
  strict validation
  ([Service environment variables](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service/#environment-variables)).

**Secrets.** Every Secret is pre-created by the operator and mounted as a read-only volume with
`items` (only the named keys), `defaultMode: 0440`, and no `subPath`, so rotations reach the files.
Secrets never become environment variables. Environment variables are readable through `/proc`,
end up in crash reports, and do not follow Secret updates. Each Secret is mounted only into the
pods whose process reads it; the first column names the pods where the set is narrower than every
Quader pod.

**Secret propagation time.** A rotated Secret reaches the mounted files of every pod within
2 minutes (the kubelet's sync period plus its cache delay). [identity-and-authentication.md](identity-and-authentication.md)
R-AUTH-014's `auth.break_glass.rotation_hold` default (2 min) equals this time; if this time
changes, that default follows.

| Value | Keys (default names) | Mount path | Configuration key set by the chart |
|---|---|---|---|
| `secrets.database` | `username`, `password` | `/var/run/secrets/quader/database/` | `database.username_file`, `database.password_file` |
| `secrets.databaseMigration` (migration and restore Jobs only) | `username`, `password` | same path in the Jobs | same |
| `secrets.databaseBackup` (backup pods only; empty = `secrets.database`) | `username`, `password` | same path in the backup pod | same |
| `secrets.databaseCA` | `ca.crt` | `/var/run/secrets/quader/database-ca/` | `database.ssl_root_cert_file` |
| `secrets.databaseClientCert` | `tls.crt`, `tls.key` | `/var/run/secrets/quader/database-client/` | `database.ssl_cert_file`, `database.ssl_key_file` |
| `secrets.storageConnections[]` (one entry per connection; the fields and pods of R-HA-072) | `access-key-id`, `secret-access-key`, the provisioner's keys, `ca.crt` | `/var/run/secrets/quader/s3-<id>/`, `…/s3-<id>-location/`, `…/s3-<id>-ca/`, `…/s3-<id>-backup/`, `…/s3-<id>-journal/` | the `*_file` keys of the element with that `id` in `storage.connections` (R-HA-072) |
| `secrets.valkey` (`api`, `packages`, `worker`, `web` only; not in backup, restore, migration or post-restore pods, R-BAK-012, R-BAK-022) | `username` (optional), `password` | `/var/run/secrets/quader/valkey/` | `valkey.username_file`, `valkey.password_file` |
| `secrets.valkeySentinel` (same pods) | `username` (optional), `password` | `/var/run/secrets/quader/valkey-sentinel/` | `valkey.sentinel.username_file`, `valkey.sentinel.password_file` |
| `secrets.valkeyCA` (same pods) | `ca.crt` | `/var/run/secrets/quader/valkey-ca/` | `valkey.tls.ca_file` |
| `secrets.valkeyClientCert` (same pods) | `tls.crt`, `tls.key` | `/var/run/secrets/quader/valkey-client/` | `valkey.tls.cert_file`, `valkey.tls.key_file` |
| `secrets.backupTarget` (backup and restore pods; only with `source: static`) | `access-key-id`, `secret-access-key`, `session-token` (only with `sessionTokenKey`) | `/var/run/secrets/quader/backup-target/` | `backup.target.credentials.access_key_id_file`, `…secret_access_key_file`, `…session_token_file` |
| `secrets.backupTargetCA` (backup and restore pods; Q-HA-146) | `ca.crt` | `/var/run/secrets/quader/backup-target-ca/` | `backup.target.ca_file` |
| `secrets.oidc[]` (one entry per provider ID; only the pods of role `api` (its main Deployment, its pools and its endpoint pools); never a pod of `packages`, worker, backup, migration or restore pods, R-AUTH-042, Q-HA-79) | `client-secret` | `/var/run/secrets/quader/oidc-<id>/` | `client_secret_file` of the provider with that `id` in `config.auth.oidc.providers` |
| `secrets.breakGlass` (the same pods as `secrets.oidc[]`, R-AUTH-014, R-AUTH-042) | `password` | `/var/run/secrets/quader/break-glass/` | `auth.break_glass.password_file`; empty value → `auth.break_glass.enabled: false` |
| `secrets.upstreamAccounts.<key>` (the pods of `api`, `packages` and `worker`, R-HA-073; one projected volume, each source optional) | `username` (`basic` only), `password` (`usernameKey`, `passwordKey`) | `/var/run/secrets/quader/upstream-accounts/<key>/` | `repositories.upstream_accounts.<key>.username_file`, `password_file`, `auth_mode`, `secret_name` (R-REPO-077) |
| `secrets.encryption` | `secrets.encryption.keys` | `/var/run/secrets/quader/encryption/` | `secrets.encryption_key_files` (ordered) and `secrets.active_key_id` (the first entry) |
| `secrets.metricsToken` | `token` | `/var/run/secrets/quader/metrics/` | `metrics.bearer_token_file` (R-OPS-006) |
| `trustedCA.*` (Secret or ConfigMap) | listed keys | `/etc/quader/ca/` | `proxy.outbound.tls.ca_files` (R-REPO-035); optionally the `ca_file` of the connections it names |
| `bootstrap.existingConfigMap` (P1) | any | `/etc/quader/bootstrap/` | configuration documents of [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) |

- **External database (HA-033).** Only an external PostgreSQL is supported. The host goes in
  `config.database.host`, credentials in `secrets.database`. No "wait for database" init container
  is rendered: the replica retries the connection at startup while not ready, and the migration Job
  retries its first connection within `activeDeadlineSeconds`.
- **Object storage (HA-053).** S3 is the only back end (INV-4), so there is no unsafe "local file
  system" default that silently breaks with a second replica. Workload identity is the default
  (`credentials.source: default`). On EKS the chart's ServiceAccount carries the role annotation
  ([IRSA](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/iam-roles-for-service-accounts.html)),
  or a Pod Identity association grants the role without one
  ([EKS Pod Identity](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/pod-identities.html)).
  Static keys use an entry of `secrets.storageConnections` (R-HA-072).
- **Bootstrap (HA-037).** The break-glass administrator is the first-start credential (R-AUTH-014).
  Further bootstrapping is `kubectl exec deploy/quader-api -- quader admin …` (R-AUTH-015), in the role that mounts the
  break-glass secret (`deploy/quader-web` before phase 6a). The chart
  renders no Job that writes tokens into Secrets: such a Job would need `create` on Secrets in the
  namespace, a permission the chart otherwise never needs. Operators store the printed token with
  their own secret tooling.

Acceptance criteria:

- `kubectl exec <pod> -- env | grep -iE 'password|secret|token'` prints nothing.
- Replacing the database Secret's password (R-HA-017) reaches `/var/run/secrets/quader/database/password`
  within 2 minutes without a restart.
- With a Service `quader-database` in the namespace, the pods start (no injected variables).

### R-HA-031 · Values reference
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: HA-029

Every value of the chart with its default. In the block below, as in the chart's `values.yaml`, every value is its default
and is commented only where its name does not say its meaning, unit, range or consequence, with an `example:` where the
default is empty (owner, 2026-11-04: no content-free comments). Keys under
`config` belong to the pages named in the comments; this page only fixes how the chart wires them.
Keys marked P1 (`gateway.create`, `contentOrigin`, `bootstrap`) enter the chart with the release that implements them, and
the keys of phase 6a (`api`, `packages`, the pools of R-HA-062) with phase 6a: the `config` subtree is validated against the
schema the binary emits (R-HA-029), so a key the binary does not know yet would fail
`helm install`. The keys under `config.backup` are [backup-and-restore.md](backup-and-restore.md)
R-BAK-011's, shown here with every key and default.

<details>
<summary>deploy/helm/quader/values.yaml</summary>

```yaml
# ── Global ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
global:
  imageRegistry: ""                     # empty = image.registry
  imagePullSecrets: []                  # example: [{name: registry-pull}]

nameOverride: ""
fullnameOverride: ""                    # empty = the release name, or <release>-quader; never cut: the render fails when a name built from it would be too long (at most 40 characters with the chart's kinds)
commonLabels: {}
commonAnnotations: {}

image:
  registry: docker.io                   # Docker Hub (build.yml publishes there)
  repository: guidedtraffic/quader       # the image of the release pipeline
  tag: ""                               # empty = chart appVersion
  digest: ""                            # example: sha256:<64 hex>; wins over tag
  pullPolicy: IfNotPresent

highAvailability:
  enforce: true                         # >= 2 replicas, a PDB and DoNotSchedule host spreading per role; Sentinel mode with >= 3 Sentinels

# ── api Deployment: quader serve --role api ───────────────────────
# The UI, the management API, the sign-in and the CI exchange; the login secrets mount here only.
api:
  replicaCount: 2                       # ignored when autoscaling.enabled
  minReadySeconds: 10
  revisionHistoryLimit: 5
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 1
      maxUnavailable: 0
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 120    # the UI's uploads and the audit exports
  spool:
    sizeLimit: 5Gi                      # holds the UI's uploads through the content route, up to config.ui.deploy.max_upload_bytes
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: 500m
      memory: 512Mi
      ephemeral-storage: 1Gi
    limits:
      memory: 1Gi                       # no CPU limit by default
  autoscaling:
    enabled: false
    minReplicas: 2
    maxReplicas: 4
    targetCPUUtilizationPercentage: 70
    targetMemoryUtilizationPercentage: 0  # 0 = no memory metric
    metrics: []                         # additional autoscaling/v2 metric specs
    behavior:
      scaleUp:
        stabilizationWindowSeconds: 0
        policies:
          - type: Pods
            value: 2
            periodSeconds: 60
      scaleDown:
        stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300
        policies:
          - type: Pods
            value: 1
            periodSeconds: 120
  podDisruptionBudget:
    enabled: true
    maxUnavailable: 1
    minAvailable: null                  # mutually exclusive with maxUnavailable
    unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy: AlwaysAllow
  topologySpread:
    enabled: true                       # render the two constraints below
    nodeTaintsPolicy: Honor             # cordoned nodes do not count as domains
    zone:
      maxSkew: 1
      whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
    host:
      maxSkew: 1
      whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule  # required with highAvailability.enforce
  topologySpreadConstraints: []         # non-empty replaces the generated constraints
  nodeFailureTolerationSeconds: 60      # not-ready/unreachable tolerations
  affinity: {}
  nodeSelector: {}                      # example: {kubernetes.io/arch: arm64}
  tolerations: []
  priorityClassName: ""                 # example: business-critical
  schedulerName: ""
  podAnnotations: {}
  podLabels: {}
  extraEnv: []                          # appended after the shared extraEnv
  pools: []                             # example: [{name: admin, paths: [/api/v1/projects], replicaCount: 2}]

# ── packages Deployment: quader serve --role packages ─────────────
# The package protocols and the raw file transfer, tokens only; no login secret mounts here.
packages:
  replicaCount: 3                       # ignored when autoscaling.enabled
  minReadySeconds: 10
  revisionHistoryLimit: 5
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 1
      maxUnavailable: 0
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 120
  spool:
    sizeLimit: ""                       # empty = spool.sizeLimit
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: "1"
      memory: 1Gi
      ephemeral-storage: 2Gi
    limits:
      memory: 2Gi                       # no CPU limit by default
  autoscaling:
    enabled: false
    minReplicas: 3
    maxReplicas: 8
    targetCPUUtilizationPercentage: 70
    targetMemoryUtilizationPercentage: 0  # 0 = no memory metric
    metrics: []                         # additional autoscaling/v2 metric specs
    behavior:
      scaleUp:
        stabilizationWindowSeconds: 0
        policies:
          - type: Pods
            value: 2
            periodSeconds: 60
      scaleDown:
        stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300
        policies:
          - type: Pods
            value: 1
            periodSeconds: 120
  podDisruptionBudget:
    enabled: true
    maxUnavailable: 1
    minAvailable: null                  # mutually exclusive with maxUnavailable
    unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy: AlwaysAllow
  topologySpread:
    enabled: true                       # render the two constraints below
    nodeTaintsPolicy: Honor             # cordoned nodes do not count as domains
    zone:
      maxSkew: 1
      whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
    host:
      maxSkew: 1
      whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule  # required with highAvailability.enforce
  topologySpreadConstraints: []         # non-empty replaces the generated constraints
  nodeFailureTolerationSeconds: 60      # not-ready/unreachable tolerations
  affinity: {}
  nodeSelector: {}                      # example: {kubernetes.io/arch: arm64}
  tolerations: []
  priorityClassName: ""                 # example: business-critical
  schedulerName: ""
  podAnnotations: {}
  podLabels: {}
  extraEnv: []                          # appended after the shared extraEnv
  pools: []                             # example: [{name: npm, paths: [/api/npm], replicaCount: 4}]

# ── worker Deployment: quader serve --role worker ─────────────────
worker:
  replicaCount: 2
  minReadySeconds: 10
  revisionHistoryLimit: 5
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 1
      maxUnavailable: 0
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 300    # jobs persist their cursor before exit
  spool:
    sizeLimit: 5Gi                      # also the working space of the image scanning's detection (config.vulnerabilities.images.scan_dir below this spool), admitted through the spool budget (sizeLimit minus spool.headroom): the unpacked database (1.6 GiB on 2026-11-10, validated with 2 GiB) and 512 MiB for the rest, validated for the pool that claims the queue vuln; the images are analysed in the scanner's spool (Q-HA-318). Workers spool only cache fills of jobs, the artifacts of a mirror pass (at most the background share B of a repository at a time, each up to the repository maxArtifactBytes), one advisory archive while a sync runs (config.vulnerabilities.sources.osv.max_archive_size, validated) and, from P1, the nuget-symbol-index job's one extracted PDB at a time (formats/nuget.md)
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: 500m
      memory: 512Mi
      ephemeral-storage: 1Gi
    limits:
      memory: 1Gi
  autoscaling:
    enabled: false
    minReplicas: 2
    maxReplicas: 4
    targetCPUUtilizationPercentage: 80
    targetMemoryUtilizationPercentage: 0
    metrics: []
    behavior: {}                        # Kubernetes defaults
  podDisruptionBudget:
    enabled: true
    maxUnavailable: 1
    minAvailable: null
    unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy: AlwaysAllow
  topologySpread:
    enabled: true
    nodeTaintsPolicy: Honor
    zone:
      maxSkew: 1
      whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
    host:
      maxSkew: 1
      whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule  # workers spread evenly; with nodes ≥ replicas no two share a node (INV-12)
  topologySpreadConstraints: []
  nodeFailureTolerationSeconds: 60
  affinity: {}
  nodeSelector: {}
  tolerations: []
  priorityClassName: ""
  schedulerName: ""
  podAnnotations: {}
  podLabels: {}
  extraEnv: []
  pools: []                             # example: [{name: vuln, queues: [vuln], replicaCount: 2}]; the main worker claims every queue no pool lists

# ── Trivy: the init container trivy of vuln-scanner-trivy, which copies the analyser into the pod (R-HA-070) ────
trivy:
  image: docker.io/aquasec/trivy:0.76.2@sha256:8f6bb947dbc528902e11f2f5be52f7b519f6a39d5d148f41166f2040499768fb  # the TRIVY_IMAGE of tools/versions.env, which a chart test holds it to: the publisher's multi-arch image; a mirror keeps the digest
  pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
  resources:                            # the copy of one binary of 163 MB (not measured)
    requests:
      cpu: 10m
      memory: 32Mi
    limits:
      memory: 128Mi

# ── vuln-scanner-trivy Deployment: quader serve --role scanner, Trivy (R-HA-065, Q-HA-372) ────
# The analysis of container images for the worker's image scanning, <fullname>-vuln-scanner-trivy; rendered while
# config.vulnerabilities.enabled and config.vulnerabilities.images.enabled are true. No secret of PostgreSQL, the object store or Valkey
# and no key ring mounts here.
vulnScannerTrivy:
  replicaCount: 2                       # ignored when autoscaling.enabled; the capacity is replicas × config.vulnerabilities.images.scanner.slots
  minReadySeconds: 10
  revisionHistoryLimit: 5
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 1
      maxUnavailable: 0
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 60     # an analysis still running at the shutdown timeout is killed and put off by the worker without an attempt
  spool:
    sizeLimit: 6Gi                      # the analyses, admitted through the budget (sizeLimit minus spool.headroom): per slot the largest image (config.vulnerabilities.images.max_image_size) plus 64 MiB, validated
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: 500m
      memory: 1Gi
      ephemeral-storage: 1280Mi         # 1 GiB and 256 MiB for the analyser's copy in trivy-bin (R-HA-070)
    limits:
      memory: 2Gi                       # one analyser per slot (config.vulnerabilities.images.memory_limit is its soft limit); an image that needs more ends this pod's analysis, never a worker
  database:                             # the container database, the loader of Trivy's database (R-HA-070, R-VULN-049)
    sizeLimit: 5Gi                      # the volume trivy-db and the loader's budget: the newest database and the one before it (1.7 GiB each on 2026-11-21); at least 4Gi, validated; follows spool.type
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: 50m
        memory: 64Mi
        ephemeral-storage: 2Gi          # one database on the node's disk
      limits:
        memory: 256Mi
  autoscaling:
    enabled: false
    minReplicas: 2
    maxReplicas: 4
    targetCPUUtilizationPercentage: 80
    targetMemoryUtilizationPercentage: 0
    metrics: []
    behavior: {}                        # Kubernetes defaults
  podDisruptionBudget:
    enabled: true
    maxUnavailable: 1
    minAvailable: null
    unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy: AlwaysAllow
  topologySpread:
    enabled: true
    nodeTaintsPolicy: Honor
    zone:
      maxSkew: 1
      whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
    host:
      maxSkew: 1
      whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
  topologySpreadConstraints: []
  nodeFailureTolerationSeconds: 60
  affinity: {}
  nodeSelector: {}
  tolerations: []
  priorityClassName: ""
  schedulerName: ""
  podAnnotations: {}
  podLabels: {}
  extraEnv: []

# ── ClamAV: the clamd container of malware-scanner-clamav and the freshclam container of malware-updater-freshclam ────
clamav:
  image: docker.io/clamav/clamav-debian:1.5.5_base@sha256:739c5ec70212e2d3e0c7719af2fba8776fb435f9932d7d3a3de2a95fcd6adde7  # the CLAMAV_IMAGE of tools/versions.env, which a chart test holds it to: ClamAV's own multi-arch image without a database
  pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
```
