```yaml
# ── malware-scanner-clamav Deployment: quader serve --role scanner of the kind clamav, clamd beside it (R-HA-068, Q-HA-372) ────
# <fullname>-malware-scanner-clamav, rendered while config.malware.enabled is true. The quader container reads one blob through the scan listener of packages and
# hands it to clamd over a Unix socket of the pod; clamd holds the signature database the quader container loaded. No secret of
# PostgreSQL, the object store or Valkey and no key ring mounts here, and none of the shared extras reaches it (Q-HA-321).
malwareScannerClamav:
  replicaCount: 2                       # ignored when autoscaling.enabled; the capacity is replicas × config.malware.scanner.slots
  minReadySeconds: 10
  revisionHistoryLimit: 5
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 1
      maxUnavailable: 0
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 60     # a scan still running at the shutdown timeout is answered scanner_draining and put off by the worker without an attempt
  spool:
    sizeLimit: 3Gi                      # the quader container's spool; the unpacking reads streams and writes nothing to it
  resources:                            # the quader container
    requests:
      cpu: 250m
      memory: 256Mi
      ephemeral-storage: 256Mi
    limits:
      memory: 512Mi
  clamd:
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: 500m
        memory: 1280Mi                  # measured: clamd holds 1.0 GiB resident with ClamAV's whole database, 1.1 GiB at its peak (Q-HA-361)
        ephemeral-storage: 1Gi
      limits:
        memory: 2Gi                     # at least 1.5Gi, checked: ConcurrentDatabaseReload is off, so a reload does not hold two databases
  database:
    sizeLimit: 1Gi                      # clamd-db: the version the quader container loaded and the next one while it loads
  clamdTmp:
    sizeLimit: 8Gi                      # clamd's temporary files; at least slots × (max_file_size + max_scan_size), checked
  autoscaling:
    enabled: false
    minReplicas: 2
    maxReplicas: 4
    targetCPUUtilizationPercentage: 80
    targetMemoryUtilizationPercentage: 0
    metrics: []
    behavior: {}                        # Kubernetes defaults
  podDisruptionBudget:
    enabled: true
    maxUnavailable: 1
    minAvailable: null
    unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy: AlwaysAllow
  topologySpread:
    enabled: true
    nodeTaintsPolicy: Honor
    zone:
      maxSkew: 1
      whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
    host:
      maxSkew: 1
      whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
  topologySpreadConstraints: []
  nodeFailureTolerationSeconds: 60
  affinity: {}
  nodeSelector: {}
  tolerations: []
  priorityClassName: ""
  schedulerName: ""
  podAnnotations: {}
  podLabels: {}
  extraEnv: []                          # the quader container's own; the shared extraEnv does not reach it

# ── malware-updater-freshclam Deployment: freshclam and quader serve --role scanner of the kind freshclam (R-HA-069, Q-HA-375) ────
# <fullname>-malware-updater-freshclam, rendered while config.malware.enabled is true and config.malware.database.source is updater. The one
# pod that reaches ClamAV's network: freshclam fetches whole signed containers, the quader container seeds its directory from the set in use
# and lists it for the worker, which takes each new set. No credential, no Secret but its TLS pair; an egress policy of the cluster admits it
# by a label of podLabels.
malwareUpdaterFreshclam:
  replicaCount: 1                       # at least 1; exempt from highAvailability.enforce: one fetcher per network (Q-HA-376)
  privateMirror: ""                     # an internal mirror of whole containers instead of ClamAV's network, rendered as PrivateMirror (R-MAL-012); example: https://clamav-mirror.example.com
  proxy: ""                             # an HTTP proxy for freshclam, rendered as HTTPProxyServer and HTTPProxyPort; example: http://proxy.example.com:3128
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
  resources:                            # the quader container
    requests:
      cpu: 50m
      memory: 64Mi
      ephemeral-storage: 64Mi
    limits:
      memory: 256Mi
  freshclam:
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: 50m
        memory: 128Mi
      limits:
        memory: 512Mi                   # TestDatabases no: freshclam does not load the database it fetched
  database:
    sizeLimit: 1Gi                      # freshclam-db: the containers (about 110 MiB) and freshclam's temporary copies
  affinity: {}
  nodeSelector: {}
  tolerations: []
  priorityClassName: ""
  podAnnotations: {}
  podLabels: {}                         # the label an egress policy of the cluster admits for the way to ClamAV's network
  extraEnv: []                          # the quader container's own; the shared extraEnv does not reach it

# ── Quader configuration (rendered to /etc/quader/quader.yaml) ─────────────────
# Chart-managed keys (secret file paths, storage.spool.dir, server.content_base_url) must not be set here (R-HA-029).
# One file serves every Deployment and Job; the role is the container argument --role.
# The hook ConfigMap of the migration Job carries the same file (R-HA-019); the restore Job mounts <fullname>-config.
config:
  server:                               # operations-and-observability.md
    base_url: ""                        # required; example: https://quader.example.com
    trusted_proxies: []                 # example: ["10.244.3.17", "10.244.5.9"] (the addresses of the ingress controller pods, never the whole pod CIDR; a prefix of length 0 is refused)
    forwarded_header: x-forwarded-for   # the one header the edge rewrites, x-forwarded-for | forwarded; the other is never read
    additional_base_urls: []
  health:                               # operations-and-observability.md
    require_object_store: false         # object storage gates only the first readiness (R-HA-008, Q-HA-1)
    shutdown_drain_delay: 5s            # default; must exceed the edge's endpoint removal time, measured at 0.2 to 1.8 s on the dev edge (Q-HA-111)
  metrics:                              # operations-and-observability.md
    enabled: true
    auth: none                          # none | static (needs secrets.metricsToken)
  log:
    level: info                         # operations-and-observability.md
  database:                             # this page
    host: ""                            # required; example: quader-db-rw.quader.svc, or the request pooler
    port: 5432
    session_host: ""                    # empty = host; required with pooler.mode transaction; example: quader-db-rw.quader.svc
    session_port: 0                     # 0 = port
    control_host: ""                    # empty = host; required with pooler.mode transaction (R-HA-058, Q-HA-20); example: quader-db-pooler-control.quader.svc
    control_port: 0                     # 0 = port
    control_name: ""                    # empty = name
    name: quader
    schema: quader
    backup_role: ""                     # empty = quader migrate grants no backup privileges; example: quader_backup (R-HA-014, R-BAK-015)
    ssl_mode: verify-full
    target_session_attrs: read-write
    connect_timeout: 5s
    pooler:
      mode: none                        # none | session | transaction (R-HA-058, Q-HA-6)
      server_connections: 0             # with transaction: the server-side total of the request and control poolers (R-HA-016); example: 100
    pool:
      max_conns: 20                     # at least 2, one is the control connection (R-HA-016)
      min_conns: 2
      max_conn_lifetime: 30m            # 5m recommended with a transaction-mode pooler
      max_conn_lifetime_jitter: 5m      # 1m recommended with a transaction-mode pooler
      max_conn_idle_time: 5m
      health_check_period: 30s
    lease_pool_size: 4
    lease_check_interval: 5s
    session:
      statement_timeout: 30s
      lock_timeout: 5s
      idle_in_transaction_session_timeout: 60s
      client_connection_check_interval: 1s
    request_statement_timeout: 5s
    retry:
      initial_backoff: 100ms
      max_backoff: 2s
      max_elapsed: 30s
    keepalive:
      idle: 15s
      interval: 5s
      count: 3
      user_timeout: 30s
    server_keepalive:                   # sent as tcp_keepalives_* startup parameters (R-HA-015)
      idle: 60s
      interval: 10s
      count: 6
    preflight:
      connection_budget: enforce        # enforce | warn
      reserved_connections: 10
      allow_superuser: false
  valkey:                               # this page
    mode: sentinel                      # sentinel | standalone (development only)
    sentinel:
      addresses: []                     # required; example: [quader-valkey-sentinel-0.quader-valkey-sentinel.quader.svc:26379, quader-valkey-sentinel-1.quader-valkey-sentinel.quader.svc:26379, quader-valkey-sentinel-2.quader-valkey-sentinel.quader.svc:26379]
      primary_name: ""                  # required; example: quader
      tls: true
      refresh_interval: 5s
    address: ""                         # standalone mode only; example: quader-valkey.quader.svc:6379
    database: 0
    key_prefix: "quader:"
    tls:
      mode: verify-full                 # verify-full | verify-ca | disable
      server_name: ""                   # host name of each address
    allow_insecure: false
    connect_timeout: 2s
    command_timeout: 500ms
    sentinel_query_timeout: 300ms
    max_conn_lifetime: 30m
    health_check_interval: 5s
    reconnect:
      initial_backoff: 100ms
      max_backoff: 5s
    circuit_breaker:
      failure_threshold: 5
      open_duration: 5s
  storage:                              # storage.md
    connections:                        # one to eight (storage.md R-STOR-050, R-HA-072); list order = write and read order; a list in the values replaces this one whole; an element is checked against the keys of R-STOR-050 (Q-HA-397)
      - id: default                     # an element without id is default, at most one may leave it out (Q-HA-394); never changes, never reused
        bucket: ""                      # required unless secrets.storageConnections[].bucketKey; example: quader-blobs
        prefix: quader                 # the default of storage.md; fixed once the connection holds data
        region: ""                      # example: eu-central-1
        endpoint: ""                    # AWS resolution; example: https://minio.quader.svc:9000 (a host without scheme means https)
        force_path_style: false         # true for MinIO, SeaweedFS and Ceph RGW
        credentials_source: default     # default | webIdentity | static (an entry of secrets.storageConnections with existingSecret)
        role_arn: ""                    # example (webIdentity): arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/quader-blobs
        encrypted: false                # true: Quader encrypts the connection's blobs and keeps the keys, so its provider reads ciphertext only; fixed once it holds data; keep the key ring and the export of the storage keys (storage.md R-STOR-075, R-STOR-090)
    upload:
      max_size: 10GiB                   # must fit the spool
    gc:
      grace_period: 24h                 # the default of storage.md; see R-HA-024
  jobs:
    schedule_tick: 10s
    lease_duration: 60s
    heartbeat_interval: 15s
    background_migrations:
      batch_size: 1000
      pause_between_batches: 100ms
  migrate:
    advisory_lock_wait: 5m              # also how long a migration waits for a backup's database phase (R-HA-019)
    ddl_lock_timeout: 5s
    ddl_lock_retries: 20
  backup:                               # backup-and-restore.md R-BAK-011 owns these keys; manual_run.* is chart-managed (R-HA-030)
    target:
      endpoint: ""                      # AWS resolution; example: https://s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com
      region: ""                        # example: eu-central-1
      bucket: ""                        # required with backup.enabled or restore.enabled; example: quader-backups
      prefix: quader
      force_path_style: false
      allow_insecure_endpoint: false
      ca_file: ""                       # system trust store
      storage_class: ""                 # bucket default; example: STANDARD_IA
      allow_same_bucket: false          # R-BAK-002, R-HA-060
      credentials:                      # same keys as storage.s3.credentials (R-STOR-031); the *_file keys are chart-managed (secrets.backupTarget, workload identity), not set here
        source: default                 # default | webIdentity | static (secrets.backupTarget)
        role_arn: ""                    # example: arn:aws:iam::210987654321:role/quader-backup-writer
        sts_endpoint: ""
      sse:
        mode: s3                        # s3 | kms | none (R-BAK-026)
        kms_key_id: ""                  # example: arn:aws:kms:eu-central-1:210987654321:key/9a8b…
        bucket_key: true
    database:
      parallel: 2                       # backup connections = 2 + parallel (R-HA-016)
      lock_timeout: 60s
      migration_wait: 15m               # below stall_timeout
      part_size: 16MiB
    copy:
      concurrency: 16
      server_side: auto                 # auto | always | never
      part_size: 256MiB
      check_existing: auto              # auto | always | never
      bytes_per_second: 0               # 0 = unlimited
    compression_level: 3                # zstd level 1–19
    exclude:
      remote_caches: false              # R-BAK-008
    retention:
      keep_last: 7                      # ≥ 1
      keep_within: 0s                   # count only; example: 720h
      sweep_interval: 168h              # full pool sweep (R-BAK-017)
    expected_interval: 24h              # drives QuaderBackupStale through its gauge (R-HA-045, R-BAK-014)
    lease_duration: 5m
    heartbeat_interval: 15s             # × 4 ≤ lease_duration
    stall_timeout: 30m                  # a run without progress cancels itself (R-BAK-013)
    finalize_timeout: 30s               # × 2 < lease_duration
    verify_sample: 1000
    run_history: 2160h                  # backup_run rows kept 90 days
    recovery_window: 0s                 # undeclared; example: 168h (R-HA-024)
    object_versioning: false
    revocation_journal:                 # R-HA-054 (MVP, Q-HA-9)
      enabled: true
      ship_interval: 5s
      replay_margin: 5m
  runtime:
    memory_limit_ratio: 0.85            # R-HA-036
  audit:                                # operations-and-observability.md R-OPS-015, R-OPS-017
    retention_days: 365                 # written to audit_policy by the migration Job (R-HA-014)
  auth:                                 # identity-and-authentication.md (OIDC providers, breakGlass.username, …)
    login_page:
      auto_redirect: true               # true: with exactly one OIDC provider the sign-in page goes straight to it; /ui/login?auto_sign_in=false still shows the page with the break-glass form. false: the page lists the providers
  authz: {}                             # empty; authorization.md
  ci: {}                                # empty; gitlab-ci-oidc.md
  # The signatures on artifacts (docs/spec/signatures.md R-SIG-040). Every key has a default and is rendered only when set here; the
  # chart reads enabled, which renders the four QuaderSignature* alerts. The anchors are declared in signatures.anchors (below
  # trustedCA), never here.
  # signatures:
  #   enabled: true                     # false: no signature is detected, checked or shown; the stored rows stay
  #   max_object_size: 256KiB           # largest signature object read, at most 1MiB
  #   trust_root:
  #     refresh: true                   # false: the release's snapshot of the public Sigstore root (no internet)
  #     url: https://tuf-repo-cdn.sigstore.dev   # or a TUF mirror of the company, https only
  # Quader's signing identity (docs/spec/signatures.md R-SIG-058). Every key has a default and is rendered only when set here; the
  # chart reads enabled, which renders the four QuaderSigning* alerts. The identity's files are the chart's (signing.identity below).
  # signing:
  #   enabled: true                     # false: Quader signs nothing, also with an identity
  #   identity:
  #     reload_interval: 1m             # how often a worker reads the identity's files again, 1s to 1h
  #     announce_period: 10m            # how long a new identity is listed before it signs; 0s: current at once
  ui:                                   # api-and-ui.md R-UI-225
    # The imprint and the privacy notice the installation serves itself (/ui/<locale>/legal/imprint and …/privacy), linked at the end
    # of every screen and of the sign-in screen. Markdown, at most 64 KiB per page and language, rendered at start under the README
    # sanitizer: no script, style or SVG, an image becomes a link. The operator answers for what the texts say. A language without a
    # text of its own shows the other one's; a page with neither has no link. Configuration, never a Secret: a change is a rollout.
    legal:
      imprint:
        en: ""                          # example: "Example Operations GmbH\\\nMusterstraße 1\\\n12345 Berlin\n\nMail: <legal@example.com>"
        de: ""                          # example: "Example Operations GmbH\\\nMusterstraße 1\\\n12345 Berlin"
      privacy:
        en: ""                          # example: "This installation records the address of every request for 30 days …"
        de: ""                          # example: "Diese Installation speichert die Adresse jeder Anfrage 30 Tage …"

# ── TLS on Quader's own listeners ────────────────────
# Every kind of pod (api, packages, worker, vuln-scanner-trivy, malware-scanner-clamav, malware-updater-freshclam) has a pair and a name of its own:
# <fullname>-<kind>.<namespace>.svc, and <fullname>-ops.<namespace>.svc for the scrape (R-HA-063). With tls.certManager the chart
# renders a cert-manager Certificate per kind into the Secret <fullname>-tls-<kind>; tls.existingSecrets names an existing Secret per
# kind instead. A pod mounts its kind's Secret only, as a directory volume without subPath, so a rotated Secret reaches its pods
# through the kubelet's atomic swap and the process reloads the files (tls.reloadInterval). tls.* configures the default client
# listener :8080 and the operations listener :8081; each entry of endpoints carries its own tls block.
tls:
  enabled: true                         # false = plain HTTP inside the cluster
  existingSecrets:                      # empty = the cert-manager Certificates below; else an existing Secret per kind with tls.crt, tls.key and ca.crt, one CA for all, a different Secret for each kind; the chart never creates them
    api: ""                             # example: quader-tls-api (names <fullname>-api.<namespace>.svc and <fullname>-ops.<namespace>.svc, usage server auth)
    packages: ""                        # example: quader-tls-packages (<fullname>-packages.<namespace>.svc and the ops name, server auth)
    worker: ""                          # example: quader-tls-worker (<fullname>-worker.<namespace>.svc and the ops name, server auth and client auth)
    vuln-scanner-trivy: ""              # example: quader-tls-vuln-scanner-trivy (<fullname>-vuln-scanner-trivy.<namespace>.svc and the ops name, server auth and client auth); needed while the image scanning is on
    malware-scanner-clamav: ""          # example: quader-tls-malware-scanner-clamav (<fullname>-malware-scanner-clamav.<namespace>.svc and the ops name, server auth and client auth); needed while the malware scanning is on
    malware-updater-freshclam: ""       # example: quader-tls-malware-updater-freshclam (<fullname>-malware-updater-freshclam.<namespace>.svc and the ops name, server and client auth)
  certManager:                          # the Certificate per kind the chart renders while existingSecrets is empty: <fullname>-tls-<kind>
    issuerRef:
      kind: ClusterIssuer               # ClusterIssuer | Issuer (an Issuer of the release namespace)
      name: ""                          # required with tls.enabled unless existingSecrets names a Secret per kind; example: cluster-ca
      group: cert-manager.io
    duration: 2160h                     # 90 days
    renewBefore: 720h                   # 30 days
    privateKey:
      algorithm: ECDSA                  # ECDSA | RSA; rotationPolicy is Always: a renewal changes the key too
      size: 256                         # ECDSA: 256 | 384; RSA: 2048 | 3072 | 4096
    extraDnsNames: []                   # names every pair carries besides its kind's, for a client that reaches a pod by port-forward; no check of the chart relies on them; example: [localhost]
    extraIpAddresses: []                # example: [127.0.0.1]
  minVersion: "1.2"                     # "1.2" | "1.3" (server.tls.min_version)
  reloadInterval: 10s                   # content poll of the mounted files (server.tls.reload_interval)
  clientCA:                             # optional mutual TLS: the edge must present a client certificate
    secretName: ""                      # empty = no client certificates requested; example: quader-edge-ca
    key: ca.crt                         # key of the CA bundle in that Secret
    auth: require                       # require | verify_if_given (server.tls.client_auth)
  backendTLSPolicy:                     # Gateway API: how the Gateway verifies quader (needs the BackendTLSPolicy CRD)
    enabled: false
    caConfigMapName: ""                 # required when enabled; example: quader-tls-ca (a ConfigMap with ca.crt: Gateway API takes no Secret here); each policy verifies its Service's kind name

# ── Existing Secrets (the chart never creates one) ──────────────────────────
secrets:
  database:
    existingSecret: ""                  # required; example: quader-db-app (CloudNativePG application Secret)
    usernameKey: username
    passwordKey: password
  databaseMigration:
    existingSecret: ""                  # empty = single-role mode; example: quader-db-owner
    usernameKey: username
    passwordKey: password
  databaseBackup:
    existingSecret: ""                  # empty = secrets.database (R-HA-014, R-HA-060); example: quader-db-backup
    usernameKey: username
    passwordKey: password
  databaseCA:
    existingSecret: ""                  # example: quader-db-ca (only ca.crt is projected)
    key: ca.crt
  databaseClientCert:
    existingSecret: ""                  # no client certificate
    certKey: tls.crt
    keyKey: tls.key
  storageConnections: []                # one entry per connection that needs a Secret (R-HA-072); each field a volume /var/run/secrets/quader/s3-<id>[-location|-ca|-backup|-journal]/; the *_file keys it sets must not be set in config (Q-HA-398); example:
  #  - connectionId: default            # matches config.storage.connections[].id; one entry per connection
  #    existingSecret: quader-s3        # the static credential (credentials_source static), or an S3 provisioner's Secret when a *Key is set; refused when nothing reads it (Q-HA-398)
  #    accessKeyIdKey: access-key-id    # example (provisioner Secret): AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
  #    secretAccessKeyKey: secret-access-key
  #    sessionTokenKey: ""              # empty = no session token
  #    bucketKey: ""                    # example (provisioner Secret): S3_BUCKET; set = the element's bucket_file, and the element has no bucket
  #    regionKey: ""                    # example: S3_REGION; set = region_file
  #    endpointKey: ""                  # example: S3_ENDPOINT (a host without scheme, which Quader reaches over https); set = endpoint_file
  #    ca: {existingSecret: "", key: ca.crt}               # the connection's ca_file, also in the backup pods; empty = the outbound trust store, or trustedCA with useForObjectStore
  #    backupSource: {existingSecret: "", accessKeyIdKey: access-key-id, secretAccessKeyKey: secret-access-key}   # backup pods only; read-only login, its element of backup.source.connections; required with credentials_source static while backup.enabled (R-BAK-030)
  #    journalReader: {existingSecret: "", accessKeyIdKey: access-key-id, secretAccessKeyKey: secret-access-key}  # post-restore and restore Jobs only; lists object versions (R-HA-023), its element of the credentials file; required in the entry of every connection without drain with journalCredentials.source static (Q-HA-399)
  valkey:
    existingSecret: ""                  # required; example: quader-valkey
    usernameKey: username               # a missing key = the "default" user
    passwordKey: password
  valkeySentinel:
    existingSecret: ""                  # Sentinels without authentication; example: quader-valkey-sentinel
    usernameKey: ""                     # empty = no Sentinel user, the file is not mounted
    passwordKey: password
  valkeyCA:
    existingSecret: ""                  # empty = system roots plus trustedCA; example: quader-valkey-ca
    key: ca.crt
  valkeyClientCert:
    existingSecret: ""                  # no client certificate; needed while Valkey keeps tls-auth-clients yes
    certKey: tls.crt
    keyKey: tls.key
  backupTarget:
    existingSecret: ""                  # required with config.backup.target.credentials.source static while backup.enabled or restore.enabled
    accessKeyIdKey: access-key-id
    secretAccessKeyKey: secret-access-key
    sessionTokenKey: ""                 # empty = no session token
  backupTargetCA:
    existingSecret: ""                  # empty = the system trust store; the backup and restore pods only; example: quader-backup-target-tls. Renders backup.target.ca_file (Q-HA-146)
    key: ca.crt
  oidc: []                              # example:
  #  - providerId: corp                 # example; matches config.auth.oidc.providers[].id
  #    existingSecret: quader-oidc-corp  # example
  #    key: client-secret               # example
  upstreamAccounts: {}                  # no account from the values (R-HA-073); example:
  #  docker-hub:                        # example; the key of a repository of the project upstream
  #    existingSecret: quader-upstream-docker-hub   # example
  #    authMode: basic                  # default; basic | bearer
  #    usernameKey: username            # default; basic only
  #    passwordKey: token               # example; default password
  breakGlass:
    existingSecret: ""                  # empty disables the break-glass account; example: quader-break-glass
    key: password                       # plaintext or Argon2id PHC hash
  encryption:
    existingSecret: ""                  # required; example: quader-encryption-keys
    keys: []                            # required; ordered, first = active; example: [2026-10.key, 2026-04.key]
  metricsToken:
    existingSecret: ""                  # needed with config.metrics.auth static
    key: token

trustedCA:
  existingSecret: ""                    # empty = no bundle; at most one of existingSecret and existingConfigMap; example: corp-ca-bundle
  existingConfigMap: ""                 # example: corp-ca-bundle (a trust-manager Bundle target)
  keys: [ca-bundle.crt]                 # the files of the source that are mounted, each a PEM bundle; they are added to config.proxy.outbound.tls.ca_files
  useForObjectStore: false              # true also sets the ca_file of every connection without its own ca (R-HA-072) to the one file of keys, for an S3-compatible store with a private CA; then it is that store's whole trust store

# ── Trust anchors of the signatures on artifacts (R-SIG-018) ──────────────────────
# Who the installation trusts as a signer, beside the shipped anchors and those an administrator adds in the UI. The chart renders
# the list into config.signatures.anchors; the migration Job (quader migrate) applies it on every install and upgrade with the scope
# configuration, removes an anchor taken out of it, and fails with the anchor's key and the reason when its material does not pass the
# checks (R-SIG-015). The API and the UI show these anchors read-only. Each entry has a key (^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$, at most 64
# characters, unique), a title (1 to 128 characters, the name shown at a signature), a kind (ca | openpgp | public-key | sigstore) and
# exactly the block of its kind. The material is public: inline, or <member>From.configMapKeyRef naming a key of a ConfigMap in the
# release namespace, which only the migration Job mounts, read-only, at /etc/quader/signature-anchors/<key>/. A Secret is not accepted.
# With migrations.mode disabled, whoever runs quader migrate provides those files. The default is no declaration; the tuning keys of
# the signatures are under config.signatures.
# signatures:
#   anchors:
#     - key: gitlab-ci-signing          # the company CA that signs the CI's images and packages
#       title: GitLab CI signing CA
#       kind: ca
#       ca:
#         certificatesFrom:             # or certificates: inline PEM, 1 to 16 certificates
#           configMapKeyRef: {name: company-ca, key: ca.crt}
#         use: codeSigning              # codeSigning (when left out) | timestamping (a timestamp authority's root, never a signer)
#         subject: {O: Example GmbH}    # optional: attributes O, OU, CN, C the signer's certificate must carry exactly
#         subjectAltNames: []           # optional: RE2 patterns, one of which an alternative name of the signer must match
#     - key: release-key                # an OpenPGP key that signs Debian repositories or files
#       title: Release signing key
#       kind: openpgp
#       openpgp:
#         keysFrom:                     # or keys: inline, 1 to 32 armored public certificates
#           configMapKeyRef: {name: release-keys, key: release.asc}
#     - key: npm-mirror-keys            # raw public keys, such as an npm registry's signing keys
#       title: npm mirror signing keys
#       kind: public-key
#       publicKey:
#         keys:                         # 1 to 16
#           - pem: |                    # or pemFrom.configMapKeyRef
#               -----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----
#               ...
#               -----END PUBLIC KEY-----
#             keyid: "SHA256:jl3bwswu80PjjokCgh0o2w5c2U4LhQAE57gj9cz1kzA"   # optional: npm's keyid
#             expires: "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z"   # optional: when the key stops signing, RFC 3339
#     - key: company-sigstore           # a Sigstore identity: who signed keyless, under which issuer
#       title: Company Sigstore
#       kind: sigstore
#       sigstore:
#         issuer: https://gitlab.example.com
#         identityPattern: "^https://gitlab.example.com/platform/.+//\\.gitlab-ci\\.yml@refs/heads/main$"   # or identity: an exact value
#         trustRoot: own                # public: the shipped public Sigstore root (when no trusted root is given) | own: the company's
#         trustedRootFrom:              # or trustedRoot: inline trusted_root.json, at most 1 MiB
#           configMapKeyRef: {name: company-sigstore-root, key: trusted_root.json}

# ── Bastions declared in the values (docs/spec/bastion.md R-BAS-127) ────────────────────
# A Bastion registration that exists because the values say so, also after a fresh database. The chart renders the list into
# config.bastions.declared; the migration Job (quader migrate) applies it on every install and upgrade: it creates a missing
# registration, makes its description, egress and token follow the entry, replaces the token when the Secret holds another value (a
# rotation is a change of the Secret and a rollout), and of a registration taken out of the list revokes the declared token and keeps
# the registration. Limits, presets, switches and tokens issued on the screen stay an administrator's; after a fresh database they are
# the registration's defaults again. The Bastions page shows the entry's members read-only. The token comes from an existing Secret of
# the release namespace: the same value the Bastion's chart reads from secrets.mainToken. Only the migration Job mounts it, read-only,
# at /var/run/secrets/quader/bastion-tokens/<name>/token; the database keeps its hash, as it does of every token. The value is a Bastion
# token (qdr_bst_, 57 characters with its checksum); a random string of a secret generator is refused, because the Bastion and the main
# installation both check the format before anything else. Make one with `quader admin bastion token generate` (needs no database:
# kubectl exec into an api pod, or run the image) or with the Bastions page's Issue token, and put it into the Secret of both releases.
# A missing Secret or a value that is not a Bastion token stops the migration Job with the entry's name. With migrations.mode disabled,
# whoever runs quader migrate provides the file.
bastions:
  declared: []                          # no declaration; example:
  #  - name: partners                   # the registration's name: ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,19}$, unique
  #    description: Partner access      # optional
  #    egress: [10.252.0.0/16]          # the networks the Bastion connects from, CIDR or single addresses; optional
  #    token:
  #      existingSecret: quader-bastion-token   # required; the Secret the Bastion's chart names in secrets.mainToken
  #      key: token                     # default token

# ── Quader's signing identity (R-HA-071, docs/spec/signatures.md R-SIG-046) ──────────────
# One identity per installation: an ECDSA P-256 key with a code-signing certificate of the company's CA, with which Quader signs as a
# registry and issues its attestations. At most one source. The Secret (tls.crt: the leaf and its intermediates, tls.key: the key,
# ca.crt: the root) reaches the worker pods only, mounted at /var/run/secrets/quader/signing/; config.signing.identity.cert_file,
# key_file and ca_file are set by the chart. A renewal reaches the workers without a restart and is announced before it signs
# (config.signing.identity.announce_period). Without either source an administrator creates the identity in the admin area
# (Admin area › Settings › Signatures). The tuning keys are under config.signing.
signing:
  identity:
    existingSecret: ""                  # example: quader-signing (tls.crt: leaf and intermediates, tls.key: ECDSA P-256, ca.crt: the root; code signing, a URI as alternative name)
    certManager:                        # the Certificate <fullname>-signing the chart renders while issuerRef.name is set
      issuerRef:
        kind: ClusterIssuer             # ClusterIssuer | Issuer (an Issuer of the release namespace)
        name: ""                        # empty = no Certificate; example: company-code-signing
        group: cert-manager.io
      commonName: Quader signing
      subject: {}                       # example: {organizations: [Example GmbH], countries: [DE]}
      uris: []                          # besides config.server.base_url, which is always the first; example: [https://quader.example.com/signing]
      duration: 2160h                   # 90 days
      renewBefore: 720h                 # 30 days; the key is ECDSA P-256 with rotationPolicy Always, not a value

bootstrap:
  existingConfigMap: ""                 # configuration documents (P1)

# ── Pod identity and security ──────────────────────────────────────────────
serviceAccount:
  create: true
  name: ""                              # <fullname>
  annotations: {}                       # example (IRSA):
  #  eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/quader-s3  # example
  automountServiceAccountToken: false   # Quader never calls the Kubernetes API

podSecurityContext:
  runAsNonRoot: true
  runAsUser: 65532                      # null on OpenShift (restricted-v2 assigns the UID)
  runAsGroup: 65532                     # null on OpenShift
  fsGroup: 65532                        # null on OpenShift
  fsGroupChangePolicy: OnRootMismatch
  seccompProfile:
    type: RuntimeDefault

securityContext:
  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
  privileged: false
  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
  runAsNonRoot: true
  capabilities:
    drop: [ALL]
  seccompProfile:
    type: RuntimeDefault

# ── Volumes: nothing ReadWriteMany, nothing persistent ─────────────────────
spool:
  type: emptyDir                        # emptyDir | ephemeral
  sizeLimit: 20Gi                       # api.spool, packages.spool and worker.spool override it
  headroom: 2GiB                        # sizeLimit - headroom = storage.spool.max_bytes
  medium: ""                            # node disk; "Memory" counts against the memory limit
  ephemeral:
    storageClassName: ""                # cluster default
    size: 50Gi                          # used with type ephemeral
    accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]        # ReadWriteOnce | ReadWriteOncePod; nothing else validates

tmp:
  sizeLimit: 1Gi                        # /tmp under readOnlyRootFilesystem

# ── Probes ────────────────────────────────
probes:
  startup:
    enabled: true
    path: /healthz
    periodSeconds: 2
    timeoutSeconds: 2
    failureThreshold: 60                # 2 minutes to bind the listeners
    custom: {}                          # replaces the generated probe
  liveness:
    enabled: true
    path: /healthz
    periodSeconds: 10
    timeoutSeconds: 3
    failureThreshold: 6
    custom: {}
  readiness:
    enabled: true
    path: /readyz
    periodSeconds: 5
    timeoutSeconds: 3
    failureThreshold: 1                 # debouncing happens in the process (health.failure_threshold)
    successThreshold: 1
    custom: {}

# ── Exposure ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
service:
  type: ClusterIP                       # ClusterIP | LoadBalancer | NodePort
  port: 8080
  opsPort: 8081
  # No sessionAffinity value: the client Service always renders sessionAffinity: None (R-HA-037).
  annotations: {}
  labels: {}
  loadBalancerSourceRanges: []
  externalTrafficPolicy: ""             # Kubernetes default; example: Local
  ipFamilyPolicy: ""                    # cluster default; example: PreferDualStack (R-HA-044)
  ipFamilies: []                        # example: [IPv6, IPv4]

ingress:
  enabled: false
  className: ""                         # cluster default IngressClass; example: traefik
  annotations: {}                       # controller-specific settings; never cookie affinity
  labels: {}
  hosts: []                             # empty = host of config.server.base_url
  # No path value: every host gets the fixed path rules of R-HA-037 (Prefix rules per route family onto <fullname>-api and
  # <fullname>-packages).
  tls: []                               # example: [{secretName: quader-tls, hosts: [quader.example.com]}]
  backendTLS:                           # how the controller reaches quader when tls.enabled; quader speaks HTTPS, so the controller must too
    controller: haproxy                 # haproxy (HAProxy Ingress, the primary target) | traefik | ingress-nginx | manual (you set the backend protocol in ingress.annotations / service.annotations)
    verify: true                        # the controller verifies each backend under its kind's name, <fullname>-api.<namespace>.svc or <fullname>-packages.<namespace>.svc (R-HA-063); traefik needs serversTransports; false = encrypted but unverified
    caSecret: ""                        # haproxy, ingress-nginx: empty = the Secret of the pair the backend serves (its kind's, or a further endpoint's own), whose ca.crt the controller reads; example: quader-internal-ca
    clientCertSecret: ""                # haproxy: Secret with tls.crt and tls.key that HAProxy Ingress presents to Quader (required with tls.clientCA); example: quader-edge-client
    serversTransports:                  # traefik: a ServersTransport per kind, reference <namespace>-<name>@kubernetescrd, with that kind's name as serverName; required with verify on traefik
      api: ""                           # example: quader-quader-api@kubernetescrd
      packages: ""                      # example: quader-quader-packages@kubernetescrd

gateway:
  enabled: false
  parentRefs: []                        # example: [{name: shared, namespace: gateway-system, sectionName: https}]
  hostnames: []                         # empty = host of config.server.base_url
  annotations: {}
  labels: {}
  timeouts:
    request: 3600s                      # R-HA-039
    backendRequest: 3600s
  filters: []                           # HTTPRoute filters on every path rule of R-HA-037
  extraRules: []
  create:                               # P1 (R-HA-053)
    enabled: false                      # attach to an existing Gateway
    gatewayClassName: ""                # example: envoy-gateway
    listeners: []                       # example: [{name: https, protocol: HTTPS, port: 443, tls: {certificateRefs: [{name: quader-tls}]}}]

endpoints: {}                           # only the default endpoint; every key in endpoints.md

contentOrigin:                          # P1 (R-HA-055); renders config.server.content_base_url (R-ARCH-029)
  host: ""                              # empty = one origin (R-ARCH-007); example: quader-content.example.net
  tls:
    secretName: ""                      # no TLS entry of its own; example: quader-content-tls

# ── Network policy: ingress rules only, one policy per Deployment, each rule with its port ─
networkPolicy:
  enabled: true
  ingress:
    http:
      from: []                          # empty = from anywhere; example: [{namespaceSelector: {matchLabels: {kubernetes.io/metadata.name: ingress}}}]
    ops:
      from:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: monitoring
    probeCIDRs: []                      # node CIDRs, for CNIs that apply policy to kubelet probes
  # No egress value: the chart renders ingress rules only, each with its port (R-HA-042, ADR-154).

# ── Monitoring ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
metrics:
  serviceMonitor:
    enabled: false
    namespace: ""                       # release namespace
    interval: 30s
    scrapeTimeout: 10s
    labels: {}                          # example: {release: kube-prometheus-stack}
    relabelings: []                     # appended after the fixed role and pool relabelings (R-HA-045)
    metricRelabelings: []
  prometheusRule:
    enabled: false
    labels: {}
    disabledAlerts: []                  # example: [QuaderSpoolNearlyFull]
    extraRules: []

# ── Migrations and restore ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
migrations:
  mode: hook                            # hook | disabled
  backoffLimit: 2
  activeDeadlineSeconds: 1800
  ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 86400
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: 100m
      memory: 128Mi
    limits:
      memory: 512Mi
  podAnnotations: {}
  extraEnv: []

postRestore:
  hold: false                           # R-HA-025 step 1: every role and pool may be at zero (replicaCount 0 and autoscaling off are required), the backup CronJob is suspended, no Job is rendered
  enabled: false                        # renders the post-restore hook Job once
  restoredTo: ""                        # required with enabled, the time t the platform restore went to, RFC 3339; example: "2026-10-28T09:15:00Z"
  skipRevocationJournal: false          # only when the source's bucket is gone (R-BAK-024)
  journalCredentials:
    source: runtime                     # runtime (the blob store's credential, a plain listing) | default (the identity of the Job's ServiceAccount lists object versions) | static (the `journalReader` of each entry of secrets.storageConnections, R-HA-072) (Q-HA-150)
  backoffLimit: 2                       # a retry applies the clean-up again; its steps are safe to repeat
  activeDeadlineSeconds: 0              # 0 = not rendered
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 60     # at least 30
  serviceAccount:
    create: true
    name: ""                            # <fullname>-post-restore
    annotations: {}                     # example (IRSA, with s3:ListBucketVersions on the blob bucket when journalCredentials.source is default): {eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/quader-post-restore"}
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: 100m
      memory: 128Mi
    limits:
      memory: 512Mi
  podAnnotations: {}                    # safe-to-evict: "false" is always added
  extraEnv: []
  extraVolumes: []                      # the post-restore Job's own, like extraEnv: it holds the owner login, the blob store and the journal reader, never the target (R-BAK-015); see backup.extraVolumes
  extraVolumeMounts: []

# ── Backup CronJob and restore Job (R-HA-060, backup-and-restore.md R-BAK-012) ──
backup:
  enabled: false                        # true turns the backup on and then needs config.backup.target.bucket (Q-HA-17)
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  timeZone: Etc/UTC
  suspend: false                        # rendered true while restore.enabled
  adoptTarget: false                    # adds --adopt-target after a restore (R-BAK-002)
  startingDeadlineSeconds: 3600
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  backoffLimit: 2                       # evictions are not counted (podFailurePolicy)
  activeDeadlineSeconds: 0              # 0 = not rendered
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 60
  tmpSizeLimit: 256Mi                   # the only volume the chart adds (R-HA-061); the commands use at most 64 MiB (R-BAK-012), the rest keeps the kubelet's sizeLimit eviction away
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: 500m
      memory: 256Mi
    limits:
      memory: 1Gi
  serviceAccount:
    create: true
    name: ""                            # <fullname>-backup
    annotations: {}                     # example (IRSA, read on the blob bucket, write on the target):
    #  eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/quader-backup  # example
  nodeSelector: {}
  tolerations: []
  affinity: {}
  priorityClassName: ""
  podAnnotations: {}                    # cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict: "false" is always added (R-BAK-012)
  podLabels: {}
  extraEnv: []
  extraVolumes: []                      # the backup pod's own, like extraEnv: the global extraVolumes reach the Deployments only (Q-HA-149); a file the configuration names (proxy.outbound.tls.ca_files) must exist here
  extraVolumeMounts: []

restore:
  enabled: false                        # renders the restore Job, no migration Job, a suspended CronJob (Q-HA-18)
  backupId: ""                          # required with enabled; example: 20261028T020000Z-7f3a
  skipRevocationJournal: false          # only when the source bucket is gone (R-BAK-024, H-37)
  extraArgs: []                         # example: [--check] for a dry run of the preconditions (R-BAK-020)
  journalCredentials:
    source: runtime                     # runtime (the blob store's credential, a plain listing) | default (the identity of the Job's ServiceAccount lists object versions) | static (the `journalReader` of each entry of secrets.storageConnections, R-HA-072); anything but runtime keeps a deletion with the runtime credential from hiding a journal entry (R-BAK-015, Q-HA-159)
  backoffLimit: 2                       # evictions are not counted, every retry resumes (R-BAK-021)
  activeDeadlineSeconds: 0              # 0 = not rendered
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 60     # at least 30; time to stop at the next safe point (Q-HA-147)
  serviceAccount:
    create: true
    name: ""                            # <fullname>-restore
    annotations: {}                     # example (IRSA, read on the target, write on the new blob prefix, read on the source journal):
    #  eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/quader-restore  # example
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: "1"
      memory: 1Gi
    limits:
      memory: 2Gi
  podAnnotations: {}                    # safe-to-evict: "false" is always added, as for backup pods
  extraEnv: []
  extraVolumes: []                      # the restore Job's own, like extraEnv; see backup.extraVolumes
  extraVolumeMounts: []

# ── Extension points ────────────────────────────────────────────
extraEnv: []                            # example: [{name: QUADER_LOG_LEVEL, value: debug}]
extraEnvFrom: []
extraVolumes: []                        # the operator's, for the Deployments only (the Jobs take backup.extraVolumes and restore.extraVolumes, Q-HA-149); the chart's volume check cannot see a claim's access mode
extraVolumeMounts: []
initContainers: []                      # run before Quader starts
sidecars: []                            # native sidecars (restartPolicy: Always) allowed
lifecycle: {}                           # none; Quader drains itself (R-HA-011)
extraObjects: []                        # extra manifests rendered with tpl
```

</details>

Acceptance criteria:

- `helm show values deploy/helm/quader` equals this block, except for formatting. A CI test
  compares the key sets.
- `helm template` with only the required values set (`config.server.base_url`,
  `config.database.host`, `config.storage.connections`, `config.valkey.sentinel.addresses`,
  `config.valkey.sentinel.primary_name`, `secrets.database.existingSecret`,
  `secrets.valkey.existingSecret`, `secrets.encryption.existingSecret`, `secrets.encryption.keys`)
  renders without error. `config.backup.target.bucket` is not among them: it is required only with
  `backup.enabled` or `restore.enabled` (Q-HA-17).

### R-HA-032 · Replicas, disruption budget, spreading and autoscaling
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: HA-009, HA-032, HA-043, HA-044

- **Replicas.** Defaults: 2 for `api`, 3 for `packages`, 2 for `worker` and 2 for each scanner, `vuln-scanner-trivy` and
  `malware-scanner-clamav` (Q-HA-16, Q-HA-75, Q-HA-316; before
  phase 6a 3 for `web`); at least 2 per role and pool with `highAvailability.enforce` (INV-12). The drain rule of R-HA-059 sets the real minimum: the
  replicas that carry the peak plus the PDB's `maxUnavailable`. When autoscaling is enabled, the
  Deployment's `replicas` field is omitted, so `helm upgrade` does not reset the autoscaler's
  choice, and `minReplicas` follows the drain rule.
- **Disruption budget.** One `policy/v1` PodDisruptionBudget per Deployment (every role, every pool) with
  `maxUnavailable: 1` and `unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy: AlwaysAllow` (R-HA-008). `maxUnavailable`
  scales with the replica count, whereas `minAvailable: 1` with one replica would block every
  drain. Backup and restore pods have none (R-HA-060).
- **Spreading.** Two topology spread constraints per Deployment (every role, every pool), rendered unless replaced
  ([topology spread](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/topology-spread-constraints/)):
  - `topology.kubernetes.io/zone`, `maxSkew: 1`, `ScheduleAnyway`;
  - `kubernetes.io/hostname`, `maxSkew: 1`, `DoNotSchedule`, for both roles, so that a role's
    replicas spread evenly over the nodes: the replica counts of any two eligible nodes differ by
    at most one, so with at least as many schedulable nodes as replicas no two share a node, and with at least
    two nodes one node loss never takes a whole role (INV-12).

  Both use `matchLabelKeys: [pod-template-hash]`, so the skew is computed per ReplicaSet and a
  rollout does not pile new pods onto the nodes the old ones leave. Both use
  `nodeTaintsPolicy: Honor`, so a cordoned node does not count as a domain and the replacement of
  an evicted pod can schedule (R-HA-059). Single-node development clusters set
  `host.whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway` and `highAvailability.enforce: false`.
- **Node loss.** Tolerations for `node.kubernetes.io/not-ready` and `node.kubernetes.io/unreachable`
  with `tolerationSeconds` from the role's `nodeFailureTolerationSeconds` (60) replace the default
  of 300 s
  ([taint-based evictions](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/taint-and-toleration/#taint-based-evictions)).
  Replicas are stateless, so recreating them early costs nothing.
- **Autoscaling.** `autoscaling/v2` per Deployment: `api` and `packages` on CPU (default target 70 %; `minReplicas` 2 and
  3, `maxReplicas` 4 and 8), `worker` and each worker pool on CPU (80 %), optional memory and custom metrics. A pool has
  an autoscaler of its own from its overrides. Scale-down is slow (one pod per 2 minutes after a
  5-minute stabilization window), because every removed pod drains its uploads, as in a node drain.
  Scaling raises the database connection demand: the budget (R-HA-016) uses `maxReplicas`, so it
  must be raised before `maxReplicas` is, unless the transaction-mode pooler carries the main pool
  (R-HA-058).
- **Placement controls.** `nodeSelector`, `tolerations`, `affinity`, `priorityClassName`,
  `schedulerName` are passed through unchanged, per role.

Acceptance criteria:

- On a three-node kind cluster with three zones labeled, three `packages` replicas land on three nodes
  and two `api` and two `worker` replicas on two each. `kubectl drain` of one node keeps at least two `packages` replicas
  and one `api` replica serving at all times, and the replacement of every evicted pod becomes ready on the remaining
  nodes. The same drain with `nodeTaintsPolicy: Ignore` leaves the `packages` replacement `Pending`,
  which documents why the value is set.
- With autoscaling enabled, a CPU load test of package downloads raises the `packages` replica count to `maxReplicas` while
  the `api` replica count stays at its minimum, and a following `helm upgrade` with unchanged values resets neither.

### R-HA-033 · Pod and container security
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: HA-045

- Pods run with the values' `podSecurityContext` and `securityContext`:
  - non-root UID/GID 65532;
  - `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`;
  - no privilege escalation;
  - all capabilities dropped;
  - seccomp `RuntimeDefault`.

  This satisfies the Kubernetes *restricted* Pod Security Standard
  ([Pod Security Standards](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/)).
  The namespace can therefore enforce `pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted`.
- Writable paths are only the spool (`/var/lib/quader/spool`, `web` and `worker`) and `/tmp` (an
  `emptyDir` with `tmp.sizeLimit`, in backup and restore pods `backup.tmpSizeLimit`). `TMPDIR`
  points to `/tmp`. The backup CronJob, the restore Job and the migration Job run with the same
  security contexts as the Deployments.
- The image is a minimal non-root base with CA certificates and time-zone data, no shell and no
  package manager. Debugging uses ephemeral debug containers. `quader admin` subcommands run with
  `kubectl exec` (no shell needed).
- `automountServiceAccountToken: false`: Quader never calls the Kubernetes API. Workload identity
  for S3 does not depend on the token mount. Both the IRSA webhook and EKS Pod Identity inject their
  own projected token volume.
- No RBAC Role or RoleBinding is rendered.
- OpenShift: the `restricted-v2` security context constraint assigns UIDs from a namespace range.
  There, `runAsUser`, `runAsGroup` and `fsGroup` are set to `null`, and everything else stays.
  The image works with an arbitrary UID in group 0 for its files.
- `extraObjects`, `initContainers` and `sidecars` may run with their own security contexts. The
  chart does not weaken Quader's container for them.

Acceptance criteria:

- `kubectl label ns quader pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=restricted` followed by
  `helm install` succeeds, and all pods start.
- `kubectl exec <pod> -- touch /x` fails with a read-only file system error.

### R-HA-034 · Probes
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: HA-046

| Probe | Endpoint (R-OPS-001) | Period / timeout / threshold | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| startup | `GET :8081/healthz` | 2 s / 2 s / 60 | Holds off liveness until the listeners are bound. Startup work that takes longer (waiting for the schema) keeps the process alive and reports not ready instead |
| liveness | `GET :8081/healthz` | 10 s / 3 s / 6 | One minute of a stuck process before a restart; never tied to dependencies (R-HA-008) |
| readiness | `GET :8081/readyz` | 5 s / 3 s / 1 | The process debounces its checks (`health.failure_threshold`), so the probe removes a pod as soon as the process says so, which matters most for the drain |

- Each probe can be disabled or replaced (`probes.<name>.custom`).
- Probes use HTTPS on the operations port when `tls.enabled` is `true` (R-HA-063); plain HTTP only when it is `false`. The port is not exposed through Ingress or Gateway
  (R-HA-037), and NetworkPolicy restricts it (R-HA-042).

Acceptance criteria: the probe settings render as in the table. R-HA-008's tests pass with them.

### R-HA-035 · Spool and temporary volumes
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: HA-005

- The spool (R-STOR-004) is an `emptyDir` at `/var/lib/quader/spool` with `sizeLimit` from the
  role's or pool's `spool.sizeLimit` (`api.spool.sizeLimit`, `packages.spool.sizeLimit`, `worker.spool.sizeLimit`,
  falling back to `spool.sizeLimit`). With `spool.type: ephemeral` it is a generic ephemeral volume (a per-pod
  PersistentVolumeClaim deleted with the pod) of `spool.ephemeral.size`
  ([ephemeral volumes](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/ephemeral-volumes/)), for nodes
  whose local disk is too small. Its access mode is `ReadWriteOnce` or `ReadWriteOncePod`, never
  shared (R-HA-061).
- The spool is scratch space for the request or job that is running and nothing else (INV-18).
  Nothing in it outlives that request: a multi-request upload keeps its parts in S3 multipart
  uploads and its state in PostgreSQL ([storage.md](storage.md)), so the next request of the same
  upload may reach another replica, and a lost pod loses no acknowledged data.
- The kubelet evicts a pod whose `emptyDir` exceeds its `sizeLimit`. The process must reject uploads
  before that point. The chart therefore sets `storage.spool.max_bytes = <role's sizeLimit> −
  spool.headroom` per Deployment, as the environment variable `QUADER_STORAGE_SPOOL_MAX_BYTES`,
  unless `config.storage.spool.max_bytes` is set. R-STOR-004's admission keeps the spool below its
  budget, so eviction never happens through uploads.
- Sizing: `spool.sizeLimit ≥ concurrent spooled uploads per pod × p95 upload size + headroom`, and
  at least `storage.upload.max_size + headroom` for `packages` (validated, R-HA-029). An `api` pod spools only the UI's
  uploads through the content route of [api-and-ui.md](api-and-ui.md) R-API-025, bounded by
  `ui.deploy.max_upload_bytes` (Q-UI-106), so its spool needs that bound plus headroom. Remote-cache fills use the
  spool too (R-STOR-004). Example: 20 concurrent uploads of 500 MB, plus 2 GiB, needs about 12 GiB.
  A `worker` pod spools only the cache fills of jobs and, from P1, the `nuget-symbol-index` job,
  which spools one extracted PDB at a time ([formats/nuget.md](formats/nuget.md) R-NUGET-021), so
  its default is smaller.
- A `worker` spool also holds one advisory archive while a sync runs ([vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md)
  R-VULN-025), and so does the spool of a worker pool that claims the queue `vuln`: the chart refuses such a spool budget (size minus `spool.headroom`) below
  `config.vulnerabilities.sources.osv.max_archive_size` while the scanning is enabled and the OSV source is `online` or
  `repository`, and the failure names both values. The spool of the worker that claims `vuln` also holds the image scanning's
  unpacked database and a detection's 64 MiB, and the chart refuses its budget below 2 GiB + 512 MiB while the image scanning is on
  (Q-HA-318).
- The spool of `vuln-scanner-trivy` holds the analyses: per slot the compressed size of the image plus 64 MiB. The chart refuses its
  spool budget (`vulnScannerTrivy.spool.sizeLimit` minus `spool.headroom`) below `slots × (max_image_size + 64 MiB)` of
  `config.vulnerabilities.images` and names the three values (R-HA-065, Q-HA-318).
- `resources.requests.ephemeral-storage` should cover the expected steady use, not the limit, so
  pods schedule on ordinary nodes. The `sizeLimit` caps the worst case.
- `medium: Memory` is allowed but counts against the memory limit. It is meant for small,
  latency-critical installations only.

Acceptance criteria:

- With `spool.sizeLimit: 3Gi` and `headroom: 1GiB`, 3 concurrent 1 GiB uploads: two succeed and the
  third receives `503` with `Retry-After` (or succeeds after a retry). The pod is never evicted
  (`kubectl get events` shows no eviction).
- `helm template … --set spool.sizeLimit=5Gi --set config.storage.upload.max_size=10GiB` fails.

### R-HA-061 · Volumes: nothing shared, nothing persistent
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: HA-005

No ReadWriteMany storage class can be assumed (owner constraint, INV-13). Quader needs none: no pod
mounts a volume that another pod writes, and no pod keeps data on a volume beyond its own life.
Every volume the chart renders:

| Pods | Mount | Volume | Access | Lifetime |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `api`, `packages`, `worker`, `vuln-scanner-trivy`, `malware-scanner-clamav` | `/var/lib/quader/spool` | `emptyDir` (default) or a generic ephemeral volume (R-HA-035) | node-local, or one ReadWriteOnce (or ReadWriteOncePod) claim per pod | the pod |
| every Quader pod | `/tmp` | `emptyDir` with `tmp.sizeLimit` (backup and restore pods: `backup.tmpSizeLimit`, because they stream, R-BAK-012) | node-local | the pod |
| every Quader pod | `/etc/quader/quader.yaml` | ConfigMap | read-only projection | — |
| every Quader pod but the scanners | `/var/run/secrets/quader/…`, `/etc/quader/ca/` | Secret or ConfigMap projections (R-HA-030) | read-only projection | — |
| `vuln-scanner-trivy`, `malware-scanner-clamav`, `malware-updater-freshclam` | `/var/run/secrets/quader/tls/` (`tls.crt`, `tls.key` and `ca.crt` of the unit's own Secret, R-HA-063); nothing else | Secret projection (R-HA-065, R-HA-068, R-HA-069) | read-only projection | — |
| `malware-updater-freshclam` | `/var/lib/clamav` (`freshclam-db`, both containers) | `emptyDir`, `malwareUpdaterFreshclam.database.sizeLimit` (R-HA-069) | node-local | the pod |

- The chart renders no PersistentVolumeClaim, no StatefulSet and no `volumeClaimTemplates`. A
  generic ephemeral volume is a claim that Kubernetes creates for one pod and deletes with it
  ([generic ephemeral volumes](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/ephemeral-volumes/#generic-ephemeral-volumes)).
  `values.schema.json` admits only `ReadWriteOnce` and `ReadWriteOncePod` as its access modes
  (R-HA-029).
- Nothing the services need is on a Quader volume: PostgreSQL holds metadata, S3 holds blobs,
  backups and the revocation journal, Valkey holds ephemeral state (INV-3, INV-4, INV-18).
- Dependencies outside the chart: PostgreSQL instances use one ReadWriteOnce claim each, owned by
  their operator (CloudNativePG: one per instance); Valkey and its Sentinels need no claim, because
  Valkey's content may be lost (R-HA-056); the S3 store is the platform's. Draining a node that
  holds a PostgreSQL instance follows R-HA-059.
- `extraVolumes` belong to the operator. The chart cannot see the access mode of a claim they
  reference, so this requirement covers the volumes the chart renders.

Acceptance criteria:

- For every value set in `ci/`, `helm template` output contains no `ReadWriteMany` or
  `ReadOnlyMany`, no `kind: PersistentVolumeClaim`, no `kind: StatefulSet` and no
  `volumeClaimTemplates` (checked with `yq` in CI).
- `helm template … --set spool.type=ephemeral --set 'spool.ephemeral.accessModes={ReadWriteMany}'`
  fails schema validation.
- The local profile's kind cluster offers only its default storage class, which provisions
  ReadWriteOnce volumes on the node, and the whole R-HA-052 suite passes there.

### R-HA-036 · Resources and Go runtime limits
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: HA-052

- Defaults: requests 1 CPU and 1 GiB memory, memory limit 2 GiB, no CPU limit (`web`). `worker`
  and backup pods: 500m and 512 MiB, memory limit 1 GiB. `vuln-scanner-trivy` pods: 500m and 1 GiB, memory limit 2 GiB, for one
  analyser per slot (R-HA-065, Q-HA-316); `malware-scanner-clamav` pods: R-HA-068's. Requests are set, never left empty, so the
  scheduler and the autoscaler have a basis.
- **CPU.** Since Go 1.25 the runtime sets `GOMAXPROCS` from the cgroup CPU *limit* and ignores
  requests ([Go 1.25 release notes](https://go.dev/doc/go1.25#container-aware-gomaxprocs)).
  Without a CPU limit it would use every CPU of the node. When `resources.limits.cpu` is unset, the
  chart therefore sets `GOMAXPROCS` from `requests.cpu` through the downward API
  (`resourceFieldRef`, divisor 1, rounded up). When a CPU limit is set, the chart sets nothing and
  the runtime's container-aware default applies.
- **Memory.** The chart passes `limits.memory` as `QUADER_RUNTIME_MEMORY_LIMIT_BYTES` (downward API).
  At startup, unless `GOMEMLIMIT` is set explicitly, the process calls `debug.SetMemoryLimit` with
  `runtime.memory_limit_ratio` × that value ([SetMemoryLimit](https://pkg.go.dev/runtime/debug#SetMemoryLimit)).
  The garbage collector then works harder near the limit instead of the container being OOM-killed.
  The rest is headroom for non-heap memory. `GOMEMLIMIT=off` is an explicit setting too: no limit.
- **Admission follows the memory.** The same limit sizes what a `web` replica admits: memory slots
  and a heap gate in step 4 of the chain ([architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-005,
  Q-ARCH-240, Q-ARCH-328). A replica that the CPU cannot keep up with answers the excess `503 server_busy`
  instead of collecting requests until the memory runs out. The admission counts bytes: a request
  holds a download of a large object until its download knows its size and settles to what it holds,
  and the caches count by what they hold, so empty caches reserve nothing. `server.max_in_flight`
  stays an upper bound; with the chart's 2 GiB and the default caches full the 1,191 memory slots bind first
  (Q-ARCH-243, Q-ARCH-270), 2,228 with empty ones. The chart refuses a `web` pod
  without a memory limit and one whose limit, with the caches full, admits fewer than 64 requests, or whose kernel share holds fewer than 64 send buffers (R-HA-029, Q-HA-70, [architecture.md](architecture.md) Q-ARCH-500).
- Buffers are bounded so that memory does not scale with transfer size: streaming bodies, spool
  instead of memory above `storage.spool.memory_threshold`, bounded metadata documents (format pages
  set limits for npm packuments and NuGet registration pages).
- Sizing profiles live in `deploy/helm/quader/profiles/{small,medium,large}.yaml` (R-HA-050). They
  are layered before the operator's values file: `helm upgrade -f profiles/medium.yaml -f my-values.yaml`.

Acceptance criteria:

- With requests 2 CPU and no limit on a 16-CPU node, `GET /api/v1/system/info` reports
  `gomaxprocs: 2`. With a limit of 3, it reports 3.
- With a 1 GiB memory limit, a load test that holds 200 concurrent large-packument requests ends
  without an OOM kill, and `go_gc_cycles_total` rises instead.
- With `QUADER_RUNTIME_MEMORY_LIMIT_BYTES` of 256 MiB, `go_gc_gomemlimit_bytes` is 85 % of it, and
  1,000 slow downloads held open leave the memory the runtime holds below 256 MiB
  (`test/integration/overload`, R-ARCH-005).
- On the dev profile, P-8's 1,000 requests/s of a 50 KiB tarball against one `web` pod whose CPU
  cannot serve them end without a restart of the pod; what it cannot serve is answered
  `503 server_busy` ([coverage/roadmap.md](../coverage/roadmap.md) Q-ROAD-10).

### R-HA-037 · Service, Ingress and TLS at the edge
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: HA-012, HA-022, HA-038, HA-039, HA-042

**Status.** Built (phase 6a, WP6a.3) for the Ingress ([ingress.yaml](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/ingress.yaml) over the table of
[_edge.tpl](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/_edge.tpl)).
The HTTPRoute of R-HA-038 reads the same table and is not rendered yet (Q-HA-81).

- **One host, split by path prefix (HA-012, Q-HA-71).** All client traffic of the default endpoint (UI, API, package
  protocols, raw files, login) uses one host, one port 8080 and one certificate. The edge splits each host by path prefix
  between the Services of the roles that serve the route families ([endpoints.md](endpoints.md) R-EP-005,
  [architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-001). The rules are fixed, not values, and every one has `pathType: Prefix`,
  which Kubernetes and the Gateway API match by whole path elements (`/api` matches `/api` and `/api/npm/…`, never
  `/apix`), and the longest matching prefix wins:

  | Path prefix | Families | Service |
  |---|---|---|
  | `/` | `ui` (`GET /`, `/ui/…`, `/auth/…`), the npm exchange at the host root (`/-/npm/v1/oidc/…`, `ci_exchange`, P1), and every path no other rule matches | `<fullname>-api` |
  | `/api/v1` | `api`, and `ci_exchange`'s `POST /api/v1/auth/oidc/token` | `<fullname>-api` |
  | `/api` | `packages`: `/api/<format>/<projectKey>/<repoKey>/…` | `<fullname>-packages` |
  | `/files` | `files` | `<fullname>-packages` |
  | `/v2`, `/.well-known` | `packages`: the host-root routes reserved by INV-6 and the host-root bindings of [endpoints.md](endpoints.md) R-EP-006 | `<fullname>-packages` |

  The path pools of R-HA-062 add their more specific prefixes onto their own Services. A path the edge matches against a
  rule of the other role (an encoded segment that the router decodes into another family, for example) reaches a role that
  does not register its family and answers the `404` of an unknown path: the edge shares load, each role's router decides
  what it serves. One family is nested inside another's prefix: the npm trusted-publishing exchange below a registry URL
  (`/api/npm/<projectKey>/<repoKey>/-/npm/v1/oidc/token/exchange/package/<name>`, [formats/npm.md](formats/npm.md) R-NPM-022, P1) belongs
  to `ci_exchange` but matches `/api`. The chart renders a rule of its own for it when R-NPM-022 is built (Q-HA-72); until
  then the route does not exist, and its path answers `404` on either role.
- **Further endpoints.** Each further endpoint has its own port, its own Ingress or HTTPRoute with its own class, hosts,
  optional wildcard host and TLS Secret, and Services by role: `<fullname>-ep-<name>` and, when its surface holds families
  of both roles, `<fullname>-api-ep-<name>` ([endpoints.md](endpoints.md) R-EP-008, Q-EP-71). Its rules are the rows of the
  table above whose families its surface holds, each to the Service of the role that serves it; an endpoint whose surface
  lies within one role is routed whole (`/`) to that Service. `ui` is never on a further endpoint.
- There is no second route that bypasses anything, because no internal component sits behind the replicas. The operations
  port is never routed by the Ingress or the Gateway.
- **No session affinity anywhere (INV-12, INV-18, [architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-032).**
  Every Service the chart renders, the role Services, the Services of pools and of endpoints, keeps
  `sessionAffinity: None`, fixed and not a value, and the edge route sets no affinity cookie. The
  chart renders no cookie or client-IP affinity on the Ingress or the HTTPRoute, and its examples
  (R-HA-039) contain none; an operator who adds
  one through annotations or `extraObjects` gains nothing, because any replica of a role can answer any
  request of its families (R-HA-001). The edge proxy balances requests over the ready endpoints of each Service.
- **The whole host, never a sub-path.** Quader owns the root of every host it is served on.
  Clients fix some routes at the host root (npm's `/-/npm/v1/` exchange prefix,
  [formats/npm.md](formats/npm.md) Q-NPM-1; `/v2/` for OCI, Q-HA-4), which INV-6 reserves next to
  `/auth/` and `/ui/`; the session cookie carries the `__Host-` prefix with `Path=/`; and
  `server.base_url` is an origin without a path
  ([operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-005). The split by prefix happens inside
  the host and never rewrites a path, so the rules of the table and the HTTPRoute matches (R-HA-038) are fixed and not
  values. `values.schema.json` declares `ingress` and `gateway` with `additionalProperties: false`, so
  `--set ingress.path=/quader` fails schema validation before anything renders (R-HA-029).
- **Load balancer (HA-022).** An Ingress controller or a Gateway API implementation (R-HA-038) is
  the load balancer. The Services are `ClusterIP` by default. `service.type: LoadBalancer` reaches one role per Service, and
  so serves a whole host only for a further endpoint whose surface lies within one role, because a cloud load balancer in
  front of one Service cannot split a host by path; clusters without an Ingress controller or Gateway route through one of
  the two.
  Plain HTTP to the internet is not a supported production setup.
- **TLS (HA-042).** TLS terminates at the edge: an Ingress TLS Secret, cert-manager through an
  annotation (`cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer`, [cert-manager Ingress](https://cert-manager.io/docs/usage/ingress/)),
  a Gateway listener, or a cloud load balancer. Traffic from the edge to the pods is HTTPS when
  `tls.enabled` is `true` (R-HA-063): the edge verifies each backend against the CA of the pair it serves, under the name of
  its kind, `<fullname>-api.<namespace>.svc` for the Services of `api` and `<fullname>-packages.<namespace>.svc` for those of
  `packages`, so a pod that holds the pair of one kind cannot pose as the other toward the edge
  ([Q-HA-348](#q-ha-348--the-edge-verifies-each-backend-under-its-kinds-name-the-setting-goes-where-each-controller-reads-it)). With `tls.enabled: false` it is plain HTTP inside the cluster (H-38). A service mesh with mutual TLS
  (Istio, Linkerd) or CNI encryption works transparently and closes H-38 at the platform level.
- `ingress.hosts` defaults to the host of `config.server.base_url`, so the URL clients use and the
  URL Quader writes into metadata cannot diverge. A further endpoint's Ingress takes its hosts from
  that endpoint's `baseUrl`, `hosts` and `wildcardHost` the same way; a wildcard host needs a
  wildcard DNS record and a wildcard certificate in its TLS Secret ([endpoints.md](endpoints.md)
  R-EP-003, R-EP-004).
- ingress-nginx, the most common controller, was retired by the Kubernetes project in March 2026
  and receives no further fixes
  ([retirement announcement](https://kubernetes.io/blog/2025/11/11/ingress-nginx-retirement/)).
  The chart's Ingress is controller-neutral: it uses only `pathType: Prefix`, which every conformant controller supports.
  The chart renders an HTTPRoute from the MVP on (R-HA-038, Q-HA-7), and new installations should prefer it.

Acceptance criteria:

- With `ingress.enabled: true`, `className: haproxy` and a cert-manager issuer, `curl -sI https://quader.example.com/api/v1/system/ping`
  returns `200` with a certificate for the host and an `X-Quader-Replica` of an `api` pod, and
  `curl -sI -H "Authorization: Bearer $T" https://quader.example.com/api/npm/web/npm-all/lodash` one of a `packages` pod.
- `curl -s https://quader.example.com:8081/metrics` and any Ingress path to the operations port
  fail. The Ingress manifest contains no rule for port 8081.
- `helm template … --set ingress.enabled=true --set ingress.path=/quader` fails schema validation
  and names `path`. Every rendered Ingress rule has `pathType: Prefix`, the rules of each host are exactly the rows of the
  table (plus the prefixes of the path pools), and each names the Service of its row; the chart test asserts the same for
  the HTTPRoute.
- During the e2e set with every role deployed, the access log of no `api` pod records a request below `/api/<format>/` or
  `/files/`, and the access log of no `packages` pod records one below `/ui/`, `/auth/` or `/api/v1/`.

### R-HA-038 · Gateway API exposure
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: HA-040

**Status.** Rendered for the default endpoint ([httproute.yaml](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/httproute.yaml), render test
`TestR_HA_038_GatewayAPIExposure`), reading the table the Ingress reads ([_edge.tpl](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/_edge.tpl)); the BackendTLSPolicies of
`tls.backendTLSPolicy` name one Service each (Q-HA-81, Q-HA-85). Not rendered: the HTTPRoute of further endpoints (R-EP-008) and the
Gateway of `gateway.create` (R-HA-053). `gateway.parentRefs` is required with `gateway.enabled`. The criteria with Envoy Gateway in kind run in the
profile `edge` (`TestEdge_R_HA_039_TransfersThroughTheIngressAndTheGateway`, [edge_test.go](../../test/e2e/edge_test.go), Q-HA-260); the production
example values render the route beside the Ingress (`TestR_HA_038_ProductionExample`, Q-HA-262).

- With `gateway.enabled: true` the chart renders an `HTTPRoute` (`gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1`).
  It attaches to `gateway.parentRefs`, with `hostnames` defaulting to the base URL's host (plus the
  content host of R-HA-055 when set), one rule per row of R-HA-037's prefix table with a `PathPrefix` match to the Service
  of its role (fixed, not values), the path pools'
  rules of R-HA-062, and on every rule `timeouts.request` / `timeouts.backendRequest` and `gateway.filters` from the values.
  The Gateway API orders `PathPrefix` matches by length, so the more specific prefix wins as in an Ingress. With
  `tls.backendTLSPolicy.enabled`, one BackendTLSPolicy per Service the HTTPRoute names. HTTPRoute timeouts are part of the Standard channel since Gateway API v1.2
  ([GEP-1742](https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/geps/gep-1742/)), so v1.2 CRDs are the minimum.
  `backendRequest` MUST NOT exceed `request`.
- `gateway.enabled: true` with an empty `gateway.parentRefs` is refused at render time (R-HA-029): an HTTPRoute without a parent attaches
  to no Gateway and would route nothing, so the chart names the missing value instead of rendering an object that does nothing
  (`quader: gateway.parentRefs is required with gateway.enabled: the Gateway the HTTPRoute attaches to`).
- The HTTPRoute is MVP (Q-HA-7). It attaches to an existing, platform-owned Gateway. A Gateway
  rendered by the chart is P1 (R-HA-053).
- Ingress and HTTPRoute may be enabled at the same time, for migrating between them with a DNS
  switch and an instant way back.
- Body size, request buffering and slash handling are not part of the Gateway API. They are set
  through implementation-specific policies (R-HA-039) that the chart does not render. `extraObjects`
  can carry them.

Acceptance criteria:

- With Envoy Gateway in kind and the policies of R-HA-039, `npm publish` of a 200 MB package and
  `npm view @acme/ui` (scoped name, encoded slash) work through the HTTPRoute, reaching `packages` pods, and the UI loads
  from `api` pods.
- Rendering with `gateway.enabled: true` and no Gateway API in the cluster fails before anything is
  created (R-HA-029).

### R-HA-053 · Chart-created Gateway
Priority: **P1** · Covers: HA-040

- `gateway.create.enabled: true` renders a Gateway named `<fullname>-gateway` with
  `gateway.create.gatewayClassName` and `gateway.create.listeners`, and attaches the HTTPRoute of
  R-HA-038 to it. The suffix avoids clashes with Services that some implementations create. It is
  meant for single-tenant clusters; shared clusters attach to a platform-owned Gateway.
- The chart does not create a TLS Secret for the listener. Certificates come from an existing Secret
  or from cert-manager's Gateway support.

Acceptance criteria: with Envoy Gateway in kind and `gateway.create.enabled: true`, R-HA-038's
criteria pass through the chart-created Gateway, and `helm uninstall` removes it.

### R-HA-039 · Proxy requirements for large and long transfers
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: HA-024

Every hop in front of Quader (cloud load balancer, Ingress controller, Gateway, corporate reverse
proxy) MUST be configured as follows. The defaults of common controllers violate most rows, and
