the failures appear only later.

| Requirement | Value | Failure if violated |
|---|---|---|
| Request body size | Unlimited, or ≥ `storage.upload.max_size` | `413` on large publishes |
| Request buffering | Off | The proxy spools the upload to its own disk and forwards it late; clients time out, and `Expect: 100-continue` rejection (R-HA-010) stops working |
| Response buffering | Off | Large downloads are written to the proxy's disk first |
| Read/send timeouts | ≥ 900 s (≥ 3600 s for multi-GB artifacts on slow links) | Long uploads and downloads cut at 60 s |
| Encoded slashes | Passed through unchanged (`%2f`, `%2F`) | Scoped npm packages (`@scope%2fname`) fail ([formats/npm.md](formats/npm.md)) |
| Path normalization, slash merging | Off | Same |
| Response caching | Off | Stale metadata, broken publishes; caching is Quader's job (remote repositories) |
| Upstream protocol | HTTP/1.1 with keep-alive | Connection churn |
| Forwarded headers | `X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Forwarded-Proto` set by the last hop, from a CIDR listed in `server.trusted_proxies` (R-OPS-005) | Wrong client IP in the audit log |

Examples for common controllers (verified 2026-10-28 against their documentation; the controller's
documentation wins):

<details>
<summary>ingress-nginx (retired; for existing installations only)</summary>

```yaml
ingress:
  className: nginx                                            # example
  annotations:
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-body-size: "0"          # example: unlimited
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-request-buffering: "off"   # example
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-buffering: "off"           # example
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-read-timeout: "3600"       # example
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-send-timeout: "3600"       # example
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Traefik</summary>

Traefik's entry points limit the time to read a whole request, including its body, to 60 s by
default (`transport.respondingTimeouts.readTimeout`,
[entry points](https://doc.traefik.io/traefik/reference/install-configuration/entrypoints/)). The
setting applies per entry point, not per route:

```yaml
# Traefik static configuration (Helm values of the Traefik chart)
ports:
  websecure:
    transport:
      respondingTimeouts:
        readTimeout: 3600s    # example
        writeTimeout: 0s      # example (Traefik default)
        idleTimeout: 180s     # example (Traefik default)
```

Traefik does not limit the body size and does not buffer unless a buffering middleware is attached.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Envoy Gateway (Gateway API)</summary>

Envoy Gateway unescapes encoded slashes and redirects by default, which breaks `@scope%2fname`.
Keep them unchanged with a `ClientTrafficPolicy` on the Gateway, created in the Gateway's
namespace ([Envoy Gateway](https://gateway.envoyproxy.io/)):

```yaml
apiVersion: gateway.envoyproxy.io/v1alpha1
kind: ClientTrafficPolicy
metadata:
  name: quader-paths               # example
  namespace: gateway-system         # example: namespace of the Gateway
spec:
  targetRefs:
    - group: gateway.networking.k8s.io
      kind: Gateway
      name: shared                  # example
  path:
    escapedSlashesAction: KeepUnchanged   # example
    disableMergeSlashes: true             # example
```

Route timeouts come from the HTTPRoute (R-HA-038).

</details>

Acceptance criteria (run through the chart's Ingress and through the HTTPRoute in CI, the set `edge`: the Ingress is HAProxy Ingress, the HTTPRoute is
attached to a Gateway of Envoy Gateway, Q-HA-260; the slow download reads a 2 GiB object, Q-HA-261):

- `curl -T 6gib.bin https://quader.example.com/files/web/generic-local/big.bin` succeeds. 6 GiB is
  above the 5 GiB single-request limit of S3, so the multipart path is covered as well.
- `curl --limit-rate 2M -o /dev/null https://quader.example.com/files/web/generic-local/big.bin` runs
  longer than 15 minutes and completes.
- `curl -s https://quader.example.com/api/npm/web/npm-all/@acme%2fui` returns the packument.
- `dotnet nuget push big.nupkg --source …` of a 1 GiB package succeeds.

### R-HA-040 · Public base URL and forwarded headers in the chart
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: HA-025

R-OPS-005 specifies URL generation and the trust rules. The chart side:

- `config.server.base_url` is required (R-HA-029). The Ingress host and the HTTPRoute host name
  default to its host (R-HA-037), so the published name and the generated URLs agree.
- `config.server.trusted_proxies` SHOULD list exactly the pod CIDR (or the node CIDR with
  `externalTrafficPolicy: Local`) of the edge proxy. A broader list lets any pod in the cluster set
  the client address that the audit log records (Security notes).
- The edge proxy does not need to forward `Host` or `X-Forwarded-Host` for Quader to generate
  correct URLs, because they come from `base_url`. This removes the catalog's class of
  "reads work, multi-step writes fail" errors caused by rewritten `Host` headers.

Acceptance criteria: R-OPS-005's criteria pass through the chart's Ingress with
`trusted_proxies` set to the ingress controller's pod CIDR.

### R-HA-055 · Optional content host at the edge
Priority: **P1** · Covers: quader-only

[architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-029 specifies the optional content origin: package
content a browser could render is served from a second host name that never receives the UI's
session cookie (Q-ARCH-10). This requirement is the chart side.

- `contentOrigin.host` names the content host. When it is set, the chart:
  - renders `server.content_base_url: https://<contentOrigin.host>` into `quader.yaml`, a
    chart-managed key (R-HA-030), so the published host and the URLs Quader generates cannot
    diverge, as for `base_url` (R-HA-040);
  - adds a rule for that host to the Ingress (path `/`, `pathType: Prefix`, R-HA-037) and an HTTPRoute rule for the
    host (R-HA-038), both to `<fullname>-packages:8080`, because the content host serves only the families `packages` and
    `files`. There is no further Service, port or Deployment: the replica
    tells the hosts apart (R-ARCH-029, with the host resolved by R-ARCH-006);
  - with `contentOrigin.tls.secretName`, adds a TLS entry of its own to the Ingress
    (`{secretName: <contentOrigin.tls.secretName>, hosts: [<contentOrigin.host>]}`), so the content
    host has its own certificate; with cert-manager's Ingress annotation (R-HA-037), cert-manager
    issues it. With a chart-created Gateway (R-HA-053), it adds an HTTPS listener `content` on port
    443 for that host with that certificate. On a platform-owned Gateway, a listener of the
    platform must cover the host.
- Host rules, checked before anything is applied:
  - `values.schema.json` accepts only a DNS host name for `contentOrigin.host`, without scheme,
    port or path. A content origin on the UI's host with another port, which R-ARCH-029 refuses
    because browsers do not isolate cookies by port, therefore cannot be configured.
  - Rendering fails when `contentOrigin.host` equals the host of `config.server.base_url` or of a
    `config.server.additional_base_urls` entry (R-HA-029).
  - A subdomain of the UI's registrable domain renders, and the replica logs R-ARCH-029's warning at
    start-up. A separate registrable domain, such as `quader-content.example.net`, is recommended.
  - The start-up checks of R-ARCH-029 stay the second line, also for installations that run the
    binary without the chart.
- The edge requirements of R-HA-039 apply to the content host unchanged. NetworkPolicies
  (R-HA-042) need no change, because the traffic reaches the same port.
- With `contentOrigin.host` empty (default) nothing extra is rendered: one origin with the content
  headers of R-ARCH-007.

Acceptance criteria:

- `helm template … --set ingress.enabled=true --set contentOrigin.host=quader-content.example.net --set contentOrigin.tls.secretName=quader-content-tls`
  renders one Ingress with the path rules of R-HA-037 for the main host and one rule `/` to `<fullname>-packages:8080` for
  the content host, a TLS entry with
  `quader-content-tls` for the content host, and `server.content_base_url: https://quader-content.example.net`
  in `quader.yaml`. With `gateway.enabled: true`, the HTTPRoute lists both host names.
- With `config.server.base_url: https://quader.example.com`, `--set contentOrigin.host=quader.example.com`
  fails and names `contentOrigin.host`; `--set contentOrigin.host=quader.example.com:8443` fails
  schema validation; `--set config.server.content_base_url=https://x.example.net` fails as a
  chart-managed key.
- R-ARCH-029's acceptance criteria pass through the chart's Ingress with Traefik and a cert-manager
  issuer, as in R-HA-037's criteria.

### R-HA-041 · Container-registry routing at the edge
Priority: **P1** · Covers: HA-027

Docker and OCI clients address a registry at the host root (`https://<host>/v2/…`). A path prefix
is not possible, so the OCI format needs `/v2/` on the client listener. INV-6 reserves `/v2/` for
the OCI distribution API (Q-HA-4): no other route may use it, from the MVP on, so the OCI format
can be added later without moving anything.

- **The reservation is MVP; the routing below is P1.** The OCI registry root is the one pattern
  `/v2/{rest...}` ([formats/oci.md](formats/oci.md) R-OCI-003); on an endpoint without the `packages` family,
  `/v2/` and everything below it answer `404` through the listener's "anything else" row
  ([architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-005). A route-table test fails when any registered
  client-listener pattern other than the OCI format's starts with `/v2/`. ServeMux's own conflict
  check is not enough, because a more specific pattern such as `/v2/x` does not conflict with
  `/v2/`.
- The chart routes the whole host to Quader (R-HA-037). `/v2/` reaches Quader without rewrite
  rules. The project key and the repository key are the first two path segments after `/v2/`
  (`docker pull quader.example.com/web/docker-all/library/alpine:3`), as below `/api/<format>/`
  ([repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-002). The OCI format page specifies this.
- Subdomain-per-repository routing (`docker-all.registry.example.com`) is not offered: a host label cannot name a
  project and a repository key, and the binding of a host label to a repository is gone
  ([endpoints.md](endpoints.md) [Q-EP-76](endpoints.md#q-ep-76--a-host-root-binds-a-repository-by-project-and-key-and-the-label-binding-goes)).
  A Docker Engine mirror is an endpoint host bound to one repository by its project and key
  (`host_roots: {mirror.example.com: web/docker-hub}`, [endpoints.md](endpoints.md) R-EP-006, R-EP-007). The OCI page
  specifies the registry side.
- The chart renders no rewrite rules or snippets. This avoids the catalog's mismatch between edge
  rewrites and the server's routing method, where pushes break while pulls work.

Acceptance criteria (when the OCI format exists):
`docker login quader.example.com && docker push quader.example.com/web/docker-local/test:1` through
the chart's Ingress succeeds without any Ingress annotation beyond R-HA-039's.

### R-HA-042 · Network policies
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: HA-054

**Status.** Built (phase 6a, WP6a.3): one policy per Deployment of the cut and the migration Job
([networkpolicy.yaml](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/networkpolicy.yaml)). Enforcement on the cluster's CNI is verified on
the kind profile's CNI only (H-41).

The owner's rule ([ADR-154](../decisions.md#adr-154--network-policies-are-ingress-rules-between-the-charts-pods-each-with-its-port),
2026-11-04): Quader writes only ingress rules, only for the pods the chart deploys and between them, and every rule names its
specific port. The chart renders no egress rule and no policy for pods it does not deploy.

With `networkPolicy.enabled: true` (default) the chart renders one NetworkPolicy per Deployment, named as the Deployment and
selecting its pods by the selector labels of R-HA-028, with `policyTypes: [Ingress]` and one rule per port the pods open:

| Policy | Port 8080 | Port of a further endpoint | Port 8081 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<fullname>-api`, `<fullname>-packages`, each of their path pools | from `networkPolicy.ingress.http.from` (empty means from anywhere, so the edge works wherever it runs) | from that endpoint's `networkPolicy.from`, for each further endpoint without a pool whose surface holds a family of the role | from `networkPolicy.ingress.ops.from` and `networkPolicy.probeCIDRs` |
| each endpoint pool (`<fullname>-packages-ep-<name>`, `<fullname>-api-ep-<name>`) | none: an endpoint pool opens no 8080 (R-EP-002) | from the endpoint's `networkPolicy.from` | as above |
| `<fullname>-worker`, each worker pool | none: a worker listens on no client port (R-HA-001) | none | as above |
| `<fullname>-vuln-scanner-trivy` (R-HA-065) | from the pods of the worker Deployment that claims the queue `vuln` (the worker pool that lists it, else `<fullname>-worker`), by their selector labels | none | as above |
| `<fullname>-malware-scanner-clamav` (R-HA-068), `<fullname>-malware-updater-freshclam` (R-HA-069) | from the pods of the worker Deployments that claim the queue `malware`, by their selector labels | none | as above |
| `<fullname>-packages` (the main Deployment), one rule more | beside its 8080 rule of the first row, port 8082 of the scan listener (R-HA-066) from the pods of `<fullname>-vuln-scanner-trivy`, `<fullname>-malware-scanner-clamav` and `<fullname>-malware-updater-freshclam` only | as the first row | as the first row |
| `<fullname>-migrate`, `<fullname>-backup`, `<fullname>-restore` | none | none | none: `ingress: []` |

- Every rule names its port, and every rule with a port carries the `from` of its row. A row whose `from` list is empty
  for 8081 (neither an `ops.from` peer nor a `probeCIDRs` entry) leaves the 8081 rule out rather than rendering an empty
  `from`, which Kubernetes reads as "from anywhere". `networkPolicy.ingress.http.from` and an endpoint's
  `networkPolicy.from` keep their meaning: empty admits the port from anywhere, so the edge works without a value.
- No rule admits one Quader pod from another but the two of the image scanning's seam: replicas of a role never open connections
  to each other (Topology), and the cut added no seam between the roles
  ([ADR-153](../decisions.md#adr-153--quader-is-cut-into-task-areas-roles-of-one-binary-network-seams-only-at-trust-or-load-boundaries)).
  The seam that ADR-212 adds is two rules of the receiving roles' policies, each admitting the sending role on the seam's port (ADR-154):
  the scanner's `8080` from the worker that claims `vuln`, the scan listener's `8082` from the scanner. Neither rule depends on
  `networkPolicy.ingress.http.from`, and neither port is ever admitted from anywhere.
- In-cluster callers that address a role's Service directly (R-HA-002), such as a Bastion in another namespace, reach
  port 8080 only when `networkPolicy.ingress.http.from` admits them; with a restricted list, their namespace or pods are
  added to it.
- **Egress.** None. The chart renders no egress rule, has no `networkPolicy.egress` values and no example file for one. What
  separates Quader's outbound connections is the address policy of
  [repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md) R-REPO-038, which every role applies in code, and beyond it the
  cluster operator's own policy; the gap is [H-516](../security/egress.md#h-516--the-chart-restricts-no-egress-of-its-pods).
  An operator who restricts egress at the cluster lets each role reach what it uses: every serving role and the migration
  Job DNS and PostgreSQL (`database.host`, `session_host`, the pooler of R-HA-058); every serving role Valkey and its
  Sentinels and the object store; `packages` the upstreams of its remote repositories and the shadowing probes; `api` the
  OIDC issuers and the upstreams it tests (R-REPO-024); `worker` the upstreams of mirrored remotes, the upstream of the image
  scanning's database repository, the advisory sources of [vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-025, the CI
  issuers' key endpoints and the scanners' `8080`; each scanner DNS and the scan listener `8082` of `packages`, and nothing else; backup
  and restore the backup target. For the scanner that policy is the containment of an analyser an image took over
  ([H-1036](../security/image-scanning.md#h-1036--the-chart-restricts-no-egress-of-the-scanner)).
- **Valkey and the Sentinels admit only Quader's pods** ([architecture.md](architecture.md) H-49).
  Whoever can write under Quader's key prefix can deny service, so the Valkey data nodes and the
  Sentinels MUST be reachable only from Quader's serving pods (`api`, `packages`, `worker`, `web`), from each other and from
  their own operator. The chart renders no Valkey (R-HA-028), so this ingress policy belongs to
  whoever runs Valkey; with Valkey in the release namespace it selects Quader's pods by their
  labels:

  ```yaml
  apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
  kind: NetworkPolicy
  metadata:
    name: quader-valkey-ingress                    # example
  spec:
    podSelector:
      matchLabels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: quader-valkey      # example: the Valkey data nodes and Sentinels
    policyTypes: [Ingress]
    ingress:
      - from:
          - podSelector:
              matchExpressions:
                - {key: app.kubernetes.io/name, operator: In, values: [quader]}
                - {key: app.kubernetes.io/instance, operator: In, values: [quader]}   # example: the release
                - {key: app.kubernetes.io/component, operator: In, values: [api, packages, worker, web]}
          - podSelector:
              matchLabels:
                app.kubernetes.io/name: quader-valkey  # example: replication and Sentinel traffic
        ports:
          - {port: 6379}
          - {port: 26379}
  ```

  The local profile applies this policy to its Valkey (R-HA-051).
- Kubelet probes: most CNIs exempt node-to-pod probe traffic from policies. Where one does not,
  `probeCIDRs` adds the node CIDRs to the 8081 rule.

Acceptance criteria:

- The chart test renders, for the default values, exactly the policies `quader-api`, `quader-packages`, `quader-worker`,
  `quader-vuln-scanner-trivy`, `quader-malware-scanner-clamav` and `quader-migrate`; `quader-api` and `quader-packages` have one rule for TCP 8080 without `from` and one for TCP 8081 from the
  namespace `monitoring`; `quader-worker` only the 8081 rule; `quader-migrate` `ingress: []`; no policy has
  `policyTypes: [Egress]` or an `egress` key, and every rule names a port. With the `customers` endpoint of R-EP-008
  (surface `[packages, files, api]`, no pool), `quader-packages` and `quader-api` each gain a rule for 8443 from
  `endpoints.customers.networkPolicy.from`; with its pool enabled, `quader-packages-ep-customers` and `quader-api-ep-customers`
  carry the 8443 and 8081 rules and no 8080 rule. With a worker pool `vuln`, `quader-worker-vuln` carries the 8081 rule only.
  With the default values `quader-vuln-scanner-trivy` exists, with a rule for TCP 8080 from the pods of `quader-worker` and the 8081
  rule, and `quader-packages` has a third rule, TCP 8082 from the pods of `quader-vuln-scanner-trivy` and `quader-malware-scanner-clamav`; with a worker pool `vuln`, the scanner's 8080 rule
  names the pods of `quader-worker-vuln` instead; with `config.vulnerabilities.images.enabled: false` neither exists.
- From a `worker` pod of the pool that claims `vuln`, a TLS connection to `quader-vuln-scanner-trivy:8080` with the worker's pair succeeds; from a pod
  in namespace `default` it times out, and so does a connection to `quader-packages-scan:8082` (e2e set `vuln`, R-VULN-046).
- From a pod in namespace `default`, `curl https://quader-ops.quader:8081/metrics` times out, and
  `curl https://quader-api.quader:8080/api/v1/system/ping` succeeds; a connection to a `worker` pod's 8080 is refused or times
  out.
- In the local profile, a connection to the Valkey and Sentinel ports from a pod in namespace
  `default`, and from the restore Job's pod, times out, while every `api`, `packages` and `worker` pod connects.

### R-HA-043 · Trusted CA bundles
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: HA-019

**Status.** Built: the values `trustedCA.*` (with their schema), the mount in every pod of the release but the scanner's (R-HA-065) and the two config paths
([_secrets.tpl](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/_secrets.tpl), [_helpers.tpl](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/_helpers.tpl),
[_validate.tpl](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/_validate.tpl)), tested by `TestR_HA_043_TrustedCA`
([trustedca_test.go](../../test/chart/trustedca_test.go)); the dev profile's Keycloak CA and the restore drill's CA go through it
([Q-HA-272](#q-ha-272--the-trusted-ca-bundle-is-mounted-in-every-pod-of-the-release-its-files-are-appended-to-ca_files-and-one-file-can-be-the-object-stores-ca)).
The acceptance's reload within 60 s is the binary's from the file; the time a Secret or ConfigMap change takes to reach the file is the
kubelet's ([H-804](#h-804--a-change-of-the-ca-source-reaches-the-pods-at-the-kubelets-pace)).

- `trustedCA.existingSecret` or `trustedCA.existingConfigMap` (for example a trust-manager `Bundle`
  target, [trust-manager](https://cert-manager.io/docs/trust/trust-manager/)) is mounted at
  `/etc/quader/ca/`. Its files populate `proxy.outbound.tls.ca_files` (R-REPO-035). They are added to the system
  roots for every outbound TLS connection: upstreams, OIDC issuers, GitLab, webhooks. They are
  reloaded within 60 s without a restart (R-REPO-035).
- With `trustedCA.useForObjectStore: true` the same bundle becomes the `ca_file` of every connection whose entry of
  `secrets.storageConnections` has no `ca` (R-HA-072), for an S3-compatible store with a private CA.
- PostgreSQL uses its own CA (`secrets.databaseCA`), never the general bundle. The database
  connection then trusts exactly the database's CA.
- Every replica mounts the same source, so there is no per-node trust store to keep in sync
  (catalog HA-006, HA-019).

Acceptance criteria: R-REPO-035's criterion passes with the bundle supplied through
`trustedCA.existingConfigMap`, and an S3-compatible store with a private CA (the local profile's
store behind a TLS endpoint) works with `useForObjectStore: true`.

### R-HA-044 · IPv6 and dual-stack
Priority: **P1** · Covers: HA-020

- Listeners bind to `[::]` and accept IPv4 and IPv6. The binary contains no IPv4-only assumption
  (address parsing, CIDR lists, `X-Forwarded-For`, log fields).
- `service.ipFamilyPolicy` and `service.ipFamilies` pass through to both Services
  ([dual-stack](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/dual-stack/)).
- `server.trusted_proxies`, `proxy.outbound.address_policy` and NetworkPolicy CIDR values accept IPv6 notation.
- Host names are used everywhere a URL is configured. IPv6 literals in `server.base_url` are allowed
  in bracket notation, but they are not recommended because certificates rarely cover them.

Acceptance criteria: on a dual-stack kind cluster (`networking.ipFamily: dual`) with
`PreferDualStack`, `curl -6` and `curl -4` against the Service both succeed. The audit log records
the IPv6 client address of the `curl -6` request.

### R-HA-045 · Monitoring integration
Priority: **MVP** · Covers: HA-055

**Status.** The PrometheusRule is rendered by the main chart with `metrics.prometheusRule.{enabled,labels,disabledAlerts,extraRules}`
(`disabledAlerts` refuses a name that is no alert), checked by `promtool check rules` and tested by `promtool test rules`
([deploy/helm/quader/tests/rules_test.yaml](../../deploy/helm/quader/tests/rules_test.yaml), `make chart-test`), one test in which the alert fires and one in
which it stays silent per alert. It carries the eight alerts of the vulnerability scanning ([vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md)
R-VULN-024, Q-VULN-55, Q-VULN-122): `QuaderVulnerabilityDataStale`, `QuaderVulnerabilitySyncFailing`, `QuaderVulnerabilityRecordsRejected` (warning), `QuaderVulnerabilityRecordsInvalid` (warning), `QuaderVulnerabilityMaliciousRecordRejected` (critical), `QuaderVulnerabilityClaimedNameMalicious`, `QuaderVulnerabilityImageScansFailing` and `QuaderVulnerabilityImageScannerUnavailable` (warning, R-VULN-041); the two of the
mirror mode (R-OPS-046); `QuaderBlobMissing` (severity `critical`, summed over the replicas, [storage.md](storage.md)
Q-STOR-152); and these sixteen rows of the table below: `QuaderReplicasNotReady`, `QuaderDatabaseUnreachable`, `QuaderObjectStoreUnreachable`,
`QuaderObjectStoreUnreachableSingleReplica`, `QuaderDatabasePoolSaturated`, `QuaderControlConnectionWaits`, `QuaderJobsStuck`, `QuaderLeaseLost`,
`QuaderMixedVersions`, `QuaderSpoolNearlyFull`, `QuaderGCStale`, `QuaderValkeyUnavailable`, `QuaderValkeyUnavailableSingleReplica`,
`QuaderValkeySentinelsDegraded`, `QuaderValkeyFailoverFlapping` and `QuaderValkeyPrimaryDisagreement`. The object-store alerts are per
connection ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-060, R-HA-072): `QuaderObjectStoreUnreachable` for every connection down on every replica,
`QuaderObjectStoreConnectionUnreachable` for one of several (Q-HA-391), `QuaderObjectStoreUnreachableSingleReplica` per connection,
`QuaderStorageReplicationBacklog`, `QuaderStorageCopyDamaged`, `QuaderStorageScrubBehind`, `QuaderStorageConnectionDetached` and
`QuaderBlobCorrupt` beside `QuaderBlobMissing`, each with a rule test that fires and one that stays silent; `QuaderStorageUnknownKey`
([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-088, package 6 of the encryption of stored content) with one that fires and two that stay silent, one read of
an unknown key and reads of a destroyed one (R-STOR-101). The ServiceMonitor is rendered
([servicemonitor.yaml](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/servicemonitor.yaml), render test `TestServiceMonitor`). The rule scopes its selectors by
`namespace`, which every scrape through the Prometheus operator carries. The binary exports every metric these rows read under the name of their
expression (Q-HA-135): the copies per state of `QuaderStorageCopyDamaged` from the hourly storage summary (package F,
[internal/blob/summary/gauges.go](../../internal/blob/summary/gauges.go), [storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-028), so that alert fires at the
earliest an hour after the summary that first counted the copy. The queue's age and the filling gauge of `QuaderStorageReplicationBacklog` and the gauge of
`QuaderStorageConnectionDetached` are exported by the reconciliation (package C,
[internal/blob/reconcile/metrics.go](../../internal/blob/reconcile/metrics.go)), from the query `ReconcileGauges`; the overdue copies of
`QuaderStorageScrubBehind` by the scrub (package D, [internal/blob/scrub/metrics.go](../../internal/blob/scrub/metrics.go)), from the
query `ScrubOverdue`.

Every alert of the table is rendered and tested (phase 7): `QuaderBackupCheckFailed` (R-HA-023, the stored report of the task `backup-check`), `QuaderRevocationJournalBacklog` (R-HA-054) and the six alerts of the backup runs, `QuaderBackupStale`, `QuaderBackupFailed`,
`QuaderBackupRunningLong`, `QuaderBackupGlobalHoldLong`, `QuaderBackupSourceDamage` and `QuaderBackupVerifyFindings`
([backup-and-restore.md](backup-and-restore.md) R-BAK-014), each with a rule test in which it fires and one in which it stays silent. The
two gauges that have no series until the event happened (Q-OPS-180) are handled in the expressions: `QuaderBackupFailed` reads the last success
as `or vector(0)`, and `QuaderBackupStale` has a clause for a backup that never succeeded ([Q-OPS-182](operations-and-observability.md#q-ops-182--the-clause-of-quaderbackupstale-for-a-backup-that-never-succeeded-reads-its-window-from-the-chart)).
The six alerts of the backup runs are rendered only while `backup.enabled` is true
([Q-HA-17](#q-ha-17--the-backup-cronjob-is-off-by-default)): with the backup off no run ever succeeds, and that clause would fire one
interval after every such installation started. `QuaderBackupCheckFailed` and the journal's alerts are rendered either way, because the
platform check and the journal serve the platform restore as well.

`QuaderBackupCheckFailed` reads `quader_backup_check_ok{check}`, which every replica exports from the report that the task `backup-check` stored in
`system_state` ([Q-OPS-185](operations-and-observability.md#q-ops-185--the-gauge-of-the-platform-check-is-read-from-the-stored-report-by-every-replica));
a check that is not declared or not readable has no series. The acceptance criteria
below that need a Prometheus scraping a running profile run in the profile `alerts` (Q-HA-263), against a Prometheus that reads the chart's
ServiceMonitor and PrometheusRule (`TestAlerts_R_OPS_046_...`, [alerts_test.go](../../test/e2e/alerts_test.go)): Valkey stopped, one replica cut off from
Valkey, three failovers, PostgreSQL fenced for three minutes, a role scaled below two replicas, a killed backup run and a suspended CronJob with the
interval at a minute, and the scenario "Maintenance stays quiet" (Q-HA-264). The object store stopped is not among them: `QuaderObjectStoreUnreachable`
is tested by its rule tests only. The production example values render the ServiceMonitor and the PrometheusRule with every alert (`TestR_HA_045_ProductionExample`).

MVP since 2026-10-28. INV-12 requires that a Valkey outage is alerted on, the backup alerts of
[backup-and-restore.md](backup-and-restore.md) R-BAK-014 are MVP, and MVP acceptance criteria
(R-HA-010, R-HA-057) expect these alerts to fire. The ServiceMonitor and the PrometheusRule are
templates over metrics the MVP already exports, so the change adds no backend work.

- **Logs.** Quader writes JSON lines to stdout only (INV-16). The cluster's log collector ships them.
  The chart renders no logging sidecars. A sidecar that needs to (e.g. a SIEM forwarder) goes into
  `sidecars`.
- **ServiceMonitor.** It scrapes the `ops` port of `<fullname>-ops`, every pod, path `/metrics`
  (R-OPS-006). When `config.metrics.auth: static`, the bearer token comes from
  `secrets.metricsToken`. Its endpoint always renders two relabelings that set the target labels
  `role` and `pool` from the pod's labels
  ([operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-006, Q-OPS-13):
  `role` from `app.kubernetes.io/component` (`api`, `packages` or `worker`; Q-OPS-161), and `pool` from the label
  `quader/pool` (R-HA-028), which carries the pool's name on the pods of each entry of `api.pools`, `packages.pools`
  and `worker.pools` (R-HA-062), `ep-<name>` on the pods of an endpoint pool, and is empty on the main Deployments, so their
  series carry no `pool`. `metrics.serviceMonitor.relabelings` is appended after these two:

  ```yaml
  relabelings:
    - sourceLabels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_app_kubernetes_io_component]
      targetLabel: role
    - sourceLabels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_quader_pool]
      targetLabel: pool
  ```
- **PrometheusRule.** Default alerts; names are stable and individually disabled with
  `disabledAlerts`:

| Alert | Expression (sketch) | For | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| `QuaderReplicasNotReady` | `min by (deployment) (kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{deployment=~"<fullname>-(api\|packages\|worker\|vuln-scanner-trivy\|malware-scanner-clamav)(-.*)?"}) < 2`, per Deployment, so one role or pool without replicas fires while the others are healthy (the Deployments are `<fullname>-<role>` and `<fullname>-<role>-<pool>` for the roles `api`, `packages` and `worker`, R-HA-062, and the scanners `<fullname>-vuln-scanner-trivy`, R-HA-065, and `<fullname>-malware-scanner-clamav`, R-HA-068, [Q-HA-341](#q-ha-341--quaderreplicasnotready-covers-the-scanner-deployment); needs kube-state-metrics) | 5m | critical |
| `QuaderDatabaseUnreachable` | `sum(rate(quader_db_retries_total{kind="connection"}[1m])) > 0 and sum(rate(quader_http_requests_total{code="503"}[1m])) > 0` | 2m | critical |
| `QuaderObjectStoreUnreachable` | `min(quader_storage_s3_circuit_open) == 1`: every connection on every replica ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-060; with one connection the expression of before) | 2m | critical |
| `QuaderObjectStoreConnectionUnreachable` | `min by (connection) (quader_storage_s3_circuit_open) == 1 unless on() (min(quader_storage_s3_circuit_open) == 1)`: one connection on every replica while another answers (R-STOR-060) | 2m | warning |
| `QuaderObjectStoreUnreachableSingleReplica` | `max by (connection) (quader_storage_s3_circuit_open) == 1 and min by (connection) (quader_storage_s3_circuit_open) == 0`, per connection | 5m | warning |
| `QuaderStorageReplicationBacklog` | `max by (connection) (quader_storage_reconcile_queue_oldest_seconds) > 3600 unless on (connection) (max by (connection) (quader_storage_connection_filling) == 1)`: not for a connection that is `filling` (R-STOR-056, [Q-HA-393](#q-ha-393--the-replication-backlog-alert-leaves-a-filling-connection-out-by-a-gauge-of-its-own)) | 30m | warning |
| `QuaderStorageCopyDamaged` | `max by (connection) (quader_storage_copies{state=~"missing\|corrupt"}) > 0`: a damaged copy not repaired (R-STOR-055, R-STOR-027) | 1h | warning |
| `QuaderStorageScrubBehind` | `max by (connection) (quader_storage_scrub_overdue_copies) > 0` (R-STOR-027) | 6h | warning |
| `QuaderStorageConnectionDetached` | `max by (connection) (quader_storage_connection_detached) == 1` (R-STOR-051) | 15m | warning |
| `QuaderStorageUnknownKey` | `sum by (connection) (increase(quader_storage_encrypted_read_failures_total{reason="unknown_key"}[5m])) > 0`: reads of an encrypted connection keep meeting records of storage keys the database lacks, until the export is imported; never `reason="destroyed_key"` ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-088) | 10m | critical |
| `QuaderDatabasePoolSaturated` | `histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(quader_db_pool_acquire_duration_seconds_bucket{db_pool="request"}[5m])) > 0.1`; the control connection's waits are the next row's ([operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-046) | 10m | warning |
| `QuaderControlConnectionWaits` | `histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(quader_db_pool_acquire_duration_seconds_bucket{db_pool="control"}[5m])) > 1`: readiness-critical loops wait for the control connection (Q-HA-20), before `invalidation` and `database` start failing on every replica (R-OPS-046); ten minutes on the five-minute window, so the waits went on for five ([Q-OPS-425](operations-and-observability.md#q-ops-425--quadercontrolconnectionwaits-fires-on-waits-that-go-on-for-five-minutes-for-10m-on-the-five-minute-window)) | 10m | warning |
| `QuaderJobsStuck` | `max(quader_jobs_oldest_queued_age_seconds) > 900` | 5m | warning |
| `QuaderLeaseLost` | `increase(quader_lease_lost_total[15m]) > 3` | 0m | warning |
| `QuaderMixedVersions` | `count(count by (version) (quader_build_info)) > 1` | 2h | warning |
| `QuaderSpoolNearlyFull` | `max by (role) (quader_spool_used_bytes / (quader_spool_used_bytes + quader_spool_free_bytes)) > 0.9`: one alert per unit, the scanner's spool included ([operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) Q-OPS-237) | 10m | warning |
| `QuaderBlobMissing` | `increase(quader_storage_blobs_damaged_total{status="missing"}[1h]) > 0`: no connection holds the blob any more | 0m | critical |
| `QuaderBlobCorrupt` | `increase(quader_storage_blobs_damaged_total{status="corrupt"}[1h]) > 0`: no connection holds the blob whole ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-052) | 0m | critical |
| `QuaderGCStale` | `time() - max(quader_gc_last_success_timestamp_seconds) > 172800` | 1h | warning |
| `QuaderBackupCheckFailed` | `min(quader_backup_check_ok) == 0` | 1h | critical |
| `QuaderRevocationJournalBacklog` | `max by (connection) (quader_revocation_journal_pending) > 0` (R-HA-054, per connection) | 15m | warning |
| `QuaderRevocationJournalQuarantined` | `sum(increase(quader_revocation_journal_quarantined_total[1h])) > 0`: an outbox row that could not be encoded was set aside, so a change is missing from the journal (R-HA-054, Q-HA-162) | 0m | critical |
| `QuaderValkeyUnavailable` | `max(quader_valkey_available) == 0` (every replica degraded, R-HA-057) | 2m | critical |
| `QuaderValkeyUnavailableSingleReplica` | `min(quader_valkey_available) == 0 and max(quader_valkey_available) == 1` | 5m | warning |
| `QuaderValkeySentinelsDegraded` | `min(quader_valkey_sentinels_reachable) < 2` (no majority of three, R-HA-056; the gauge counts the answers to a probe of every configured Sentinel, R-HA-057) | 5m | warning |
| `QuaderValkeyFailoverFlapping` | `max(max_over_time(quader_valkey_primary_changes_total[1h]) - min_over_time(quader_valkey_primary_changes_total[1h])) > 2` (failovers repeating, [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) Q-OPS-15) | 0m | warning |
| `QuaderValkeyPrimaryDisagreement` | `max(quader_valkey_primary_views) > 1`: replicas name different primaries, for example one still bound to a demoted primary (Q-OPS-15, R-ARCH-031) | 5m | critical |
| `QuaderBackupStale` | `time() - max(quader_backup_last_success_timestamp_seconds) > 1.5 * max(quader_backup_expected_interval_seconds)`, or `quader_backup_last_success_timestamp_seconds` absent for longer than `backup.expected_interval` ([backup-and-restore.md](backup-and-restore.md) R-BAK-014). Renamed from `QuaderBackupTooOld` | 0m | critical |
