run, under the npm load, and asserts the stall of the failure table: no `503` of the edge, `/readyz` `200` on every replica, and every pooler's
failure window shorter than `health.database_outage_grace`, the time after which a replica's failing `database` check takes it out of its
Service (Q-OPS-31). The bound is the configuration's, not a measured value. Every pooler leg keeps the rendered `pgbouncer.ini` and the log
of every pooler instance in its artifacts. Two full nightlies showed what this decision did not see (F-165): PgBouncer tries the server again
only when a client asks, which the reading of the window now accounts for
([Q-HA-370](#q-ha-370--a-pooler-instances-failure-window-ends-a-server_login_retry-after-its-last-failed-server-attempt)), and a connect
that gets no answer adds `server_connect_timeout` to a switchover, which the poolers now bound at 5 s
([Q-HA-371](#q-ha-371--the-poolers-give-up-a-server-connect-after-5-s)).

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-058 (the switchover bullet and the example), R-HA-059 rule 5 (the pooler row), the failure table's switchover row; R-HA-058's acceptance criteria;
[deploy/dev/pooler.yaml](../../deploy/dev/pooler.yaml), [docs/developer/local-profile.md](../developer/local-profile.md), the pooler requirements of the
[README](../../README.md) and of the manual ([configuration](../manual/admin/configuration.md#behind-a-transaction-mode-pooler), [runbook](../manual/admin/runbook.md)).

### Q-HA-303 · The harness clients close their TLS connections without close_notify, so a closing connection does not end a kubectl port-forward

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the e2e tests reach single pods and the test upstreams through supervised `kubectl port-forward` processes
([Q-HA-64](#q-ha-64--how-the-end-to-end-tests-of-the-access-core-hold-valkey-down-reach-a-replica-directly-and-get-the-login-configuration-into-the-dev-profile)).
Two nightly legs failed on a request that a forward cut (`e2e (vuln)` of run 43698804297, `e2e (vuln-long)` of run 44067104691): kubectl had ended the
forward on `read: connection reset by peer` from the pod's socket, and the request after it never reached the pod. The reset is the teardown of the
connection before: the server closes after the answer of a `Connection: close` request, the client's TLS close_notify can arrive before that close, and
Linux closes a socket with unread data with a reset. kubectl ends a forward on a reset of any of its connections. A setup request through a forward was
already repeated on a new forward (`overForward`); a request of a test was not, and should not be on the grounds of a harness fault alone.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The harness clients close without close_notify (chosen) | `quietTLS`: the TLS dial of the `api` client, the stub control clients and the CI issuer double returns a connection whose Close ends the TCP connection only | Removes the cause: a FIN carries no data, so the server's close stays a FIN; reproduced on Linux, 0 resets in 400 connections against 3 of 200 (immediate close) and 200 of 200 (close 20 ms late) with close_notify | A client the harness does not own (a package manager in a client pod) still sends it; those run inside the cluster, not through a forward |
| (b) Repeat every GET and HEAD of a test on a new forward after a transport error | `send` uses `overForward` for safe methods | Covers every cause of a broken forward | A request of an assertion is repeated, and a cut it should report is retried away; it treats the symptom |
| (c) Keep-alive connections through a forward | Fewer closes | Fewer teardowns | The client's close of an idle connection meets the same race; a reused connection that the server closed adds a failure of its own, and the scatter profile needs a new connection per request at the edge |

**Choice:** (a). A request of a test through a forward is still sent once, and a cut is still reported.

**Rationale:** The alert ends nothing the client still needs: the answer was read in full before the connection is closed, and the server does not wait
for the alert. The development agent would revisit the choice if a forward still ends on a reset in a run's `portforward-*.log` artifacts with the
quiet close in place; the cause is then another one and is read from those files.

**Applied in the spec:** none. [docs/developer/e2e.md](../developer/e2e.md#m1-tests) ("The control clients and a broken forward") and item 16 of
its [findings](../developer/e2e.md#findings-of-the-suite).

### Q-HA-304 · A setup that fails says whether a registry or the machine was the cause, and the test IdP is not restarted inside the wait

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: `make dev-up` of `e2e (ci-ha)` in the nightly run 44067104691 ended with `quader-db has 1 ready instances, want 2` and `deployment
"quader-keycloak" exceeded its progress deadline`; no test ran. The runner was slow in every step, those without network as well: against the 17
hosted e2e legs of the runs 44067104691 and 44186978088, freeing disk space took 368 s (85 to 155 s), Set up Go 61 s (9 to 18 s), `make image`
847 s (111 to 173 s), `make dev-up` 839 s until it failed (148 to 203 s for the whole stack), the failure-only cluster state 328 s (4 to 8 s) and
`make dev-down` 116 s (2 to 29 s). Image pulls took up to 156 s each, and the PostgreSQL image was pulled again on the second instance's node
(155 s), which completed its join about 40 s after the 10-minute wait had ended. Keycloak's startup probe (60 x 5 s) restarted its first start
after 300 s, so the second start had 3 minutes 20 s of up.sh's 10 left. No pull failed. up.sh printed only the last lines of the two task logs,
which named none of this.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The failure names its cause, and the startup probe allows the wait (chosen) | `explain_setup_failure` (deploy/dev/lib.sh): a failed pull is printed as a cause outside the repository; otherwise the slowest pulls, the probe restarts, the pods that are not ready and the machine's pressure; Keycloak's startup probe 120 x 5 s | The next occurrence says whether a registry or the machine failed; a slow start is no longer thrown away and begun again inside the same wait | A runner this slow still fails the leg |
| (b) Pull the dependency images on the host and load them into kind | One pull per image, `kind load` to the nodes | One pull from the registry instead of one per node | Each node still imports the image, so the disk writes grow on the disk that was slow; the cause here was the machine, not the registry |
| (c) Longer waits | e.g. 20 minutes for PostgreSQL and Keycloak | PostgreSQL's second instance had finished its join 40 s after the wait | No measurement says when either would have been ready; Keycloak's second start wrote its first log line after 91 s; a slower failure on a broken runner holds the runner longer |

**Choice:** (a). No wait of up.sh changes: the startup probe's budget is raised to the wait that bounds the start anyway, from the
measurement of that run; a hang still fails at the same 10 minutes.

**Rationale:** The setup can only be as fast as the machine; what it owes the reader is the cause. A failed pull is the case the repository cannot
help and must say so plainly; a slow machine shows in the pull durations and in the pressure, both read at the moment of the failure. The development agent would revisit
(b) if a failure names a registry, and (c) if a failure shows a dependency that progressed steadily and needed a little more than its wait.

**Applied in the spec:** none. [docs/developer/local-profile.md](../developer/local-profile.md#troubleshooting),
[docs/developer/e2e.md](../developer/e2e.md#findings-of-the-suite) (item 17).

### Q-HA-305 · A stall of the kind nodes is told apart from a neighbour's load, and a fault test does not start on a sick cluster

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. Extends
[Q-HA-300](#q-ha-300--every-e2e-set-records-what-starved-the-kind-nodes-inside-the-nodes-whether-it-passes-or-fails).

Context: the evidence of Q-HA-300 was read for the first time in a red run on 2026-11-18 (nightly 44186978088, leg `ha-faults`,
`TestHAFaults_ValkeySlow`). What it showed, and what it could not:

- From 23:58 to 00:12 the leg's first four fault tests ran under the same npm load with a warm-up p99 of 0.5 to 1 s, the host's CPU pressure
  at 400 to 480 ms per second and a load of 50 to 75 on 32 CPUs. At 00:12:28, when the load of `ValkeySlow` started and 66 s before Valkey was
  slowed, the `full` CPU stall of the leg's nodes (every task of the node waiting at once) rose from 25 to 165 ms per second to 200 to 495,
  the host's load rose to 247, the edge's idle share fell from about 60 % to 0 % with its connections stuck at 813 and its connection rate at 0,
  k6's p50 rose to 2 to 35 s, a `packages` pod was `OOMKilled` at 00:13:34 (limit 1 GiB) and both edge pods were restarted by their liveness
  probes at 00:15:03 and 00:16:03. It ended when the load stopped at 00:17:40.
- The runner cluster's `Scheduled` events put the leg on the node `k8s-runner-omega` with one other kind leg (`edge` of the same run) from
  23:44, and eight small jobs of "Test and Release" 44205650371 (Angular build, Trivy with an image build, golangci-lint, unit tests, release tooling,
  NuGet vectors, integration shards b and c) on the same node from 00:10:54 to 00:10:57. Before 00:10:54 that node had the two kind legs and
  one one-minute job.
- Read on the runner cluster the same night: the job's Docker daemon (the privileged `dind` container) sees the cgroup root of the machine;
  the kind nodes of every leg, their k6 containers and the image builders are children of the top-level cgroup `docker` (`cpu.weight` 100),
  the runner pods and the small jobs' steps are under `kubepods` (`cpu.weight` 1250). When the 32 CPUs are all asked for, every kind cluster on
  the machine together is guaranteed about 100/1550 of them (two CPUs) while the small jobs ask for the rest. Measured on the same node at 00:41
  over 20 s: `docker` (two kind legs and their containers) 19.4 CPUs, `kubepods` (five small jobs and the runner processes) 5.7, the machine
  25.2 of 32, steal 0.5 %.
- What the evidence could not show: the CPU time of the leg's nodes against the small jobs' in the window (Q-HA-300 recorded pressure, not
  use), the other runner pods on the machine, and what filled the `packages` pod's 1 GiB (its memory guard, R-ARCH-005, shed nothing).

The test then injected the fault into the stalled cluster and judged the fault's latency condition against a warm-up p99 of 46 s, a baseline
that was itself the failure.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The recorder reads the machine's cgroups and the pods; the fault tests check their warm-up (chosen) | `e2e-evidence.sh` adds `io` pressure and the CPU time to every row, the host's busy and steal time from `/proc/stat`, one row per top-level cgroup of the machine (`cg:<name>`: pressure, CPU time, `cpu.weight`, members) and per container of `docker` (`cgd:`) from a helper container with the daemon's cgroup tree mounted read-only, the job's own containers (`containers.tsv`), and per pod of each kind node its CPU time, memory by kind and OOM kills (`pods.csv`); `runLoadFault` reads k6's warm-up before it injects the fault and fails with "the cluster was not healthy before the fault" when a request already broke the load's condition | The next stall says whose CPU it was and what filled a killed pod; the failure names its cause instead of the fault; no fault is judged against a sick baseline | One helper container and a wider CSV per leg; a fault test on a sick cluster ends earlier and says less about the fault |
| (b) Record only, no warm-up check | — | The fault always runs | The fault's verdict mixes in what happened before it, as in run 44186978088 |
| (c) A latency bound on the warm-up | Fail when the warm-up p99 is above a value | Catches a slow but error-free baseline (run 42994478570: 1.4 s) | A new wall-clock bound without a requirement behind it; the load's own condition already covers errors |
| (d) Serialize the kind legs of both workflows with `concurrency` | One group for every kind leg | Fewer legs side by side | GitHub keeps one pending run per group and cancels the others, and the release would wait behind the nightly, which the owner's rule forbids; the neighbours of run 44186978088 were small jobs, which a group of kind legs does not hold back |

**Choice:** (a). The warm-up check uses the load's own condition (`only2xx304` and what the NuGet half holds), which the end of the run applies
to the warm-up anyway: a run is red in exactly the cases it was red before. The one place where this is stricter is the node loss of the set
`ha-suite`, which tolerated k6 failures up to 10 s after the replacements were ready, warm-up included; a failure before the node is lost is
not the node loss's. The recorder's helper runs from the kind nodes' image (bash is in it), on no network, and ends at its stop file or after
`QUADER_E2E_EVIDENCE_MAX_SECONDS` like the other loops.

**Rationale:** the stall family (H-795, F-119, F-124, the stall of the set `push`) kept its cause open because the recordings could not separate
the leg from its neighbours; with the CPU time per cgroup that is one subtraction (the family's runs before 2026-11-18, which no
recorder of the CPU time covered, were closed on 2026-11-23, and what opens a stall again is in
[e2e.md](../developer/e2e.md#reading-a-stall)). The cgroup layout on the runner is the owner's
(the runner definitions are not in this repository): what it means for the runner classes is recorded in
[promt.md](../projektplan/promt.md) section 8 with the measurements above.

**What the recorder reads on each runner class** (since the runner change of 2026-11-18, which gave the Docker daemon of a `large` job a cgroup
parent inside its own pod). The first leg on the new layout (`e2e (push)` of Test and Release 44384406557) showed the gap: its ten own containers had
no `cgd:` row, because the recorder read the children of the top-level `docker` only, and the pod's memory limit, which now counts the kind nodes,
was not recorded at all. The recorder now finds the daemon's cgroup parent instead of assuming it: once per set, a helper container looks up the
cgroup directory of the first kind node in the daemon's cgroup tree (down to six levels) and takes its parent; the pod is the `pod<uid>` (or
`…-pod<uid>.slice`) directory below `kubepods` on that path. `/proc/self/cgroup` of a container is not used: on cgroup v2 a container has its own
cgroup namespace and reads `0::/`.

| Class | Daemon's parent | Rows |
|---|---|---|
| `self-hosted` | `/docker` | as before: `cg:<name>` per top-level cgroup, `cgd:<id12>` per container of `/docker` (own and neighbours', told apart by `containers.tsv`) |
| `large` | `/kubepods/burstable/pod<uid>/docker` | in addition `daemon:parent` (the leg's containers) and `daemon:pod` (the runner pod) with the columns of the `cg:` rows, `cgd:<id12>` also for the containers of the daemon's parent, and `pod-memory.csv` (the pod's `memory.current`, `memory.peak`, `memory.max`, the `oom` and `oom_kill` counts of `memory.events`, the `oom` count of `memory.events.local`, and `anon`, `file`, `kernel`, `shmem`, `slab_reclaimable` and `sock` of `memory.stat`) every 5 s; its last row heads the evidence's `README.txt`, with the peak of `anon` and of what cannot be given back (`anon + shmem + sock + kernel - slab_reclaimable`) over the leg |
| not found | — | as `self-hosted`, and the log says so once |

The leg's own and the neighbours' containers keep one row kind, `cgd:`, in both classes, and `containers.tsv` stays the rule for telling them
apart: on `self-hosted` the parent is shared, so a separate prefix for the daemon's own parent would separate them on `large` only, and the
readings of the existing rows keep working. The search runs once per set; the per-second work grows by two rows on `large` only.

**Applied:** `deploy/dev/e2e-evidence.sh`, `test/e2e/npm_ha_test.go` (`runLoadFault`), `test/e2e/npm_load_test.go` (`warmUpFailures`),
`test/e2e/nuget_ha_test.go`, `internal/tools/e2eevidence` (the search and the sampler against fabricated cgroup trees of both classes);
[docs/developer/e2e.md](../developer/e2e.md#reading-a-stall).

### Q-HA-306 · The pooler's own answers to a switchover are retried; a wrong password at connect is not

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the first runs of `TestHAPooler_Switchover` (Q-HA-302; run 44206453722, the poolers at PgBouncer's default `server_login_retry`) answered 8
k6 requests with Quader's own `500` besides the edge's `503`s. Verified in the replicas' logs (`npm request failed status=500 code=internal`) and the
poolers' logs of that run, two answers of PgBouncer that `classify` ([retry.go](../../internal/meta/postgres/retry.go)) took for final:

- `FATAL: invalid server parameter (SQLSTATE 08P01)`, at the moment of the switchover: PgBouncer had linked the client to a server connection of the old
  primary and was setting the client's parameters on it (`varcache_apply failed: FATAL: terminating connection due to administrator command`). The
  client's statement was not sent; PgBouncer links a server at the first statement of a transaction, so it never meets a `COMMIT`.
- `FATAL: password authentication failed for user "quader" (SQLSTATE 28P01)`, 15 s later: the clients that waited for a server connection when the
  pooler's login on the new primary failed (its verifier had changed, Q-HA-302) get the server's error. Their statement did not run either.

The fix of Q-HA-302 shortens the window but does not remove either answer: the old primary's connections end at every switchover, and the new
primary's verifier changes at every promotion.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Retry both, `28P01` only on an authenticated connection (chosen) | `08P01` with `invalid server parameter` and a `28P01` that is not inside pgx's `ConnectError` are `retryFailover` | The request waits out the switchover as R-HA-015 says; a wrong password of Quader's own still fails at once (it comes at connect) | Two more PgBouncer texts and one structural rule to keep |
| (b) Retry every `28P01` | The code decides | No structural rule | A wrong password in `secrets.database` would be retried until `max_elapsed` on every request instead of failing at connect |
| (c) Leave them final | Nothing changes | | Every switchover behind a pooler answers some requests `500`, which R-HA-007's failure table does not allow |

**Choice:** (a). PostgreSQL itself sends `28P01` only during authentication, which pgx reports as a `ConnectError`; on an established connection it
can only come from a pooler that forwards its own failed server login. `TestClassify` has the three cases.

**Readiness** (R-OPS-001). The `database` and `schema` checks read the same classification (`postgres.IsOutage`), so the pooler's
two answers are an outage the readiness grace applies to, as the switchover is for the requests: without that a replica would leave its
Service in exactly the window `TestHAPooler_Switchover` requires it to stay in. A credential refused at connect still gates after the usual
debounce and names the password in the check's error. When the database password is really changed on the server, the check meets the
pooler-forwarded `28P01` at most once per pooled control connection: PgBouncer closes that client, the next check dials, and Quader's own
login is then refused at connect (the pooler fetches the new verifier for every client login), which gates with the password named in
`readiness check failing`. `TestMarkOutage` (`internal/app`) has both shapes, the connect-time one from a backend that refuses the startup.

**Rationale:** both answers mean "no server yet", and the statement was not run, so running it again is safe. The development agent would revisit the
match when PgBouncer changes the text (the pinned CloudNativePG pooler image is what the test of Q-HA-302 runs), or if a pooler forwards a server's
`28P01` on a connection whose statement may have run.

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-058 (the switchover bullet). Code: [retry.go](../../internal/meta/postgres/retry.go).

### Q-HA-307 · The registry row's shutdown writes are retried within their step

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: F-146 (`e2e (push)` of Test and Release 44384406557) asked why the row of a drained worker stayed `ready`. Read from its
evidence: the row the test found was not the drained process's but that of the same pod's earlier process, killed with `SIGKILL` by
`TestE06Lease` four minutes before and restarted in place by the kubelet under the same name; the drained process signed off (only one
row of that name was left, and nothing deletes the killed process's row before 24 h). The test is fixed (it now follows instance UIDs,
R-HA-059). Read from the code while finding that out: the two writes a stopping replica makes to its row were each tried once. The mark
`draining` (`Registry.Drain`) failed on the first refused or ended connection and only logged it; the final deletion (`Registry.Stop`) had
one attempt of 5 s and returned its error to the composition root, which printed it as plain text after `stopped`. A switchover of the
primary ends every connection for some seconds (14 s in F-146's run), so a stop inside that window left a row behind although the
database answered again well inside the pod's grace period.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) One attempt each, as before | Nothing to change | Simplest | A stop during a switchover leaves a row that is listed as lost (not marked) or as signed off (marked) although the database came back in time |
| (b) Retry each write within its step (chosen) | The mark retries until the end of the drain step (2 s on a worker, the drain delay on a serving replica), then the heartbeat writes `draining` on the control connection until the close phase; the deletion retries for at most 15 s and never past the close deadline. Pause 250 ms, doubling to 2 s; each attempt of the deletion has at most 5 s, of the mark the loops' call timeout | A switchover shorter than the time left is ridden out; the plan's deadlines still bound everything, so the exit deadline holds (R-HA-011); a healthy stop is unchanged (one attempt) | A stop against a database that does not answer waits up to 15 s longer in its close phase than before |
| (c) Retry until the close deadline | No window of its own | Covers a failover of a lost node as well (30 s and more) | A worker without running jobs, whose close phase starts at once, would sit up to 114 s (grace 120 s) in front of a dead database before its pod goes, which holds a rolling update for that long |

**Choice:** (b). The interval follows `retryFailover` of the job writes (200 ms doubling to 2 s); 15 s is the switchover of F-146 (14 s)
with room, and the close deadline is the outer bound. The first failure is logged at once with the write's name ("replica row: write
failed; retrying until its shutdown step ends"), the outcome after a retry or the failure with what the row will be listed as (Q-OPS-210:
signed off when the mark reached it, lost when neither write did). **Rationale:** the registry is what the status screen shows the
operator; a row that is left because one statement met the seconds of a switchover is a false warning for 24 h. The development agent
would revisit the 15 s if a drain run shows a deletion that needed more inside the grace period, or if a rolling update is seen held by
the window.

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-011, R-ARCH-024 steps 1 and 6 ([architecture.md](architecture.md)), R-OPS-003
([operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md)). Code: `Drain`, `Stop` and `retryShutdownWrite` in
[replica_registry.go](../../internal/cluster/replica_registry.go). Tests: `TestR_ARCH_024_RegistryDrainRetriesTheMarkWithinTheDrainStep`,
`TestR_ARCH_024_RegistryDrainRetriesEndWithTheDrainStep`, `TestR_HA_011_RegistryStopRetriesTheDeletion`,
`TestR_OPS_003_RegistryStopNamesWhatTheRowLeftBehindIsListedAs`, and `TestShutdownThroughASwitchover` in
[shutdown_failover_test.go](../../test/integration/coordination/shutdown_failover_test.go), which ends the replica's connections and
refuses new ones for 2 s inside each step.

### Q-HA-308 · A heartbeat does not turn a row back from draining

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the heartbeat reads the replica's state, then writes the whole row with an upsert. A heartbeat that read `ready` just before
`SIGTERM` and reached the database just after the mark `draining` wrote `ready` over it. Read from the code, not seen in a run: the next
heartbeat writes `draining` again, but a replica whose next heartbeat does not come (the stop ends it) and whose deletion fails leaves a
row that is listed as lost instead of signed off (Q-OPS-210).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Order the two writes in the process | The mark waits for a heartbeat under way | No SQL change | The heartbeat runs on the control connection, which a stalled database holds; the drain step would wait on it (Q-HA-283) |
| (b) The upsert keeps `draining` (chosen) | `state = CASE WHEN replica.state = 'draining' THEN replica.state ELSE EXCLUDED.state END` | `draining` is the last state of an instance (a new process has a new `instance_uid`), so nothing ever needs to leave it; one statement, no ordering | The rule lives in SQL |

**Choice:** (b), in `UpsertReplica` ([cluster.sql](../../internal/meta/postgres/queries/cluster.sql)). **Rationale:** the state an
instance reaches at `SIGTERM` is final for that instance; the database is the one place that sees both writes in order. The development
agent would revisit it if an instance ever had to leave `draining` (an aborted shutdown), which R-ARCH-024 does not have.

**Applied in the spec:** R-OPS-003 ([operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md)).

### Q-HA-309 · A heartbeat that has not reached the row for longer than the stale bound is logged once as what it means

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: F-146 asked for a heartbeat that cannot write for longer than its bound to be visible in the log and in the replica's own
health. Each failed heartbeat logged "replica heartbeat failed" every `system.heartbeat_interval`, which says nothing about what it costs:
once the row is older than `system.heartbeat_stale_after`, the other replicas list this one as lost.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A reported readiness check `registry` | A new check in R-OPS-001's table | Shows in `/readyz?verbose=1` | The heartbeat runs on the control connection, which the `database` check already probes and degrades on after the outage grace; a second check reports the same outage, and the row that would carry it is the one that cannot be written |
| (b) One error line when the bound is passed, one line when the heartbeat is back (chosen) | "replica heartbeat not written for longer than system.heartbeat_stale_after: the other replicas list this replica as lost …" with the time since the last write, and "replica heartbeat written again" | Says what the outage means at the moment it starts to matter, once; the replica's health already shows the cause through the `database` check | No new probe signal |

**Choice:** (b), `noteHeartbeat` in [replica_registry.go](../../internal/cluster/replica_registry.go). **Rationale:** the health signal
exists (the `database` check on the same connection); what was missing is the line that ties it to the registry. The development agent
would revisit it if a heartbeat is seen failing while the `database` check passes, which would mean the two no longer share their
connection.

**Applied in the spec:** R-OPS-003. Test: `TestR_OPS_003_RegistryLogsAHeartbeatThatWentStale`.

### Q-HA-310 · A replica that reaches the database at no point of its shutdown leaves a lost row, and nothing in the process removes it

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: W-13 left this gap open, and F-146 asked to close it as far as the process can: a replica that could neither mark nor delete its
row because PostgreSQL was away for its whole shutdown leaves a row in its last state, `ready`, which is listed as lost (a warning for
24 h, [api-and-ui.md](api-and-ui.md) Q-UI-602). After Q-HA-307 that takes a database that does not answer for the drain step, the server
phase and up to 15 s of the close phase: 35 s and more on a worker, an outage the operator sees anyway.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The next replica of the same Deployment removes rows of earlier pods it can prove gone | Read the pods from Kubernetes | Exact | Quader holds no Kubernetes permissions and is not given any for this |
| (b) The stopping process writes its sign-off to Valkey, which survives a PostgreSQL failover; the readers of the registry honour it | A key per instance with the heartbeat's stale bound as its expiry | Covers the case when Valkey answers | Every reader of the registry (the list, `CountFillingReplicas`, the key-ring views, the leases' view, the journal) would read two stores for one fact; Valkey is optional for correctness (INV-3) and may be the thing that is away; a second source of truth for a warning |
| (c) Nothing; the row is a warning and the log says why (chosen) | The process logs "replica row neither marked draining nor deleted: the database did not answer during the shutdown …" at error level; the drain test tells this case from a sign-off that failed while the database answered | No new mechanism; the row is the truth: the process ended without signing off | The warning stays for 24 h, until the prune |

**Choice:** (c). **Rationale:** the case is a database outage of at least the length of a stop, which is itself the thing the operator
has to look at; the warning names the replica and its last heartbeat, and the role keeps its ready replicas. The development agent would
revisit it if such rows are seen after drains in which the database was not away for the whole stop (that would be a defect of Q-HA-307,
not this case), or if the registry gets a second store for another reason.

**Applied in the spec:** R-OPS-003. Test: `checkRegistryAfterDrain` of `TestE14Drain` ([e14_drain_test.go](../../test/e2e/e14_drain_test.go))
names this case apart.

### Q-HA-311 · The rolling upgrade starts from the newest release before the commit that the chart repository lists

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: finding F-130. `TestUpgrade_R_HA_020_RollingFromThePreviousRelease` started from the newest `vX.Y.Z` tag merged into HEAD.
Since the rename ([ADR-199](../decisions.md#adr-199--the-product-is-renamed-from-trove-to-quader-with-the-token-prefix-qdr_-and-a-new-mark))
the tags of the former name stay in git while the chart repository no longer lists their charts and Docker Hub no longer has their
images (`guidedtraffic/trove:0.16.0` and `guidedtraffic/quader:0.16.0` both answer `404` on 2026-11-18); `v0.56.0` to `v0.62.0`
are published under the new name. A tag is also there minutes before its release is: Semantic Release creates it, then
`Release Docker & Helm` pushes the image and only after that the chart (its job `release-helm-gh` needs `build`), and GitHub Pages
serves the new index a little later. A nightly run on a commit after a fresh release could thus pick a tag without a chart and fail
at the install for a reason that is not the product's. [Q-HA-281](#q-ha-281--tests-run-before-a-release-not-after-it) forbids a test
of a published release as a check after the release; a leg that starts from the previous published release to test the commit
gates nothing and is not such a test.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The newest release tag merged into HEAD (as before) | git alone | No read before the install | Picks a tag whose chart is not published yet or no longer offered |
| (b) The GitHub release list | `gh release list` in the test | The releases as GitHub shows them | A token in the test; a GitHub release exists before its image and chart, so the race of (a) stays; the list does not know which releases are ancestors of the commit |
| (c) A pin in `tools/versions.env` | One value read by the test and the job | Never races | Stale from the next release on: raised by hand with every release, or the test starts from an older one without saying so; Renovate does not know the value |
| (d) The newest release tag merged into HEAD and not at HEAD whose chart the repository's `index.yaml` lists (chosen) | `priorrelease.Pick` over `git tag --merged HEAD` and the index of `https://guided-traffic.github.io/quader/` | The input is exactly what the install fetches; a chart is published only after its image, so a listed chart has its image; a newer tag that is not listed is passed over and logged with the reason | One read of the index before the install; a release published minutes ago is the start of the next run, not of this one |

**Choice:** (d). Without a start the test does what the leg needs: a checkout without a release tag (a shallow clone) and an index
that does not answer after three tries fail it, because the leg could not do its job and a skip would hide that; an index that lists
none of the release tags before the commit skips it with that reason, because there is no published release to upgrade from, which
only the first release under a new name meets.

**Rationale:** the test starts from what an operator would upgrade from, and reads it where the install reads it, so the start and
the install cannot disagree. The release a run missed by minutes is the start of the next run. The development agent would revisit
it when the chart moves to an OCI registry (the list of the chart's tags there replaces the index), or when the release notes name
an oldest release to upgrade from (from the first stable release, R-HA-021): the test then also starts from that one.

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-020 (the status). Code: [test/e2e/priorrelease](../../test/e2e/priorrelease/priorrelease.go) (`Listed`,
`Pick`, unit-tested without a cluster), `previousRelease` in [upgrade_env_test.go](../../test/e2e/upgrade_env_test.go);
[e2e.md](../developer/e2e.md#the-upgrade-tests).

### Q-HA-312 · A commit that cannot be upgraded to without a new database skips the upgrade from the release until the first stable release

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: before the first stable release a migration file may be edited, renamed or removed, and any step may contract
([Q-ARCH-340](architecture.md#q-arch-340--no-backward-compatibility-until-the-first-stable-release)). The runner then refuses a
database that applied the earlier file (the checksum check stays on), so the upgrade from a release that applied it needs a new
database. The rolling test failed on an added step headed `-- quader:phase contract` and did not look at changed files, which would
fail the migration Job fifteen minutes into the leg and read like a defect of the product.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) As before | Fail on an added contract step only | Nothing to build | A red dispatch for a change the rule allows; an edited file is found by the Job, not by the test |
| (b) Install and upgrade anyway | The migration Job decides | The test shows what an operator would meet | A red leg for an allowed change, after a full install |
| (c) Read the migration directory's changes since the release first (chosen) | `git diff --name-status <release> HEAD` on `internal/meta/postgres/migrations` (`priorrelease.Breaks`): a step the release applied that was changed, removed or renamed, or an added contract step, skips the test with the files named while `EnforceMigrationPhases` is `false`, and fails it once it is `true` | The answer comes before any install, with its cause; switching the phases on at the first stable release makes the test strict with no further edit | A skipped dispatch is green: the reader has to look at the skip and its reason in the test report |

**Choice:** (c).

**Rationale:** the leg exists to show a zero-downtime upgrade; where the rule allows the commit to need a new database there is
none to show, and saying so in seconds is worth more than a red leg after a full install. The same switch that brings the expand and
contract rules back turns the skip into a failure, so the test cannot stay lenient by being forgotten. What it does not see: a change
that breaks the old pods without touching a migration (an API or a stored format the old release cannot read during the window);
that still fails the test, as it should once the promise holds. The development agent would revisit it at the first stable release
with the other switches of Q-ARCH-340.

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-020 (the status). Code: `Breaks` in [test/e2e/priorrelease](../../test/e2e/priorrelease/priorrelease.go),
`requireUpgradable` in [upgrade_env_test.go](../../test/e2e/upgrade_env_test.go).

### Q-HA-313 · The upgrade across the cut is no longer tested, and R-HA-064 loses its end-to-end criterion

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.
**Followed** on 2026-11-19 by [Q-HA-315](#q-ha-315--the-charts-upgrade-bridge-across-the-cut-is-removed-the-binary-keeps-the-role-web-for-development-and-tests): option (c), the next change this decision named, is built, except that
the binary keeps the role `web` for development and tests.

Context: finding F-130. `TestUpgrade_R_HA_064_AcrossTheCut` installed `v0.16.0`, the last release before the cut into roles, and
ran the three steps of R-HA-064 under the loops (exit criterion E6a.7 of the roadmap). That release was published under the former
name, which [ADR-199](../decisions.md#adr-199--the-product-is-renamed-from-trove-to-quader-with-the-token-prefix-qdr_-and-a-new-mark)
left without a migration path; the chart repository no longer lists it, and Docker Hub has neither `guidedtraffic/trove:0.16.0` nor
`guidedtraffic/quader:0.16.0`. Every release named Quader (from `v0.56.0`) has the roles, so no Quader installation can be on the shape
before the cut, now or later.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Rebuild the start from source | Build the image and the chart of `v0.16.0` from its tag under the new names, then run the test as before | The steps and the guard's reads stay verified | Tests an artifact no user has and a path no Quader installation can take; a tree 40 releases old built with today's pins is a project of its own |
| (b) Remove the test and E6a.7; keep R-HA-064 and the bridge, the guard held by its chart test (chosen) | `TestUpgrade_R_HA_064_AcrossTheCut`, its constant and its part of the harness go; the guard's decisions stay tested by `TestRolesBridge` with given facts | The change of this finding stays a change of the tests; nothing in the product moves | The bridge stays in the chart for an upgrade that cannot happen, and its reads of the cluster (`lookup`) are verified by no test |
| (c) Remove R-HA-064 with everything that serves it | The chart's bridge (`web.enabled`, `web.routed`, the guard and its reads, the alert `QuaderBridgeLeftOn`, `ci/bridge.yaml`), the chart's rendering of the role `web`, the UI's fallback of [Q-UI-111](api-and-ui.md#q-ui-111--during-the-upgrade-across-the-cut-the-ui-falls-back-to-files-against-a-replica-of-the-old-shape), H-518's half for `web` | The owner's rule: no migration path for installations that do not exist | Spans the chart, the binary, the API's role enums and the UI; it is a change of the product with its own renders and checks, not part of a test finding |

**Choice:** (b) here; (c) is the next change, an open item for the plan. What the cut test held beside the steps stays held: the
edge's access lines ([Q-HA-131](#q-ha-131--the-upgrade-tests-read-the-edges-access-lines-for-answers-without-a-backend)), the loops
and the migration report run in the rolling test; the guard's two refusals and the render under `helm template` are held by
`TestRolesBridge`. The asset skew that [Q-HA-99](#q-ha-99--the-uis-hashed-assets-across-an-upgrade) let the cut count ends with it:
`requireClean` takes no release any more and fails every failed iteration.

**Rationale:** the requirement served installations of the former name, which by ADR-199 are set up again rather than upgraded; a
test of it could only be built on an artifact no one runs. Keeping the bridge one change longer costs nothing an installation can
meet, because a fresh installation never renders it. The development agent would revisit it with the removal of the bridge. At the
first stable release the upgrade guarantees return (R-ARCH-025, R-HA-020, R-HA-021), and an upgrade test must then cover, from the
published N−1: the rolling upgrade under the client and browser loops with no failed iteration and no answer of the edge without a
backend, the rollback, and every change of the chart's shape between N−1 and N (a renamed or removed Deployment or Service, a moved
route) through the stepwise path its release notes give, as this test did for the cut.

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-064 (the note, the status, the acceptance criteria), Q-HA-95, Q-HA-99, the roadmap's E6a.7. Code:
[upgrade_test.go](../../test/e2e/upgrade_test.go), [upgrade_loops_test.go](../../test/e2e/upgrade_loops_test.go) (`requireClean`),
[upgrade_env_test.go](../../test/e2e/upgrade_env_test.go); [e2e.md](../developer/e2e.md#the-upgrade-tests),
[upgrades.md](../manual/admin/upgrades.md#what-is-not-verified-yet).

### Q-HA-314 · The nightly run runs the rolling upgrade of the commit; the upgrade from the published release stays on dispatch

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. It narrows
how [Q-ARCH-340](architecture.md#q-arch-340--no-backward-compatibility-until-the-first-stable-release) (owner, 2026-11-06) is applied
to the nightly run, not its rule.

Context: Q-ARCH-340 took the set `upgrade` out of the nightly run because the upgrade from the latest release fails once a commit
changes a migration the release applied. The set also held `TestUpgrade_R_HA_020_AcrossTwoBundles`, which installs the commit itself
with its second UI bundle and rolls it to the image under test: it needs no published artifact and no compatibility between
releases, and it tests what every rolling upgrade of an installation goes through on one schema (the window with two builds, the
drain, an edge without gaps, the shared asset store of Q-HA-120). The set had not run since 2026-11-06; that day the job took 30 to
48 minutes on a GitHub-hosted runner, the test across two bundles 5 of them and the bring-up about 25.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The whole set on dispatch only (as before) | No nightly leg | No nightly cost | The rolling of the product is watched by nobody; the set had not run for twelve days |
| (b) The whole set nightly | One leg, as before the switch | Every upgrade test every night | Before the first stable release the commit need not serve beside the release (Q-ARCH-340): the leg turns red for changes the rule allows, which Q-HA-312 catches only where they touch a migration |
| (c) Cut the set by what it tests (chosen) | The set `upgrade` is the rolling upgrade of the commit and runs nightly; the set `upgrade-release` is the upgrade from the published release and runs on a dispatch that names it or the job (`select-leg` with `nightly: "false"`) | What can only fail for a defect of the commit runs every night, on a runner of its own (GitHub-hosted, no lane of the large class); what rests on compatibility stays where Q-ARCH-340 put it | Two legs, each with a bring-up of its own when both are dispatched |

**Choice:** (c).

**Rationale:** a set is cut by what it tests (`CLAUDE.md`), and the two tests test different things: one the rolling of a build,
the other the compatibility of two releases, which is a promise only from the first stable release on. The nightly leg costs one
GitHub-hosted runner for about half an hour. The development agent would revisit it at the first stable release, when the leg
`upgrade-release` runs nightly as well (its matrix entry's `nightly` becomes `"true"`, one of the switches of Q-ARCH-340).

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-020 (the note), Q-ARCH-340 (a note). Code: `.github/workflows/performance.yml` (job `e2e-upgrade`, two
legs), `.github/actions/select-leg` (the input `nightly`), [deploy/dev/e2e.sh](../../deploy/dev/e2e.sh) (the sets `upgrade` and
`upgrade-release`); [releasing.md](../developer/releasing.md#ha-and-performance-nightly).

### Q-HA-315 · The chart's upgrade bridge across the cut is removed; the binary keeps the role `web` for development and tests

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. It applies
the owner's rule of 2026-11-06 (no backward compatibility before the first stable release, `CLAUDE.md`,
[Q-ARCH-340](architecture.md#q-arch-340--no-backward-compatibility-until-the-first-stable-release)) to what
[Q-HA-313](#q-ha-313--the-upgrade-across-the-cut-is-no-longer-tested-and-r-ha-064-loses-its-end-to-end-criterion) left behind.

Context: Q-HA-313 removed the end-to-end test of the upgrade across the cut into roles, because no Quader release precedes the cut
and so no installation can take that path, and left the bridge in the chart for a change of its own. Everything the bridge consisted
of served that one path: R-HA-064 with its three steps; the values `web.*` (`web.enabled`, `web.routed` and the sizing of the
`web` Deployment); the Deployment `<fullname>-web`, its endpoint pools `<fullname>-web-ep-<name>`, the Service `<fullname>`, the
edge of the old shape (every host whole to `<fullname>`) and a BackendTLSPolicy for it; the guard of steps 2 and 3 with its reads
of the cluster (`quader.bridgeFacts`, `quader.bridgeGuard`); the notes of steps 1 and 2; the alert `QuaderBridgeLeftOn`
(Q-HA-92); the value set `ci/bridge.yaml` and the chart tests of it; the UI's download link that fell back to `downloadUrl`
([Q-UI-111](api-and-ui.md#q-ui-111--during-the-upgrade-across-the-cut-the-ui-falls-back-to-files-against-a-replica-of-the-old-shape));
the 50 connections that [Q-HA-98](#q-ha-98--the-connection-budget-of-the-bridge-in-the-scatter-profile) added to the dev
profile's PostgreSQL. The spec names no other use of any of these, and none is a choice an operator has on a fresh installation:
`web.enabled` defaulted to `false`, and a value set without it never rendered the role `web` (R-HA-002).

The binary's role `web` ([architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-001, Q-ARCH-295) is used by more than the bridge. It is the
default role of the integration harness (`Stack.Start` in [test/integration/testenv](../../test/integration/testenv/replica.go),
a replica that serves every family on one listener and claims no job; 57 integration packages), the role of the replicas of the
unit tests of `cmd/quader`, `internal/app`, `internal/api/v1`, `internal/authz`, `internal/cluster`, `internal/config` and others,
and the role the e2e driver's peers and the `quader admin` commands open the database with (`meta.RoleWeb`).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Keep the bridge until the first stable release | Nothing changes | No work; the steps stay ready | A chart shape, two values, a guard that reads the cluster, an alert and a UI fallback for a path no installation can take: what the owner's rule forbids |
| (b) Remove the bridge from the chart, the dev profile and the UI; the binary keeps the role `web` for development and tests (chosen) | R-HA-064, the `web` values, their schema, templates, guard, notes, alert, CI value set and tests, the UI fallback and Q-HA-98's connections go; `web` stays a role of the binary, the API's role enums and the status screen, documented like `all` as a role the chart never renders | The product loses everything only the old shape needed; the integration tests keep testing what they test; the remaining roles render byte for byte as before | The binary keeps a role no deployment runs, and the API's role enums and the status screen keep its name |
| (c) As (b), and remove the role `web` from the binary, the API's role enums and the status screen | The integration harness and the unit tests start `all` or an `api` and `packages` pair behind a path router instead | The binary knows only the roles a deployment or the local profile runs | `all` claims jobs and holds leases, so what 57 integration packages test changes with it; a pair behind a router is a change of the harness of its own; neither is a change of the product, and done tonight it could not be run on the stack across all packages |

**Choice:** (b). What an operator who had set the values sees now: the chart's schema refuses the key `web` before anything
renders (`helm` reports `values don't meet the specifications of the schema(s) in the following chart(s): quader: - at '':
additional properties 'web' not allowed`), so a values file that still carries a `web:` block fails `helm template`,
`helm install` and `helm upgrade` until the block is deleted; nothing else in the rendering changes. The PrometheusRule loses
`QuaderBridgeLeftOn`, and `QuaderReplicasNotReady` matches the Deployments of `api`, `packages` and `worker` only.

**Rationale:** a fresh installation never rendered the bridge, and no Quader installation can reach the shape it bridged from, so
everything that existed for it is a migration path for installations that do not exist. The role `web` in the binary is a different
matter: its users are the tests, not an upgrade, and removing it would rewrite the integration harness for no change of the
product; it is described now as what it is, a development role like `all`. The development agent would revisit (c) when the
integration harness starts `api` and `packages` replicas behind a path router (the shape of the e2e profile `scatter`), from
which point the role `web` has no use. At the first stable release the upgrade guarantees return (R-ARCH-025, R-HA-020,
R-HA-021): a change of the chart's shape between N−1 and N (a renamed or removed Deployment or Service, a moved route) then
needs a stepwise path in the chart and its release notes again, with an upgrade test that runs it, as R-HA-064 gave the cut.

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-064 (removed), the topology, R-HA-001 (the role list), R-HA-002, R-HA-016 (the budget and its
example), R-HA-020, R-HA-021 (the row of the cut), R-HA-028, R-HA-029 (the rows of the guard and of `web`), R-HA-030, R-HA-031
(the values block), R-HA-035, R-HA-037, R-HA-038, R-HA-042, R-HA-045, R-HA-055, the security notes (Valkey); Q-HA-73, Q-HA-74,
Q-HA-79, Q-HA-86, Q-HA-90, Q-HA-92, Q-HA-98, Q-HA-130, Q-HA-131, Q-HA-132, Q-HA-313 (notes), Q-HA-120 (an option's wording);
[architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-001 and Q-ARCH-295; [api-and-ui.md](api-and-ui.md) Q-UI-111, the status screen's
groups and the example of the encryption status; [endpoints.md](endpoints.md) R-EP-002 and R-EP-008;
[operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) (the registry's roles, the examples, the metrics note);
[repositories-and-proxy.md](repositories-and-proxy.md), [storage.md](storage.md), [formats/nuget.md](formats/nuget.md) (a
criterion that named `web.spool`), the [spec README](README.md);
[H-518](../security/roles-and-trust-boundaries.md#h-518--the-development-roles-web-and-all-hold-both-halves-of-the-cut).

### Q-HA-316 · The scanner runs as two replicas of one slot, with 2 GiB of memory and 60 seconds to drain

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. The role and its
Deployment are the owner's (2026-11-20, ADR-212); the figures are the development agent's estimates, not measured.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) 2 replicas × 1 slot, requests 500m and 1 GiB, limit 2 GiB, grace 60 s (chosen) | One analysis per pod at a time | An image that ends its pod's analysis (memory, spool) costs no other image anything; two replicas survive a drain and a node loss | Throughput is two analyses at a time until an operator raises the replicas or turns the autoscaler on |
| (b) 1 replica × 2 slots | Fewer pods | Less memory reserved | No replica during a drain; an image can end or read the other analysis of its pod (H-1037) |
| (c) 2 replicas × 2 slots, limit 4 GiB | More throughput | Double capacity | The collateral of (b), and twice the memory reserved for an installation that scans little |

**Choice:** (a). The 2 GiB limit leaves room above the analyser's soft limit of 512 MiB for its peaks and for the scanner's process; the
grace period lets an analysis near its end finish and kills a long one, which the worker puts off without an attempt (Q-VULN-162).
**Rationale:** a pod per analysis is the isolation the role exists for; scale by replicas. The development agent would revisit the figures
after one measurement of the analyser's peak memory and duration on a large image (a measurement, not a test: run once, written down).

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-031, R-HA-032, R-HA-036, R-HA-065; [vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-025.

### Q-HA-317 · The scanner serves the chart's pair by default; a pair of its own is a value

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. **Superseded** by the
owner's decision [Q-HA-345](#q-ha-345--every-kind-of-pod-has-a-tls-pair-and-a-name-of-its-own-and-the-chart-issues-the-pairs) (2026-11-20):
every kind of pod has a pair of its own, which the chart issues; `scanner.tls.secretName` and `tls.secretName` are gone. Kept as the record of
what was decided before.

Its entries in the decision log: [ADR-212](../decisions.md#adr-212--the-image-analysis-runs-in-a-role-scanner-that-holds-no-secret), [ADR-215](../decisions.md#adr-215--every-kind-of-pod-has-a-tls-pair-and-a-name-of-its-own-which-the-chart-issues).

Context: the owner's rule is that every link inside the chart speaks TLS and that certificates rotate without a restart. The chart's pair is
the one the edge trusts for the backends (R-HA-037).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The chart's pair by default; `scanner.tls.secretName` names a pair of its own (chosen) | Nothing to provision for the plain path | The scanning works with the Secret every installation has; an operator who wants the edge's key out of the scanner adds one Certificate | By default an analyser that an image took over can read the key the edge trusts for `api` and `packages` (H-1035) |
| (b) A pair of its own, required | A second Secret in every installation | The edge's key never enters the scanner | One more prerequisite for an installation that wants the default scanning |
| (c) The chart issues the scanner's pair itself | A self-made CA in the chart | No operator step | A CA the chart would have to keep and rotate, which the chart never does (`tls.secretName` is never created by it) |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** what the key enables is an impersonation of a backend toward the edge, which needs a position in the pod
network that the scanner does not have (no service account, no Kubernetes API); the default stays simple and the option closes it. The
development agent would revisit this if the chart ever renders a cert-manager Certificate itself, which would make (b) free.

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-031, R-HA-065, R-HA-066; H-1035.

### Q-HA-318 · The working space moves with the analysis: the chart checks the scanner's spool, and the worker's returns to 5 Gi

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. Supersedes the
check of Q-VULN-148.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Scanner: budget ≥ `slots × (max_image_size + 64 MiB)`, default `sizeLimit` 6 Gi; worker of `vuln`: budget ≥ 2 GiB + 512 MiB, default `worker.spool.sizeLimit` 5 Gi (chosen) | Each spool is checked against what it holds | Every slot of a scanner fits its largest image, so the scanner never waits for room; the worker gives back the 3 GiB the images took | Two checks instead of one |
| (b) Keep the worker at 8 Gi and add the scanner's | No change for the worker | — | 3 GiB per worker pod reserved for images it no longer holds |
| (c) No check for the scanner | The runtime answers `spool_too_small` | Less chart code | The install passes and the largest images are never analysed |

**Choice:** (a), with `spool.headroom` (2 GiB) as the margin of the analyser's own files (H-871): 6 Gi gives a budget of 4 GiB against the
3 GiB and 64 MiB one slot needs. The worker's check and default change in the change that builds the scanner, because until then the images
still pass through the worker's spool; the values reference of R-HA-031 shows 8Gi until that change, and `scanner.` is listed among the
unbuilt values of its test until then. **Rationale:** the check belongs to the volume that holds the bytes. The development agent would revisit
this when the analyser's own writing is bounded at the operating system (H-871), which would let the margin shrink.

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-031, R-HA-035, R-HA-065; [vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-036, Q-VULN-145, Q-VULN-148.

**Revisited 2026-11-21** ([ADR-229](../decisions.md#adr-229--the-scanner-unit-detects-as-well-and-the-analyser-comes-from-its-own-image)):
the worker's check goes with the detection, because no worker holds the database or a detection's files any more; the scanner's check stays
and covers a detection too (64 MiB, less than an analysis). The database has a volume and a check of its own (R-HA-070, Q-HA-380).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `<fullname>-scanner` and `<fullname>-packages-scan`, always `ClusterIP` (chosen) | Two Services that no value exposes | `service.type: LoadBalancer` on the client Services cannot put the scan listener on the internet; the selectors are exact | Two more objects |
| (b) A port `scan` on `<fullname>-packages` | One Service fewer | Less to render | Every port of a `LoadBalancer` Service is public, so the scan listener would be too |
| (c) A headless Service | Addresses of pods | The worker could pick a pod | The worker would need to resolve and track pods; Q-VULN-170 balances through the Service |

### Q-HA-320 · The scanner admits only the worker Deployment that claims the queue `vuln`

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-212](../decisions.md#adr-212--the-image-analysis-runs-in-a-role-scanner-that-holds-no-secret).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The pods of the pool that lists `vuln`, else of `<fullname>-worker` (chosen) | The chart knows which Deployment claims the queue | Least privilege: the workers that never run the scan job cannot reach the scanner | A change of the pools changes the rule (in the same apply) |
| (b) Every pod with the component `worker` | One selector | Simple | Workers of other queues reach a port they never use |

job needs the scanner.

### Q-HA-321 · The shared extras of the chart do not reach the scanner

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-212](../decisions.md#adr-212--the-image-analysis-runs-in-a-role-scanner-that-holds-no-secret).

Context: `extraEnv`, `extraEnvFrom`, `extraVolumes`, `extraVolumeMounts`, `initContainers` and `sidecars` apply to every Deployment, and an
operator puts credentials into them (a Secret as `extraEnvFrom`, a token file as a volume).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The scanner takes none of them; `scanner.extraEnv` is its own (chosen) | An operator adds to the scanner on purpose | No secret meant for the other roles reaches the pod that holds none | An operator who wants a proxy variable in every pod sets it twice |
| (b) They apply as to every Deployment | One rule | Nothing to explain | A credential meant for the database's roles lands in the scanner without anyone deciding it |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the property of the role is what it does not hold, so nothing should reach it by default. The development
agent would revisit this if operators need a shared value in the scanner that `scanner.extraEnv` cannot carry.

**Revisited 2026-11-21** (R-HA-070): unchanged, and it covers the two containers the pod gains: neither the init container `trivy` nor the
