### Q-HA-322 · With `tls.enabled: false` the scanner's links are plain, as every link of such an installation

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The links follow `tls.enabled` (chosen) | Plain HTTP without TLS, no client certificate | One switch for the installation, as H-38 accepts it | The worker is not authenticated to the scanner; the scan token and the ingress rules remain (H-1043) |
| (b) The chart refuses the image scanning without TLS | A failed render | The links are never plain | An installation that runs without TLS for a reason of its own loses the scanning, or has to switch TLS on for it alone |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the scan token is what decides what the scanner reads, and it is verified by `packages` whatever the
transport; the installation that switched TLS off has accepted H-38 for every link. The development agent would revisit this if the owner
removes `tls.enabled: false`.

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-066; H-1043.

### Q-HA-330 · Step 10 waits for Valkey's first answer, and the startup check names the wait

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. It builds
the owner's decision [Q-HA-293](#q-ha-293--a-replica-waits-for-valkeys-first-answer-before-its-first-readiness-for-a-bounded-time).

Context: the Valkey client is started at step 7 of [architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-024 and keeps trying in the
background; `NewValkey` waits only for the first attempt (`connect_timeout` + 2 × `sentinel_query_timeout` × Sentinels + 1 s,
4.8 s with three Sentinels at the defaults) and returns whatever that attempt met. The readiness registry
([health.go](../../internal/observability/health/health.go)) knows gating checks, first-only checks and reported checks; the
`valkey` check is reported and gates the first readiness only on a configuration error. The question is where the bounded wait
for the first answer lives.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `NewValkey` blocks until the answer or the bound | Step 7 waits | No change outside the client | Every later step (the domain areas, the client listener) waits behind it, so a start during a failover takes the bound plus the rest of the start; the Bastion and every test that builds a client would wait too |
| (b) The `valkey` check holds the first readiness while it has no answer and the bound has not passed | A third way for a reported check to gate, in the readiness registry | `/readyz` names `valkey` under `failing` during the wait | The check runs every `valkey.health_check_interval` (5 s), so readiness follows an answer and the bound up to 5 s late; a new state in the registry for one check |
| (c) Step 10 waits, after every other step, until `Valkey.Answered` is closed or the bound has passed since the client started; the `startup` check's reason is `waiting_for_valkey` meanwhile (chosen) | `awaitValkeyAnswer` in [wire_valkey.go](../../internal/app/wire_valkey.go), called by `bootstrap` in [app.go](../../internal/app/app.go) before the start-up check passes; the forced refresh of step 10 evaluates every check at once afterwards | The wait overlaps the other start steps; readiness follows the answer and the bound at once; the registry and the `valkey` check keep their rules; a refusal ends in the same place as a refusal answered at once | During the wait `/readyz` names `startup` under `failing`, and Valkey only in the verbose checks (`valkey` degraded with its reason code) |

**Choice:** (c). The `startup` check fails with the reason `waiting_for_valkey` while the step waits (`startupCheck` in
[app.go](../../internal/app/app.go)), and with `starting` before. The log has one INFO line when the wait begins (with the
client's reason code, the bound and the time left), one INFO line when the answer ends it, and one WARN line when the bound ends
it: `valkey gave no answer within valkey.startup_answer_timeout: the replica becomes ready without it and runs degraded until
Valkey answers; a wrong credential or certificate shows only then`, with the bound, the reason code and the reason text. A client
that answered before step 10 logs nothing. A replica stopped during the wait ends step 10 with its context.

**Rationale:** the wait is part of the start, and the start's last step is the one place that runs once, after everything else,
and that already forces the registry to evaluate every check. (b) would put the start's timing into the registry and answer late
by up to a check interval; (a) would serialise the start behind Valkey. Readiness after the wait is decided by the unchanged
checks: an accepted credential passes, a refusal is a `ConfigError` that gates the first readiness, silence is `degraded`.
Revisit if operators read `"failing":["startup"]` as a fault of Quader rather than a wait for Valkey; the `valkey` check could then
carry the wait as (b) does, with a wake-up of the registry on the answer.

**Applied:** R-HA-008 (the Valkey bullet); [architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-024 step 10;
[operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-001 (the `startup` row). Code and tests: see Q-HA-293.

### Q-HA-331 · An answer is the login or its refusal, and the first connection also writes the probe key and runs the take script

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: read in valkey-go v1.0.79 (`pipe.go`, `_newPipe`): a connection opens with one pipeline `HELLO 3 AUTH <user>
<password> SETNAME <name>` and `CLIENT SETINFO` (whose errors are ignored); `SELECT` only for a database other than 0. In Sentinel
mode the client first asks a Sentinel on an authenticated connection. The login therefore proves the credential and nothing else:
a user without `EVAL` and `EVALSHA`, which the take of the limits needs since
[Q-LIM-57](usage-and-limits.md#q-lim-57--the-request-windows-are-decided-and-counted-in-one-step-by-a-script-in-the-round-trip-of-stage-7),
or whose key pattern does not cover `valkey.key_prefix`, logged in, became ready and met `NOPERM` at the first limited request
and at the first probe: the circuit opened and closed in turn and every limit counted per replica. The server-settings row of
R-HA-056 said "no scripting command" until this change, so that ACL was the documented one.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The login only | An answer is HELLO answered (accepted) or a refusal that `classifyStartup` already reads | No new command | The window Q-HA-293 closes for a wrong password stays open for a wrong ACL: the replica is ready and counts its limits alone |
| (b) The login, and on the first connection one write of the replica's probe key and the take script with no key, as `EVAL` and then `EVALSHA` (chosen) | `checkAccess` in [valkey_answer.go](../../internal/cluster/valkey_answer.go); the script with no window and no marker reads and writes nothing and answers `{1, nil}`; the script runs only for a client made with `WithScriptCheck` (the main installation's) | Catches the ACL that the documents made likely and a key pattern that misses the prefix; three commands once per process; `EVAL` first loads the script, so a user with `EVALSHA` but no `EVAL` is caught as well | Other commands of R-ARCH-031's list are not checked ([H-1050](#h-1050--only-the-probe-write-and-the-take-script-are-checked-at-start-another-missing-command-shows-at-its-first-use)) |
| (c) Every command of the list at start | Each command once | Complete | Writes, publishes, subscribes and opens a transaction in the installation's keyspace at every start for what the first use shows as well; `ACL DRYRUN` would test them without effect, but it is an administrative command the user must not have |

**Choice:** (b). What each outcome of an attempt is, and why:

| The attempt meets | Answer or silence | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `HELLO 3 AUTH` answered with the server map by the data node (after a Sentinel named it on an authenticated connection), and the access check passes or fails for another reason than a refusal | answer: accepted | The server checked the credential. Another failure of the access check (`OOM`, a deadline after the login) is logged and left to the health probe, which reports it as before |
| A server below 9.0 answers `HELLO` | answer: accepted, the client runs degraded (`unsupported`) | The version is a state, not a credential (R-ARCH-031) |
| `WRONGPASS` or `NOAUTH` from the data node, or from every reachable Sentinel | answer: refused | The credential was checked and rejected |
| `NOPERM` from `HELLO`, a Sentinel command, the probe write or `EVAL`/`EVALSHA` of the access check | answer: refused | The user may not do what Quader needs; the log names the step (`the take script (EVAL): NOPERM …`) |
| A certificate the replica does not trust, a host name the certificate does not carry, a server that does not speak TLS, a TLS alert (a client certificate refused) | answer: refused | The server answered the handshake; the mismatch does not pass with time. A certificate the replica does not trust is not silence |
| Every reachable Sentinel answers that it does not know `valkey.sentinel.primary_name` | answer: refused | As Q-HA-13 (d); during a failover a Sentinel still names the old primary, so a null answer is not a failover |
| A connection, a handshake or a command that ends at its deadline | silence | A starved or partitioned node, or a primary that died before the Sentinels noticed |
| A refused or reset connection, EOF | silence | A pod that is restarting or being rescheduled |
| No Sentinel reachable | silence | The Sentinels are restarting or cut off |
| A Sentinel names a primary that does not answer | silence | A failover in progress |
| `LOADING`, `MASTERDOWN`, `BUSY`, `TRYAGAIN` | silence | A node that is loading or a replica without its primary; it passes |
| A host name that does not resolve | silence | A pod being rescheduled has no DNS record for seconds; a mistyped name shows only after the bound ([H-1051](#h-1051--a-mistyped-valkey-or-sentinel-address-is-silence-and-the-replica-becomes-ready-degraded-after-the-bound)) |

A refusal sets the client's start-up error, closes `Answered` and is classified as before (`auth_failed` for `WRONGPASS`,
`NOAUTH` and `NOPERM`, `config_error` for TLS and the primary name; `quader_valkey_errors_total{kind}` `auth`, `tls`,
`no_primary`). The log line `valkey configuration error` carries the server's reply, never the password or its length.

**Rationale:** the owner asked that a wrong credential show before the first request; a wrong ACL has the same consequence (the
replica counts its limits alone) and is found by the same answer for three commands once per process. The Bastion's user has no
scripting command (R-BAS-034), so the script runs only with `WithScriptCheck`; its probe write is checked as well, which changes
nothing for its readiness (Q-HA-333). Revisit when another command is added to the list that an operator's ACL is likely to deny,
or when a missing command is found in a running installation (then (c), or that command in (b)).

**Applied:** R-HA-008, R-HA-056 (the ACL row and an acceptance criterion); [architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-031 (the
ACL and the start); [privilege-footprint.md](../security/privilege-footprint.md#valkey).

### Q-HA-332 · The bound is the setting `valkey.startup_answer_timeout`, 30 s by default

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. The owner
was told that the bound is derived from the measured failover times.

What the bound has to cover is a start during an ordinary failover: the primary is lost as the replica starts, the Sentinels name
a new one, and the replica's next attempt reaches it. The numbers, each with its source:

| Quantity | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `down-after-milliseconds` | 5 s recommended for production and set in the local profile; 3 s in the integration stack | R-HA-056 server settings; [local-profile.md](../developer/local-profile.md#valkey-and-sentinel); [sentinel.conf](../../test/integration/conf/sentinel.conf) |
| `failover-timeout` | 60 s in the local profile (Valkey's default); 15 s in the integration stack | the same |
| Election after `down-after` | up to 1 s of random delay before a Sentinel starts, then up to 10 s for the election: 16 s after the loss at 5 s | [valkeyhold.go](../../test/e2e/valkeyhold/valkeyhold.go) (`AssistAfter`, Q-HA-181) |
| Degraded window the spec allows a running replica after a primary loss | `down-after-milliseconds` + 15 s = 20 s | R-HA-057, criterion "Primary loss" |
| Measured: planned failover, every replica on the new primary | 2 s (E0.13, `TestNPMHA`, `TestNuGetHA`); 7.4 to 8.0 s (`TestHAFaults_ValkeyPlannedFailover`, nightly 42601429868) | [e2e.md](../developer/e2e.md) |
| Measured: primary pod force-deleted | 10 s (E0.13) | [e2e.md](../developer/e2e.md) |
| One retry of a starting client | backoff up to `reconnect.max_backoff` 5 s, then the attempt: up to 0.9 s for three Sentinels at `sentinel_query_timeout` 0.3 s and up to `connect_timeout` 2 s for the primary, then up to 0.6 s for the probe of the Sentinels after a failure: 8.5 s | [config/valkey.go](../../internal/config/valkey.go), `connectLoop` and `connectFailed` in [valkey.go](../../internal/cluster/valkey.go) |
| A split election after a drain | the next automatic failover after 2 × `failover-timeout` = 120 s | Q-HA-181; this is "a Valkey that is away for longer" and is not meant to fit |

So the answer of a start during an ordinary failover comes at most one retry after the new primary is named: 10 s + 8.5 s =
18.5 s for the slowest measured failover, 20 s + 8.5 s = 28.5 s for the worst the spec allows. 30 s holds both, the measured case
with 11.5 s to spare. Against the chart's probes ([values.yaml](../../deploy/helm/quader/values.yaml) `probes`): the startup and
liveness probes read `/healthz`, which never reads readiness (R-OPS-001) and is served from step 2 on, before the wait, so the
startup probe's budget (2 s × 60 = 120 s) and the liveness probe's (10 s × 6 = 60 s) are not spent by it; the readiness probe
(5 s, failure threshold 1) only keeps the pod out of the Service. A Deployment's progress deadline (Kubernetes' default 600 s, the
chart sets none) is far above the bound; `minReadySeconds: 10` comes after it.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A constant of 30 s | Nothing to configure | The plain path | An operator of a Valkey that fails over more slowly (a larger `down-after-milliseconds`, a managed service that takes a minute) cannot make a start during its failover wait for the answer |
| (b) A setting `valkey.startup_answer_timeout`, default 30 s, 0 to 5 min, 0 = no wait (chosen) | [config/valkey.go](../../internal/config/valkey.go), validated by the configuration check | The default fits the reference topology; a slower Valkey gets a longer bound; the integration harness sets 0 for its stacks with Valkey stopped, which test the degraded mode and not the start | One more key, an expert one; 0 brings back the window Q-HA-293 closed, and the documentation says so |
| (c) Derived at run time from the client's settings | `connect_timeout`, the backoff and the Sentinel timeout | Follows the client's settings | The Sentinels' `down-after-milliseconds` and the election dominate the sum, and the client cannot read them |

**Choice:** (b). The ceiling of 5 minutes keeps the owner's "a Valkey that is away for longer holds no start" true for every
value: above it a start would wait out the split election of Q-HA-181 and more. The bound counts from the client's start at step
7, so the time of steps 8 and 9 is part of it.

**Measured with real Sentinels on 2026-11-24** (a measurement, not a test, by the rule "Tests stay runnable" of the repository's
`CLAUDE.md`): on instance 2 of the integration stack (three Sentinels, `down-after-milliseconds` 3 s, `failover-timeout` 15 s), the
primary's container was paused with `docker pause`, so it accepted connections and answered nothing, and a client of
`internal/cluster` started at once with the production defaults of the retry (`connect_timeout` 2 s, `sentinel_query_timeout` 0.3 s,
`reconnect.max_backoff` 5 s). It had no start-up error, got its first answer 6.1 s after its start from the promoted replica and was
bound to it: a fifth of the bound, and below the 18.5 s computed above for the slowest failover measured on a cluster (a primary pod
force-deleted, 10 s, with `down-after-milliseconds` 5 s where the stack has 3 s). One run; the election's random delay makes the next one differ by a second or two.
It was not kept as a test: the failover took seconds, but returning the stack to its initial layout (the old primary back as a replica,
the Sentinels' view of it, a failover back) took another 31 s, 38 s in all, and the flow it would hold is held in milliseconds by
`TestR_HA_008_StartDuringASentinelFailoverWaitsForTheNewPrimary` (unit, `internal/cluster`, a stand-in Sentinel that first names a
primary that never answers). To repeat it: the case `TestFailover` of `test/integration/valkey` shows the helpers (`sentinelPrimary`,
`waitSentinelReplica`, `restoreLayout`); `QUADER_TEST_VALKEY_CONTAINERS` names the containers in the order of
`QUADER_TEST_VALKEY_NODES`.

**Rationale:** the default follows from the numbers above; the setting exists for the one thing Quader cannot know, the failover
time of a Valkey it does not run. Revisit when a start during an ordinary failover reaches the bound (the WARN line while the
Sentinels fail over), or when the measured failover times change (a new Valkey operator, other Sentinel settings).

**Applied:** R-HA-056 (the configuration block); [README.md](../../README.md) (the configuration reference);
[operations.md](../manual/admin/operations.md). The chart passes `config.valkey.startup_answer_timeout` through like every other
key of the section; no chart file changes.

### Q-HA-333 · The Bastion does not wait for Valkey's first answer

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: every role of the binary (`api`, `packages`, `worker`, and the development roles `web` and `all`) starts the Valkey
client at step 7 and runs step 10, so all of them wait (Q-HA-330); the `shell` has no client. The quader Bastion
(`--role bastion`) uses the same client, `cluster.NewValkey` with `WithoutKeyspace`, from
[shared/valkey.go](../../internal/bastion/shared/valkey.go) (`Open`), and its Valkey is optional: "Valkey being unavailable never
makes a replica unready" ([bastion.md](bastion.md) R-BAS-034), and that includes a refusal, which `Open` only logs.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The Bastion waits as well | Its start holds until the first answer or the bound | One rule for every process | A wait ends in the same state as no wait: a refusal does not hold a Bastion back, so the wait would only delay its readiness |
| (b) The Bastion keeps its start; its client checks the probe write at the first connection like every client, without the script (chosen) | `Open` logs a refusal found in the first attempt as before | R-BAS-034 unchanged; a wrong key pattern of the Bastion's user is logged at start | A Bastion with a wrong credential behind a silent first attempt logs the refusal only when it comes |

**Choice:** (b). **Rationale:** the owner's decision is about a replica that would take requests and count its limits alone
before its mistake shows; a Bastion does that whatever the answer, by R-BAS-034. Revisit if the Bastion's first readiness is ever
to be held on a Valkey configuration error; the wait of Q-HA-330 then applies to it unchanged.

**Applied:** nothing in [bastion.md](bastion.md); [valkey.md](../developer/valkey.md#start-up) says which clients run the script.

### Q-HA-340 · With `tls.ops`, the scanner mounts the pair of its operations listener

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. **Superseded** by
[Q-HA-347](#q-ha-347--tlscertmanager-issues-a-certificate-per-kind-tlsexistingsecrets-names-a-secret-per-kind-instead): `tls.ops` is gone, because the pair
of every pod is its kind's already, and the operations listener serves it. Kept as the record of what was decided before.

Context: R-HA-065 lists the scanner's volumes as five and nothing else. With `tls.ops.secretName` the configuration file names the
operations listener's own pair (`server.ops_tls`, R-HA-063), and the ServiceMonitor verifies every pod behind `<fullname>-ops` against that
Secret's CA under `<fullname>-ops.<namespace>.svc`; the scanner's pods are behind that Service.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The scanner mounts the ops pair, as every other pod does with `tls.ops` (chosen) | A sixth volume, only with `tls.ops.secretName` | The scrape of the scanner verifies like every other; one rendered configuration file serves every role | One more key in the scanner's pod, of a listener that admits probes and scrapers only |
| (b) The scanner's operations listener inherits the client pair | Five volumes always | The list of R-HA-065 holds | The ServiceMonitor fails to verify the scanner's pods when the two pairs come from different CAs; the scanner needs a configuration file of its own |
| (c) No scrape of the scanner | — | — | Its series (`quader_scanner_*`) and its alert's evidence are gone |

**Choice:** (a) ([vuln-scanner-trivy.yaml](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/vuln-scanner-trivy.yaml), `TestR_HA_065_TheScannerHoldsNoSecretOfTheInstallation`
in `test/chart`). **Rationale:** the pair of the operations listener is the one every pod serves to probes and scrapers; it grants nothing on
the image scanning's links. The development agent would revisit this if the operations listener of the scanner moves to plain HTTP.

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-061, R-HA-065.

### Q-HA-342 · The end-to-end case reads the scanner pod's files from its live spec

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: R-HA-065's end-to-end criterion lists the files below `/var/run/secrets/` with `kubectl exec`. The image is distroless: the binary
and the analyser, no shell and no `ls`.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Read the running pod's volumes, their items and the container's mounts with `kubectl get pod -o json` (chosen) | The files the kubelet projects are exactly the items of the pod's Secret volumes | No change to the image; the live spec includes whatever an admission webhook added, which is what the criterion guards against | The files themselves are not listed |
| (b) `kubectl debug` with an ephemeral busybox container | A shell beside the scanner | Lists the files | The namespace's Pod Security level and the scanner's user decide whether it may read them; a second image to pin |
| (c) A `quader` subcommand that lists a directory | A list from inside | Lists the files | A command in the product for a test |

**Choice:** (a) (`TestVuln_R_VULN_041_AnImagePushedToALocalRepositoryIsAnalysedByAScannerPod`, `test/e2e/vuln_scanner_test.go`). **Rationale:**
what the kubelet mounts is what the pod spec projects; reading the spec after admission is the faithful check without a tool in the image.
The development agent would revisit this if the image gains a shell for another reason.

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-065.

**Revisited 2026-11-21** (R-HA-070): the same read covers the init container `trivy` (one volume, no Secret) and the container `database`
(the scanner's Secret, `trivy-db` read-write, a `/tmp` of its own), and that `quader` mounts `trivy-bin` and `trivy-db` read-only. The

### Q-HA-343 · The scanner pod names no service account of the chart

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The scanner's pod sets no `serviceAccountName` and `automountServiceAccountToken: false` (chosen) | It runs under the namespace's `default` account and mounts no token | The chart's account may carry a cloud identity of the object store (IRSA, workload identity); a pod that holds no secret should not hold that either | An operator who restricts the namespace's `default` account sees the scanner use it |
| (b) The chart's service account, with the token not mounted | As the other pods | One account | The cloud identity is bound to the account, not to the token mount: a web-identity webhook injects its own projected token by the account's annotation |
| (c) An account of its own (`scanner.serviceAccount`) | A new object and value | Explicit | A value and an object for an account that needs no right |

**Choice:** (a) ([vuln-scanner-trivy.yaml](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/vuln-scanner-trivy.yaml), `TestR_HA_065_TheScannerHoldsNoSecretOfTheInstallation`).
**Rationale:** the scanner calls no API, so the account it runs under matters only for what an injection could attach to it, and `default`
carries nothing the chart added. The development agent would revisit this if a cluster's policy refuses pods of the `default` account; the
value of option (c) then follows.

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-065; [security/privilege-footprint.md](../security/privilege-footprint.md) and its gap
[H-1070](../security/privilege-footprint.md#h-1070--the-scanner-runs-under-the-namespaces-default-service-account).

### Q-HA-344 · The scanner carries the serve label; the Valkey policy of the local profile names Valkey's clients

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the pods of the chart's serving Deployments carry `quader/serve: "true"`, which the Service `<fullname>-ops` selects (and with it
the ServiceMonitor), and which the local profile's Valkey policy (`deploy/dev/valkey.yaml`, `quader-valkey-clients`) and the dev scripts
(`drain.sh`, `valkey-credential.sh`) read as "Quader's pods". R-HA-065 wants the scanner behind `<fullname>-ops`; the security pages say
that Valkey's ingress example does not admit the scanner. With the label on the scanner, the profile's policy admitted it to Valkey.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The scanner keeps the label; the Valkey policies of the profile (`valkey.yaml`, `restore-ns.yaml`) admit the components `api`, `packages`, `worker` and `e2e-driver` by name (chosen) | An allow-list on the side that needs one | The ops Service and the ServiceMonitor see the scanner as R-HA-065 says; a component added later reaches Valkey only when named | The policy repeats the list of roles |
| (b) No serve label on the scanner | The scanner outside every selector of the label | No policy change | A second ops Service or a second ServiceMonitor endpoint for one Deployment; the label's one meaning ("served by the ops Service") breaks |
| (c) The label, and `NotIn [scanner]` in the policies | A deny-list | One line | A future component that holds no Valkey credential is admitted by default |

**Choice:** (a). `drain.sh` evicts the scanner's pods with the release's, as it always did by the release's labels, and now waits for the
scanner's rollout too; the drain tests of the nightly watch the replicas of `api`, `packages` and `worker` (`selQuader`) and neither pick
a node by the scanner nor check its pods, which is right for a pod that serves no client and keeps no job. `valkey-credential.sh` closes the
Valkey connections of every serving pod's address; the scanner has none, so it is not affected. **Rationale:** the label says what the
ops Service selects; who may reach Valkey is said where Valkey is. The development agent would revisit this if the chart rendered Valkey's
policy itself.

The list missed the component `e2e-replica` of the extra replicas that `TestE12Valkey` starts (Test and Release 44803754281, `e2e (push)`:
they reached no Sentinel and could not see their misconfiguration); `valkey.yaml` names it now, and the E0.12 case with every Sentinel
unreachable starts its replica with the scanner's component label, so the leg shows that the policy drops the scanner. `restore-ns.yaml`
keeps its list: the suite starts no extra replica in the restore namespace.

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-065; [local-profile.md](../developer/local-profile.md), [e2e.md](../developer/e2e.md#the-driver).

### Q-HA-345 · Every kind of pod has a TLS pair and a name of its own, and the chart issues the pairs

Status: **Decided by the owner (2026-11-20)** — option (c). Supersedes [Q-HA-317](#q-ha-317--the-scanner-serves-the-charts-pair-by-default-a-pair-of-its-own-is-a-value)
and what [Q-VULN-163](vulnerability-scanning.md#q-vuln-163--the-worker-proves-itself-to-the-scanner-with-the-charts-certificate) says of the
chart's one pair.

Context: the owner's installation certificate allows server authentication only, so with the one pair of `tls.secretName` the scanner stayed
not ready (R-HA-065). The review of the scanner role found that the scanner held the pair the edge trusts for `api` and `packages` (H-1035),
that a pair of the scanner's own had to carry the edge's name (R-HA-066), and that the links admitted any client certificate of the CA (the
owner's issuer had issued 76 certificates, 28 of them with client authentication); Q-HA-317 had dismissed a required pair of the scanner's
own until the chart would render cert-manager Certificates itself. The owner asked: "Option A, macht es vielleicht Sinn das jeder Pod-kind
sein eigenes Cert erhält?" The options were put to him so:

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) As built: one pair for all | The scanner holds the edge's key | Nothing to provision beyond the one Secret | A taken-over analyser holds the identity the edge trusts for `api` and `packages`, and every link admits any holder of a certificate of the CA |
| (b) Only the scanner gets a pair and a name of its own, required; the rest share | A second Secret, the scanner's name checked on its links | The edge's key leaves the scanner; one more Secret, not four | A special case for one kind; `api`, `packages` and the worker still share one identity |
| (c) Every kind of pod (`api`, `packages`, `worker`, `scanner`) gets a pair and a name of its own; each link checks the name of the other side; the chart issues the pairs through cert-manager from one issuer value itself; an installation without cert-manager names a Secret per kind | Four Certificates the chart renders, or four Secrets | One rule without a special case, also for future kinds; a chart that knows the names and the usages, so the operator writes neither | cert-manager becomes the standard path; over (b) it gains little for `api`, `packages` and the worker |

The owner answered: "Option c".

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-031, R-HA-037, R-HA-063, R-HA-065 to R-HA-067, Q-HA-346 to Q-HA-349;
[architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-038, Q-ARCH-552, Q-ARCH-553;
[vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) Q-VULN-185;
[ADR-215](../decisions.md#adr-215--every-kind-of-pod-has-a-tls-pair-and-a-name-of-its-own-which-the-chart-issues);
[security/image-scanning.md](../security/image-scanning.md) H-1035, [security/transport-encryption.md](../security/transport-encryption.md)
H-1071 to H-1073.

### Q-HA-346 · Four kinds hold a pair; each names its kind and the operations Service

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. The names of the
scanners' kinds, `scanner` here and `malware-scanner` of R-HA-068, are superseded by the owner's decision
[Q-HA-372](#q-ha-372--a-unit-that-runs-a-tool-carries-the-tools-name) (2026-11-21): `vuln-scanner-trivy` and `malware-scanner-clamav`.
The rest stands; the text below keeps the names of its day.

Context: the owner's decision names the kinds `api`, `packages`, `worker` and `scanner`. Left to work out: what a pool is, which other pods of
the chart would need a pair, the names each pair carries, and its usages. The pods of a kind run the same code and mount the same secrets
(R-HA-030); a pool is a Deployment of its role for a share of the load (R-HA-062). The migration Job, the backup and restore pods and the
post-restore Job open no TLS listener (a backup run serves its counters in plain HTTP while it lasts, R-BAK-014) and call no pod of Quader. The Bastion is a
chart of its own whose clients dial `<fullname>-api.<namespace>.svc`.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Four kinds; pools and endpoint pools carry their role's pair; the Jobs and the backup pods none; the names `<fullname>-<kind>.<namespace>.svc` and `<fullname>-ops.<namespace>.svc`; `server auth` on every pair, `client auth` on the worker's and the scanner's only (chosen) | Three or four Certificates | The kind is where the secrets differ, so a stolen pair separates what a takeover of its pod would separate; the names of `api`, `packages` and `scanner` are their Services' names, so a client that dials the Service (the Bastion, the worker) verifies without a name of its own; a pair of `api` or `packages` cannot pose as a client on a link | The worker has no Service, so its name is an identity only |
| (b) A pair per Deployment, pools included | A Certificate per pool | Finer | The edge and the links would need a name per pool; a pool holds its role's secrets, so its own pair separates nothing a thief of the pod could not do |
| (c) Four kinds, every pair with `client auth` | One Certificate template | Simpler | A stolen pair of `api` or `packages` would be a client certificate that no link needs, accepted wherever only the CA is checked |

**Choice:** (a). The ops name is in every pair because one ServiceMonitor endpoint scrapes every pod under one name (Q-HA-349). The Bastion
keeps its own chart's pair. **Rationale:** the boundary of a pair is the boundary of what its pod holds; the usages follow what each kind does
on a link. The development agent would revisit this when a pool runs code or holds secrets its role's main Deployment does not, or when a Job
calls a pod of Quader.

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-063, R-HA-066.

### Q-HA-347 · `tls.certManager` issues a Certificate per kind; `tls.existingSecrets` names a Secret per kind instead

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the owner's decision is one issuer value for the chart and a Secret per kind for an installation without cert-manager. Left to
work out: the values, the checks, the keys, where the CA of the links and of the edge comes from, and what becomes of the values of the
one pair. Before the first stable release nothing has to stay compatible.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `tls.certManager.issuerRef` (`name`, `kind` `ClusterIssuer`, `group`) renders `Certificate` `<fullname>-tls-<kind>`; `tls.certManager` holds `duration` 2160h, `renewBefore` 720h, the private key (ECDSA 256, `rotationPolicy: Always`) and extra names for port-forward clients; without an issuer, `tls.existingSecrets.<kind>`, each a different Secret with the fixed keys `tls.crt`, `tls.key`, `ca.crt`; the render fails with neither, with both, or with one Secret for two kinds; `tls.secretName`, `certKey`, `keyKey`, `tls.ops`, `scanner.tls` and `tls.backendTLSPolicy.hostname` go (chosen) | One way per installation | The plain path is one value; the chart writes the names and usages; a Secret named twice would bring back one pair for several kinds, so it is refused | An installation that names its Secrets writes four |
| (b) The issuer path only | No `tls.existingSecrets` | Less to render | The owner's decision names the Secret path |
| (c) `tls.existingSecrets` that may name one Secret for several kinds | Lenient | An operator with one pair keeps it | Undoes the decision without a word, and a pair for all would need every name and both usages |

**Choice:** (a). The CA comes from the Secrets themselves: a pod verifies its links against the `ca.crt` of its own Secret, the edge against
that of the Secret of the pair the backend serves (`ingress.backendTLS.caSecret` names another when the operator wants one), and the
ServiceMonitor against that of `api`'s Secret. All of them must chain to one CA, which one issuer gives. The Certificates are ordinary objects
of the release, not hooks, so cert-manager renews them; on a first install a pod waits for its Secret until cert-manager has issued it. The
extra names are for the local profile's tests, which reach single pods through a port-forward under `localhost`; a name every pair carries is
a name no check relies on. The names of the values follow the Bastion's chart (`tls.existingSecret`, `tls.certManager.issuerRef`, `duration`,
`renewBefore`), so the two charts are configured alike. **Rationale:** the plain path stays one value, and a value that could undo the owner's
rule does not exist. The
development agent would revisit this when an operator needs a key the Certificate template does not offer (a subject, a CA bundle of
trust-manager for the links).

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-031, R-HA-063, R-HA-065; [endpoints.md](endpoints.md) R-EP-008.

### Q-HA-348 · The edge verifies each backend under its kind's name; the setting goes where each controller reads it

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the default endpoint's Ingress routes the paths of one host to the Services of two kinds, and each controller reads its backend
settings in a different place: HAProxy Ingress reads backend keys from the Ingress and from each Service, Traefik its transport from each
Service, the Gateway API's BackendTLSPolicy targets a Service, and ingress-nginx reads `proxy-ssl-name` from the Ingress only. One Ingress
per host is what the tests, the local profile and an operator's annotations (body size, timeouts) are written against, and cert-manager's
ingress-shim must see an Ingress's TLS Secret once.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The name per Service where the controller reads it there (HAProxy Ingress, Traefik, BackendTLSPolicy); for ingress-nginx an Ingress per kind, the `spec.tls` on the first only (chosen) | One Ingress for the primary controller, two for ingress-nginx | Each backend is verified under its kind's name; the primary path changes nothing an operator wrote on the Ingress | ingress-nginx, retired in March 2026, gets a second Ingress that carries the operator's annotations too |
| (b) An Ingress per kind for every controller | Two Ingress objects everywhere | One mechanism | Every operator annotation lands on two objects; tests and the local profile that address the Ingress by name split |
| (c) One name shared by `api` and `packages` toward the edge | One name per Ingress, as before | Nothing changes at the edge | A stolen pair of either kind passes as the other toward the edge, the separation the owner chose |

**Choice:** (a). The CA defaults to the `ca.crt` of the Secret of the pair the backend serves, so verification needs no value. Traefik's
ServersTransport carries the name, so the operator names one per kind (`serversTransports.api`, `.packages`). **Rationale:** the name belongs
to the backend, so it goes where the controller reads a backend's settings. That HAProxy Ingress takes `secure-sni` from the Service
annotation was looked at on the local profile's kind cluster (the HAProxy Ingress chart 0.16.3) with the change that built this: with the Service
`quader-api` annotated with the name of `packages`, `/api/v1/system/ping` through the edge was answered `503`, and `200` again with its own
name. The development agent would revisit this when ingress-nginx is dropped from the chart.

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-037, R-HA-063; [endpoints.md](endpoints.md) R-EP-008.

### Q-HA-349 · Every pair also carries the operations name, and the scrape verifies that name

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: one ServiceMonitor endpoint scrapes the Service `<fullname>-ops`, which selects the pods of every kind on `8081`; Prometheus takes
one `serverName` per endpoint.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Every pair carries `<fullname>-ops.<namespace>.svc`; the ServiceMonitor verifies it against `api`'s `ca.crt` (chosen) | One name more per pair | One scrape configuration, as before | A pair of any kind passes as the operations listener of any pod toward the scrape (H-1071) |
| (b) An ops Service and a ServiceMonitor endpoint per kind, each under its kind's name | Four Services and endpoints | The scrape checks the kind | Four objects to keep in step for a read of metrics; the ops name would stay in no pair, but the scrape's `ca` would still be one CA |
| (c) The scrape without a name check | Nothing to name | — | Any certificate of the CA would pass, also a stranger's |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the scrape reads metrics and sends a bearer token only with `metrics.auth: static`; a forged answer needs a
position in the pod network and changes numbers, not data. The development agent would revisit this when a scrape carries a credential that a
false operations listener could take (H-1071).

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-063.

### Q-HA-361 · The malware scanner's default size

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. Its figures were
measured on 2026-11-21 (below) and the request of `clamd` lowered to them.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) 2 replicas of 2 slots; `clamd` 1.5 GiB requested, 2 GiB limit, no concurrent reload; 8 GiB of temporary space (chosen) | About 5 GiB of memory limits | Survives a drain and a node; four calls at a time, one kept for a waiting download | Memory that a small installation pays even when it stores little |
| (b) 1 replica | Half | Cheaper | A drain stops every scan, and under the switch every new download |
| (c) Concurrent reload on | Scans go on during a reload | No pause | Twice the memory at each reload |

**Choice:** (a); the figures were ClamAV's documented ones until the scanner was built. **Applied in the spec:** R-HA-068;
[malware-scanning.md](malware-scanning.md) R-MAL-027.

Measured on 2026-11-21 with `clamd` of `CLAMAV_IMAGE` (1.5.5, linux/arm64) in the malware scanner pods of a kind cluster on the development
machine, and the same image in Docker, once each; ClamAV's whole database of that day (main 63, daily 28189, bytecode 339: 3,628,278
signatures, 113 MB of files) was deployed to the profile's database repository from the copy `freshclam` had fetched for the source tree's scan
(R-MAL-031), so no second download from ClamAV's network was made:

| What | With ClamAV's whole database | With the tests' database of a few signatures |
|---|---|---|
| `clamd` resident (`VmRSS`), loaded | 994 and 1,000 MiB in the two pods | 21 MiB |
| the `clamd` container's cgroup peak (`memory.peak`), loaded | 1,001 and 1,052 MiB (page cache included) | — |
| `clamd`'s resident peak through a `RELOAD` (`ConcurrentDatabaseReload no`) | 990 MiB, no second copy; with the option on 1,929 MiB (Docker) | — |
| load at a start, `clamd` alone (Docker) | 8.3 s to the first `PONG` | under a second |
| a new malware scanner pod from its start to ready (the loader's fetch from the scan listener, the load) | 21 s | 9 s |
| a new version: the loader's next look (at most a minute), its fetch and the `RELOAD`; the pod is not ready while `clamd` loads | under 60 s, the load about 9 s | — |
| one `INSTREAM` of random bytes, warm (the first of each size in brackets) | 1 KiB 3 ms (12 ms), 1 MiB 5 ms (78 ms), 100 MiB 250 ms (4.3 s) | — |

`clamd` ran as user 65532 with a read-only root file system and every capability dropped (the chart's security context): it writes only its
socket in `/run/clamd`, its temporary files in `/var/tmp/clamd` and nothing in `/var/lib/clamav`, which the scanner fills. With these figures
`clamd` requests 1280Mi (from 1536Mi); its limit stays 2Gi, which leaves the slots' scans 0.9 GiB above the loaded database.
