### Q-HA-370 · A pooler instance's failure window ends a `server_login_retry` after its last failed server attempt

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: F-165 of the project plan. `TestHAPooler_Switchover` failed in two full nightlies, each time on one instance of a pooler whose
sibling was back after about 8 s: `quader-db-pooler-rw-…-82mgv` with 33.7 s (run 44653040868, 2026-11-20) and
`quader-db-pooler-control-…-6slbk` with 69.4 s (run 44828435420, 2026-11-21), against a bound of 20 s. The test measured each instance's
window from its first to its last failure line. Read in the artifacts of both runs: PgBouncer starts a server attempt only when a client
asks for one, and not within `server_login_retry` of the last; the client that starts it is refused with the pool's last error ("server login
has been failing, cached error: …"). After its failed login on the new primary (the second failure of Q-HA-302, 00:37:43.783), 6slbk
refused the one client that came 0.75 s later, inside the retry second, and then had no client for 61 s: every replica keeps a single
control connection (the control pool's `max_conns` and `min_conns` are 1), each had gone to the sibling, and the next one to reach 6slbk was a
connection that a replica replaced at its lifetime (60 s + jitter in the profile), 61.7 s after that replica had logged in at the sibling.
That client was refused with the error of 00:37:43.783, the server login it started succeeded at once, and the next client was served. The
pod used 0.000 cores for the whole minute (the leg's `pods.csv`). 82mgv ended the same way after 13.7 s without a client; before that its
pool for the authentication query had a connect that failed only after 15 s (Q-HA-371).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The window ends at the instance's last failed server attempt plus its `server_login_retry`, or at its last failure line when that is earlier; a later refusal is logged, not counted (chosen) | `poolerlog.Read`; the retry is read from the instance's rendered `pgbouncer.ini` | Measures what the bound is about: how long the server could not be reached or logged in to, plus the one interval PgBouncer then waits; independent of how many clients an instance gets; a connect that hangs counts to its end | The refusal of the first client after a quiet spell is not in the window, only in the test's log |
| (b) The window ends at the instance's first successful server login after the switchover | The `new connection to server` lines | One event to read | An instance that no client asks makes no login: 6slbk's window would again be 69 s |
| (c) Keep the first-to-last reading, and send a client to each instance every second | A probe per instance | The window would be what a client sees | Load the test adds only to make its reading true |
| (d) `min_pool_size` on the poolers, so an instance keeps a server connection without clients | PgBouncer's own refill | Would remove the quiet spell | PgBouncer's documentation enforces it only for a pool with a client or a forced user; with CloudNativePG's `auth_query` and no client it does nothing in exactly this case (not tried) |

**Choice:** (a). Read with it, the four instances of 2026-11-21 had 7.6 to 9.1 s (6slbk 8.6 s) and those of 2026-11-20 7.3 to 8.1 s,
except 82mgv with 21.1 s, which stays a failure for the reason Q-HA-371 removes. **What stays:** an instance whose last server login failed
and that then gets no client refuses its next client once, however much later; Quader retries that answer (`08P01` "server login has
been failing", Q-HA-266) and the
client after it is served. Under load the client that starts the next attempt comes milliseconds after the retry interval, and is logged the
same way.

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-058 (the switchover bullet, its acceptance criterion), Q-HA-302's test paragraph. Code:
[poolerlog](../../test/e2e/poolerlog/poolerlog.go), `poolerFailures` in
[ha_pooler_switchover_test.go](../../test/e2e/ha_pooler_switchover_test.go). Tests: `TestR_HA_058_…` in
[poolerlog_test.go](../../test/e2e/poolerlog/poolerlog_test.go), built from the lines of both runs.

### Q-HA-371 · The poolers give up a server connect after 5 s

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: F-165, the run of 2026-11-20 (44653040868). The pool of `quader-db-pooler-rw-…-82mgv` for CloudNativePG's authentication query
(`postgres/cnpg_pooler_pgbouncer`) started a connect at 05:15:12.5, while the read-write Service moved to the new primary; it got no answer
and failed at 05:15:27.510 with `connect failed (age=15s)`, PgBouncer's `server_connect_timeout` of 15 s by default, which bounds the connect
and the login together ([config](https://www.pgbouncer.org/config.html#server_connect_timeout)). While an attempt is under way a pool starts
no other, so for those 15 s the instance could authenticate no new client: it refused each with the pool's cached `connect failed` until the
clients had gone to its sibling (the last at 05:15:22.7). The instance's user pool connected to the new primary from 05:15:15.5 on, and its
attempts in the seconds before failed at once. Of the eight instance logs of both runs this is the only connect that took more than a second;
why that one got no answer is not known (the run kept no packet trace; a connection tracked to an address the Service was leaving is a
candidate). Q-HA-302's arithmetic counted only failed logins, one `server_login_retry` each; a connect that hangs adds
`server_connect_timeout`, and 15 s on top of a promotion of 2.6 to 8.1 s is past `health.database_outage_grace` (20 s): an instance that meets
it cannot log in a client for longer than the grace, and both instances of a pooler meeting it would take every replica out.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `server_connect_timeout: "5"` on both poolers, a requirement of R-HA-058 (chosen) | A connect or login without an answer is given up after 5 s and tried again a second later | The worst case per instance stays below the grace: a promotion of 8.1 s, a hung connect of 5 s and two retries of 1 s are 15.1 s; one parameter that CloudNativePG's Pooler allows (its webhook's list, 1.30.0) | A connect plus TLS plus login slower than 5 s is cut; inside a cluster it takes milliseconds |
| (b) 2 or 3 s | — | A hung connect costs less | Less room for a login on a loaded node or a PostgreSQL that is busy starting up |
| (c) Keep 15 s and accept the case | — | No change | An instance that cannot log in a client for longer than the grace; the test fails whenever it happens |

**Choice:** (a). The value leaves the grace a margin of about 5 s for the slowest promotion measured, and keeps a factor of a thousand over
an ordinary connect and login. Not run on a cluster before it landed: the next run of a pooler leg shows the value in the log of
`requirePoolerProfile`. That run (44862237399, 2026-11-21) showed `server_connect_timeout 5` on all four instances and windows of 7.6
to 10.5 s; no connect hung in it, so the 5 s themselves have not been exercised. Why the connect of 2026-11-20 got no answer is not
searched further (2026-11-23): there is no packet trace to read, and a connect that hangs now costs an instance at most 5 s, inside the
grace. What would show it again is `TestHAPooler_Switchover`: it logs each instance's window with its last failed server attempt and
fails when the longest reaches `health.database_outage_grace` (Q-HA-370).

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-058 (the switchover bullet and the example), R-HA-059 rule 5 (the pooler row), the failure table's switchover
row; [deploy/dev/pooler.yaml](../../deploy/dev/pooler.yaml), the pooler requirements of the [README](../../README.md) and of the manual
([configuration](../manual/admin/configuration.md#behind-a-transaction-mode-pooler), [runbook](../manual/admin/runbook.md)).

### Q-HA-372 · A unit that runs a tool carries the tool's name

Status: **Decided by the owner on 2026-11-21**, on his own initiative after he saw the two scanner Deployments on his cluster; the boundary
is the development agent's, told to him the same morning. Supersedes the names of the kinds `scanner`
([Q-HA-346](#q-ha-346--four-kinds-hold-a-pair-each-names-its-kind-and-the-operations-service), R-HA-065) and `malware-scanner` (R-HA-068)
and of their value blocks, and, through [architecture.md](architecture.md#q-arch-561--processscanner_kind-names-the-tool-trivy-or-clamav)
Q-ARCH-561, the values of `process.scanner_kind`; what those decisions decided stands. Its boundary was moved by the owner the same day
([Q-HA-373](#q-ha-373--every-name-an-operator-or-an-auditor-reads-of-a-scanner-unit-carries-its-tool)): the system subjects, the readiness checks, the label `listener` of the worker's links and the log components of the two units
carry the unit's name too; the table below keeps the boundary of its morning. The length of the names it built is checked since [Q-HA-374](#q-ha-374--the-chart-refuses-a-fullname-too-long-for-the-names-it-builds-and-never-cuts-it).

The owner's words: "Die Deployments quader-scanner und quader-malware-scanner sind mir nicht differenziert genug. quader-scanner ist
trivy? Dann quader-vuln-scanner-trivy. quader-malware-scanner hätte ich auch lieber quader-malware-scanner-calmav genannt. Also immer so
benennen, dass man sieht um welches Tool es sich handelt und das man später evtl mal mehrere Tools nebeneinander laufen lassen kann."
("calmav" is a typo of his; the tool is ClamAV, the name `clamav`.)

Decision:

- A kind of pod that exists to run one third-party tool, and everything named after it, is named `<purpose>-scanner-<tool>`: the image
  scanning's scanner is the kind `vuln-scanner-trivy`, the malware scanner the kind `malware-scanner-clamav`. Their Deployments,
  Services, PodDisruptionBudgets, autoscalers, NetworkPolicies, Certificates and Secrets (`<fullname>-tls-<kind>`), their component label,
  the names in their certificates (`<fullname>-<kind>.<namespace>.svc`), the keys of `tls.existingSecrets` and the names the chart writes
  into the configuration (`server.scan_clients`, the scanners' URLs and server names, `malware.scan_listener.client_name`) follow from the
  kind, one entry of `quader.tlsKindTable` each (R-HA-063).
- The chart's value blocks are flat, one per unit, like `api`, `packages` and `worker`: `vulnScannerTrivy` and `malwareScannerClamav`,
  so that a second tool for a purpose is a block beside the first. `freshclam` names its tool already and stays.
- A second tool for the same purpose gets a name of its own beside the first and replaces nothing.

The boundary, the development agent's: what is the same whichever tool does the work keeps the name of its purpose.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The tool's name on what runs the tool; the purpose's name on everything a second tool would share (chosen) | The kinds, their objects, certificates and value blocks, `process.scanner_kind`'s values; not the role `scanner`, the jobs, queues and tasks (`malware-scan`, the queue `malware`, `malware-sync-db`, `vuln-sync-trivy-db`), the configuration keys `vulnerabilities.images.scanner.*` and `malware.scanner.*` (the worker's one link per purpose), the system subjects `image-scanner` and `malware-scanner`, the readiness checks `scanner` and `malware_scanner`, the listener labels of the worker's links (`scanner`, `malware-scanner`) and the metric names | A second tool adds a unit and leaves a verdict, a setting, a gate, a dashboard and an alert as they are; the repositories `upstream/scanner-trivy` and `upstream/scanner-clamav` named their tool already | The worker's link per purpose is a single URL; a second tool for one purpose needs a list there, built when that tool is |
| (b) The tool's name everywhere a scanner is named | `trivy`/`clamav` in jobs, keys, subjects and metrics too | One rule without a boundary | A second tool would rename or fork what is the same for both: the verdict of a blob, the gate, the audit and the alerts |
| (c) The tool's name on the Deployment only | `metadata.name` changes, the kind and its Secret and values keep the old names | Smallest change | Two names for one unit: the Deployment `…-malware-scanner-clamav` with the label, Secret and value block `malware-scanner` |

**Choice:** (a).

Consequences: the records of the decisions of 2026-11-20 on this page (Q-HA-316 to Q-HA-349, Q-HA-360 to Q-HA-364) keep the names of their
day; the requirements listed below carry the new ones. An installation upgraded from the old names (pre-alpha, no alias,
[architecture.md](architecture.md) Q-ARCH-340) loses the Deployments, Services, PodDisruptionBudgets, autoscalers, NetworkPolicies and
Certificates `<fullname>-scanner` and `<fullname>-malware-scanner` and gets the new ones; the Secrets `<fullname>-tls-scanner` and
`<fullname>-tls-malware-scanner` that cert-manager wrote stay behind, since cert-manager leaves a Certificate's Secret in place when the
Certificate goes unless it runs with `--enable-certificate-owner-ref`, and may be deleted by hand; an installation that names its Secrets
renames the keys of `tls.existingSecrets`, and one that set `scanner:` or `malwareScanner:` renames the blocks (the schema refuses the old
keys). The longest name derived from a kind, the Service `<fullname>-malware-scanner-clamav`, is a DNS label only while `<fullname>` has at
most 40 characters; `quader.fullname` cut at 50 and the chart did not check the sum that morning, as it had not for
`<fullname>-malware-scanner` (47) and `<fullname>-packages-scan` (49); [Q-HA-374](#q-ha-374--the-chart-refuses-a-fullname-too-long-for-the-names-it-builds-and-never-cuts-it)
checks it since.

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-002, R-HA-011, R-HA-030 to R-HA-032, R-HA-035, R-HA-036, R-HA-042, R-HA-045, R-HA-061, R-HA-063, R-HA-065 to
R-HA-068; [architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-001, R-ARCH-036, Q-ARCH-561. Chart:
[_tls.tpl](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/_tls.tpl) `quader.tlsKindTable`,
[vuln-scanner-trivy.yaml](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/vuln-scanner-trivy.yaml),
[malware-scanner-clamav.yaml](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/malware-scanner-clamav.yaml); the rule in the repository's
[CLAUDE.md](../../CLAUDE.md).

### Q-HA-373 · Every name an operator or an auditor reads of a scanner unit carries its tool

Status: **Decided by the owner on 2026-11-21**, on the builder's report of the names Q-HA-372 had left with the purpose's: "Vom Builder
gemeldet, nicht geändert: direkt nacharbeiten. Das ist alles wichtig und muss umgesetzt werden." It moves the boundary of
[Q-HA-372](#q-ha-372--a-unit-that-runs-a-tool-carries-the-tools-name) for the names below; how they are written is the development
agent's ([operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md#q-ops-221--a-scanner-units-readiness-check-is-its-name-in-camel-case-the-same-in-the-process-that-calls-it)
Q-OPS-221, [Q-OPS-222](operations-and-observability.md#q-ops-222--the-loader-of-the-signature-database-logs-as-its-unit)).

Context: Q-HA-372 renamed the two scanner units and every object named after them, and kept the purpose's name on what a second tool
would share. Four kinds of name stayed that an operator or an auditor reads and that name a unit, not a purpose: the label `listener` of the
TLS series of the worker's links (`scanner`, `malware-scanner`); the log field `component` of the two scanner processes (`scanner`,
`malware-scanner`, and `malware-database-loader` for the malware scanner's loader); the readiness checks (`scanner` in both kinds of scanner
and in the role `all`, `malware_scanner` on a worker without a malware scanner); and the system subjects of the scanners' reads
(`image-scanner`, `malware-scanner`), which the scan listener's request log, the decision point's allow and the usage records' credential
column show. The owner's rule of Q-HA-372 is "immer so benennen, dass man sieht um welches Tool es sich handelt".

**Choice:** every name an operator or an auditor reads of a scanner unit is the unit's name (`vuln-scanner-trivy`, `malware-scanner-clamav`): the label `listener` of a link's TLS series, the log field `component`, the readiness check in camel case and the system subject of its reads; what a second tool would share keeps its purpose's name.

Decision, the owner's sentence applied:

- **The label `listener` of a link's TLS series** names the unit the link reaches, at both of its ends: `vuln-scanner-trivy` on the
  worker's call of the image scanner and on that scanner's listener, `malware-scanner-clamav` on the worker's call of the malware scanner and
  on its listener. The listener's HTTP server and the reloader of its material log under the same name. The scanner's pull keeps `scan`:
  it reaches the scan listener of `packages`, which runs no tool.
- **The log field `component` of a scanner's process** is the unit's name, `vuln-scanner-trivy` or `malware-scanner-clamav`, the loader of
  the signature database included (Q-OPS-222). The process's components are named after the unit too, which a failed start or stop
  names: the scanner `vuln-scanner-trivy` or `malware-scanner-clamav`, the worker's links `link-vuln-scanner-trivy` and
  `link-malware-scanner-clamav`, the loader `malware-scanner-clamav-database-loader`.
- **The readiness check of a scanner unit** is the unit's name in camel case, in the scanner's process and in the process that would call
  it: `vulnScannerTrivy` (the image scanner's own, and the reported check of the role `all`), `malwareScannerClamav` (the malware scanner's
  own, and the reported check of a worker without `malware.scanner.url`) (Q-OPS-221). The System page has a sentence for each.
- **The system subject of a scanner's reads** is the unit's name: `system:vuln-scanner-trivy`, the claim `s` of a scan token, the principal
  of the scan listener's request log and the source of the decision point's allow; `system:malware-scanner-clamav`, the claim `s` of a blob
  token and the principal of the malware routes. The usage records' credential column of their reads carries the same names. The
  authorization model holds no reason to keep a purpose's name here: the decision point finds a system subject's fixed rule by its name
  ([system.go](../../internal/authz/system.go)), so a second tool for a purpose would be a second name with the same rule, one case more,
  and an auditor reads which tool read.

What keeps its purpose's name: the role `scanner` and its area; the jobs, queues and tasks; the configuration keys
`vulnerabilities.images.scanner.*` and `malware.scanner.*`; the repositories `upstream/scanner-trivy` and `upstream/scanner-clamav`; the
metric names; the error codes `scanner_busy`, `scanner_draining`, `scanner_unavailable` and `scanner_lost`, which answer for whichever
scanner is called; and the subjects of the worker's own tasks (`system:image-database`, `system:malware-database`, `system:malware-scan`).
The table `malware_scanners`, what the worker saw of the scanners it calls, kept its purpose's name until it went
([malware-scanning.md](malware-scanning.md) Q-MAL-110).

Consequences: dashboards, alert rules and log queries of an installation that select `listener="scanner"` or `listener="malware-scanner"`,
`quader_health_check_passing{name="scanner"}` or `{name="malware_scanner"}`, the field `component` `scanner`, `malware-scanner` or
`malware-database-loader`, or the credential `image-scanner` or `malware-scanner` of the usage records match nothing after the upgrade and
are changed by hand (pre-alpha, no alias, [architecture.md](architecture.md) Q-ARCH-340); the chart's own rules and the runbooks select none
of them. Usage rows written before the upgrade keep their old credential. While a rollout runs replicas of both versions, a scan or blob
token signed by one is refused by the scan listener of the other.

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-002, R-HA-065, R-HA-066, R-HA-068; [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-001,
R-OPS-008; [architecture.md](architecture.md) R-ARCH-038; [authorization.md](authorization.md) R-AUTHZ-002;
[usage-and-limits.md](usage-and-limits.md) R-LIM-001; [formats/oci.md](formats/oci.md) R-OCI-037; [malware-scanning.md](malware-scanning.md)
R-MAL-006. Code: [link_tls.go](../../internal/httpserver/link_tls.go), [wire_scanner.go](../../internal/app/wire_scanner.go),
[scan.go](../../internal/auth/registrytoken/scan.go), [blob.go](../../internal/auth/registrytoken/blob.go),
[system.go](../../internal/authz/system.go), [subject.go](../../internal/limits/subject.go); the System page's sentences in
[system-status.ts](../../web/src/app/features/system/system-status.ts).

### Q-HA-374 · The chart refuses a fullname too long for the names it builds, and never cuts it

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. The task is the
owner's, with [Q-HA-373](#q-ha-373--every-name-an-operator-or-an-auditor-reads-of-a-scanner-unit-carries-its-tool): the chart checks the
length of the names it builds. Amended on 2026-11-21: the updater's Service `<fullname>-malware-updater-freshclam` (R-HA-069) is now the longest name, 26 characters more, so the bound is a `<fullname>` of at most 37 characters; the rule stands.

Context: `quader.fullname` cut at 50 characters "so that every derived name stays a valid DNS label". Since Q-HA-372 the longest name
built from `<fullname>` alone is the Service `<fullname>-malware-scanner-clamav`, 23 characters more, a DNS label only for a `<fullname>` of
at most 40; a release name between that and the cut rendered and failed at the API server, not at the render. The names that carry a
value of the installation (a path pool, an endpoint and its pool) were checked already, each with its value (R-HA-029, R-HA-062), and so was
the backup CronJob's limit of 52.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) One check over every name built from `<fullname>` alone, computed from `quader.tlsKindTable` and the fixed suffixes; `quader.fullname` never cut (chosen) | The tightest name decides; the render fails naming it, its length, and the longest release name and `fullnameOverride` that fit | Fails before anything is applied, with what to do; a kind added to the table moves the bound by itself; no name changes without a word | A `<fullname>` of 41 to 50 characters that rendered before now fails (pre-alpha, no installation has one) |
| (b) The same check, and the cut lowered to the computed bound | Names always fit | Never a failure for the name | A cut renames without a word; two releases whose names agree in their first 40 characters render the same objects into one namespace; the check never fires |
| (c) The cut kept at 50, the check over the kinds the release renders only | A release without the malware scanning may keep a longer name | More room for some releases | Switching the malware scanning on later fails the upgrade for a name chosen long before; the bound moves with values |
| (d) The cut lowered to 40, no check | Smallest change | One line | A hard-coded number that goes stale with the next kind, and (b)'s faults |

**Choice:** (a) ([_validate.tpl](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/_validate.tpl) `quader.validateNames`, [_helpers.tpl](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/_helpers.tpl)
`quader.fullname`). The names checked: the Service and the certificate name `<fullname>-<kind>` of every kind of the table, whether the
release renders it or not, so that switching a kind on never fails for its name; the Services `<fullname>-ops` and
`<fullname>-packages-scan`; the Jobs `<fullname>-migrate`, `<fullname>-restore` and `<fullname>-post-restore-<8 hex>`, whose names are label
values of their pods (63 each); the CronJob `<fullname>-backup` (52). With today's table `<fullname>` has at most 40 characters: a release
name of at most 33 (`<release>-quader`), one of at most 40 that contains `quader`, or a `fullnameOverride` of at most 40. The CronJob's own
check became a row of this one: every `<fullname>` it accepts leaves `<fullname>-backup` at 47 at most. Certificates and Secrets
(`<fullname>-tls-<kind>`), ConfigMaps, NetworkPolicies, disruption budgets and autoscalers are DNS subdomains of up to 253 characters and
are not checked. The chart test renders the boundary: 40 renders, 41 fails, a release name of 33 renders and one of 34 fails, and the bound
holds with both scannings off. **Applied in the spec:** R-HA-028, R-HA-029, Q-HA-372's consequence.


### Q-HA-375 · The updater is `malware-updater-freshclam`

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. The name was told
to the owner on 2026-11-21 with his decision to move `freshclam` out of the worker.

Context: the owner's rule (Q-HA-372, ADR-223) names a unit that exists to run one third-party tool `<purpose>-scanner-<tool>`, so that the
tool shows and a second tool can stand beside the first. The updater runs a tool and scans nothing.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `malware-updater-freshclam`: the rule read as `<purpose>-<function>-<tool>`, the function `updater`, the tool the program the unit runs (chosen) | Deployment, Service, certificate, Secret, `tls.existingSecrets` key, value block `malwareUpdaterFreshclam`, readiness check `malwareUpdaterFreshclam`, log `component`, metric and link label | Says what the unit does and with which program; `cvdupdate`, ClamAV's other supported tool, would be `malware-updater-cvdupdate` beside it | 26 characters after `<fullname>`, the longest name the chart builds: `<fullname>` at most 37 |
| (b) `malware-scanner-freshclam` | The rule's words kept | One pattern | Calls a unit a scanner that scans nothing |
| (c) `malware-updater-clamav` | The project's name, as the scanner has | Matches `malware-scanner-clamav` | Two tools of the ClamAV project could not stand side by side under it |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the rule's aim is that the tool shows and a second one fits; the function word is what `scanner` was for
the scanners. The development agent would revisit this if the owner wants the word `scanner` on every tool unit. **Applied in the spec:**
R-HA-002, R-HA-063, R-HA-069; [operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) Q-OPS-224; [decisions.md](../decisions.md)
ADR-225 (which reads ADR-223's pattern as `<purpose>-<function>-<tool>`).

### Q-HA-376 · One updater, replaced, not rolled, and outside the rule of two

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. The one replica is
the owner's ("Default reicht uns 1 replica").

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-225](../decisions.md#adr-225--the-clamav-updater-is-a-deployment-of-its-own-and-clamavs-definitions-are-a-repository-format).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `replicaCount: 1` by default, exempt from `highAvailability.enforce`, `strategy: Recreate`, no disruption budget, no autoscaler (chosen) | One fetcher at any time | ClamAV's guidance of one fetcher per network; a rollout never runs two; nothing waits for the updater, so its minute of absence costs nothing | During a rollout or a drain the worker's runs record `updater_unavailable` for that minute |
| (b) `RollingUpdate` with a surge | The roles' default | No gap | Two `freshclam` for a moment, each with its own seed |
| (c) Two replicas under `enforce` | The rule of two | Survives a node | Two fetchers from one network, for a pod whose loss costs nothing |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-HA-069.

### Q-HA-377 · `freshclam.conf`: whole signed files, no `NotifyClamd`, and the mirror as a value

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `ScriptedUpdates no`, no `NotifyClamd`, `DatabaseMirror database.clamav.net` or `PrivateMirror` from `malwareUpdaterFreshclam.privateMirror`, the proxy from `malwareUpdaterFreshclam.proxy` (chosen) | The chart's values hold what is the pod's | Whole signed containers ([malware-scanning.md](malware-scanning.md) Q-MAL-93); the error line at every update goes; an internal mirror is one value; the proxy moves from Quader's configuration, which never read it, to the unit that uses it | Two values more in the chart |
| (b) The configuration keys under `config.malware.database` as before | One place for the malware scanning | — | Keys of Quader's configuration that no Quader process reads |
| (c) A free text `extraConfig` for `freshclam.conf` | Any option | Flexible | An operator could turn on what the design rules out (patches, `NotifyClamd`, another database directory) |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-HA-069; [malware-scanning.md](malware-scanning.md) R-MAL-010, R-MAL-012, R-MAL-027.

### Q-HA-378 · The analyser's binary is copied by an init container of its own image into a volume the scanner mounts read-only

Status: **Decided by the owner** (2026-11-21, "Option b", [ADR-229](../decisions.md#adr-229--the-scanner-unit-detects-as-well-and-the-analyser-comes-from-its-own-image))
for the init container of the analyser's own image; the read-only mount and the copy's details are the development agent's.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) An init container of `trivy.image` copies the binary with the image's `cp` into `trivy-bin`, which `quader` mounts read-only (chosen) | One image of the publisher's, pinned by digest | The release stays one image; the binary is the publisher's build, byte for byte the archive's (checked by the owner's measurement on arm64); a taken-over analyser cannot replace it, because the mount is read-only and the copy belongs to the pod's user | A node pulls a third party's image at a scanner pod's start (H-1182) |
| (b) The same, with `trivy-bin` read-write in `quader` | Fewer mount options | — | Measured: the copy belongs to user 65532, the user of every analyser, so one taken-over analysis could replace the binary for every later analysis and detection of the pod |
| (c) An image volume (`volumes[].image`) instead of the init container | No copy | No extra disk | Not on by default in every Kubernetes the chart supports (R-HA-049, 1.34 to 1.37); which release turns it on was not verified |
| (d) A second Quader image with the analyser, built with every release | The owner's option (a) | No third-party pull | Two images per release, which the owner did not choose |

**Choice:** (a). The image's `cp` is BusyBox's, which runs as the pod's user on the read-only root file system (measured with Docker on
2026-11-21, not in a pod). **Rationale:** the owner's pattern, with the one mount option that keeps the binary out of the analyser's hands.
The development agent would revisit this when image volumes are on by default in the oldest Kubernetes the chart supports.

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-065, R-HA-070; [vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-033, R-VULN-036. **Built on
2026-11-21** ([vuln-scanner-trivy.yaml](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/vuln-scanner-trivy.yaml)); the copy as user 65532 on a read-only
root file system without capabilities ran in a pod of the kind cluster (R-HA-070).

### Q-HA-379 · The loader is a regular container with a liveness probe on a port of its own and no readiness probe

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A container `database` beside `quader`, operations listener on `:8083`, liveness only (chosen) | The pod's readiness stays the scanner's | Analyses go on while a database loads; a hung loader is restarted; no port collides | Its metrics are not scraped (the ServiceMonitor reads `8081`); its state shows through the scanner's report |
| (b) A native sidecar (an init container with `restartPolicy: Always`) | Started before the scanner | Ordered start | The scanner needs no order: it is ready without a database |
| (c) A readiness probe on the loader | The pod waits for the database | No detection on a pod without one | A pod start and every new database would take the pod out of the Service, analyses included |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the database is the detection's need, not the pod's; the call answers `database_loading` where it is
missing. The development agent would revisit this if an operator needs the loader's own metrics.

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-070; [architecture.md](architecture.md) Q-ARCH-564.

### Q-HA-380 · The database volume follows `spool.type`, 5 Gi by default, and the chart refuses less than 4 Gi

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the database unpacks to 1,807,314,944 bytes (measured on 2026-11-21) and grows; the loader keeps two while the next unpacks.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A volume `trivy-db` of its own, an `emptyDir` or an ephemeral claim as `spool.type` says, 5 Gi, checked against 2 × 2 GiB (chosen) | Room for two databases with room to grow | The scanner's spool budget stays the analyses'; a node with small disks gets a claim as the spool does | One volume more per pod |
| (b) Below the scanner's spool | One volume | Less YAML | The loader is another container, which would need the spool read-write, and the analyses' check (Q-HA-318) would compete with 1.7 to 3.4 GiB |
| (c) `medium: Memory` | Fast | — | 1.7 GiB of memory per pod for data the page cache keeps anyway |

**Choice:** (a). A database that outgrows the room for two still loads: it replaces the newest (R-VULN-049). **Rationale:** the volume that
holds the bytes carries the check (Q-HA-318's rule). The development agent would revisit this when the database passes about 2 GiB (H-872).

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-070; [vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-049.

### Q-HA-381 · One pin by digest, the chart's value held equal by a chart test, and one Renovate group that reviews a new version

Status: **Decided by the owner** (2026-11-21) for the pattern: one pin by digest in `tools/versions.env`, the same value in the chart, a chart
test that holds them equal, one Renovate group, and the digests of the release archive kept by hand go. Which updates merge by themselves is
the development agent's.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A new digest of the same version merges by itself; a new version is a pull request to review (chosen) | Group `trivy` over `TRIVY_IMAGE` and `trivy.image` | A rebuilt image of the same release reaches the installations; a new version, which makes the scanners analyse every stored image again (its analyses are of another version, Q-VULN-199) and may read another database schema than the release's `2`, is read first | Fixes of a new release wait for a review |
| (b) Every update merges by itself, as ClamAV's patch releases | Fastest fixes | Fewest hands | A version that needs a new database schema would stop every detection, and every release re-analyses every image unasked |
| (c) By hand only | No Renovate | — | The pin falls behind the publisher's fixes (H-1003) |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** a new analyser version is a change of what Quader reports and of its cost, so it is read; a new digest of
the same version is not. The development agent would revisit this if the publisher moves to releases that never change the database schema
within a minor line.

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-070. **Built on 2026-11-21:** `TRIVY_IMAGE` in [tools/versions.env](../../tools/versions.env), the chart's
`trivy.image` held to it by `TestR_HA_070_TheLoaderWritesTheDatabaseThatTheScannerReadsReadOnly`, and the group `trivy` of
[renovate.json](../../renovate.json): the image manager of `tools/versions.env` and the manager of the chart's tool images both find the
image, a digest merges by itself through the rule of the Docker images, and a patch, minor or major version gets `automerge: false` and the
label `trivy-version`.

### Q-HA-382 · The image scanning is on in the chart's defaults and off in every test profile but `vuln` and the platform matrix

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. That the
development profile starts the scanner units only in the legs whose tests need them, so that every other leg loads the small image alone,
was told to the owner with his decision.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `values-dev.yaml` switches it off; `values-vuln.yaml` and the platform matrix switch it on and load `TRIVY_IMAGE` into the kind cluster as `CLAMAV_IMAGE` is loaded (chosen) | Only the legs that read a scanner run one | Every other leg starts no scanner pod and pulls nothing of the analyser; the chart's real wiring still runs on a cluster in `vuln` and on the oldest and newest Kubernetes | Two profiles to keep in step |
| (b) On everywhere | As today | One profile | Each kind leg pulls about 60 MB from Docker Hub and runs two scanner pods no test reads |
| (c) Off everywhere | No pull | Cheapest | The init container, the read-only mounts and the loader never run on a cluster |

**Choice:** (a). The selectors of `drain.sh` and the Valkey policy's test do not depend on the scanner Deployment; the platform matrix keeps
`vuln-scanner-trivy` among the kinds it waits for. **Rationale:** the owner's rule that a test moves no more than its assertion needs.

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-067; [vulnerability-scanning.md](vulnerability-scanning.md) R-VULN-046. **Built on 2026-11-21:**
[values-dev.yaml](../../deploy/dev/values-dev.yaml) switches the image scanning off, [values-vuln.yaml](../../deploy/dev/values-vuln.yaml)
switches it on with `trivy.image: quader-e2e-trivy:dev`, which [up.sh](../../deploy/dev/up.sh) pulls and loads from `TRIVY_IMAGE` in the
profile `vuln` beside ClamAV's; the restore drill's installation is off too (Q-HA-387), and the platform matrix loads nothing and reads the
init container back from the API server (Q-HA-386).

### Q-HA-383 · A private mirror changes one value per image, and nodes without a registry load the images beforehand

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Mirror each image by its index digest and set `image.*`, `trivy.image` and `clamav.image`; nodes without a registry get the images loaded and keep `IfNotPresent`; the manual says both (chosen) | Values only | No code; the digests stay the pins | The operator mirrors three images instead of one |
| (b) A value that bundles the analyser into the Quader image again | `image.withAnalyser` | One image to mirror | A second image per release, which the owner did not choose |
| (c) Quader serves the analyser's image to its nodes by default | A remote repository of Docker Hub as the default of `trivy.image` | No third-party pull by the nodes | The nodes would need the edge's name and a level or a pull secret before the first install; the default must work without Quader |

**Choice:** (a), and (c) is named as a way an operator may take by configuration (R-HA-070). **Rationale:** the pin is the same everywhere;
only the registry's name differs. The development agent would revisit this if an operator's registry rewrites digests on copy.

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-070. **Built on 2026-11-21:** the README (Helm values, "Images from a mirror of your own, or nodes without a
registry") and the operations manual ([operations.md](../manual/admin/operations.md#vulnerability-scanning)); the chart test renders a
mirrored `trivy.image` with `global.imagePullSecrets`.

### Q-HA-384 · The mirror and the proxy are checked so that no value adds a line to `freshclam.conf`

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. It settles
what R-HA-069 left open about the shape of `malwareUpdaterFreshclam.privateMirror` and `proxy` while building the chart (2026-11-21).

Context: both values are written as they are into `freshclam.conf`, a file of one option per line in a ConfigMap. A value with a line break
would add an option the design rules out (`NotifyClamd`, `ScriptedUpdates yes`, another `DatabaseDirectory`); a URL with a user and a
password would put a credential into a ConfigMap, which every reader of the namespace's ConfigMaps sees. `freshclam` refuses a
`PrivateMirror` on ClamAV's own network; `HTTPProxyServer` takes a host name and `HTTPProxyPort` a number, so an `https://` proxy would be
reached in plain HTTP all the same.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `values.schema.json` holds the shape: `privateMirror` empty or `http(s)://<host>[/<path>]` with no whitespace, no `@`, no query and no fragment, `proxy` empty or `http://<host>[:<port>]`; the template refuses a mirror whose host is `clamav.net` or ends in `.clamav.net` (chosen) | Shape by the schema, meaning by the template | No value adds a line; no credential lands in a ConfigMap; helm names the key in both cases; the proxy's port defaults to 80 as `freshclam` does | A proxy that needs a user (`HTTPProxyUsername`), or an IPv6 literal as the proxy host, is refused; neither is asked for |
| (b) Only the host check of R-HA-069 | The words of the spec | Least code | A line break in a value reaches `freshclam.conf` |
| (c) Proxy credentials from a Secret, rendered into the file at start | Full proxy support | Covers an authenticating proxy | A Secret in the pod that talks to the internet, which R-HA-069 keeps free of any credential |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the updater is the one pod that reaches the internet and holds no credential; a value that can change what
`freshclam` does, or carry a credential, is the thing to refuse. The development agent would revisit this when an installation needs an
authenticating proxy. **Applied in the spec:** R-HA-069. Code: [values.schema.json](../../deploy/helm/quader/values.schema.json),
[_malware.tpl](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/_malware.tpl) `quader.validateMalwareUpdater`.

### Q-HA-385 · The signing identity's Secret reaches the worker pods only, and the chart renders its Certificate on request

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) An existing Secret or a cert-manager `Certificate` the chart renders, at most one; mounted into the worker pods only; the key fixed to ECDSA P-256 with `rotationPolicy: Always` (chosen) | The pattern of the TLS pairs (R-HA-063) | The key reaches the one kind of pod that signs ([signatures.md](signatures.md) Q-SIG-56); cert-manager renews it, with a new key, without a restart; P-256 is what npm needs (Q-SIG-53) | A key that a company CA can issue only as RSA cannot come this way |
| (b) Mounted into every replica, as the key ring is | | One mount rule | The key in `api` and `packages`, which never sign |
| (c) The existing Secret only; cert-manager left to the operator | | Less to render | Every operator writes the same `Certificate`, and the usages and the key type are easy to get wrong |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-HA-071; [signatures.md](signatures.md) R-SIG-046.

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. It settles how

| (b) Load `TRIVY_IMAGE` into the matrix's cluster as `vuln` does | As Q-HA-382 reads | The text of Q-HA-382 | About 60 MB moved into a cluster whose pods never start: the load proves nothing |
| (c) Start the scanner pod in the matrix | The copy on 1.34 and 1.37 | Runs the init container on both versions | Needs the scanner's certificate, its configuration and the Quader image on a cluster built to start nothing; the copy uses no feature that differs between the versions |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the owner's rule that a test moves no more than its assertion needs; the copy itself runs in `vuln`
(R-VULN-046). The development agent would revisit this if the matrix starts pods.

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-070, Q-HA-382; [k8s-matrix.sh](../../deploy/dev/k8s-matrix.sh).

### Q-HA-388 · `make trivy` keeps the binary under the tag and the digest, and `make versions-check` refuses a `trivy` of another version on the path

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough. It settles what
R-HA-070 leaves open about where `make trivy` puts the binary and what `make versions-check` compares (2026-11-21).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `.bin/trivy-<tag>-<first 12 hex digits of the index digest>/trivy`, the directory printed by `make trivy-dir` for the job that puts it on `PATH`; `versions-check` compares the binary (on Linux) and any `trivy` on `PATH` with the tag (chosen) | A new digest of the same version is a new directory | A rebuilt image of the same release is taken out again, never a stale copy reused (the global rule that a tool's binary carries its pin); the workflow names no part of the pin itself; a second analyser on the machine is found | A developer's `trivy` of another version on `PATH` (Homebrew's, for one) fails `versions-check` until it is removed |
| (b) `.bin/trivy-<tag>/trivy` | The tag alone | Shorter | A new digest of the same tag keeps the old binary |
| (c) The binary only, not `PATH` | As before for Trivy | No local failure | Two analysers on one machine stay unseen |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** one version of every tool, on the machine as in CI; the analyser on `PATH` is the one a developer would
run against an image. The development agent would revisit this if a host tool of the developers' needs a `trivy` of its own.

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-070; [Makefile](../../Makefile) `trivy`, `trivy-dir`, `versions-check`;
[release.yml](../../.github/workflows/release.yml) job `container-scan`.

Status: **Decided by the planner in the owner's absence** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

### Q-HA-393 · The replication backlog alert leaves a filling connection out by a gauge of its own

Status: **Decided by the builder** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-239](../decisions.md#adr-239--several-object-store-connections-every-blob-on-every-connection-a-row-per-copy-one-reconciliation-and-a-scrub-per-copy).

Context: R-HA-045's row of `QuaderStorageReplicationBacklog` fires "for a connection that is not `filling`", but no metric of
[storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-060 says which connection is filling; the state is derived from `storage_connections.filled_at`
(R-STOR-051). A fill of large blobs keeps its oldest gap older than an hour: the pass queues up to `storage.reconcile.queue_limit`
(10,000) rows, and 10,000 blobs of 100 MiB *(example)* at `bytes_per_second: 100MiB` take about 2.8 hours.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A gauge `quader_storage_connection_filling{connection}`, 1 while the connection is `filling`, exported from `storage_connections` by every `web` and `worker` replica beside the queue gauges (package C); the alert adds `unless on (connection) (max by (connection) (quader_storage_connection_filling) == 1)` (chosen) | The state from the row that holds it | Names exactly what the row says; an absent gauge removes nothing, so the alert errs towards firing | One family more for package C |
| (b) One gauge of every state, `quader_storage_connection_state{connection,state}` | A general state metric | Dashboards could use it too | Six series per connection for one clause; the admin area reads the API, not metrics |
| (c) No clause | The table without its condition | Nothing to export | The warning fires through every fill of an installation with large blobs, and is learnt to be ignored |
| (d) `quader_storage_connection_fill_ratio < 1` as the sign of filling | An existing gauge | Nothing new | An active connection after an outage has a ratio below 1 as well, so the alert would stay silent for the outage it exists for |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-HA-045; [storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-056 (the gauges of the reconciliation);
[operations-and-observability.md](operations-and-observability.md) R-OPS-008's table. Code: [_rules.tpl](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/_rules.tpl),
the rule tests; the gauge itself: [internal/blob/reconcile/metrics.go](../../internal/blob/reconcile/metrics.go) and the query
`ReconcileGauges` ([reconcile.sql](../../internal/meta/postgres/queries/reconcile.sql)), registered by package C.

### Q-HA-394 · An element without id is default in the chart, as in the binary

Status: **Decided by the builder** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-239](../decisions.md#adr-239--several-object-store-connections-every-blob-on-every-connection-a-row-per-copy-one-reconciliation-and-a-scrub-per-copy).

Context: R-HA-072 listed "an element without `id`" among the refusals, and R-HA-029's row read the same; [storage.md](storage.md)
R-STOR-050 says that an element without `id` is `default`, that at most one may leave it out, and gives `[{bucket: quader-blobs}]` as the
plain path. A list in the values replaces the default list whole, so an operator's element has no `id` unless it is written.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The chart applies the binary's rule: an element without `id` is `default`, the rendered element carries `id: default`, two elements without one are refused as two of `default` (chosen) | One rule in chart and binary | The plain path of R-STOR-050, one key, works; chart and binary accept the same lists; the file says what the mount paths say | None found |
| (b) The chart refuses an element without `id` | Every `id` written | Explicit | The chart refuses what the binary accepts; one more line on the plain path the owner wants simple |
| (c) The chart passes an element without `id` unchanged | The binary defaults it | The file as given | The chart needs the `id` for the entries and the mounts anyway |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-HA-072, R-HA-029. Code: `quader.connectionId` in [_storage.tpl](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/_storage.tpl).

### Q-HA-395 · The values of the one store are refused by the templates with the keys that took their place

Status: **Decided by the builder** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-239](../decisions.md#adr-239--several-object-store-connections-every-blob-on-every-connection-a-row-per-copy-one-reconciliation-and-a-scrub-per-copy).

Context: an upgrade may carry `config.storage.s3`, `secrets.s3`, `secrets.s3CA`, `secrets.backupSource` or `secrets.journalReader`.
`secrets` is `additionalProperties: false`, so without a declaration Helm's schema check refuses `secrets.s3` first with "additional
properties 's3' not allowed", which names no new key; `config.storage` is open, so `config.storage.s3` would pass the chart and stop
the pods at start.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The schema declares the five keys as markers with a description and no type; the first check of the templates refuses each with a sentence that names the keys that took its place (chosen) | A refusal that explains the move | The upgrade stops at helm, before anything is applied, with the new keys spelled out; checked before every other rule, so no consequence of the move (an empty bucket) is reported first | Five removed names stay declared in the schema |
| (b) Nothing declared | The schema of the new values only | A smaller schema | Helm's message names no new key, and `config.storage.s3` reaches the pods |
| (c) The chart translates the old values into the list | No action for the operator | Nothing breaks | A migration path, which the rule of the stage before the first stable release forbids |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-HA-072, R-HA-029. Code: `quader.validateStorageMoved` in
[_storage.tpl](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/_storage.tpl), the markers in [values.schema.json](../../deploy/helm/quader/values.schema.json).

Status: **Decided by the builder** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it. **Superseded on 2026-11-22** by the rest of

| (b) Keep `secrets.backupSource` and `secrets.journalReader` until the rest of E | The old values for now | Nothing changes for the backup and the restore | Two rewrites of every installation's values; values R-HA-072 removes |
| (c) Render `backup.source.connections` and one credential per connection now | The target form | Final | The binary of today refuses both: the key is unknown, the file is read with `KnownFields` |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-HA-072. Code: `quader.backupSourceConfig`, `quader.backupConnection` and
`quader.journalConnection` in [_storage.tpl](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/_storage.tpl), `quader.journalCredentialsConfigMap` in
[_backup.tpl](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/_backup.tpl).

### Q-HA-399 · A static journal reader is required for every connection without drain

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Its entry in the decision log: [ADR-239](../decisions.md#adr-239--several-object-store-connections-every-blob-on-every-connection-a-row-per-copy-one-reconciliation-and-a-scrub-per-copy).

Context: with `journalCredentials.source: static` the interim form required the `journalReader` of the first connection (Q-HA-396). The
journal goes to every connection without `drain: true` (storage.md R-STOR-059), and the replay reads each; a connection that the
credentials file does not name is read with the runtime credential and a plain listing, where a delete marker set with the runtime
credential hides an entry (R-HA-054).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The entry of every element without `drain: true` needs a `journalReader`; a draining connection's is used when it has one; the refusal names every connection that lacks one (chosen) | The file names every connection the journal goes to | Each copy of the journal is read with versions, so no holder of one connection's runtime credential can hide an entry on it; a draining connection, whose credential may be gone, does not block the render | An operator with several connections creates a versioned login per provider |
| (b) At least one `journalReader` | Lenient | One login suffices | The connections without one are read with a plain listing, so the static source protects only some copies, which the value does not say |
| (c) The first connection's, as before | The interim | Nothing to change | The other connections' entries are read without versions |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** `static` promises the version listing; it should hold for every copy the replay reads. The development agent
would revisit this if a provider offered no versioned login and an operator needed static readers on the others only.

**Applied in the spec:** R-HA-072, R-HA-029's refusal. Code: `quader.journalReadersMissing` and `quader.journalCredentialElements` in
[_storage.tpl](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/_storage.tpl), [_validate_backup.tpl](../../deploy/helm/quader/templates/_validate_backup.tpl),
`TestR_HA_072_SeveralConnectionsAndAProvisioner`.

### Q-HA-415 · The chart carries no key of the stored content

Status: **Decided by the planner in the owner's absence** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it. That the storage keys are
drawn by Quader, lie once sealed in the database and are never handled by an operator is the owner's (2026-11-22, decisions 4 and 15).

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) No key, no Secret and no value for the stored content beyond `encrypted` and `keyed_names` in a connection's element (chosen) | The key ring Secret stays the only key the chart mounts | One secret to escrow; nothing an operator can get wrong when he adds an encrypted connection | The chart cannot tell an operator to export the storage keys; the manual and the README do (storage.md R-STOR-090) |
| (b) A Secret per encrypted connection holding its storage key | Keys in Kubernetes | A key an operator can see | A second place for a key that lies in the database, the drift the owner rejected for the data keys |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-HA-072, [storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-075, R-STOR-083.

### Q-HA-416 · A destruction of storage keys is journaled and replayed after a restore

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner sees it when it is built.

Context: [storage.md](storage.md) Q-STOR-309 (b) lets the operator destroy a retired connection's storage keys (R-STOR-097 to R-STOR-099).
A restore of a backup taken before the destruction, or a point-in-time restore to before it, loads the keys again. R-HA-054 said "Replay
never grants access and never deletes content"; [Q-HA-9](#q-ha-9--making-revocations-survive-a-database-restore-h-37) is the development
agent's, not the owner's.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `system.storage.keys_destroyed` carries the journal flag; the replay destroys the keys again, per identifier, before any replica starts (chosen) | A handler of the domain `storage_keys` with three outcomes: a sealed row destroyed (`applied`), a destroyed row (`already in effect`), no row: a destroyed row inserted from the identifier with `created_at` = `destroyedAt` (`applied`) | The journal exists for exactly this, and both restore paths replay it; an inserted row keeps a later import and the connection id from bringing the key back | It bends "never deletes content": a replay may destroy a key that was destroyed after *t*; a journal entry forged with the runtime credential could destroy the keys of a live connection at a restore, which [Q-HA-417](#q-ha-417--the-replay-destroys-the-keys-only-of-a-connection-the-restoring-configuration-does-not-name) keeps to connections the restoring configuration does not name ([H-1375](../security/stored-content-keys.md#h-1375--a-forged-journal-entry-can-destroy-a-retired-connections-keys-at-a-restore-before-the-operator-does)) |
| (b) The keys come back, and the operator runs `destroy` again | No journal entry | Replay stays as it was | Silent: a restore undoes the destruction until someone remembers |
| (c) The restore reads the `destroyed` lists of newer manifests | From the backup's target | No journal | Covers no point-in-time restore, and no destruction after the newest backup |

**Choice:** (a). The handler announces the area `storage_keys` and writes no audit event, like the other handlers. It is registered from
`internal/app`, because `internal/blob/keys` lies in the infrastructure layer and may not import `internal/journal`, a domain package
([layers.go](../../internal/archtest/layers.go)). **Applied in the spec:** R-HA-054; [backup-and-restore.md](backup-and-restore.md)
R-BAK-024; [storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-099.

### Q-HA-417 · The replay destroys the keys only of a connection the restoring configuration does not name

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner sees it when it is built.

Context: whoever holds a connection's runtime credential can write journal objects
([H-553](backup-and-restore.md#h-553--a-journal-object-can-be-overwritten-with-the-runtime-credential)). As Q-HA-416 first stood, the
handler destroyed the keys any entry named: an entry forged with a live connection's identifiers would destroy its keys at the next restore,
and the blobs only that connection holds would be lost, since an import skips a destroyed key ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-103) and a
later replay destroys again. Every other forged entry can only revoke or disable. A connection the restoring installation configures is not
retired, and the command refuses such a connection ([storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-098), so a genuine entry never names one.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Skip an entry whose connection the restoring configuration names: outcome `skipped` with its reason as a warning, the restore goes on (chosen) | One check against the configuration the restore already holds | A forged or stale entry cannot destroy a key Quader still uses; the restore is not held up by an entry anyone with a runtime credential can write | A forged entry can still destroy a retired connection's keys before the operator did ([H-1375](../security/stored-content-keys.md#h-1375--a-forged-journal-entry-can-destroy-a-retired-connections-keys-at-a-restore-before-the-operator-does)) |
| (b) Refuse the whole replay | A suspicious entry stops the restore | Nothing applied from a journal that holds a forgery | Whoever can write a journal object can block every restore, and the revocations of the same journal are not applied either |
| (c) Apply everything as Q-HA-416 first stood | No check | Simplest | A forged entry destroys the keys of a live connection, and its blobs are lost |

**Choice:** (a). `skipped` is the replay's word for an entry it does not apply (R-HA-054 "Replay run"); the entry's note carries the
reason, which the replay prints as a warning line and lists among the summary's warnings. **Applied in the spec:** R-HA-054;
[storage.md](storage.md) R-STOR-099; [security/stored-content-keys.md](../security/stored-content-keys.md) H-1375.

### Q-HA-425 · The replay of a destruction that knows no configured connection destroys nothing

Status: **Decided by the development agent** (package 7 of the encryption, at its build) — selected from the options below; the owner sees
it when it is built.

Context: Q-HA-417 skips an entry whose connection the restoring configuration names. The handlers of the journal get what they may depend on
through `journal.Env` (now, the restore point, the change log), which held no configuration; the two callers of the replay, `quader backup
restore` and `quader admin post-restore`, each hold their configuration. A caller that forgot to pass the connections would hand the handler
an empty list, and every entry would look like one of a connection that is not configured.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `journal.Env.StorageConnections`, filled by both callers from `storage.connections`; an empty list skips every destruction with a note (chosen) | Fail closed | A caller that passes nothing destroys no key; a configuration always has at least one connection, so an empty list is never a real configuration | A field of the journal's environment that one handler reads |
| (b) The same field, an empty list taken as "nothing configured" | Fail open | — | A caller that forgot the field destroys the keys of every connection a forged entry names |
| (c) The handler reads the configuration itself | No new field | — | `internal/blob/keys` and the handler hold no configuration; the restore's configuration is the caller's |

**Choice:** (a). **Applied in the spec:** R-HA-054.

### Q-HA-446 · The database's memory per connection is a figure of the documents, not a check of the preflight

Status: **Decided by the development agent** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the walkthrough.

Context: the nightly of 2026-11-20 measured what a connection of a serving pod costs the PostgreSQL primary: a `packages` pod with a pool
of 20 gave back 120 to 155 MiB when it ended, 6 to 8 MiB a connection. The development profile's primary, sized without that figure, was
8 MiB from its limit of 1 GiB for at least a day and then killed in a drain; it may use 3 GiB since
([local-profile.md](../developer/local-profile.md)). The preflight of R-HA-016 compares the connection budget with `max_connections`, and
neither the README's sizing table nor the manual said how much memory the primary needs for that budget.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The README's sizing section and the manual's scaling section give the figure and size the primary from the budget; the preflight checks connections only (chosen) | One sentence in each, marked as one measurement | The operator sizes from the budget the chart prints in its notes, which counts a rollout's extra pod per role (Q-HA-86) | Nothing checks it |
| (b) The migration Job logs the budget times 8 MiB beside `shared_buffers` as a warning | A number at every upgrade | The operator meets it without reading | The Job reads the database through SQL and sees no memory limit of the server's container or machine; the warning would be a guess presented as a check, from one measurement |

**Choice:** (a). **Rationale:** the preflight checks what it can read, and it can read `max_connections` but not the memory the server
has. The figure is one measurement on the development profile; it is replaced when a reference load test measures the profiles
([H-803](#h-803--the-sizing-profiles-are-not-measured)). **Applied in the spec:** R-HA-016; the [README](../../README.md)'s sizing
profiles and the manual's [operations](../manual/admin/operations.md#scaling-api-packages-and-worker).

### Q-HA-487 · The Valkey outage with a replaced packages pod runs in the nightly's npm-ha, not only in the closing run

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-23** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the
walkthrough. Amends [Q-HA-67](#q-ha-67--where-and-how-often-the-scenarios-under-npm-load-run) for this one scenario.

Context: under Q-HA-67 the 5-minute Valkey outage of R-HA-052, with a `packages` pod deleted meanwhile under the npm load, ran in
`TestNPMHAClosing`, which only the set `npm-ha-closing` selects, and that set runs only in a closing dispatch of Test and
Release. No such dispatch ran from 2026-11-18 to the reading of 2026-11-23, so the scenario (the replacement becomes ready with
Valkey degraded, R-HA-008; degraded clears within `open_duration + health_check_interval + 5 s`, R-HA-057) held nothing in that
time.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The case moves into `TestNPMHA`, the nightly's `npm-ha` (chosen) | Every night, after the drain, the switchover and the Valkey failover, under the same npm load | A scenario of R-HA-052 runs at least daily; no new set, cluster or leg | About seven minutes more of lane 1 of the nightly, the longest lane (Q-ARCH-431), so the night grows by that |
| (b) A closing dispatch on a schedule | | No change of the tests | A closing dispatch runs the fuzz legs and every closing set, hours of runners, for one scenario |
| (c) As before | | Nothing | A test that nothing runs holds nothing |

**Choice:** (a). `TestNPMHAClosing` is gone; the set `npm-ha-closing` runs `TestNPMHA`, `TestNPMHACrash` and `TestNPMPerf`, and
with them the outage. **Cost:** one subtest of about seven minutes (one minute of load before the stop, five minutes of outage,

[e2e.sh](../../deploy/dev/e2e.sh). Elsewhere: [e2e.md](../developer/e2e.md#drain-and-failover-under-npm-load).

### Q-HA-488 · nuget-ha keeps the drain under the NuGet load and leaves the switchover and the Valkey failover to npm-ha

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-23** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the
walkthrough. Amends [Q-HA-100](#q-ha-100--the-nuget-part-of-r-ha-059s-load-and-how-it-runs-beside-npms).

Context: `TestNuGetHA` ran drain variant A, the PostgreSQL switchover and the Valkey failover of R-HA-052, each under the npm and
the NuGet load together, the same three scenarios `TestNPMHA` runs under the npm load in the same night (G5-08 of the triage of
2026-11-23). A switchover and a failover test the server: whether a replica answers without an error while the database or Valkey
moves. What NuGet's client adds is how `dotnet restore` and `dotnet nuget push` behave across connections that are cut, which the
drain does (it evicts the `packages` pods that hold them), and the drain under both loads is R-ARCH-024's first acceptance criterion.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) `nuget-ha` runs the drain alone (chosen) | `TestNuGetHA` keeps drain variant A under both loads; the switchover and the failover stay in `TestNPMHA` | About ten minutes less of the heaviest leg of lane 1 every night; nothing NuGet's client does goes untested | The server's answers during a switchover are judged under the npm load only |
| (b) Keep the three | | Nothing changes | A repeat of npm-ha's server tests on a leg twice as heavy |
| (c) Merge `drain-load-b`, `-c`, `-e` into one cluster run as well | | One cluster instead of three | The variants drain different nodes and leave the cluster in different states; a failure of one would hide the others |

**Choice:** (a). The test `TestNuGetHA_R_REPO_058_MirrorStatusFromEveryReplica` of the same set stays. **Cost:** the leg
`nuget-ha` loses two subtests of about five minutes each. Not verified: a run of the shortened set; the next night shows it.

[e2e.md](../developer/e2e.md#drain-and-failover-under-nuget-load).

### Q-HA-489 · Every image of the development profiles carries the checkout's tag, and the charts run the image they were given

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-23** — selected from the options below; the owner reviews it at the
walkthrough.

Context: two defects of the development profiles, found by the reading of 2026-11-23 (F-058, F-077, F-160, F-059). (1) `up.sh`,
`bastion.sh` and `restore-ns.sh` load `QUADER_IMAGE` into the kind nodes, but the values pinned `repository: guidedtraffic/quader`,
`tag: dev` and the helm calls set neither, so with `QUADER_IMAGE=foo:bar` the pods ran `guidedtraffic/quader:dev`; another image was
loaded and never used. (2) Every image of the profiles had a fixed tag (`guidedtraffic/quader:dev`, `quader-e2e-driver:dev`, the
seven stubs', the clients'), in the one Docker daemon of the machine, so a builder's worktree and the main checkout that built at the
same time tagged over each other and each ran whichever was tagged last.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) A tag per checkout, `DEV_TAG` (`dev` in a main checkout, `dev-<worktree directory>` in a git worktree, `QUADER_DEV_TAG` overrides), on every image the profiles build and run, and the charts' `image.registry`, `image.repository` and `image.tag` set from the image the script was given (chosen) | One script, [dev-tag.sh](../../deploy/dev/dev-tag.sh), read by `lib.sh`, the Makefile (once, when a recipe needs it) and `client-images.sh` | Two checkouts never run each other's image; the main checkout and every runner keep `dev`, so nothing of the pipeline or the owner's commands changes; `QUADER_IMAGE` alone is enough, as `up.sh` promised | Every script and manifest that named `:dev` names the variable |
| (b) Refuse a `QUADER_IMAGE` whose tag is not `dev` | | One check | Leaves (2); a worktree still overwrites the main checkout's image |
| (c) `docker tag "$IMAGE" guidedtraffic/quader:dev` before the load | | The values stay | Retags the shared name, which is (2) itself |

**Choice:** (a). The tag also names the analyser's and ClamAV's images of the `vuln` profile (`trivy.image`, `clamav.image`) and the
marked image of the upgrade set (`<tag>-marked`); `e2e.sh` hands `QUADER_IMAGE` and `QUADER_IMAGE_MARKED` to the tests. With the build
switched off (`QUADER_E2E_<SET>_CLIENTS_IMAGE_BUILD=0`), `e2e.sh` checks that the clients images are in the local Docker and names
the missing one and the switch (F-078). What it does not separate: the kind cluster and its edge port (`QUADER_DEV_CLUSTER`,
`QUADER_DEV_HTTP_PORT`), which a second checkout still sets itself. Verified on the development machine on 2026-11-23: a profile
started from a worktree (`quader-w7`) without `QUADER_IMAGE` loaded `guidedtraffic/quader:dev-agent-…`, and its migration Job ran
`docker.io/guidedtraffic/quader:dev-agent-…` (a two-day-old build retagged for the check, older than the tree's configuration, so
the release itself did not start); `TestMakeListsTheIntegrationPackagesOnlyWhenARecipeNeedsThem` holds that a make of another
target runs no git for the tag, `TestTheE2EImageBuildsRemoveTheUntaggedImagesTheyLeft` the label and the prune of the e2e images.

The image a script runs is `QUADER_IMAGE` and nothing else. Its tag reaches helm as `--set-string`, and helm applies every `--set-json`,
then every `--set`, then every `--set-string`, whatever their order on the command line, so an image among the extra arguments
(`QUADER_HELM_EXTRA`, `QUADER_BASTION_HELM_EXTRA`, `QUADER_RESTORE_HELM_EXTRA`) lost to the script's own tag without a word: the
interface-mismatch scenario (Q-BAS-111) passed `--set image.tag=iface`, both installations kept the checkout's image, and
`TestBastion_R_BAS_049_InterfaceMismatch` timed out waiting for the mismatch (Test and Release 45187733127 and 45191858474, the first
runs after this change). The scripts refuse an `image`, `image.registry`, `image.repository`, `image.tag` or `image.digest` among their
extra arguments and name `QUADER_IMAGE` (`refuse_image_extra` of [lib.sh](../../deploy/dev/lib.sh)), and the scenario gives its image
as `QUADER_IMAGE`; `TestAnImageAmongTheExtraHelmArgumentsIsRefused` and `TestAProfileScriptRunsTheImageItsCallerGave` hold both.

**Applied in the spec:** none (development tooling). Code: [dev-tag.sh](../../deploy/dev/dev-tag.sh), `image_values` and
`release_values` of [lib.sh](../../deploy/dev/lib.sh), [up.sh](../../deploy/dev/up.sh), [bastion.sh](../../deploy/dev/bastion.sh),
[restore-ns.sh](../../deploy/dev/restore-ns.sh), [e2e.sh](../../deploy/dev/e2e.sh), the stubs' manifests, the build scripts of the
clients images, the [Makefile](../../Makefile). Elsewhere: [local-profile.md](../developer/local-profile.md#one-image-tag-per-checkout).

### Q-HA-490 · The development profile's root CA is Ready before a leaf is requested

Status: **Decided by the development agent on 2026-11-23** — the repair the reading of 2026-11-23 named; the owner reviews it at the
walkthrough.

Context: the certificate operator's log of a red `e2e (ci)` showed the profile's root `quader-dev-ca` issued at 16:28:35.29 and again
at .60, and five leaves signed with the first key in between, the edge's among them; no client of the second root trusts those. The
same double root was in the red `e2e (push)` of F-127. `up.sh` applied [pki.yaml](../../deploy/dev/pki.yaml), the self-signed Issuer,
the root, the CA Issuer and every leaf, in one `kubectl apply`.

| Option | What it means | For | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) The root first: apply the objects labelled `quader-dev/pki=root`, wait until the root's Certificate and the CA Issuer are Ready, then apply the file (chosen) | One file, one label, one wait | No leaf is requested while the root can still change; the leaves are signed by the root that stays | A few seconds more at a start |
| (b) Two files | | The order is the files' | Every reference to `pki.yaml` changes |
| (c) Wait for the leaves and reissue those signed by a replaced root | | Repairs after the fact | Needs to detect the mismatch; a client may have read the wrong chain already |

**Choice:** (a). Not verified: that the double issuance does not recur in the pipeline (it was seen in single runs; the next runs'
certificate operator logs, kept in `kept-pod-logs/` of the evidence, show it). Verified on the development machine: a start of the
profile issues the root once (one CertificateRequest `quader-dev-ca-1`) and every leaf after it.

**Applied in the spec:** none (development tooling). Code: [pki.yaml](../../deploy/dev/pki.yaml), `task_pki` of
[up.sh](../../deploy/dev/up.sh). Elsewhere: [local-profile.md](../developer/local-profile.md#how-upsh-works).
